title: Transcript ledger
detail: Parse ~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl; sum tokens by tool, command head and MCP server to find the top 10 token sinks.
because: parses ~/.claude private transcript files

title: Output-size histogram
detail: What share of tool-result tokens sits below vs above the 6k-char threshold? Shows whether the threshold is the biggest lever.
because: agnostic size-distribution analysis

title: Tokenizer ground truth
detail: Compare count_tokens vs chars/4 vs tiktoken on ~500 real outputs per content type; tests the unit="chars" assumption.
because: offline tokenizer comparison at dev time

title: Cache-aware cost model
detail: A saved token is worth ~1.25x write plus 0.1x per remaining turn; rank savings in dollars, not tokens.
because: agnostic cost model, pluggable price book

title: Net savings accounting
detail: Net = saved - note - recovery (greps of the saved original, cat of it, command re-runs); measure the recovery rate on real sessions.
because: net savings accounting measurement

title: Replay harness
detail: Feed recorded tool events through hook.run offline and print a per-rule savings table, so every idea can be A/B'd in seconds without an LLM.
because: offline replay harness over recorded tool events

title: Task-success A/B
detail: Run 20-30 fixed repo tasks with the hook on and off; compare tokens, turns and pass rate. Catches 'saved tokens, cost more turns'.
because: task-success A/B benchmark

title: Regret log
detail: Whenever the original gets grepped, record which rule removed what was needed.
because: regret logging analysis tooling

title: Strip ANSI and OSC escapes
detail: Colors, cursor moves, OSC-8 hyperlinks (which duplicate the URL).
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Removes every ESC sequence (colours, cursor moves, titles, truncated ones); an OSC-8 hyperlink becomes 'text (uri)' unless the visible text equals the uri, so link targets are kept.
check_loses: colours and styles, cursor movement, window titles, cwd and shell-integration marks (OSC 0/7/133), OSC-8 link params such as id=, and a truncated escape's partial bytes

title: Collapse CR progress updates
detail: Collapse \r progress updates to the final frame (pip, curl, wget, npm, docker, git clone).
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Within a line, only the last non-empty carriage-return frame is kept; CRLF endings, line count and trailing CRs are untouched.
check_loses: intermediate progress frames

title: Normalise line endings and invisibles
detail: CRLF to LF, strip trailing whitespace, BOM, zero-width characters, nbsp.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: CRLF and CR-CR-LF become LF, trailing blanks and CRs are removed, BOM/ZWSP/word-joiner/soft-hyphen are deleted and nbsp becomes a space; ZWNJ/ZWJ and unified diffs are left byte-identical.
check_loses: CR count before LF, trailing whitespace (so a Markdown two-space hard break is lost), invisible characters used as markers, nbsp-versus-space distinction

title: Collapse blank-line runs
detail: Runs of 3+ blank lines to one.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Runs of 3+ blank lines (whitespace-only counts as blank) become one; every non-blank line and every paragraph break survives in order.
check_loses: how many blank lines a run of three or more had, and whitespace on the collapsed blank lines

title: Dedent common leading whitespace
detail: Display-only blocks only, never text that will be edited.
because: deterministic whitespace transform on display-only output
check: Removes the whitespace prefix shared by every non-blank line of an indented display block; relative indentation is kept, and source excerpts, line-numbered file views and diffs are left byte-identical.
check_loses: the absolute column offset of the block (relative indentation between lines is kept)

title: Whitespace tokenization study
detail: Tabs vs spaces and long space runs in aligned columns; measure which forms the tokenizer likes.
because: tokenizer measurement study
check: Seven whitespace transforms are measured with harness.tokens on built-in samples; the measurement is deterministic and order-independent, each transform passes an independent fidelity oracle, and each leaves unsafe samples (empty table cells, TSV, Makefile recipes) untouched.

title: Glyph substitution
detail: Smart quotes and dashes to ASCII, box-drawing borders to a plain pipe char, check/cross/emoji to ASCII, spinner frames removed; measure tokens per char per class.
because: deterministic glyph substitution on tool output
check: Box-drawing glyphs become | - +, a pure horizontal rule line becomes '---', curly quotes/dashes/minus become ASCII (quotes only on lines without that ASCII quote), check/cross/warning marks become [ok] [x] [!], and lone braille spinner frames are dropped.
check_loses: glyph shape (light/heavy/double borders, quote and dash style), the width and junction positions of horizontal rules, which of several check/cross glyphs was used, spinner frames (a one-cell braille meter before a word is misread as a frame)

title: Drop stdout/stderr duplicates
detail: When both streams contain the same text (2>&1 plus tee).
because: deterministic dedupe within one tool result
check: In a Bash tool_response whose stderr equals stdout or a block of whole lines of it, stderr becomes '[stderr = stdout lines i-j]'; a reader resolves the pointer to the exact original, and mismatching, tiny, other-tool or malformed responses pass through untouched.
check_loses: stderr as a separate stream: the model sees stdout lines i-j once instead of a second copy

title: Dedupe repeated failure blocks
detail: pytest and similar tools print each failure in the body and again in the summary.
because: deterministic dedupe within one tool result
check: A failure block repeated byte-for-byte later in the same output (jest summary) becomes one marker line, and a pytest summary message identical to the first E line above becomes a marker; the exact original is restored from the text above, and anything not provably identical is left in place.

title: NFC-normalise Unicode
detail: Combining characters inflate tokens; tiny win.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Decomposed letters in plain words (letters, marks, apostrophes, hyphens, edge punctuation) are composed to NFC; lines that list files or contain a path, URL or address, and tokens that look like identifiers, keep their exact code points.
check_loses: the decomposed code-point form of ordinary words (canonically equivalent, but not byte-identical)

title: Consecutive identical lines
detail: Collapse to 'line [xN]'.
because: calibration case: repeated line collapse
check: A run of two or more identical lines becomes one 'line [xN]'; any original line that already ends in ' [xN]' is written with an explicit ' [x1]' so decode restores the exact bytes.

title: Non-consecutive exact duplicates
detail: First occurrence plus '[xN total]'.
because: exact duplicate line folding
check: Each distinct line of 12+ characters is kept once, at the position of its first occurrence, with ' [xN total]' giving how often it occurred; every other line stays in place and in order.
check_loses: where the second and later copies of a folded line sat among the other lines (only their number survives); lines under 12 characters are never folded

title: Template mining (Drain3)
detail: '<TS> INFO req <ID> ok in <N>ms' becomes one template plus a variable table; test the reconstructible form vs first/last example plus count.
because: local template mining of log lines

title: Periodic multi-line blocks
detail: Retry loops that repeat a k-line stanza, detected and folded.
because: fold repeated line blocks
check: A stanza of k>=2 lines repeated back to back N times is written once followed by '[the k lines above: xN total]'; decode restores the exact bytes, including lines shaped like the marker.

title: Timestamp factoring
detail: Hoist the shared date to a header; per-line times or deltas. A timestamp can cost 10-15 tokens x 1000 lines.
because: hoist shared timestamp prefix
check: The most common date+separator among timestamped lines moves to one header line; lines that start with hh:mm:ss get it back on decode, lines of other dates and untimed lines are untouched, and the time text is kept exactly as written.

title: Column-prefix factoring
detail: Hoist '[INFO] [worker-3] [mod.x]' when constant over a run.
because: hoist constant column prefix
check: Runs of 3+ consecutive lines that open with the same '[..] [..] ' token sequence share one '§N prefix' header; the remainders follow verbatim and decode restores the exact bytes.

title: Homogeneous pass lines to a count
detail: '412 PASSED lines omitted', failures kept verbatim.
because: count passing lines; text transform

title: Counter sequences
detail: 'Downloading 17/200' x200 becomes first, last and count.
because: fold counter progress sequences

title: Tree-ify file listings
detail: find, ls -R, rg --files: print each directory once instead of the full path per line.
because: tree-ify path listings
check: A one-path-per-line listing is rewritten so each line holds only the path components not shared with the line above (indented by the shared count); line order and exact path text are restored by decode.

title: Group grep/rg hits by file
detail: 'file:' then indented '12: ...' instead of repeating the filename per line.
because: group grep hits by file
check: A run of 3+ 'file:LINE:text' hits in the same file becomes one '§N file' header plus N 'LINE:text' rows; every other line (context, separators, other output) stays verbatim and decode restores the exact bytes.

title: Strip git boilerplate
detail: (use "git add ...") hints, hint: lines, remote: banners, repeated CRLF warnings.
because: strip git boilerplate lines
check: Removes (use "git ...") advice lines, hint: lines of commands that did not fail, and remote: progress/blank lines; runs of per-file CRLF warnings fold into one line listing every file; every other line, including remote: content and hints of a failed command, is kept in order.
check_loses: git's advice wording ((use "git ...") lines; hint: lines when no error:/fatal:/rejected line is present; remote: progress and blank lines) and the one-warning-per-file layout (file names are kept)

title: Collapse redundant diff headers
detail: diff --git / index / --- / +++ on display-only diffs.
because: collapse redundant diff headers
check: Each plain-modification header block (diff --git / index / --- / +++ for an unchanged 100644 file) becomes '== path'; every hunk, every body line and every other kind of header block is unchanged, as an independent diff parser confirms.
check_loses: the abbreviated blob ids on the index line, the constant mode 100644 and the a/ b/ prefixes of plain-modification headers: the result cannot be used with git apply or git am

title: JSON minify
detail: Verify with json.loads equality; probably the cheapest big win on pretty-printed MCP output.
because: JSON minify, parse-verified
check: All whitespace outside strings is removed from a complete JSON document; number spellings (1E5, 1.0, big ints), duplicate keys, key order and every string byte are untouched, and anything that is not valid JSON is returned as is.
check_loses: indentation, newlines and spaces between tokens (including the trailing newline)

title: Columnar encoding for uniform object arrays
detail: TOON or CSV with a header; round-trip tested on GitHub, Jira, Slack lists.
because: columnar encoding of JSON arrays
check: An array of at least three objects becomes one header line of keys plus one comma-separated line per object; decoding restores each object's keys in their original order, absent keys (distinct from null and ""), nested values and number lexemes.
check_loses: whitespace between JSON tokens (the decoded array is minified)

title: Drop null/empty/default JSON fields
detail: null, "", [], false.
because: drop null/empty JSON fields

title: Per-MCP-server key blocklists
detail: GitHub *_url templates, node_id, gravatar_id, _links; Jira self/avatarUrls; Slack blocks. Built from captured outputs.
because: key blocklists keyed by MCP tool name

title: Dedupe repeated nested objects
detail: Same user object x50 defined once and referenced.
because: dedupe repeated nested objects
check: Object values that occur more than once in a JSON document are defined once in a legend and replaced by a §k token (nested repeats first); decoding substitutes them back, so the document parses to the same tree.
check_loses: whitespace between JSON tokens (output is minified); a repeated object must match byte for byte after minifying, so key order or number spelling differences keep copies separate

title: Strip comments and blank lines in YAML/TOML/INI
detail: Config-style outputs.
because: strip comments in config text
check: Full-line comments, trailing comments (TOML and YAML only) and blank lines are removed from TOML, INI and YAML (block maps and sequences, quoted and plain scalars, | and > block scalars; other YAML is left alone); a # inside a quoted string, a URL fragment, a multi-line string or a block scalar is never touched, and every parser that reads the original (tomllib, configparser, a YAML-subset loader) reads the result identically.
check_loses: comments, blank lines (before a line that starts at column 0) and spaces before a trailing comment; INI trailing comments are not comments to configparser, so they stay

title: Fixed-width table padding to single separators
detail: ps, docker ps, kubectl get, df.
because: collapse table padding
check: A fixed-width text table is stored as one geometry header (leading gap, per-column width and L/R alignment, gap widths) plus tab-separated trimmed cells; decoding re-pads every line to the identical bytes, and any table the geometry cannot express exactly is left untouched.

title: Markdown table padding and separator rows
detail: Reduce to minimal form.
because: minimise markdown tables
check: GFM pipe tables lose their cell padding and become |a|b| rows with a minimal :-: / -: / :- delimiter row; cell text (trimmed), column count and alignment are kept, and fenced code, text with pipes that is not a table, tables without outer pipes and ragged tables are left as they were.
check_loses: whitespace around cell text and the number of dashes in the delimiter row

title: HTML cleanup
detail: Drop script/style/svg/nav/footer and class/style/data-* attributes; compare HTML-to-Markdown vs trafilatura/readability.
because: local HTML cleanup of fetched text

because: slim XML test and coverage reports

because: elide base64 blobs in text

because: strip signed-URL tails

because: round float noise in metrics

because: cap per-line length

because: pytest output noise rules, text transform

because: build tool output noise rules

because: docker layer chatter text rules

title: kubectl, terraform, helm noise pack

because: infra CLI output noise rules

title: apt and brew noise pack
detail: Get:N, Reading package lists, Unpacking, Setting up.
because: apt/brew output noise rules

title: Linters and type checkers grouping
detail: Group diagnostics by rule: message once, then the file:line list.
because: groups linter diagnostics by rule
check: Within each run of consecutive 'file:line[:col]: message' lines, a message that occurs twice or more is written once as '§N message' followed by N location lines; singletons and every other line stay as written.
check_loses: the order of diagnostics inside one run (locations are listed by message, in first-seen order)

title: Compiler backtraces
detail: Keep first/last N lines of include stacks and 'in instantiation of' chains.
because: trims compiler include/instantiation chains

title: Stack traces
detail: Collapse framework frames (site-packages, node_modules, java.base/, <frozen importlib>) to '... 14 framework frames'.
because: collapses framework stack frames

title: Drop rarely used columns
detail: ls -l, ps, du, lsof; test whether the agent tolerates it.
because: drops rarely used CLI columns, text rewrite

title: SQL and DB MCP results
detail: Drop all-null columns, truncate blob columns.
because: drops null/blob columns in DB results

title: Pack-discovery tool
detail: Cluster lines across captured outputs by template and rank templates by total tokens; finds the next noise rules from data instead of guessing.
because: analysis tool ranking line templates in captures

title: Re-read of unchanged file
detail: Replace with 'unchanged since read at turn N'; key on mtime and hash.
because: stub unchanged re-read, keyed on args and content hash
check: A Read whose returned text hashes the same as an earlier Read of the same path and range becomes a one-line pointer to that turn; edits by the model or anyone else, a different range or path, compaction and a rewrite that kept size and mtime all show the full text.

title: Re-run with identical output
detail: Replace with a stub.
because: stub identical re-run output
check: A re-run of the same command in the same cwd with byte-identical output (exit status included) becomes a one-line pointer to the previous literal output; changed output, another command string or cwd, a different exit status or compaction show the full text.

title: Re-run with changed output
detail: Show only the delta vs the previous run plus 'N lines unchanged'; should help most in edit-and-test loops.
because: delta vs previous run output, deterministic
check: A re-run whose output changed is shown as keep/drop/add line counts plus only the new lines, vs the previous run of the same command; replaying the chain from the last literal output rebuilds every run exactly, chains are capped, and the full text is shown when the delta is not shorter.

title: Overlapping reads and greps
detail: Trim lines already shown earlier.
because: trim lines already shown in earlier results
check: Lines of a Read range already shown from the same unchanged file become 'lines a-b already shown at turn N' pointers and Grep hits already shown become path:line keys, new lines stay literal in place; a changed file, a different file, shifted line numbers, an Edit or compaction show everything.

title: Stub-safety test
detail: Invalidate state on PreCompact, /clear and subagent boundaries (subagents do not share context); measure the dangling-stub rate.
because: stub-safety test measuring dangling-stub rate

title: Shorten the note
detail: Cut ~80 tokens to ~15, e.g. 'ctxprune 12,430->6,100 chars; full: <id>'; check Claude still uses it correctly.
because: shorter note text appended to tool result
check: The note shrinks to 'ctxprune <before>-><after> chars; full: <path>' (hundreds of chars less per compressed call) while still giving both sizes and a path whose file equals the original output byte for byte; no note is emitted when nothing is compressed or the original cannot be saved. Whether Claude still uses the terse note correctly needs a live transcript.

title: Full note once per session
detail: Terse tag afterwards.
because: terse note after first, deterministic from history
check: The first compressed output of a session (marker file per hashed session id, created O_EXCL so racing hooks yield one winner) gets the full note and every later one a terse '<sizes>; full: <path>' tag; every note still opens to the exact original, other sessions, missing ids and unwritable state all get the full note. Caveat: after context compaction the early full note may be gone, the terse tag keeps the path.

title: Shorter saved-path or id
detail: The 16-hex path is token-heavy; try a fixed .ctxprune/ relative path or 'ctxprune show <id>'.
because: shorter saved-output id in the note
check: A short id (8 hex, or 'ctxprune show <id>' / '.ctxprune/<id>.txt') replaces the 55+ char absolute path; on an id collision with different content the id is lengthened so two outputs never alias (a 4-hex id with the current trust-if-exists logic returns the wrong file for some of 1,000 outputs, the extending store for none); 'show' matches ids exactly so '../' cannot escape. A relative path breaks after cd, so it needs the cwd or an absolute fallback.

title: Net-savings gate
detail: Skip when estimated saved tokens are under ~200.
because: net-savings gate on estimated tokens
check: Adding 'skip when the estimated saving is under 200 tokens (800 chars)' to the 0.95 rule means every shipped output saves more than its note costs (net chars > 0 over a 119-point size x ratio grid; the current rule alone ships 10 net-negative points, 9 of them only when CTXPRUNE_MIN_CHARS is lowered to 2000), a skipped output is returned untouched with no file written, and big wins still ship; the price is the small positive savings the gate forgoes (reported as a number).

title: Threshold sweep
detail: 1.5k, 2k, 3k and 6k chars, reporting net tokens and latency; can likely drop a lot when the server is running.
because: threshold sweep measurement

title: Auto-start ctxprune serve from a SessionStart hook
detail: Removes the ~2 s cold start so low thresholds become viable; measure p50/p95 per call.
because: SessionStart hook auto-start

title: Skip-list by file type, not command name
detail: cat build.log, tail, and git log without -p are safe; cat src/*.py is not.
because: skip list keyed on command string file types
check: Whether a Bash output is kept verbatim is decided by the files and git mode it reads (source and config extensions, unknown files, globs, patch output, stdin of unknown origin, unparseable commands stay verbatim; .log/.out/.err files, git log without a patch flag, git diff/show with only summary flags and pipes from non-file producers are compressible): on a 67-command labelled corpus no editable-file read is released, 15 safe commands the name-based regex blocks are released, and 8 reads of source or diffs that the name-based regex lets through (tail/awk/tac, FOO=1 cat, sudo cat, git -C or --no-pager diff, git log --patch) are now kept verbatim.

because: tests hook matcher support for WebFetch/Task

because: rewrites command string with quiet env defaults
check: For commands that run chatty tools, 'export NO_COLOR=1 [GIT_PAGER=cat]; ' is put in front of the unchanged command and '--no-fund' after 'npm install|i|ci|add'; arguments, quoting, pipes and exit status are unchanged, anything the user already set stays theirs, other commands are byte-identical.

title: Property tests for every lossless rule
detail: Round-trip or parse-equality, idempotent, never grows output (hypothesis fuzzing).
because: property tests for lossless rules

title: Golden corpus
detail: Per-rule snapshot diffs from real captured outputs.
because: golden corpus snapshot tests

title: Rule-interaction tests
detail: Ordering and double application.
because: rule-interaction tests

title: Hook latency budget
detail: Enforce p99 under a fixed limit.
because: latency budget test

title: Edit-safety simulation
detail: Copy a line from processed output into an Edit old_string and check it matches the real file.
because: edit-safety simulation test

title: Saved-originals hygiene
detail: Disk growth, TTL cleanup, secret redaction at save time.
because: local saved-original store cleanup, independent of harness

title: Strip echoed source lines and caret markers from diagnostics
detail: Drop the echoed source line, gutter and ~~~/^^^ squiggles from ruff full format, tsc --pretty, esbuild and babel; file:line:col plus message suffices. Python 3.11+ traceback marker lines and difflib '?' lines go too. Measured: ruff 1763 vs 525 chars concise, tsc 1460 vs 298 plain.
test: Run ruff and tsc in full and concise modes and collect 100 tracebacks; count tokens saved; replay fixes to check agents resolve errors from file:line:col alone.
because: strips echoed source and carets from diagnostics
check: Drops the echoed source line, gutter and ~~~/^^^ marker lines under ruff, gcc, clang and tsc --pretty diagnostics, the ^^^^ marker lines in Python 3.11+ tracebacks and difflib '?' hint lines; every diagnostic header (file:line:col, code, message), traceback frame with its source line, exception line, help/note line and summary line is unchanged.
check_loses: the code excerpt and the exact column span shown under each diagnostic (the start column stays in the header), ruff's fix-preview diff under 'help:', gcc/clang caret underline widths, and difflib's character-level change hints; a gutter line carrying a label or fix-it text is kept

title: Drop pytest -vv Common items and Full diff sections
detail: In a -vv dict failure the repr appears in the assert line, Common items, Full diff and the FAILED summary line. Measured: 4940 chars total; Common items 642, Full diff 918, FAILED line 678. Keep Differing items and +/- lines only.
test: Generate failing dict, list, str and dataclass asserts under -vv; tokenise each section; verify the +/- lines alone preserve every difference.
because: drops duplicate pytest -vv sections

title: Per-tool key pruning for CLI JSON reporters
detail: eslint -f json embeds each flagged file's full source (seen in eslint 9) plus nodeType, messageId, usedDeprecatedRules; jest --json reportedly repeats fullName; webpack --json reportedly lists reasons and issuerPath per module. Blocklist these keys per tool.
test: Run eslint, jest, webpack and npm audit with JSON output on a mid-size repo; rank keys by total chars; blocklist the top ones; check agents still act correctly.
because: key blocklists for CLI JSON reporters
check: Recognises eslint -f json, jest --json, webpack --json and npm audit --json by shape and removes per-tool noise keys (eslint source/usedDeprecatedRules/fix/suggestions/messageId/nodeType, jest fullName/failureDetails/location/duplicate suite message, webpack reasons/issuerPath/identifier, npm audit cwe/cvss/nodes); every problem with file:line:col:rule:message, every test with status and failure text, a suite that failed to run, all modules, assets, errors and totals are unchanged.
check_loses: eslint autofix text and suggestion ranges, the full source of each file, rule messageIds and deprecation notices; jest duplicate fullName, failureDetails matcher objects, per-suite timestamps and the aggregated suite message when per-test failures exist; webpack module reasons, issuer chains and profiling; npm audit CWE and CVSS vectors, install paths and the effects list; whitespace of pretty-printed input

title: Lockfile and lockfile-diff digest without integrity hashes
detail: package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.lock, uv.lock and go.sum hunks become 'pkg old->new' lines; integrity hashes and resolved URLs dropped. Here, 823k of uv.lock's 858k chars sit on sha256 lines. Needs a lockfile exception to the git diff skip.
test: Take git diff for 20 lockfile-touching commits; compare tokens raw vs digest by line class; try :(exclude) lockfile pathspecs in PreToolUse; check agents still name changed versions.
because: lockfile hunks to pkg old-new lines
check: In a git diff, the hunks of package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, Cargo.lock, uv.lock and go.sum become a header plus 'name old->new' / '+ name ver' / '- name ver' lines; every (name, version) pair that left or entered the lockfile survives, and every non-lockfile diff stays byte-identical.
check_loses: integrity hashes, resolved URLs, file sizes and upload times, dependency lists and specifier ranges (including the 'requires-dist' / root 'dependencies' lines that record a changed constraint), engines/license/bin fields, and the context lines of the hunk

title: Extract plaintext traceback from framework debug HTML pages
detail: curl against a dev server returns Django's debug 500 page: 80,349 chars here for a one-line KeyError, while its traceback_area textarea holds 1,703. Werkzeug and Rails error pages reportedly embed plaintext copies too. Extract that, drop the rest.
test: curl broken routes on Django, Flask and Rails dev servers; compare page vs extracted traceback tokens; also test injecting an Accept: text/plain header via PreToolUse.
because: extract traceback from debug HTML
check: A Django debug page (textarea#traceback_area) or Werkzeug page (textarea in div.plain) is replaced by one header line plus the unescaped plaintext traceback; every frame (file, line, function), the innermost frame, Exception Type/Value, request line, versions, chained-exception count and template-error lines are unchanged; other HTML (404 pages, pages with two candidates, markup in the textarea) is untouched.
check_loses: the page markup and CSS/JS, the per-frame source context and local variables table, the request META, GET/POST and cookies tables, the full settings table, and any exception text that appears only in the browser view

title: Keep only the latest watch-mode compile cycle
detail: tsc --watch, vite, webpack --watch and vitest re-print a full report per change; earlier cycles' errors are stale. When a background-output poll returns several cycles, keep the last plus a cycle count. Needs BashOutput in the hook matcher.
test: Verify that BashOutput results reach PostToolUse; run tsc --watch, edit a file three times, poll; compare full log with last-cycle-only and check stale errors never mislead.
because: keep last watch cycle within one output

title: Rails, Django and Alembic log pack: one line per request
detail: Rails logs Started, Processing, Parameters, SQL lines with caller arrows, Rendered timings and Completed (from memory); Django logs 'Not Found' then the access line. Emit one line per request. Django migrate printed 18 'Applying... OK' lines of 21; collapse OK runs and banners, keep failures.
test: Drive 50 requests and run migrate, db:migrate and alembic upgrade on sample apps; compare raw vs collapsed tokens; check the slow or failing request is still findable.
because: one-line-per-request log folding
check: A quiet Rails request block (status below 400, under 500 ms, only recognised lines) becomes 'METHOD /path -> status Nms Ctrl#action sql=N ar=X'; slow, failing, error-bearing and unrecognised blocks stay verbatim; Django runs of 3+ '  Applying x... OK' become one line with count, first and last migration; a 'Not Found:/Bad Request:/...' line above its access line (several reason lines in a row all look at the same access line) is dropped; Alembic 'Context impl' and 'transactional DDL' lines fold to a count.
check_loses: the client address, timestamp, parameters, SQL text, view timings and caller arrows of quiet requests, the middle migration names of a long run, and the Django reason line that the access line repeats

title: Webpack, Vite and Next build report digest
detail: Webpack default stats list every module with [built] flags and nested 'modules by path' groups (from memory); Next.js prints a route-size table plus a constant legend. Keep warnings, errors, top assets by size and totals. A tiny vite build was only 4 lines.
test: Build a 300-module webpack app and a Next.js app; classify lines by template; check which lines agents ever act on versus errors and warnings.
because: build report digest, text transform
check: In a webpack report only the 5 largest 'asset' lines stay (runs of smaller ones become one line with their count and exact total bytes) and runs of 2+ leaf module lines fold to a count, while the 'modules by path' group sizes, every WARNING/ERROR block and the compiled-with line stay; in a Next.js report the constant legend and the 'chunks/...' lines under the shared total fold to counts and every route row stays.
check_loses: the names, flags and sizes of assets beyond the 5 largest (count and total remain), the path and size of each leaf module, the sizes of individual shared Next.js chunks, and the legend text

title: Dedupe warnings across test files and worker PIDs
detail: pytest's warnings summary repeats the same DeprecationWarning under many test files; Node prints '(node:PID) [DEPxxxx]' per jest worker; React act() warnings carry component stacks. Normalise PID, path and line numbers, then fold to message, count and first location.
test: Collect pytest and jest runs from five repos; normalise PIDs and paths; count duplicate warning blocks and the tokens they hold.
because: dedupe warnings in test output

title: One line per finding for npm audit, SARIF and scanners
detail: npm audit text prints a title plus GHSA URL per advisory (handlebars 4.0.5 gave 20 such lines in 4,915 chars). For it and semgrep/CodeQL SARIF, trivy, grype, pip-audit, emit 'pkg version advisory fixed-in' or 'file:line rule message'; drop fingerprints, URL arrays, CVSS vectors.
test: Run npm audit and semgrep --sarif on sample repos; compare digest tokens; verify every file:line and fixed-in version survives and the agent picks the right fix command.
because: scanner output to one line per finding
check: npm audit text and SARIF 2.1.0 become one compact line per finding (package+range+severity+GHSA id+title+fix, or file:line+level+rule+message); URL prefixes, boilerplate, fingerprints, snippets, rule help and tag arrays are dropped; every finding identity and fix command survives and anything unrecognised passes through unchanged.
check_loses: the advisory URL (derivable from the GHSA id), 'Severity:'/'fix available via' wording, SARIF fingerprints, code snippets, rule help/markdown/tags/helpUri, invocation records, secondary locations (only counted) and message whitespace

title: Normalise JSON string escapes and inline nested JSON strings
detail: Decode redundant \u003c, \u0026, \/ and \r\n escapes inside string values. When a string value is itself JSON (MCP text wrappers, webhook payloads), inline it as structure to drop the \" escape layer. Verify by parse equality.
test: Scan captured MCP JSON for \uXXXX, \r\n and string values that parse as JSON; compare token counts before and after; assert parsed values equal.
because: normalise JSON string escapes
check: Redundant string escapes (\uXXXX for printable characters, \/) are written as the characters, and a string value that is itself a JSON object or array is inlined as structure inside {"§json": ...}; every value, number spelling, duplicate key and key order is preserved, and input that already uses the marker key is escaped with a "§raw" prefix.
check_loses: the exact text of an inlined JSON string (its whitespace and escape spelling; only its parsed value survives), whitespace between tokens, and the spelling of \uXXXX / \/ escapes; \r\n escapes stay escaped because a raw newline cannot live inside a JSON string

title: Minify pretty-printed JSON blocks embedded in mixed output
detail: Find balanced {...} or [...] blocks starting at line start inside logs, aws CLI, curl -v or debug prints. Validate with json.loads and minify only that block, leaving surrounding text alone. Whole-output JSON minify misses these.
test: Over a replay corpus, count indent whitespace bytes inside valid JSON blocks of outputs that are not pure JSON; tokenise before and after.
because: minify embedded JSON blocks
check: A balanced {...} or [...] block that starts at column 0 and ends its line, and that json.loads accepts, is minified in place; every other byte of the output (log lines, repr dicts, [section] headers, indented JSON) is untouched.
check_loses: whitespace between tokens inside the minified blocks

title: Hoist constant key-value pairs out of JSON records
detail: In NDJSON logs (pino, zap, slog, docker --json) and record arrays, find keys with identical values on nearly every record (service, host, pid, type, version). Print once in a header, delete per row, keep exceptions inline.
test: On sample NDJSON and GitHub list outputs, measure the share of key-value pairs constant on 90% or more of rows, and token delta after hoisting.
because: hoist constant JSON key-values
check: Keys that hold the same value in at least 90% of the records, sit at the same position and exist in every record are printed once in a header (position, key, value); records that differ keep the pair inline, and decoding re-inserts the pairs at their positions.
check_loses: whitespace between tokens (records are minified)

title: Auto-mine derivable JSON fields instead of hand blocklists
detail: Per MCP tool, detect fields whose value is a template of sibling fields (html_url from repo plus number, *_url from url, node_id) or constant across a corpus. Emit drop lists automatically; originals stay in the saved file.
test: Run the miner over captured GitHub, Jira and Slack MCP outputs; list candidate fields with removable tokens; hand-review 30 for false positives.
because: mine derivable JSON fields locally
check: In a JSON array of >= 5 objects, leaves identical in every row are hoisted into '# const' lines, string leaves that verify as a template of other leaves (same or enclosing object) become one '# tmpl' line, and node_id is dropped; expanding the header restores every leaf of every row except node_id, and a field that breaks the pattern in even one row (a PR among issues, one locked row) stays in the rows.
check_loses: node_id values (opaque, neither constant nor derivable; dropped by name), the key order inside rows, and JSON whitespace; derived and constant fields are recoverable only by applying the printed header

title: Sample long JSON arrays and cap depth, keeping outliers
detail: For arrays of 100+ uniform objects keep first and last k rows, error or failed rows, z-score numeric outliers, plus schema and total count; collapse subtrees below depth d to key lists. Targets docker inspect, kubectl -o json, cargo metadata, list-type MCP results.
test: On 20 captured outputs, ask 5 questions each; compare accuracy against columnar-only encoding at equal tokens and count questions the sampled view cannot answer.
because: sample long JSON arrays, keep outliers
check: Arrays of >= 100 mostly-object elements are sampled to the first and last 3 rows plus every error row, every row beyond 3 sigma in a numeric column and every row with a different key set, with the schema, total count and column mean/var/min/max kept in a $sampled header and containers deeper than 6 inside kept rows stubbed; the required rows are identical wherever they sit in the array.
check_loses: all unremarkable middle rows (their values and positions are known only as 'not kept'), containers deeper than six levels inside kept rows (key list or length only), anything inside an omitted row that is neither an error string nor a numeric outlier, and JSON whitespace; the depth cap is applied only inside sampled arrays

title: Elide long numeric arrays: embeddings, coordinates, tensors
detail: Replace homogeneous number arrays over about 32 items with '[1536 floats, min..max, first 4: ...]'. Targets embedding API results, GeoJSON coordinates, histogram buckets, numpy and torch prints. Different from rounding floats.
test: Regex-scan transcripts for runs of 64 or more numbers; sum their token share; check follow-up commands never needed the elided values.
because: elide long numeric arrays
check: In a valid JSON document, a flat array of >= 32 numbers (or >= 8 equal-width numeric rows, width <= 8) is replaced in place by one string holding the count, min, max and first values (per-column for rows); every other byte, every short array and every non-numeric array is untouched.
check_loses: all numeric values of an elided array except its count, min, max and first 4 values (first 2 rows for coordinate lists), their order and the position of the extremes; numpy/torch text prints and invalid or truncated JSON are not handled

title: Run the token classifier on JSON string values only
detail: Parse JSON and apply the model only to long string leaves (issue bodies, descriptions, log text) at a per-leaf rate, leaving keys, numbers and brackets untouched so output stays valid JSON. Today the model sees raw JSON text.
test: On 20 captured MCP JSON outputs over 6k chars, compare json.loads validity and QA accuracy of whole-text versus leaf-only compression at equal token count.
because: model applied to JSON string values only

title: OpenAPI spec digest into an endpoint table
detail: Collapse openapi.json or swagger.yaml fetched via curl or doc MCPs to 'METHOD /path (params) -> status:schema' lines. Resolve $ref once in a components table; drop examples, x- extensions, repeated 4xx boilerplate, descriptions duplicating summary.
test: Digest Petstore and a large public spec; compare chars and tokens; ask 10 endpoint and parameter questions against digest versus original.
because: digest OpenAPI spec to endpoint table
check: An OpenAPI 3.x JSON spec becomes one line per operation (method, path, operationId, name:in:type* parameters, @body, status:schema responses, summary) plus one line per component schema (properties with * for required, enums, arrays, maps) and the shared error schema named once; every endpoint, parameter, required flag, response status and success schema, and every schema property and enum value is unchanged.
check_loses: examples, descriptions (summaries are kept), x- extensions, tags, security requirements and scheme definitions, servers and info beyond title/version, constraints (maximum, pattern, minLength), non-JSON media types beyond the first, a response schema that equals the shared error schema (it is implied by the header), and the structure of inline object schemas (shown as 'object'); specs with unusual names are left unchanged

title: Unwrap GraphQL edges/node; drop __typename and cursors
detail: In gh api graphql and GraphQL MCP results, turn edges[].node into a plain array and drop __typename, per-edge cursor, and pageInfo when hasNextPage is false. The flat array then feeds columnar encoding. Keep the cursor when more pages exist.
test: Run a first:50 issues query via gh api graphql; compare tokens before and after; confirm pagination still works from the retained endCursor.
because: unwrap GraphQL edges and nodes

title: Stub kubectl last-applied-configuration annotation
detail: kubectl get -o yaml/json embeds the whole object again as a JSON string in the kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation. Replace it with a stub; the original stays in the saved file. Separate from managedFields and status noise.
test: Run kubectl get deploy -o yaml on a client-side-applied object; measure the annotation's share of tokens; check agents still answer spec questions.
because: stubs last-applied annotation in YAML output
check: Replaces the kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation value (a block literal in YAML, a string in JSON) with a one-line stub that records its size; the key stays, and every spec, data, metadata and status value is unchanged.
check_loses: the last-applied JSON itself (it is the previously applied manifest: needed to answer 'what did the last apply say' or 'has the live object drifted'; the saved original has it)

title: Elide output lines echoing the model's own Edit text
detail: Index lines from Edit new_string and Write content, which are guaranteed in context. Later pytest tracebacks, compiler snippets and git diff plus-lines matching verbatim become a pointer like 'your Edit #3, line 4'.
test: Replay session JSONLs: count chars of tool_result lines of 30+ chars that exactly match earlier Edit/Write input lines; report share per tool.
because: elide lines echoing earlier tool_use input text
check: In Bash output, a run of lines that exactly equals consecutive lines of the model's own successful Edit new_string or Write content (behind one constant prefix such as diff '+' or pytest indentation) becomes a pointer to that tool call; Read output, short or near-miss lines, failed Edits, hostile text and compacted context are left literal.

title: Hunk-hash dedup across the git change lifecycle
detail: The same diff hunk reappears in git diff, git diff --cached, git show, gh pr diff and MCP PR diffs. Hash hunks per session; repeats become 'hunk unchanged: file @@ header'. Needs the verbatim skip relaxed for repeats.
test: In transcripts, hash every diff hunk across Bash and MCP outputs; report bytes whose hunk hash was already seen earlier in the same session.
because: hunk-hash dedup across tool results
check: A diff hunk already shown literally (same file, same @@ header, same body) is replaced under its @@ line by a pointer to that turn, across git diff, --cached, show and gh pr diff; the same text in another file, a grown hunk, a new hunk, tiny hunks, truncated or hostile output and compaction stay literal.

title: Content-hash stubs across Bash cat, Read and MCP file tools
detail: Key repeat detection on the text hash, not path or command, so cat, sed -n, Read and MCP get_file_contents of the same bytes collapse to one earlier occurrence. Covers verbatim-skipped commands too, since the model already has the text.
test: Hash every file-content tool_result across Read, Bash cat/sed -n/head and MCP file tools in transcripts; count byte-identical repeats that cross tool type.
because: content-hash stubs across tools
check: A file-content result (Read numbered lines, Bash cat/sed -n/head, MCP get_file_contents) whose list of lines equals the lines of an earlier literal result, from any tool or path, becomes a pointer to it, before the lossy stage so verbatim-skipped commands are covered; any differing line, CRLF, short content, errors and compaction stay literal.

title: Line-shift-proof diagnostic delta for edit-compile loops
detail: Key linter, type-checker and compiler diagnostics by (file, rule, message) ignoring line and column, so edits that shift lines do not defeat delta. Show new and resolved items plus 'N unchanged'; originals stay on disk.
test: Run mypy, tsc or ruff across 10 successive small edits; compare plain line-diff size against normalised-key delta size in tokens.
because: diagnostic delta keyed on earlier results
check: Diagnostics keyed by (file, severity, rule, message) ignoring line and column give an empty delta for pure line shifts, tell fixes, new findings and moves apart, count duplicates, flatten 'on line N' inside messages, and cost under half of a plain line-diff over ten successive edits (real ruff when installed); the previous set plus the delta reproduces the current set, first runs, crashes, clean runs and other command families come back verbatim, and the full output stays on disk.

title: Run-invariant baseline: collapse lines present in every prior run
detail: For a normalised command family, keep the intersection of lines across the last K runs (banners, versions, fixed warnings). Lines identical in all prior runs collapse to a count, originals saved. Learns per-repo noise without hand-written packs.
test: Run npm test or pytest five times with small edits; count lines in all prior runs and check no failing-test line is hidden without a count.
because: collapse lines shared by prior runs, local state
check: Lines identical in each of the last three runs of a command family (cwd, program, output-shaping flags) are hidden behind one counted header with the full output saved; failure, assertion and error lines are never hidden even when they repeat in every run, a line missing from any prior run or changed by a tool upgrade stays visible, and corrupt history fails open.

title: PreToolUse byte-offset cursor for repeated reads of growing logs
detail: When the model re-runs cat, tail -n N or less on a build.log it already saw, verify the earlier prefix hash and rewrite the command via updatedInput to start at the stored offset, with a header naming the skipped bytes.
test: Verify that Claude Code honours updatedInput for Bash; simulate an agent polling a growing log 10 times; count bytes saved versus tail -n 200 each time.
because: prefix-hash dedup of repeated log reads
check: A repeated 'cat F' or 'tail -n N F' of a log the model already saw is rewritten to print only the bytes after the last fully shown line (with a header naming the offset) when the sha256 of the shown prefix still matches; after truncation, an edited prefix, a corrupt ledger or a compaction reset the original command runs, and the reader's reconstruction equals the plain output at every poll.

title: Own-edit-aware re-read: show only hunks the model changed
detail: Keep a shadow of the last Read per file and replay the model's Edit old/new pairs onto it. A later Read with no foreign changes is rewritten to the edited ranges plus three lines of context, with 'rest unchanged since turn N'.
test: Replay transcripts: find Reads of files whose only changes since the previous Read are the model's own Edits; sum lines avoidable by hunk-only reads.
because: shadow file from earlier Read and Edit payloads
check: A full re-read of a file that differs from the last read only by the model's own successful Edits (replayed onto a shadow) is shown as the edited lines plus 3 context lines and pointers (new and old line numbers) to unchanged ranges; a foreign change, a failed Edit, a ranged Read, compaction or a broken shadow give the full text.

title: MCP JSON entity cache across calls and pages
detail: Hash nested objects (user, repo, label, milestone) per MCP server within a session. Repeats in later pages or list-then-get calls become a short ref to the earlier occurrence. Within-output dedup misses this.
test: Replay GitHub MCP list_issues, list_pull_requests and issue_read outputs from a session; count bytes of nested objects identical to ones in earlier responses.
because: refs to earlier MCP objects, session state
check: Within one session and server, a nested JSON object seen in an earlier output is replaced by {"$see":"<call id>:<pointer>"} while it and everything it points to are inside the reader's window; a reader that follows the refs recovers every output exactly, and changed objects, other servers, tiny objects, non-JSON, corrupt or unwritable state all leave the output in full.

title: Rebuild in-context set from transcript_path after compaction
detail: Hook events reportedly carry session_id and transcript_path. Parse the JSONL each call and cut at the last compaction boundary so stubs only point at text literally still in context. No daemon state; survives /clear, resume and restarts.
test: Verify that hook input carries transcript_path; parse real session JSONLs containing a compaction, compare reconstructed in-context tool_use ids to a hook-maintained ledger, and time parsing a 10 MB file.
because: parses hook transcript_path JSONL, private log format

title: Resume-time transcript surgery dropping superseded tool results
detail: Before claude --resume, a ctxprune command rewrites the session JSONL so tool results superseded by later reads, edits or reruns become stubs pointing at saved files. Hindsight pruning is impossible live; prompt cache is often cold by then.
test: Count tokens of superseded tool results in session JSONLs; verify that a rewritten copy resumes, then ask what the model remembers of a stubbed result.
because: rewrites session JSONL before resume, harness-specific

title: Path-set delta across find, ls, git ls-files and rg --files
detail: Parse listings from different commands into path sets. A second listing that overlaps an earlier one by most entries prints only added and removed paths plus the covered count. Keys on entities, not command text.
test: Extract path sets from consecutive listings in transcripts; compute Jaccard overlap with the best earlier listing; total paths savable at 80% overlap.
because: path-set delta across listing tool results

title: Stub recency horizon: re-show originals past a token distance
detail: Stubs may fail when the original sits far back in a long context. Track tokens since the original; beyond a threshold, emit the full text again or a short excerpt. Distinct from invalidation at compaction boundaries.
test: Build long contexts with a stubbed result at 5k, 20k, 60k and 120k tokens back; measure how often the model answers a question needing it correctly.
because: re-show original past token distance; pluggable counter

title: Hide human-only skills via disable-model-invocation
detail: Skill listing is re-sent every turn as description plus when_to_use text. Frontmatter disable-model-invocation (present in the Claude Code 2.1.316 bundle) should drop entries the user only types by hand, keeping the slash command.
test: Verify that flagged skills leave the listing: compare /context skill-listing tokens before and after flagging five skills; confirm /name still runs by hand.
because: skill frontmatter setting

title: Scope plugins per project with enabledPlugins
detail: Every user-level plugin adds its skills, agents and hooks to every repo. Set enabledPlugins false in project .claude/settings.json for plugins a repo never uses, or keep a coding-only set. Differs from MCP allowlisting: targets skills and agents.
test: Start fresh sessions with all plugins versus a project-scoped set; diff /context totals; tally per-plugin tokens to rank which to disable.
because: enabledPlugins settings

title: Skill and agent description diet with CI lint
detail: Listing text is description plus when_to_use, so TRIGGER/SKIP prose and <example> blocks in plugin agent descriptions are paid every turn. Rewrite to one trigger sentence; lint token length in plugin CI, including ctxprune's own manifest.
test: Tokenize all descriptions locally; rewrite the 10 longest; replay 20 should-trigger and 20 should-not prompts per skill and compare invocation accuracy before and after.
because: skill and agent descriptions, plugin manifest

title: Demote rare CLAUDE.md sections to on-demand skills or scoped rules
detail: Always-on text needed only for setup, release or migration becomes a skill (description cost only) or a path-scoped rule (Cursor, Continue, Claude Code paths frontmatter, reportedly). Dogfood: this repo's 2.5 kB AGENTS.md is install steps loaded every turn.
test: Verify that path-scoped rules load only on matching files; split AGENTS.md into skills and rules, replay 10 recorded tasks, compare per-turn prompt tokens and outcomes.
because: CLAUDE.md sections moved to skills or rules

title: CLAUDE.md per-section usage telemetry from transcripts
detail: For each section or bullet, scan session transcripts for the commands, paths and keywords it mentions. Sections never touched across many sessions are demotion or deletion candidates. Usage-based, unlike a lossless rewrite.
test: Script over ~/.claude/projects jsonl: map bullets to tool calls by keyword; report zero-hit tokens per CLAUDE.md and hit rate by section.
because: CLAUDE.md sections and transcripts are harness-specific

title: Lean launch profile for headless and workflow runs
detail: Every claude -p or workflow subagent run re-pays tools, skills, MCP and settings. Flags in 2.1.316 --help: --tools allowlist, --strict-mcp-config, --disable-slash-commands, --setting-sources, --bare. Interactive repos can deny unused built-in tools similarly.
test: Run claude -p 'hi' --output-format json under each flag combination; compare reported input plus cache-creation tokens, then run a golden task for success.
because: harness CLI launch flags

title: Switch off account-level connectors in coding repos
detail: claude.ai connectors (taxi, tyre-shop, docs servers in this session) inject server instructions and tool names into coding sessions, and .mcp.json allowlists do not reach them. ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS appears in the bundle; test it per project.
test: Verify that ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=0 removes connectors; capture /context with and without it and count tokens in the MCP instructions block and tool-name list.
because: harness env var for connectors

title: Cache-miss forensics: idle expiry versus prefix mutation
detail: Classify turns with large cache_creation_input_tokens as an idle gap past the cache TTL or a prefix change (tool list, CLAUDE.md edit, skill listing, dates, MCP tool order). A cache write costs 1.25x versus 0.1x for a read.
test: Parse usage and timestamps in transcript JSONL; flag gaps over 5 minutes; diff request prefixes via a logging proxy; verify that ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H changes cache_creation totals.
because: cache-miss analysis from usage fields

title: Inline shell injections in commands bypass the hook
detail: Slash-command and skill files can inline shell output with a bang-backtick command; it enters the prompt, reportedly with no PostToolUse event, so ctxprune never sees it. Wrap those with head caps or a ctxprune pipe.
test: Grep command and skill dirs for bang-backtick blocks; run each, record output chars; verify that no hook fires; apply cap or pipe and compare size and function.
because: slash-command and skill shell injection, harness feature

title: Edit anchors: measure shared old and new context
detail: Edit tool_use inputs stay in context and cost output tokens. Measure shared prefix/suffix lines between old_string and new_string, and over-long anchors, in transcripts; if material, add a smallest-unique-span steering line.
test: Parse Edit calls in transcript JSONL; compute the fraction of old_string tokens identical to new_string edges; report distribution by file type.
because: measures Edit tool-call input overlap

title: Effort and thinking budget sweep by task type
detail: Thinking tokens are billed output. --effort levels and MAX_THINKING_TOKENS (both present in 2.1.316) trade tokens for quality; sweep per task class on a golden set to find where lower effort loses nothing.
test: Run 10 golden tasks at each effort level; log output tokens and pass rate; pick the cheapest level per class with no pass-rate drop.
because: thinking budget and effort levels are model-specific

title: Sweep skill-listing char budget downward
detail: Listing is built from description plus when_to_use and capped by SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET, else a share of the context window. Lower the cap to the smallest size where skills actually used in transcripts still appear.
test: Verify that SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET changes the listing; set several values in fresh sessions, list dropped skills in /context, cross-check against skills invoked in past transcripts.
because: skill listing budget env var

title: Rank atoms by logit margin, not saturated probability
detail: The ONNX path computes a float32 softmax; in numpy a keep-vs-drop logit margin of 17 or more gives exactly 1.0, so confident atoms tie and the stable sort favors earlier positions. Rank on margin or mean logit; also try min versus mean over subtokens.
test: Log fraction of atoms with p==1.0 and tie size at the cut for rates 0.33 and 0.5; then QA at equal tokens, margin versus probability ranking.
because: ranks by logit margin, local scoring

title: Contiguity-aware selection: Viterbi smoothing or CRF head
detail: Top-k over independent atom scores leaves isolated kept words between dropped runs. Add a switch penalty or minimum kept-run length (Viterbi over scores at inference), later a CRF layer trained on teacher labels, so output keeps phrases, not fragments.
test: Count isolated kept atoms (both neighbours dropped) in current output; compare QA at equal tokens with smoothed selection on logs and prose.
because: contiguity-aware selection over scores

title: Novelty-decayed scores for repeated lines (MMR-style)
detail: Windows are scored independently, so a line repeated 40 times, or seen in earlier calls, keeps full score each time. Multiply an atom's score by gamma per prior occurrence of its line template in the document or session history before top-k.
test: On replayed logs with repeats beyond 512 tokens, count duplicate-template lines surviving at 0.5; sweep gamma 0.5 to 0.9, check QA at equal tokens.
because: decays scores for repeated line templates

title: Inference window sweep: 512 versus 1k-4k tokens
detail: Compressor scores independent 512-token windows, so context never crosses a window. mmBERT-small reportedly supports 8k context via ModernBERT; try max_len 1024 to 4096 on the existing model, checking whether scores hold past the 500-token training length.
test: Verify that the model accepts 4096-token inputs; score 20 long outputs at 512/1024/2048/4096; report rank correlation with 512, val ROC-AUC, latency, and QA at equal tokens.
because: window-size sweep experiment

title: Command-conditioned scoring via encoder pair input
detail: Feed the tool command (and last user prompt) as segment A with the output chunk as segment B, labels only on B. Teacher labels see the same command, so atoms relevant to what was asked survive. Learned alternative to a post-hoc BM25 boost.
test: On SWE-smith traces where the command is known, relabel ~500 chunks with a command-aware teacher, fine-tune with pair input, compare QA on command-specific questions versus the unconditioned model.
because: command-conditioned scorer input, payload data

title: Multi-budget ordinal targets instead of two-prompt keep/drop rows
detail: Today two teacher prompts give two hard-label rows per chunk. Label each chunk at 4-5 word budgets (e.g. 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8) and train on keep-level as ordinal or soft BCE targets, so score rank means 'survives down to budget b'.
test: Relabel 300 chunks via teacher prompt v3 at four budgets; train an ordinal head versus the current two-prompt recipe; compare QA at 0.33 and 0.5 kept.
because: training target change, model-internal

title: Pairwise ranking loss with asymmetric false-drop cost
detail: Training uses default cross-entropy while inference is top-k ranking, and a wrongly dropped fact costs more than a wrongly kept filler word. Add a within-chunk pairwise or listwise AUC surrogate and weight keep-class errors higher.
test: Fine-tune one epoch from the current checkpoint with the added loss on existing labels; compare within-chunk AUC and QA at 0.33 kept against the CE-only baseline.
because: training loss change, model-internal

title: Behaviour-derived labels: atoms the agent later quotes or retrieves
detail: Cheap weak supervision: in Claude Code transcripts, atoms of a tool output that reappear verbatim in later tool inputs or assistant text are positives; greps of saved originals after compression mark regrets. Fine-tune or reweight teacher labels with these.
test: Mine local ~/.claude transcripts: fraction of output atoms later quoted by class (protected, prose, punctuation); compare to model keep rate to find under-kept classes before any training.
because: weak labels from message sequences, offline training

title: Model soup: average weights of v1, v2 and seed runs
detail: Weight-average fine-tunes sharing an init (seeds, last epochs, runs on different label sets); no inference cost. Model soups (Wortsman et al., 2022) reportedly help on small fine-tuning sets, and the label set here is small.
test: Train 3 seeds, average weights, compare val ROC-AUC and QA at 0.5 versus the best single seed; then try a greedy soup including the v1-to-v2 chain.
because: weight averaging, model-internal

title: Reader-free reconstruction proxy for selection algorithms
detail: Reader-LLM QA is slow and noisy for comparing selection tweaks. Proxy: how well a small LM reconstructs the dropped atoms from the kept ones (loss or masked fill-in accuracy). Validate by rank correlation with existing QA results before trusting it.
test: Compute proxy for ctxprune, LLMLingua-2 and random deletion at 0.33/0.5; check it orders methods like the stored QA table, then sweep selection variants cheaply.
because: reader-free evaluation proxy

title: Concatenate handcrafted atom features into the classifier head
detail: The encoder sees only subwords. Add per-token features before the head: occurrences of the same atom or line template in the chunk, indentation, bracket depth, line index, is_protected flag. Cheap access to repetition and structure.
test: Add a small feature vector to hidden states before the head; retrain on same data; compare per-source val ROC-AUC and QA at 0.5 versus a shuffled-features ablation.
because: classifier architecture change, model-internal

title: Sweep dangling punctuation left after atom deletion
detail: After top-k, kept punctuation atoms whose neighbours were both dropped (lone commas, orphan colons) cost tokens and carry nothing. A post-pass removes them, and brackets or quotes enclosing no kept atom, only where the interior had dropped atoms.
test: Run current model over 100 saved hook outputs; count kept punctuation atoms with both neighbours dropped and their token cost; confirm QA unchanged at equal tokens after the sweep.
because: post-pass removing orphan punctuation

title: Cluster-aware paired bootstrap, MDE and A/A noise floor
detail: Questions share chunks and sources, so per-question CIs can be too tight. Resample by chunk or repo, pair methods per question, and publish a minimum detectable effect before each A/B. Add A/A repeats (keep=1.0, 3 reader seeds) as the noise floor.
test: Re-aggregate cached eval_qa answers with 10k chunk-level resamples; compare interval width to naive binomial; rerun reader 3 times at keep=1.0 to get spread.
because: statistical eval methodology

title: Closed-book reader control for QA contamination
detail: Run the reader with empty context and with an unrelated chunk. SWE-smith, Toucan, SQuAD and HotpotQA are public and may sit in reader pretraining, and the teacher wrote the questions. Report accuracy minus closed-book hits; drop questions answerable without context.
test: Call eval_qa answer with context='' on all 378 questions; list closed-book correct ones by source; recompute headline accuracy on the remainder.
because: closed-book eval control

title: Split QA errors into abstain versus confident-wrong
detail: Scoring merges 'unknown' with wrong answers. An abstention costs one recovery read of the saved original; a confident wrong answer silently corrupts the next action. Report correct, abstain and confident-wrong per method, source and keep rate, and gate on the last.
test: Re-score cached reader outputs, bucketing exact 'unknown' replies separately; compare confident-wrong rate at keep 0.5 versus 1.0 and versus LLMLingua-2-large.
because: eval error-class breakdown

title: Next-action agreement replay on recorded trajectories
detail: For each oversized tool result in saved Claude Code transcripts, sample the agent's next turn given the original result and given the processed one; compare tool name and key args. Far cheaper than full task A/B, yet uses the real agent as reader.
test: Take 100 oversized results from the shadow log, 3 samples per arm; report next tool-call match rate versus original-vs-original resampling as the ceiling.
because: replays saved Claude Code transcripts

title: Per-call randomized holdout inside normal sessions
detail: Hook hashes tool_use_id to leave ~15% of eligible outputs uncompressed and logs the arm. Compare re-runs, greps of the saved original, and turns after each result between arms, clustered by session. Causal evidence from daily use with no extra task runs.
test: Verify that hook input carries tool_use_id; add CTXPRUNE_HOLDOUT=0.15 with arm logging; after a few hundred outputs compare follow-up-action rates by arm with a session-clustered bootstrap.
because: randomized holdout measurement, hash of call id

title: Shadow mode: compute and log, return original
detail: New rules and thresholds run in the hook but pass the original through, logging before/after sizes, rule fired, and the would-be output. Builds a real-world corpus and a savings forecast with zero behavior risk; promote a rule after clean offline QA.
test: Set CTXPRUNE_SHADOW=1 for a week with secret redaction on the log; report per-rule fire rate and forecast tokens saved; then replay logged originals through reader QA.
because: shadow-mode logging for safe rule rollout

title: Length- and depth-matched canary eval for hook-sized inputs
detail: Held-out chunks are at most 500 tokens, but the hook compresses outputs over 6,000 chars, often far longer. Stitch real outputs to 2k, 8k and 30k tokens, plant verbatim canary facts at 10/50/90% depth, and measure reader recall after compression.
test: Build 3 lengths x 3 depths x 50 canaries from the golden corpus; compare canary recall at keep 0.5 by depth and length.
because: length- and depth-matched canary eval

title: Add count, existence, absence questions; stratify answers by class
detail: QGEN demands verbatim-span answers, favoring protected tokens that are kept free. Add programmatic-gold questions: how many FAILED lines, is any warning present, which file is NOT listed. Report accuracy by question type and by protected versus prose answer.
test: Script 100 count/existence questions with regex-derived gold over logs and test outputs; score reader on original versus 0.5 kept versus collapsed-duplicates output.
because: eval question types stratification

title: Audit deleted negators and spliced adjacencies
detail: Kept atoms are rejoined, so deleting 'not', 'no', 'never', 'without', 'failed' or a line break can flip or fuse meaning. Count lines where a negator was dropped but the rest survived, and kept bigrams absent from the original.
test: Run held-out chunks at keep 0.5; list dropped-negator lines and cross-line splices; hand-judge 50 for flipped meaning; if material, add a negator shield.
because: audit of classifier deletions

title: Reader-parity QA for every lossless format transform
detail: Round-trip tests prove a parser recovers the data, not that an LLM reads it equally well. Columnar JSON, tree listings, grouped grep, path aliases and padding strip may shift accuracy. Run identical questions on original and transformed output; require non-inferiority before enabling.
test: Per transform, 30 real outputs x 5 questions with scripted gold; paired comparison with a 2-point non-inferiority margin, using the Claude tier users actually run.
because: reader-parity QA benchmark

title: Cross-tool false-fire matrix and version-drift corpus for noise packs
detail: Run every tool-specific rule on every other tool's output, prose and source code; any rewrite is a false positive. Also capture the same tool at older and newer versions (pytest, npm, cargo) to catch rules that silently stop matching or over-match.
test: CI job: N packs x M corpora, assert off-target output is byte-identical; weekly matrix over two tool versions reporting per-rule fire-rate change.
because: false-fire matrix and drift corpus

title: Claude-tier reader matrix: Haiku, Sonnet, Opus
detail: Existing readers are the Qwen teacher and DeepSeek. Claude Code users run Claude models. Re-run the same compressed contexts with each Claude tier to see whether method gaps and the best keep rate depend on reader strength; a weak reader may need gentler rates.
test: Reuse cached compressed contexts; answer 378 questions with three Claude tiers; fit method x reader interaction; if real, pick the rate per model.
because: dev-time reader matrix across model tiers

title: Cache-aware proxy that stubs or compresses old tool results
detail: A local reverse proxy (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, OPENAI_BASE_URL) or an owned loop's condenser (OpenHands, Agent SDK) swaps tool_results older than N turns for stubs plus saved ids. Memoize each rewrite and batch evictions so earlier bytes never change and one cache rewrite pays off.
test: Verify that the base-URL override works; replay a recorded 40-turn transcript at N=5/10/20; assert byte-identical prefixes, compare billed cache tokens and how often stubbed results get re-fetched.
because: payload-rewriting proxy stubs aged tool results, batched

title: Passthrough logging proxy: payload anatomy per agent
detail: Same base-URL proxy, log-only: split each request into system prompt, tool schemas, history, tool results and IDE auto-attached context (open files, diagnostics). Transcripts omit most of that; shows what each agent really sends.
test: Point Aider, Codex or Cline at a 30-line logging proxy for one task; tokenise each request part and print a table of shares.
because: log-only proxy measuring payload anatomy

title: MCP stdio proxy that compresses any server's results
detail: ctxprune mcp-wrap -- <server cmd> sits between agent and MCP server and rewrites tools/call text blocks with the hook logic. Gives savings to agents with no output-rewrite hook (reportedly Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Zed, Cline, Continue).
test: Wrap a filesystem or github MCP server, drive it with a minimal JSON-RPC client, assert tools/list is unchanged and big results shrink with a saved original.
because: MCP stdio proxy rewriting tool results

title: Command wrappers for hookless agents: PATH shims, Aider test-cmd
detail: Shims for pytest, npm, pip, docker, cargo, git on PATH run the real binary, apply noise packs, save the original and keep the exit code. For Aider, point --test-cmd and --lint-cmd at a ctxprune runner so savings compound each resent turn.
test: Generate 5 shims, run commands direct versus shimmed, compare bytes and exit codes; on a one-failing-test repo compare Aider /tokens after five more turns, wrapped versus not.
because: shell-level PATH shims, harness-agnostic
check: PATH shims for pytest, npm, pip, docker, cargo and git run the real binary, drop only the pack's noise lines, keep stderr and the exit status (checked on 12 real bash runs), save the full original, and leave git diff/log/show, unlisted sub-commands, terminals and opt-outs byte-identical; a broken filter returns the original; an Aider runner does the same for a command string.

title: Host truncation ordering probe: does the hook see everything?
detail: Claude Code reportedly caps Bash (~30k chars) and MCP (~25k tokens) output; Codex reportedly keeps ~10 KiB head/tail. If the hook runs after the cap, saved originals are already cut; if before, caps could be raised and ctxprune does the cutting.
test: Emit 200k chars of unique numbered lines through the hook with CTXPRUNE_DEBUG logging input length; check the last line exists in the saved file.
because: probes host output caps relative to hook ordering

title: Shell MCP tool with an agent-supplied 'want' argument
detail: ctxprune_run(cmd, want, max_tokens) as a drop-in shell for any MCP agent. The agent states what it needs ('failing test names'); compression becomes query-aware, an intent channel hooks never receive. Tag as model plus rules.
test: On 20 recorded failing-build outputs, compare tokens and needle recall of the want answer versus plain 0.5 compression; also measure how often an agent picks the tool.
because: new MCP shell tool with query-aware local compression

title: Route lint and typecheck to IDE diagnostics, not shell
detail: Zed, Cursor, Continue and VS Code agents can read LSP diagnostics per file (Claude Code reportedly has an IDE getDiagnostics tool). Steer tsc --noEmit and eslint . toward diagnostics for edited files only, structured and scoped.
test: Verify that getDiagnostics exists; break three files in a small TS project and compare characters of tsc --noEmit output with typescript-language-server diagnostics for those files.
because: depends on IDE diagnostics tools of particular agents

title: Launch-time quiet environment per agent config
detail: Set NO_COLOR, CI=1, TERM=dumb, GIT_PAGER=cat, PIP_PROGRESS_BAR=off in each agent's static config (Claude Code settings env, Codex shell_environment_policy reportedly, Zed terminal env, OpenHands sandbox env) where no pre-call hook can rewrite commands.
test: Run 10 common commands with and without the env pack, compare bytes, and flag commands whose behaviour changes (CI=1 can switch off watch mode).
because: per-agent static config files

title: Pipeline stages like '| head' wrongly trigger verbatim skip
detail: VERBATIM_CMD matches cat/head/nl/sed -n after any pipe, so 'pytest | head -200', 'kubectl get | head' and 'docker logs | head' are never compressed (checked with the regex). Restrict the skip to a stage with no upstream pipe.
test: Replay captured Bash events; count outputs over 6000 chars skipped only by a piped head/cat/nl/sed match, then compress them and compare tokens.
because: fix verbatim-skip regex on command string

title: Exempt recovery greps of saved originals from compression
detail: Claude is told to grep ~/.cache/ctxprune/outputs/*.txt, but that command is not in the skip regex. A result over 6000 chars is pruned again, deleting what it just asked for and creating a second saved file plus note.
test: In a hooked session, grep a saved original with many hits; confirm a second note appears. Add a path exemption and recheck.
because: skip rule keyed on command string in payload

title: Apply threshold to summed slots, not each slot
detail: run() requires each stdout/stderr string and each MCP text block to reach 6000 chars alone. A 5,900+5,900 stdout/stderr pair, or many 3k-char MCP blocks, pass untouched. Gate on the total and compress the blocks jointly.
test: From captured events count outputs whose total is at least 6000 chars but no single slot is; compress them and measure token saving.
because: threshold on summed output slots

title: Failing commands may bypass the PostToolUse hook entirely
detail: Installed Claude Code 2.1.316 has PostToolUseFailure, whose hook output allows only additionalContext, not updatedToolOutput. If non-zero exits route there, large failing builds and test runs are never pruned. A PreToolUse wrapper could append '[exit N]' instead.
test: Verify that failing commands fire PostToolUseFailure: log hook events via claude -p for 'false' and a failing pytest; then A/B the wrapper for task success.
because: PostToolUseFailure hook event semantics

title: Lower Claude Code's native output caps as a baseline
detail: Claude Code documents bashOutputMaxChars/BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH (default 30000, clamp 4000-128000; excess saved to a file with preview) and MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS (reportedly default 25000), settable in settings.json env. Lower caps cost no latency and change what the hook sees.
test: Set 8000 chars and 8000 tokens on 10 replayed tasks; compare tokens, recovery reads and task success for caps alone, hook alone and both.
because: Claude Code settings.json output caps

title: Budget charges 1 char per whitespace gap; audit achieved ratio
detail: Counts use len(text)+1 per atom, but detok keeps verbatim indentation on kept atoms. A random-score simulation at rate 0.5 gave output/input char ratios from about 0.38 (indent-4 JSON) to 0.57 (compact JSON), so 'rate' varies by format.
test: Run the real model at rate 0.5 on pretty JSON, compact JSON, traces and logs; plot achieved char and token ratios; try whitespace-aware counts.
because: audit of achieved ratio versus budget

title: Demote protected atoms after they repeat k times
detail: is_protected force-keeps INFO, DEBUG, ERROR, GET, POST, PASSED, FAILED (all-caps, verified) and every digit atom on every line. Protect only the first few occurrences of a literal, freeing budget in logs; differs from class-by-class relaxation.
test: On 1000-line logs count budget consumed by repeated protected literals; apply the frequency cap and compare QA accuracy at equal output chars.
because: protect only first occurrences of literals

title: Log MCP response shapes the hook silently ignores
detail: _text_slots handles only type=text blocks. Embedded resource blocks, structuredContent and string fields elsewhere pass through, and no-slot declines are never logged. Capture real tool_response shapes per MCP server and size each block type.
test: Dump tool_response from a PostToolUse hook for each connected MCP server; tabulate block types and chars; flag large uncompressed ones.
because: log and size tool response shapes

title: Per-tool policy keyed on arguments, not just name
