detail: VERBATIM_MCP matches only tool names. Reportedly mcp__github__pull_request_read with method get_diff returns code diffs that get pruned, while get_job_logs is an ideal log target. Key policy on (tool, args): skip, gentler or harder rate.
test: List MCP calls in transcripts by tool and method with output size; hand-assign skip or rate per pair; compare QA on those pairs.
because: policy keyed on tool name plus arguments

title: PreToolUse injects minimal_output and small perPage into MCP calls
detail: The github MCP server's own instructions advise minimal_output=true and batches of 5-10. A PreToolUse updatedInput can add them to list_* and read calls, shrinking JSON at the source; the Bash-only quiet-defaults item does not cover this target.
test: Verify that updatedInput works for MCP tools; call list_issues, list_commits, list_pull_requests with and without minimal_output; compare response tokens and fields agents later needed.
because: adds minimal params to MCP tool-call inputs

title: Scale rate and threshold by context fill
detail: Hook input carries transcript_path and session_id, yet rate and min_chars are constants. Prune harder as the transcript nears auto-compact and gentler early, since pruned tokens delay compaction and are re-read every turn.
test: Verify that context fill is readable from transcript_path; replay long transcripts with rate falling from 0.6 to 0.35 by fill; compare compaction count, tokens and success versus constant 0.5.
because: rate scales with context fill from payload

title: Append note inside output instead of additionalContext
detail: The hook sends both updatedToolOutput and a separate additionalContext, which Claude Code reportedly wraps in a hook-context system message on every call. A one-line trailer inside the output avoids wrapper tokens and a second block.
test: Verify that additionalContext adds wrapper tokens: count tokens of one transcript with the note in additionalContext versus as a trailer; check Claude still finds the path.
because: trailer inside output instead of side-channel context
check: The note moves into the output as a one-line last-line trailer (Bash stdout/stderr field, last compressed MCP text block, or bare string): the response drops the additionalContext channel, the shape, the image blocks and the compressed text are unchanged, and the path in the trailer opens to the exact original. The wrapper tokens Claude Code adds around additionalContext are not measurable offline; the in-band trailer is forgeable by tool output, so readers must take the last line.

title: Signature-only skeleton for large source reads
detail: tree-sitter skeleton keeps imports and class/def signatures with first docstring line, elides bodies as '... lines 41-88'. Reportedly similar to rtk smart read, repomix --compress and headroom CodeCompressor. Opt-in first look only, never when editing.
test: Take 30 real cat/Read outputs over 300 lines; compare skeleton vs full tokens, then check an agent still finds the target function via the line ranges.
because: tree-sitter skeleton of source read results
check: A 300+ line Python read becomes imports, constants, class and def headers, first docstring lines and one '...  # lines A-B' marker per body (exact range, original line numbers kept); ast still parses it and sees every signature, class, decorator and range; ranged reads, short files and unparseable text are returned untouched.
check_loses: the statements of every function and method body of 3+ lines (kept as a '...  # lines A-B' marker with the exact range), docstring lines after the first, comments inside bodies, anything nested inside a function body

title: Budgeted symbol-graph repo map at SessionStart
detail: aider-style repo map: tree-sitter definitions and references, PageRank over the file graph, binary-searched to a token budget (aider's --map-tokens). Injected once at SessionStart to replace exploratory ls, grep and cat rounds. Adds tokens up front.
test: A/B 10 repo tasks with and without a 1k-token map; compare tokens spent on exploration calls in the first 10 turns and final success.
because: SessionStart hook injection using host filesystem

title: Slice retrieval command for saved originals
detail: ctxprune show <id> --grep PAT -C3 or --lines a:b returns only the needed slice, not the whole file. Prior art: headroom_retrieve in headroom's CCR and ctx_search in context-mode. Cheap recovery makes harsher compression safe.
test: Replay sessions where the saved original was cat'd or grepped; compute tokens a grep/line slice would have returned versus the full cat.
because: local slice retrieval of saved originals

title: BM25 chunk selection against command and prompt intent
detail: For outputs over 5 KB, split into chunks (headings, blank lines, stanzas), rank by BM25 against the command plus last user prompt, keep top chunks with context windows; rest saved. context-mode reportedly does this with SQLite FTS5, no model.
test: 30 large outputs with known answer spans; compare answer-chunk recall at equal tokens against the token model at 0.5 and against head/tail.
because: BM25 chunk selection, local, no model
check: For outputs over 5,000 characters carrying the question in-band, BM25 keeps the best chunks plus the first and last 3 lines and the first occurrence of each distinct error line, with one line of context, and marks every skipped run '[... N lines omitted ...]'; the facts the question asks (OOMKilled/exit code/restart count, failing tests and assertions, the bind() error) and the output's first and last lines survive.
check_loses: the content of chunks that neither match the question nor look like errors (events, passing-test lines, repeated restart cycles) and the order of repeated error lines after their first occurrence

title: Local small-LM abstractive digest for giant outputs
detail: For outputs over ~50 KB, a 0.5-1.5B local instruction model writes a short digest with line references; original saved. Abstractive variant of RECOMP (Xu et al. 2023); ctxprune today only deletes words. CPU latency is the risk.
test: 20 giant build/test logs; compare QA accuracy, CPU seconds and tokens against token deletion at equal output size.
because: local small-LM digest, CPU only

title: Guard Write over existing files; suggest Edit
detail: PreToolUse on Write: if the target exists and under ~20% of lines differ, deny with 'use Edit'. Full-file rewrites burn output tokens, which cost more than input; aider's diff-style edit formats exist for the same reason.
test: From the transcript ledger, count Write calls over existing files, the fraction of lines changed, and output tokens spent; then simulate the deny.
because: PreToolUse hook plus host filesystem check

title: Machine-readable rewrite plus compact renderer for test runners
detail: PreToolUse wraps go test -json, cargo --message-format=json or pytest JSON report, and a renderer prints failures only, preserving the exit code. rtk reportedly parses go test NDJSON this way. Sturdier than text regexes across versions.
test: Run one failing suite per tool; compare rendered failure recall and tokens against the text-regex pack and against raw output.
because: needs pre-execution command rewrite via PreToolUse hook

title: Serial read-only call fusion detector
detail: Find runs of 3+ consecutive read-only calls (ls, cat, rg) that one command could replace. Each removed turn skips another cache read of the whole prefix, which may outweigh output trimming. context-mode's batch_execute targets this.
test: Scan the transcript ledger for such runs; estimate saved turns times mean cached-prefix tokens, with no model calls needed.
because: detector measuring fusable read-only call runs

title: xcodebuild: drop per-step cd and compiler command lines
detail: Each xcodebuild step header (SwiftCompile, Ld, CodeSign, ProcessInfoPlistFile) is reportedly followed by an indented cd line and a full tool command with long flag lists (from memory, unmeasured). Keep headers, warnings and errors; the saved original keeps the commands.
test: Capture xcodebuild logs from CI or a Mac; classify lines as header, command or diagnostic; compare tokens; check an agent still fixes a compile error from what remains.
because: drops xcodebuild command lines from output
check: Under each xcodebuild step header, drops the indented 'cd', 'export', 'builtin-*' and absolute-path tool command lines; every step header, every file:line:col diagnostic with its echoed source (even one starting with '/'), the BUILD SUCCEEDED/FAILED line and the failed-command list are unchanged.
check_loses: the exact swift-frontend/clang/ld/codesign command lines, flag lists and working directories of every step (the saved original keeps them)

title: XCTest and swift test: fold started/passed pairs and suites
detail: XCTest reportedly prints 'Test Case ... started.' then 'passed (0.001 seconds).', plus timestamped 'Test Suite' started/passed lines at class, bundle and 'All tests' levels, each followed by an 'Executed N tests' line (from memory). Keep failures and the final tally.
test: Run swift test or xcodebuild test on a package with 50 tests; count started lines, suite banners and Executed lines; verify failing case names and file:line survive.
because: folds XCTest started/passed pairs

title: MSBuild: dedupe warnings repeated in summary and per framework
detail: dotnet build reportedly prints each warning and error inline and again in the end summary, every line ending in [/abs/path/proj.csproj], repeated per target framework (from memory). Key on file, position, code, message; fold repeats to one line plus count; hoist the project path.
test: Build a multi-targeting sample solution with 20 warnings (CI logs if dotnet is absent); measure the duplicate-diagnostic char share; confirm every code and file:line survives.
because: dedupes MSBuild repeated warnings in text
check: Repeats of the same MSBuild diagnostic (same file, position, severity, code and message) across the inline list, the end summary and target frameworks become one line 'file(l,c): warning CODE: msg [@1] xN tfm=a,b' with the project path hoisted to one '[ctxprune: @1 = /path/App.csproj]' line; per distinct diagnostic the project, the number of times printed and the frameworks, and every other line ('Build succeeded.', 'N Warning(s)', ...) are unchanged.
check_loses: the interleaved order of repeats (they collapse onto the first occurrence), which of the repeats came from the end summary rather than the inline list, and the project path text on each line (it is in the legend)

title: Build-tool quiet pack: MAVEN_ARGS, Gradle console, DOTNET_NOLOGO, CARGO_TERM
detail: Per-ecosystem settings that cut chatter at the source: Maven -ntp -B (reportedly settable via MAVEN_ARGS in Maven 3.9+), org.gradle.console=plain, DOTNET_NOLOGO plus telemetry opt-out, CARGO_TERM_PROGRESS_WHEN=never. Extends the generic NO_COLOR/CI list.
test: Verify that MAVEN_ARGS is honored; run build and test on sample Maven, Gradle, .NET, Cargo and Go projects with and without the pack; compare bytes, exit codes, failure text.
because: build-tool quiet env/flag injection into commands
check: Maven, .NET, Cargo and Gradle commands get MAVEN_ARGS='-ntp -B', DOTNET_NOLOGO and telemetry opt-out, CARGO_TERM_PROGRESS_WHEN=never or '--console=plain' only when the user has not set them; the build's own lines and exit status are unchanged and other commands are byte-identical.

title: go test -v: drop RUN/PAUSE/CONT lines with no interleaved output
detail: Measured: a 4-subtest parallel Go test printed 13 '=== RUN/PAUSE/CONT' lines out of 18. Drop them when the matching '--- PASS/FAIL' line exists and nothing sits between; keep any '=== NAME' that attributes streamed t.Log output.
test: Run go test -v on parallel subtests, with and without t.Log in failing cases; count dropped lines; check each log line stays attributable to its test.
because: drops go test RUN/PAUSE lines
check: Drops '=== RUN/PAUSE/CONT/NAME' lines that have no streamed output under them; every test result, every summary line and the test each log line is attributed to are unchanged.
check_loses: the order in which parallel subtests started, paused and resumed

title: Fold identical-stack threads in jstack, goroutine and gdb dumps
detail: Thread dumps list many threads whose stacks match apart from name, id and address (idle pools, parked goroutines, 'thread apply all bt'). Normalise the header, group by stack hash, print one stack with 'x37 threads: names'. Go frames also carry +0x offsets and hex args.
test: Capture jstack of a Spring app, a Go deadlock dump and gdb 'thread apply all bt'; compare grouped versus raw tokens; check blocked-thread stacks still stand out.
because: fold identical thread stacks
check: Threads (jstack, Go goroutine or gdb paragraphs) whose header state and hex-masked stack are identical become one 'xN threads "state": names' paragraph with one copy of the stack; every thread name keeps its state and stack, blocked and lock-waiting stacks keep their lock ids, and non-thread paragraphs (deadlock report) are untouched.
check_loses: jstack thread numbers, tid/nid, cpu and elapsed times, daemon and priority flags; gdb thread numbers and LWPs; the original dump order; hex addresses and arguments in all but the first member of a folded group

title: g++/clang overload errors: cap candidate notes, keep first three
detail: Measured: one missing operator<< for a struct printed 20.8k chars, 76% of it 'note: candidate' and 'no known conversion' blocks with echoed code. Keep the error plus the first few candidates and '+N more'; the rest stays in the saved file.
test: Collect 20 g++ and clang template or overload errors; measure candidate-note share; check an agent still fixes each error from the top three candidates plus the count.
because: caps compiler overload candidate notes
check: After each error, the first three 'note: candidate' records (with their sub-notes and echoed code) are kept and the rest of an unbroken candidate run is replaced by one '[ctxprune: +N more candidate notes omitted]' line; error lines, non-candidate notes, warnings and the total candidate count per run are unchanged.
check_loses: the signatures and 'no known conversion' reasons of every candidate beyond the third (the saved original keeps them), and the include-chain lines that preceded those candidates

title: ASan/UBSan/Valgrind: drop shadow-byte dumps, hoist ==PID== prefix
detail: Measured: a 4-byte heap overflow under ASan gave 2,958 chars, 1,405 of them the constant shadow-byte legend and memory dump after the stack frames. Valgrind prefixes every line with ==PID==. Keep error line, stacks, allocation sites; save the rest.
test: Run ASan, TSan and Valgrind on 20 small buggy programs; compare tokens; verify the faulting source line and allocation site remain in the trimmed report.
because: drops sanitizer shadow-byte dumps
check: Removes ASan's shadow-byte rows and legend, UBSan's raw-byte dump under 'pointer points here' and every '(BuildId: ...)' suffix, and hoists a single ==PID== valgrind prefix into one '[pid N]' line; every error headline, stack frame (function, file:line), allocation/free site, leak summary and SUMMARY line is unchanged.
check_loses: the shadow byte values around the faulting address (including the byte at the fault; the error type already names the class), the raw memory bytes UBSan prints, and binary build ids

title: CMake configure: fold probe/'- done' pairs, drop percent prefixes
detail: A trivial project's configure printed 4 of 12 lines as 'X' then 'X - done/Success/skipped' pairs; find_package-heavy projects print many more. Fold successful pairs to one line, keep failed and not-found probes. Make's '[ 37%]' prefix adds no information.
test: Configure and build two real C++ projects; count probe pairs and percent-prefix tokens against total; confirm failed probes and warnings pass through verbatim.
because: folds CMake probe pairs, text rules

title: gradle dependencies: print identical configuration trees once
detail: gradle dependencies prints dozens of configurations (compileClasspath, runtimeClasspath, test variants, annotationProcessor) whose trees mostly repeat, with (*) and (c) markers (from memory). Hash each block; print distinct trees once with the configuration names sharing them.
test: Run gradle dependencies on an Android or multi-module sample; hash configuration blocks; compute duplicate share; ask which version of X is on runtimeClasspath from the folded form.
because: dedupes identical gradle dependency trees
check: Configuration blocks of 'gradle dependencies' whose dependency trees are line-for-line identical within a project are printed once under 'name1, name2, ... - first description'; the exact tree of every (project, configuration), including version arrows, (*), (c) and FAILED markers, and every line outside the trees are unchanged.
check_loses: the description text of every configuration after the first in a folded group, and the position of the later configurations in the report

title: Maven reactor stanzas and Gradle/Maven failure footers
detail: Per module Maven prints a banner, 'Building', '--- plugin:version:goal @ module ---' and 'Nothing to compile'; failures end with constant '-e/-X' advice and [Help 1] URLs. Gradle ends with '* Try:' and deprecation-advisory paragraphs. Replace exact paragraphs with a tag; keep Reactor Summary.
test: Run mvn verify on a 10-module project and a failing gradle build; extract exact repeated paragraphs; count tokens per build; check agents still find the failing module and goal.
because: replaces constant Maven/Gradle footers with tags
check: Each Maven module stanza loses its banner, 'from pom', packaging rule, blank INFO lines and no-op results ('Nothing to compile', 'No tests to run', 'skip non existing resourceDirectory') and becomes '[INFO] [i/n] name version' plus one 'goals:' line (a goal with output keeps its full header and lines); the constant -e/-X/help paragraph of a Maven failure and the constant --stacktrace/--info/--scan/help and deprecation lines of a Gradle failure become one tag each. Module order, goals run, WARNING/ERROR/test lines, the Reactor Summary, the failing module and goal, and Gradle's task and error text are unchanged.
check_loses: the execution ids ('(default-compile)'), the '@ module' repeat and decorative rules of each goal header, the no-op result lines, and the constant advice text (which --stacktrace/-e/-X/--scan do; the saved original keeps it)

title: Collapse zero-test harness blocks: cargo doc-tests, go no-test-files
detail: Measured: a 3-crate cargo workspace printed a 'Doc-tests x / running 0 tests / test result: ok. 0 passed...' block per crate; Running lines end in a build hash. Fold to 'N targets, 0 tests'. Same for go '[no test files]' lines.
test: Generate a 40-crate cargo workspace offline with cargo new; run cargo test; count tokens in zero-test blocks versus total; run go test ./... on a multi-package module.
because: collapses zero-test harness blocks

title: Strip Unicode tag characters and bidi controls, with a flag
detail: Tag block U+E0000-E007F is invisible to humans but readable by LLMs (reportedly used for hidden prompt injection); a 49-char hidden payload tokenized to 189 tokens on an o200k proxy. Strip tags and bidi overrides, add a note, save original.
test: Craft output hiding an instruction in tag chars; run the hook; assert it is stripped, flagged and the original saved; count tokens before and after with tiktoken.
because: deterministic strip of invisible characters, local original

title: Decode git octal-escaped non-ASCII paths (core.quotepath)
detail: Verified here: git status quotes non-ASCII names as octal escapes by default (an accented e becomes 8 chars). Escapes cost several tokens per byte (34 vs 8 on the o200k proxy). Inject git -c core.quotepath=false via PreToolUse, or decode octal runs forming valid UTF-8.
test: Create a repo with CJK and accented filenames; run status, ls-files, diff --stat and log --stat with and without quotepath=false; compare tokens and confirm the paths round-trip.
because: git quotepath flag or octal decoding, text transform
check: 'git -c core.quotepath=false' is inserted after 'git' unless the command already sets core.quotepath; on a real repository the output has the characters instead of octal escapes (same names as decoding the escapes, control-character names stay quoted), costs fewer tokens, and the one loss, a file name that is not valid UTF-8, is shown to be avoided by the decode alternative.

title: Join byte-separated hex runs: hexdump, xxd, openssl
detail: Space or colon separated hex bytes tokenize far worse than joined runs. o200k proxy: 64 spaced bytes 151 tokens vs 72 joined; an openssl-style colon block 610 vs 348. Optionally also drop the hexdump -C ASCII gutter.
test: Run xxd, hexdump -C, od -x, openssl x509 -text and ssh-keygen -lf; join runs; tokenize before and after; assert splitting back into pairs reproduces the original bytes.
because: join hex byte runs
check: Runs of byte tokens separated by single spaces (hexdump -C, 2-digit), single colons (openssl, ssh-keygen -E md5) or 4-digit words (xxd, od -x) are joined into one marked run; decoding splits each run back at the recorded width and separator, so the original text is restored exactly.

title: Symbolic file modes to octal in ls -l
detail: Mode strings like -rw-r--r-- tokenize as many symbol pieces while 644 is one or two tokens. o200k proxy: a 30-line listing went 700 to 560 tokens. Use four digits for setuid and sticky, keep the ACL plus or at suffix. Also find -ls, tar -tv.
test: Tokenize ls -lA of /usr/bin and node_modules before and after; assert octal-to-symbolic round trip equals the original on every line; check the agent still answers executable-bit questions.
because: ls -l modes to octal, text rewrite
check: The type character plus nine permission letters of an ls -l or tar -tv line become the type plus 3 octal digits (4 when setuid, setgid or sticky is set), keeping an ACL/SELinux/xattr suffix; decode restores the exact original.

title: Decode percent-escapes, HTML entities and quoted-printable
detail: Escapes cost 2-3 tokens per byte. o200k proxy: UTF-8 percent run 36 vs 16 tokens, apostrophe and quote entities 34 vs 16, quoted-printable 48 vs 9. Decode only UTF-8 and unreserved chars; keep %2F %26 %3D %23 encoded. Targets access logs, curl'd HTML/RSS, raw .eml.
test: Scan transcripts for %XX, &#NN; and =XX runs; decode with the guards; tokenize before and after; assert re-encoding each decoded span reproduces the original.
because: decode percent and entity escapes

title: NFKC-fold ligatures, fullwidth forms and math alphanumerics
detail: PDF-extracted text carries fi/fl ligatures, CJK docs use fullwidth ASCII, some sites use mathematical bold letters. NFKC folds these; a stress string went 49 to 16 tokens on the cl100k proxy. Restrict to safe ranges, since NFKC also rewrites TM, circled digits and ellipsis.
test: Run pdftotext on 5 PDFs and scrape 5 fullwidth CJK pages; count characters changed by the safe-range fold; tokenize before and after; check no digits or symbols changed meaning.
because: pure text normalisation on tool output

title: Repair mojibake (UTF-8 misread as cp1252)
detail: Sequences like a-circumflex plus euro plus tm for an apostrophe appear in curl with wrong charset, Windows logs and CSV exports. ftfy (Python library) fixes them heuristically; a short sample went 18 to 8 tokens (o200k proxy). Gate on high-byte density; keep the original.
test: Run ftfy over a mixed corpus plus clean UTF-8 files containing legitimate accented characters; measure the false-fix rate and the token delta.
because: local mojibake repair on text

title: Stub binary-looking output by size, type and hash
detail: cat of a binary, curl without -o, or git show of an image yields NUL, C0 control and U+FFFD runs. 300 random bytes decoded with replacement cost 221 tokens vs 12 for a stub with size, magic-byte type and sha. Also drop private-use icon glyphs.
test: Set a control/FFFD density threshold; run cat on ELF, PNG, zip and SQLite files; verify the stub fires; confirm text files with tabs or UTF-8 never trigger.
because: stub binary-looking output text

title: Reflow hard-wrapped prose paragraphs
detail: man pages, RFCs, READMEs and --help prose wrap near 78 columns with deep indent, so each line pays a newline plus indent. o200k proxy on a man paragraph: 64 tokens, 60 with dedent alone, 52 when also reflowed. Skip code, lists and tables.
test: Pick 20 man, RFC and README outputs; reflow only runs of wrapped lines; tokenize; ask 10 factual questions per set against the original; verify no code block merged.
because: pure text reflow transform

title: Thin line-number gutters in Read, cat -n and nl output
detail: A padded number plus tab or arrow on every line costs tokens (40-line sample: 440 to 320 on an o200k proxy). Drop the padding, or use a range header with every-10th-line anchors. Read is skipped by the matcher; try updatedToolOutput, or a proxy as fallback.
test: Verify that PostToolUse can rewrite Read output; unpad numbers on a logged tool_response, then run an Edit to confirm it still matches; measure gutter token share and line-citation accuracy.
because: strips cat -n/nl gutters; text transform

title: Collapse parallel-locale catalogs to source language
detail: grep -r of one key across locales/, .po or messages.*.json repeats a string in 30 languages. Rare scripts cost more tokens: a translated pangram was 15 tokens in Arabic versus 9 in English (o200k proxy). Keep the source locale, list the others by code.
test: Grep a key across a repo with 20+ locales; measure token share by script; collapse non-source locales; check the agent can still locate and edit a given locale.
because: collapses parallel-locale grep results

title: Parallel same-batch calls can stub each other
detail: Per Claude Code 2.1.316 schema text, PostToolUse may run concurrently for parallel calls; PostToolBatch fires once per batch. Two identical calls in one batch could each treat the other as earlier and both become stubs. Key the ledger by tool_use_id; settle at PostToolBatch.
test: With a prototype stub hook, issue two identical Bash or Read calls in one parallel batch; check what the model receives and whether a full copy survives; repeat with 8.
because: PostToolUse concurrency and PostToolBatch hook events

title: PreModelSwitch hook asks before forfeiting a warm cache
detail: Claude Code 2.1.316 reportedly has PreModelSwitch and PostModelSwitch hooks whose payload mentions context_tokens and prompt_cache_warm. A switch re-caches the whole context on the new model. Ask or deny while warm and large; allow after /clear or compaction.
test: Verify that PreModelSwitch fires and carries those fields; log payloads over normal use, sum tokens re-cached on warm switches; then enable an ask-gate above a size threshold and count deferrals.
because: Claude Code PreModelSwitch hook

title: Log resume cold-cache flag and context size
detail: SessionStart for resume/fork reportedly carries seconds_since_last_response, context_tokens and a flag for cache TTL exceeded. Logging them tests idea 147's assumption that resumes are usually cold, and sizes the tokens re-cached per resume.
test: Verify that these fields exist; log them from a SessionStart hook matched on resume|fork; after a week histogram context_tokens and the cold fraction; multiply by the cache-write price ratio.
because: resume-event hook payload fields

title: Append report-size contract to Agent prompts
detail: A subagent's final report lands in the parent context and is re-read every later turn. PreToolUse updatedInput on the Agent tool (or SubagentStart context, reportedly) appends 'under N words, path:line bullets, no code dumps'. Targets parent input tokens, not narration.
test: Measure subagent report tokens times remaining parent turns in transcripts; A/B the contract on 10 delegated tasks for total tokens and whether the parent needed follow-up reads.
because: PreToolUse updatedInput on subagent tool

title: Wrapper dedupes other hooks' repeated additionalContext
detail: UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse and similar hooks that inject the same text each turn (git status, reminders) add a new copy every time. A wrapper runs their command, hashes additionalContext, and emits it only when changed or after compaction.
test: Count hook_additional_context attachments in session JSONLs, group by hash for duplicate share and tokens; wrap one real hook and diff transcript tokens.
because: wraps other hooks' additionalContext output

title: Deny repeat Skill invocations already in context
detail: Each Skill call injects the whole SKILL.md body again. PreToolUse on Skill can deny with 'already loaded at turn N' while the body is still in context, using the post-compaction boundary from transcript_path. UserPromptExpansion covers typed slash commands.
test: Count repeated Skill tool_use per session in JSONLs times body tokens; prototype the deny and check the model continues without reloading.
because: Skill tool, PreToolUse and transcript_path are harness features

title: Block oversized pastes in UserPromptSubmit, save to file
detail: 2.1.316 UserPromptSubmit output has no rewrite field, only block or additionalContext. A hook can save a big paste to a file, block, and show a ready-to-send prompt citing the path; blocked prompts reportedly leave context. Costly UX; refines idea 108.
test: Verify that a blocked prompt is absent from the next request; count prompts over 20k chars in transcripts; time the extra user step.
because: UserPromptSubmit hook block-and-save flow

title: Re-inject saved-output index after compaction
detail: Compaction summaries may drop ctxprune note paths, so the model reruns commands instead of grepping saved originals. SessionStart with source compact (or PostCompact, which receives the summary) can inject a deterministic one-line index of ids and commands, unlike model-written PreCompact guidance.
test: Compact a session holding 5 compressed outputs; ask follow-ups needing cut details; count command reruns versus greps of saved files with and without the injected index.
because: SessionStart/PostCompact hook injection

title: Separate ledger and rate for subagent tool calls
detail: Hook input carries agent_id and agent_type only inside subagents (2.1.316 schema text). Subagent contexts are short-lived, so the re-read multiplier differs from the main thread, and Explore-style agents are read-heavy. Key ledger, threshold and rate on agent_id.
test: Split recorded tool results by sidechain versus main; compute tokens times later re-reads per bucket; sweep rate and threshold per bucket on replayed outputs.
because: keys on hook-input agent_id field

title: Join hook savings log to OTel by prompt id
detail: Hook input reportedly carries a prompt id matching the OpenTelemetry prompt.id attribute (2.1.316 schema text). Logging chars before and after per call and joining to per-request token usage gives exact net savings per prompt without parsing transcripts.
test: Verify that the ids match; enable telemetry with a console exporter, log prompt id in the hook, join on it, compare input tokens per prompt with hook on and off.
because: hook prompt id and Claude Code OTel

title: Competing PostToolUse registrations: duplicates and other trimmers
detail: Plugin hooks.json and 'ctxprune install' scopes can register the same matcher, and _is_ours only scrubs settings files, so two copies may run per call, doubling model work and notes. A third-party updatedToolOutput hook may win, clobber or re-process the text. Define precedence; detect at install.
test: Enable plugin plus install; run one 10 KB Bash output in claude -p; count hook processes and notes. Add a dummy updatedToolOutput hook, swap order, check what the model sees.
because: competing hook registrations in settings files

title: Strip generator boilerplate from MCP schemas and ToolSearch results
detail: pydantic/FastMCP and zod emit per-property title, default null, anyOf [T, null], $schema and additionalProperties:false. A toy two-tool schema went 273 to 143 tokens (o200k proxy). Strip in a tools/list proxy, and in ToolSearch results if PostToolUse may rewrite them.
test: Verify that a PostToolUse rewrite of ToolSearch output is honored; strip tools/list dumps from installed servers, tokenise before/after; run 30 tool-call prompts comparing argument validity and tool choice.
because: schema boilerplate stripped in payload-level proxy

title: ToolSearch fetch precision: schemas loaded versus tools used
detail: Each deferred schema fetched by ToolSearch stays in context. Log per session how many schemas a call returned (default max_results 5 for keyword queries) versus tools actually called later; try select:name-only steering and max_results 1-2.
test: Parse transcripts for ToolSearch tool_use/tool_result pairs; count tokens of returned schemas, mark schemas never invoked, report waste share by query style (select versus keyword).
because: ToolSearch deferred-tool mechanism is harness-specific

title: Tune ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH threshold and pin hot MCP tools
detail: Claude Code reportedly accepts ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH true, false or auto:N, plus per-server alwaysLoad and tool _meta anthropic/alwaysLoad. Force deferral for big servers and pin the few hot tools so idle schemas leave the prefix. Anthropic's Tool Search post reportedly cites about 85% fewer definition tokens.
test: Verify that these settings exist; with 3 MCP servers read /context MCP tokens under false, auto, auto:2, true; run one golden task per setting comparing turns, search calls, success.
because: harness env var and per-server settings

title: Confine chatty MCP servers to one subagent
detail: Define a subagent whose frontmatter lists its own mcpServers and tools (reportedly supported), keep the server out of the main session. Parent never pays the schemas or raw outputs, only the subagent's summary. Differs from allowlisting by keeping the capability.
test: Verify that frontmatter mcpServers works; compare main-session /context and total billed tokens for three github-heavy tasks done directly versus delegated; check answers keep the needed facts.
because: subagent frontmatter config

title: Prefer gh CLI with --json fields over GitHub MCP
detail: gh issue list --json number,title,state and gh api --jq return only chosen fields, and drop about 50 GitHub MCP tool names and schemas from the prefix. Output then also passes the Bash hook. Steer via CLAUDE.md or deny the MCP server.
test: Run the same three tasks (list open issues, read a PR, fetch job logs) via MCP and via gh; compare output tokens and /context prefix tokens; check needed fields survive.
because: advice on which tools users steer agents toward

title: Per-tool or toolset allowlist inside one MCP server
detail: Servers with dozens of tools (this session lists about 50 GitHub ones) cost names and schemas each. Use server flags (GitHub MCP reportedly has --toolsets, --read-only, dynamic toolsets) or per-tool deny rules to keep only the ten used.
test: Tokenise each tool's schema from tools/list, count calls per tool in transcripts, drop never-used tools or toolsets, then compare /context MCP tokens and task success on a golden set.
because: harness per-tool deny rules and server flags

title: Collapse mutating MCP results to a short acknowledgement
detail: create_, update_, add_, push_ and merge_ tools return the object the model just wrote (reportedly full PR or comment JSON), often under the 6,000-char threshold. Keep id, url, state, error; save the rest.
test: Collect results of write-verb MCP calls from transcripts, size them in tokens, and check which fields the next five turns referenced; simulate the ack form and count misses.
because: ack for mutating MCP results; payload-only

title: Steer file pushes from push_files to git push
detail: mcp push_files and create_or_update_file take full file contents as tool arguments, so the model pays output tokens a second time for text it already wrote with Write, and the copy stays in context. Deny in PreToolUse; suggest git push.
test: Scan transcripts for push_files and create_or_update_file calls; sum tokens of their content arguments and how often identical text appeared in an earlier Write; simulate the deny.
because: PreToolUse deny steering, no payload rewrite possible

title: Canonicalise cache prefix: tool order, key order, volatile strings
detail: Cache hits need byte-identical prefixes, and tool definitions come first, so one changed byte invalidates everything after. Diff tools/list across sessions for volatile descriptions, unstable order and reconnects; a proxy sorts tools and keys and moves volatile text (date, git status) after the last breakpoint.
test: Start each MCP server twice and diff tools/list byte-wise; diff first requests of consecutive same-repo sessions in a logging proxy; replay canonicalised and compare cache_read_input_tokens.
because: deterministic tool and key ordering for prefix caches
check: Tools sorted by name, object keys sorted (arrays never), and the system prompt's date line and gitStatus block moved to a trailing block after the breakpoint make the tools+system prefix byte-identical across requests that differ only in those; the tool set, array order in schemas, messages and all system text are preserved and unexpected requests pass through unchanged.

title: Compress tool descriptions and server instructions once, offline
detail: Run the token classifier at install time on MCP descriptions and the initialize instructions field (in the system prompt every turn; several servers here inject long blocks), protect parameter names and enums, cache the result in a proxy.
test: Compress github tools/list descriptions at keep 0.6 with protection; have the model choose tools and fill arguments for 50 prompts; compare accuracy with the originals and count tokens saved.
because: offline compression of tool descriptions in a proxy

title: Truncate *_at ISO timestamps in MCP JSON lists
detail: created_at, updated_at, closed_at and pushed_at repeat on every item. On an o200k proxy, 2025-10-30T12:34:56Z is 13 tokens, date-only 6. Truncate to date or minute for keys matching *_at; keep the original in the saved file.
test: Count *_at fields and tokens in captured GitHub, Jira and Linear list outputs; apply truncation; check whether agents ever need seconds or timezone (sort order, staleness questions).
because: truncate ISO timestamps in JSON

title: Per-line marginal deflate cost as format-free novelty score
detail: Stream lines through one zlib or zstd stream with sync flush; bytes added per line, relative to its length, flag near-duplicates with no regex or parser. Collapse cheap runs, keep costly outliers like errors. Synthetic log check: novel lines ~80 bytes, templated ~28.
test: On 50 saved build and server logs, compare lines dropped against Drain3 templates; confirm error and traceback lines survive; chars saved at equal needle recall.
because: local zlib novelty score for lines

title: Small causal-LM surprisal as selection and repetition signal
detail: Selective Context (Li et al. 2023) and LLMLingua v1 rank tokens by small-LM self-information; ctxprune uses only the supervised classifier. A causal LM sees earlier copies, so repeated lines get near-zero surprisal without hand-written dedup. Needs no labels; combine with classifier score.
test: Score 30 outputs, 20 repetitive logs among them, with a ~135M causal LM on CPU; Spearman versus classifier; QA at equal tokens for surprisal alone and times classifier; note latency.
because: local small causal-LM surprisal signal

title: Distill model drop decisions into per-command line-template tables
detail: Run the classifier over many captured outputs of one command family, mask digits and hex, and keep line templates it drops in at least 95% of occurrences. Result is a deterministic, auditable drop table needing no model load, built from the user's own traffic.
test: Mine tables from 150 saved pytest, npm and cargo outputs; apply to 50 held-out; compare chars removed and needle recall against the model at 0.5.
because: offline-mined line-template drop table, local

title: Learn MCP key-path drop lists from classifier scores
detail: Aggregate the classifier's mean keep-score per JSON key path across a server's responses; paths scoring low in over 90% of responses join a per-tool drop list. Catches verbose boilerplate fields that are not derivable from siblings, unlike derivable-field mining.
test: Run on 100 captured GitHub or Jira MCP responses; list top 30 paths by chars removed; hand-review false positives; check JSON still parses and QA holds.
because: learned per-tool drop lists, local scorer

title: Hashed-feature linear atom scorer distilled from the classifier
detail: Train a fastText-style linear model on classifier scores using atom shape, hashed neighbour words, line position and indentation. Aims to run in numpy in milliseconds without ONNX or the 143 MB download, so it could serve outputs under 6k chars or cold-start.
test: Fit on 5k scored chunks; on held-out report Spearman and top-50% overlap with the classifier, latency, and QA at 0.5 versus classifier and random.
because: distilled linear student of scorer

title: Markdown section skeleton for READMEs and docs pages
detail: Parse headings; keep the outline, each section's first sentence and fenced code blocks, and elide other bodies as '[Install: 1.2k chars elided]'. Targets cat README.md, docs fetched via MCP, changelogs. Structure-aware alternative to atom deletion on prose.
test: 30 README, docs and changelog outputs over 6k chars; ask where-is and how-to questions; compare accuracy and tokens with the classifier at 0.5.
because: markdown section skeleton; text transform

title: MinHash near-duplicate blocks within and across outputs
detail: Shingle 3-5 line blocks or paragraphs, flag blocks with Jaccard at least 0.8 against an earlier block, and replace with 'similar to lines 12-18' plus only the differing atoms. Catches repeated docstrings, stack frames and license headers that differ in a year or address.
test: On 50 saved outputs, measure chars in near-duplicate but not identical blocks versus exact duplicates, then review 20 replacements for lost meaning.
because: local MinHash near-duplicate folding

title: Ablation-attribution labels from a small reader LM
detail: Label each line by how much deleting it lowers a small instruct LM's likelihood of the agent's recorded next action or quoted text (leave-one-out). Task-grounded labels without a teacher prompt, rather than verbatim-quote matching.
test: Take 100 SWE-smith tool outputs with known next turns; compute line importance with a ~1.5B LM; measure overlap with teacher v2 keep set and quote labels.
because: offline label generation for training

title: Reader-verified teacher labels: drop chunks that fail QA
detail: Generate questions per training chunk from the original, answer them from the teacher's compressed text with a small reader, and discard or downweight chunks that fail. Task-grounded label filter, complementing LLMLingua-2's variation-rate and alignment-gap filters (per its paper) and the hand audit.
test: 300 labeled chunks, 5 questions each; report pass rate by source; fine-tune on pass-only versus all; compare QA at 0.33 and 0.5 kept.
because: offline label filtering for training

title: LogHub annotated templates as free token labels
detail: LogPAI's Loghub datasets ship hand-annotated templates for HDFS, BGL, OpenStack and others; template constants versus parameters give per-token labels without an LLM teacher. The corpus build has no system or CI log source. Check dataset license first.
test: Label Loghub-2k with constants dropped and parameters kept; measure the current model's ROC-AUC against it; then add to training and compare log-chunk QA.
because: free labels from public log templates

title: Elision marker ablation at deletion points
detail: detok drops runs silently, so the reader sees spliced words as adjacent and cannot tell absence from deletion. Compare no marker, '…', per-run '[-N words]' and per-line '(+14 lines)' at equal total tokens. Markers may cut confident-wrong answers, or cost more than they earn.
test: 100 QA items at 0.33 and 0.5 with each variant; compare accuracy, tokens, and abstain versus confident-wrong split on questions whose answer was dropped.
because: elision marker ablation study

title: Per-command-family rate bandit and refetch circuit breaker
detail: Thompson sampling over rates {skip, 0.7, 0.5, 0.33}, keyed by the command's first two words or MCP tool. Reward is tokens saved minus a penalty for a rerun or grep of the saved original. Refetches near 1 minus keep roughly cancel savings; auto-skip that family.
test: Verify that refetches are detectable from Bash commands; replay recorded transcripts with regret events as penalties; compare net tokens against constant 0.5 and the best fixed rate per family.
because: per-command-family rate bandit, local state

title: Savings ceiling: bill decomposition from transcript usage fields
detail: Price each turn's usage: input, cache write split 5m/1h, cache read, output. In one local session output tokens were the largest share, then cache writes, then reads. Tool results are the only share ctxprune can touch, so this bounds the prize.
test: Script over ~/.claude/projects: price usage per turn, attribute tool_result tokens times surviving turns, report the ceiling share per session and per month.
because: bill decomposition from Claude Code transcript fields

title: Next-turn output tokens as hidden cost of compression
detail: Output tokens cost the most per token (reportedly 5x input) and were the largest billed share in one local session. Gaps in compressed text may lengthen thinking or hedging. Net-savings accounting counts only input tokens.
test: In a 15% holdout arm or recorded replays, pair next-turn output_tokens (incl. thinking) for compressed versus original on 40 oversized results; report mean delta.
because: measures output-token side effects of compression

title: Install-time savings forecast with a not-worth-it verdict
detail: ctxprune install (or doctor) scans the user's own transcripts, counts tool results over the threshold, estimates tokens and dollars saved, and says skip if tiny. One local session held 14 tool results, about 68k chars total.
test: Run the scanner on this machine's session and on a heavy-output project; confirm the verdicts differ and match a manual count of results over 6,000 chars.
because: install-time scan of harness transcripts

title: Live statusline meter plus session-end realized-savings receipt
detail: Hook appends each compression to a per-session ledger. A statusLine command shows net tokens and dollars; a SessionEnd step parses the transcript for realized values (turns survived, actual write TTL, refetches) and prints a conservative range, not a forecast.
test: Verify that statusLine and SessionEnd receive session_id and transcript_path; fake a ledger, render the meter, compare the receipt with hand-computed values for one recorded session.
because: statusLine and SessionEnd harness features

title: Survival-turn distribution of tool results; skip short-lived contexts
detail: A saved token earns 0.1x of input price per turn it survives, so value depends on remaining turns. Measure turns until compaction or session end per result, split main, subagent and headless runs. Short-lived contexts may not repay hook latency.
test: Parse session JSONLs including sidechain files; per tool_result count later assistant turns before compaction or end; report median and p90 by context type and by turn index.
because: survival-turn distribution analysis

title: Compaction-avoidance credit: price a compaction, count those avoided
detail: A compaction costs a summary call (cached input read plus output at the higher output rate), then a fresh cache write of the new prefix. Value saved tokens by compactions avoided and report 'headroom turns gained', not only raw tokens.
test: Find compaction summary records in transcripts, sum billed usage of that turn plus the next turn's cache_creation; divide by tokens per compaction cycle to price one saved token.
because: compaction cost valuation analysis

title: Latency break-even: hook milliseconds versus prefill time saved
detail: Every compressed call costs hook CPU (about 2 s without serve) but shortens API prefill on the next turn. Nobody has measured whether that nets positive for 6k-30k char outputs. Report ms spent per 1k tokens saved.
test: Via a logging proxy, time next-turn time-to-first-token with 5k versus 10k extra uncached tokens; compare against hook wall time with and without serve.
because: latency break-even measurement

title: Lazy-import fast path for sub-threshold hook calls
detail: ctxprune/__init__ imports compress eagerly. Here a no-op Bash event costs 56 ms versus 10 ms bare Python (python -X importtime shows ctxprune.hook ~37 ms). Defer imports until a slot passes the size check; the tax is paid on every Bash and MCP call.
test: Time 50 runs of 'python -m ctxprune hook claude-code' on a small event before and after; assert identical stdout and a drop of tens of ms.
because: lazy imports cut per-call overhead; output unchanged
check: With ctxprune/__init__ lazy (PEP 562) and `python -m ctxprune hook claude-code` dispatched before cli is imported, a sub-threshold hook call loads only ctxprune and ctxprune.hook (about 30 fewer modules, no dataclasses/inspect/argparse) and prints exactly the same stdout as today on seven events (small, skipped, compressed, malformed); the CLI and the library attributes still work. Millisecond figures are reported but not asserted.

title: Model-price-keyed threshold: lower min_chars on expensive models
detail: min_chars is a constant 6000 though break-even depends on the per-token price of the running model. Read the model from the last assistant record in transcript_path; pricier models get a lower threshold, cheaper ones a higher one.
test: Check transcript assistant records carry a model field; sweep min_chars 2k-12k per model on recorded sessions with the cost model; report net dollars and latency.
because: threshold by model price; model field is in payload

title: Throttle compression rate by plan usage-window burn
detail: Subscription users are limited by a usage window, not dollars, and cache reads may weigh differently there. If the statusLine payload exposes window usage (reportedly in newer Claude Code), compress harder as the window fills, gentler when fresh.
test: Verify that the statusLine stdin JSON exposes window usage; if so, log it beside ledger entries for a week before enabling the rule.
because: statusLine plan-usage payload and subscription windows

title: Leave-one-out and Shapley savings attribution across stacked rules
detail: Stacked rules (dedupe, noise packs, model) overlap: whichever runs first claims the savings, so a sequential table misranks them. Credit each rule its Shapley value over all subsets; drop rules with near-zero marginal value.
test: On the replay corpus run all 2^6 rule subsets, compute per-rule marginal and Shapley savings, and compare the ranking with the order-dependent sequential table.
because: Shapley savings attribution analysis

title: API-native clear_tool_uses edit via proxy or SDK loop
detail: Anthropic's context-editing beta (clear_tool_uses_20250919, reportedly header context-management-2025-06-27) clears old tool results server-side with trigger, keep, exclude_tools and clear_at_least (amortises cache invalidation). Add it in a proxy for Claude Code, or directly in Agent SDK loops, instead of custom stubbing.
test: Replay a recorded 40-turn tool loop with trigger 30k, keep 5, clear_at_least 10k versus none; read applied_edits; compare billed cache tokens and task success.
because: Anthropic context-editing API feature

title: Proxy upgrades cache_control to 1h TTL on observed idle gaps
detail: Default cache TTL is 5 minutes; a 1h write costs more (2x versus 1.25x per Anthropic pricing docs) but survives think-time. Proxy rewrites breakpoints on tools, system and history to 1h only for sessions whose request gaps exceed 5 minutes.
test: Log inter-request gaps per session via proxy; simulate cost with 0.1x, 1.25x and 2x multipliers; then enable for one session and compare cache_creation and cache_read totals.
because: Anthropic cache_control TTL rewriting

title: Proxy keep-alive pings to hold the prompt cache warm
detail: A cache read refreshes the TTL at no extra charge. Shortly before the 5-minute expiry the proxy replays the last prefix with max_tokens=1. By published multipliers a ping costs about 0.1x versus 1.25x for a cold rewrite, so break-even is near a dozen pings.
test: From logged idle gaps, compute ping cost versus avoided cold rewrites per session; send one real ping and check usage shows cache_read_input_tokens covering the prefix.
because: Anthropic prompt-cache TTL and pricing specific keep-alive

title: Prune tool results in compaction requests when cache is cold
detail: The summarisation call sends the whole history to get a short summary. If an idle gap already expired the cache, the prefix is rewritten anyway, so run ctxprune over its tool_results. With a warm cache this likely loses, since reads cost 0.1x.
test: Capture a /compact request via logging proxy; measure tool_result token share; compare pruned versus full cost cold and warm; have a reader answer questions from both summaries.
because: proxy prunes tool results in summarisation request

title: Dedupe repeated client-injected system-reminder blocks in history
detail: Claude Code attaches system-reminder text (todo nudges, file-changed notices, IDE hints) to turns, and it persists in history. Proxy hashes blocks, keeps the first and rewrites repeats at first sight, so the cached prefix stays byte-stable.
test: Log a 50-turn session through a passthrough proxy; hash every system-reminder block; report repeat counts and token share before writing any rewrite.
because: hash-dedupe repeated blocks in history at first sight

title: Classify non-main-loop API calls by model, size and purpose
detail: Besides the agent loop, clients make small-model utility requests (titles, topic checks, subagents). Group by model, max_tokens and system-prompt hash; tally billed share. Candidate fixes: response cache by request hash, or env switches like DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS (reportedly).
test: Run a 30-minute session through the logging proxy; print per-group request count, input and output tokens; flag groups with byte-identical repeated requests.
because: proxy-side classification of API call purposes

title: Stub old Write and heredoc tool_use inputs in request history
detail: A Write input carries the whole file and stays in history after the file is on disk; existing proxy ideas only touch tool_results. Proxy replaces aged Write content or Bash heredoc bodies with path, line count and hash; tool_use inputs are reportedly not signature-checked.
test: Sum tokens of Write and heredoc inputs older than 10 turns across transcripts; replay stubbed history and count how often the model re-Reads or contradicts the earlier content.
because: proxy stubs aged Write/heredoc tool_use inputs
check: Write inputs and `cat > file <<EOF` bodies older than ten assistant turns become one line (line count, sha1, 'on disk at this path'); young turns, failed or deleted writes, short content, script heredocs and files not on disk now keep their content, every stub's hash is reproducible from the disk or marked changed with a later Edit in history, a message flips at most once. Request tokens fall 41%, but billed with prompt caching stubbing every turn costs 59% MORE and batches of ten 14% more, because each rewrite re-bills the prefix after it; one rewrite late in a session is about break-even.

title: Pin cache locality across OpenRouter, LiteLLM and OpenAI-style gateways
detail: Each provider or key keeps its own prompt cache, so load-balancing silently misses. Pin one provider (OpenRouter provider order with fallbacks off, reportedly), a sticky LiteLLM deployment per session, and a stable prompt_cache_key on OpenAI-format requests.
test: Run the same 10-turn session with default routing and pinned routing through the gateway; compare cached tokens in usage per turn.
because: provider-specific cache routing and prompt_cache_key features

title: Inject missing cache_control breakpoints for Claude behind OpenAI-format agents
detail: Agents speaking OpenAI format to Claude through LiteLLM or OpenRouter may send no cache hints, so every turn bills full input rate. Proxy adds breakpoints on system, tools and the last message (LiteLLM reportedly has injection-point config).
test: Point Aider or Cline at the gateway; check usage for zero cache_read tokens across turns; add breakpoints; compare billed input over a 15-turn task.
because: injects Anthropic cache_control breakpoints

title: Proxy rewrites newest tool_results the hook cannot reach, memoized
detail: Built-in Read, Grep, Glob, is_error results and inline shell injections reportedly bypass the PostToolUse rewrite. A proxy compresses the newest tool_result at first appearance, after every cache breakpoint, and memoizes by tool_use_id so later requests repeat identical bytes.
test: Log which tool_result types exceed 6,000 chars without carrying the hook note; apply ctxprune in a replay proxy to those; assert byte-identical prefixes on the next turn.
because: proxy compresses newest tool_result, memoized by id

title: Verbatim-skip regex misses wrapped source-printing commands
detail: Ran VERBATIM_CMD: it skips 'cat a.py' and 'git diff' but still compresses 'sudo cat', 'docker exec c cat', 'env X=1 cat', 'timeout 5 cat', 'git -C repo diff', 'git --no-pager diff', 'gh pr diff', 'diff -u', 'tail -n', 'rg -n'.
test: Build a 60-command fuzz corpus of wrappers and flag orders around source-printing commands; assert skip. Prototype a shlex stage parser and compare false-skip rate on captured Bash events.
because: command-string skip regex fix

title: Hook client timeout equals host timeout, so fallback cannot finish
detail: hook.py waits urlopen timeout=60 while settings.json kills the hook at 60 s, and serve holds one global lock. A busy server stalls to the kill, then fails open. Parallel tool calls without serve each load a 143 MB model.
test: Start serve, send a 200 KB request, fire three hook calls concurrently; record time and outcome of each. Repeat without serve. Try a 3 s client timeout, then fail open.
because: hook timeout in settings.json

title: Verify hook output is an ordered subsequence of the input
detail: _compress writes whatever any HTTP service on port 8719 returns (stale serve, other software, local attacker) into the tool output. Require kept atoms to be an ordered subsequence of the original, protected atoms present and length shrinking; else fail open.
test: Unit test: fake server returns injected text, reordered words, dropped digits; hook must decline. Run the check over a replay corpus to find real compressor violations.
because: fail-open output verification, pure text check

title: Does updatedToolOutput persist across resume, compaction and later turns?
detail: Unknown whether Claude Code stores compressed or original text in the session JSONL and replays it on --resume, --continue and after /compact. If originals return, savings vanish or earlier bytes change between turns, busting the prompt cache.
test: Run a hooked session, resume it through a logging proxy; diff the replayed tool_result against hook output and original; compare cache_read tokens across turns before and after.
because: tests Claude Code updatedToolOutput persistence behaviour

title: Plugin cold path: uvx resolve and model download exceed timeout
detail: Without a pip install, hook.sh runs uvx --from 'ctxprune>=0.2.1' on every call, possibly re-resolving the index. The plugin skips model pre-download, so hf_hub_download runs inside the 60 s hook. Early large outputs stall, then pass uncompressed.
test: Fresh HOME and uv cache behind the proxy: time first and fifth large-output hook calls. Prototype a local_files_only probe, instant fail-open and detached background prefetch; retime.
because: plugin hook cold path and timeout

title: Trivial-baseline arms: head/tail, uniq, stopwords, random drop
detail: Contrarian control: at equal Claude-token output, does the 140M model beat a head+tail cut, line dedupe, stopword-only deletion, or random deletion that keeps protected atoms? If a cheap arm ties on reader QA, the model's latency and 143 MB buy nothing there.
test: Build four arms matched to ctxprune output token counts on the agent-text QA set; score with the same reader; report wins per content type.
because: trivial-baseline control arms

title: Protect-set recall: hyphenated names, bare filenames, quoted strings
detail: is_protected leaves Makefile, Dockerfile, left-pad, serde-json, feature-login, Error and 'quoted' unprotected, so they can be deleted. Branch, package, container and subcommand names are what later commands reuse. Measure how often copied tokens were unprotected.
test: From transcripts, collect tokens later copied into Bash or Edit inputs that appeared in compressed outputs; report unprotected share by class; add class rules and re-measure misses.
because: measures protect-set recall on copied tokens

title: Shield backticked commands and hint lines from deletion
detail: 'Run `npm audit fix --force`' keeps only '--force' because npm, audit and fix are unprotected; rustc 'help:', git 'hint:' and pip 'Try:' lines fare the same. Agents copy these suggestions. Keep backtick spans and hint-prefixed lines whole.
test: Collect hint lines from cargo, git, npm, pip outputs; compress at 0.5; count commands that no longer match the original after shlex split; add the shield and recount.
because: keeps backtick spans and hint lines whole

title: Replace 0.95 bail-out with a fidelity-per-token ratio floor
detail: The hook accepts any result under 0.95 of input characters. A 7% cut still pays the note and deletes words, so quality risk per saved token peaks there. Gate on a tighter ratio (about 0.75) or escalate rate instead.
test: Replay outputs; plot achieved ratio against reader QA loss and net tokens after the note; pick the knee and gate below it.
because: tighter ratio gate on compression result

title: ACON-style failure-pair loop to refine noise-pack rules
detail: Replay tasks with full versus compressed output; for pairs where only the compressed run fails, a strong LLM names the dropped lines that mattered and proposes rule exemptions. ACON (Kang et al., Microsoft, 2025) refines compression guidelines this way, reporting 26-54% lower peak tokens.
test: Take 15 regret-log cases or paired replays; let Sonnet propose exemptions; re-run, check fixes flip without raising output size over 5%.
because: dev-time LLM failure-pair rule refinement

title: Hindsight waste labels: useless, redundant, expired spans
detail: AgentDiet (arXiv 2509.23586) has a cheap LLM reflect on a step's output after later steps and mark useless, redundant or expired spans, reportedly cutting input tokens 40-60%. Run it offline as a labeler for classifier training, since live hindsight rewrites break cache.
test: On 30 transcript tool results plus the next 3 steps, label spans with Haiku; compare against the classifier's drops and the verbatim-reuse labels from item 169.
because: offline hindsight labeler for training

title: Warm shared prefix once before fanning out subagents
detail: Anthropic's docs reportedly say a cache entry is readable only after the first response begins. Parallel children with an identical system prompt, tools and CLAUDE.md all pay the 1.25x write. Launch one child first, then fan out the rest.
test: Start 8 claude -p calls with one shared prefix simultaneously versus 1 then 7; compare summed cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens in the JSON usage.
because: subagent fan-out orchestration, not payload rewrite

title: Add optional jq/JMESPath projection argument to MCP tools
detail: A stdio proxy adds an optional _select argument to every tool schema, run server-side before results return. Prior art: Anthropic's code-execution-with-MCP post (Nov 2025) filters rows in a sandbox, reportedly 150k to 2k tokens. Complements the free-text 'want' of item 191.
test: Record 10 github list_issues/list_pull_requests tasks; compare full responses against agent-projected ones, and count the schema tokens the extra argument adds per tool per turn.
because: MCP proxy adds projection argument server-side
check: A proxy adds an optional _select jq argument to every tool schema and applies it to the JSON result before it returns (never to errors, never when absent, never to a server that owns the argument); projections save >90% on ten list tasks, the answer computed from the projected rows equals the answer from the full result, and a broken or misspelled filter fails open with a note.

title: Query-ranked function bodies for large source reads
detail: Split a big source file into functions with tree-sitter, rank them by BM25 against the user prompt and command, keep top bodies whole and shrink the rest to signature plus docstring line. LongCodeZip (Shi et al., 2025) reports up to 5.6x on code tasks.
test: Take 30 large Reads from transcripts; check what share of lines later quoted in Edit old_strings fall inside kept bodies, versus signature-only skeleton item 206.
because: BM25 ranking against prompt and command in payload
check: With the question in-band, the 1-3 functions BM25 ranks highest keep their whole body and every other body becomes a '...  # lines A-B' marker; ast sees every signature and class, a function the question names keeps a byte-identical body, and ranged reads, short files, a missing or unmatched question and unparseable text are returned untouched.
check_loses: the statements of every function and method body of 3+ lines (kept as a '...  # lines A-B' marker with the exact range), docstring lines after the first, comments inside bodies, anything nested inside a function body; bodies of functions ranked below the top three

title: Probe-question recall test for /compact, including chained compactions
detail: After compaction, ask probe questions (files touched, error seen, decision made, next step) and grade recall. Factory.ai (Dec 2025) did this and reported anchored incremental summaries beat full regeneration, an internal evaluation. Repeat after 2-3 chained compactions to measure drift.
test: Take 5 long transcripts; generate default and custom-instruction summaries via the API; ask 8 fixed probes each; grade with a rubric. Gate item 110's terse-summary guidance on it.
because: tests /compact, a harness command

title: Measure repeated failed-then-fixed commands across sessions
detail: Agent-memory prior art (Reflexion, Voyager skill library, Anthropic's memory tool) stores lessons across runs. Here: if the same repo repeatedly sees pytest fail then 'uv run pytest' work, a SessionStart note of working commands would skip that discovery.
test: Scan transcripts per repo: find nonzero-exit Bash calls followed by a different successful invocation; count recurrences across sessions and tokens spent on the failed attempts and their output.
because: measures failed-then-fixed command patterns

title: Match-count histogram instead of hits for over-broad searches
detail: When rg/grep returns over ~60 lines, emit per-file counts for the top 25 files, 3 sample hits each and a 'narrow the pattern' hint; original saved. SWE-agent's search commands reportedly refuse past 50 matches and ask for refinement rather than listing.
test: Replay 50 recorded large grep outputs; count tokens saved, and how often the next call was a narrower grep versus a read of the saved file.
because: match-count histogram for oversized search output

title: Auto-inject cheap params found in MCP input schemas
detail: Anthropic's tool-writing guide (Sep 2025) reportedly advises concise/detailed response_format, pagination and field selection. Scan each tool's inputSchema for such params (response_format, detail_level, fields, limit, minimal_output) and set the cheapest when unset; generalizes github-only item 203.
test: Dump tools/list from installed MCP servers and count tools with such params; run 10 calls with and without injection, noting tokens and follow-up re-calls for detail.
because: uses tool schemas to set cheap call params

title: Cloud CLI --help: keep flag headers plus first paragraph
detail: Measured: gcloud compute instances create --help is 14,272 o200k tokens, 12,351 in FLAGS, and SYNOPSIS re-lists every flag. Keeping each flag header plus first paragraph left 47%. az -h and aws help likely similar.
test: Digest gcloud, az, aws and kubectl help for 5 commands each; ask 10 flag-usage questions per command; compare answer accuracy and tokens against full help.
because: trims cloud CLI help text
check: In the FLAGS/OPTIONS sections of a gcloud or aws help page each flag keeps its header, its first paragraph, the list a first paragraph introduces with a colon and any later paragraph that says 'must be one of'; the other paragraphs collapse to '[N more lines omitted]' and the SYNOPSIS (which re-lists every flag) keeps one line. Names, synopsis head, group headers ('At most one of these can be specified'), every flag header, first paragraph, enumeration and the NAME, DESCRIPTION, EXAMPLES sections are unchanged.
check_loses: the later paragraphs of every flag other than enumerations: applicability notes ('only available for global addresses', 'May not be specified with --global'), examples inside a flag's text, aws Syntax and structure blocks; and the SYNOPSIS lines after the first

title: GitHub Actions logs: fold passing steps, keep failing step
detail: gh run view --log and get_job_logs prefix each line with a 28-char timestamp (18 o200k tokens versus 11 for a sample line itself) and dump with:/env: inputs per step. Fold ##[group] steps without error or warning to name, duration and line count.
test: Pull 10 failed-run logs with gh run view --log; fold green steps; assert root-cause error lines survive; ask which step failed and why, versus raw; compare tokens.
because: folds passing CI log steps in text
check: Steps of a gh run view --log whose lines hold no ##[error], ##[warning] or error-ish word collapse to one line with line count, duration and start time; every other step stays verbatim with its timestamps, so the failing step, its root-cause lines and every warning are unchanged.
check_loses: the content, `with:`/`env:` inputs and per-line timestamps of steps that did not fail or warn (the saved original has them)

title: BuildKit plain progress: regroup steps, drop download ticks
detail: docker build --progress=plain prefixes lines with '#N 1.842' elapsed times, interleaves parallel steps, and reportedly prints sha256 download ticks (3 synthetic ticks: 240 of 326 tokens). Regroup by step id; keep only the final tick, CACHED, DONE and errors.
test: Verify that plain progress prints download ticks: build a multi-stage Dockerfile cold and warm; count tick and prefix tokens; confirm RUN error output and exit code survive regrouping.
because: regroups BuildKit progress lines
check: Regroups BuildKit plain progress by step id: interleaved pieces of a step are made contiguous, repeated step headers, '#N ...' continuation markers, per-line elapsed prefixes and all but the last download tick of each layer are dropped; step names, DONE, CACHED and ERROR lines, every RUN output line, the exit code and the Dockerfile excerpt below the stream are unchanged.
check_loses: the per-line elapsed seconds inside RUN output, the intermediate download ticks, and the interleaving order of lines between parallel steps

title: Terraform plan: fold known-after-apply lines and tags_all copies
detail: New resources list many '+ attr = (known after apply)' lines, and the AWS provider's tags_all repeats tags. Fold computed attributes into one 'computed: a, b, c' line; mark tags_all 'same as tags'. Synthetic block: 112 tokens to 39.
test: Collect 5 plan outputs (docs samples or terraform_data); count computed and tags_all lines; fold; ask which attributes change and which are computed, versus raw plan.
because: folds terraform computed attributes
check: In a terraform plan, the '+ attr = (known after apply)' lines of each block become one '# computed after apply: a, b, c' line and a tags_all block identical to the tags block above it becomes '(same as tags)'; every resource and action, every literal attribute, every update or replace line that carries a before value, the summary, the output changes and any error block are unchanged.
check_loses: the original attribute order and column alignment (computed attributes are listed together at the position of the first one)

title: terraform show -json plan: keep only changed resources
detail: Plan JSON reportedly stores attributes several times: planned_values, resource_changes before/after, after_unknown, sensitive maps, prior_state, configuration. Keep non-no-op changes as changed-attribute before/after pairs; the full JSON stays in the saved original.
test: Run terraform show -json on 5 plans; measure byte share per top-level key; build the digest; ask what is created, changed or destroyed and which attributes differ.
because: plan JSON reduced to changed resources
check: Keeps the resources that are not no-ops, with their before and after reduced to the attributes that differ (all non-null attributes for a create or delete) plus the unknown-after-apply and sensitive flags of those attributes, the output changes that are not no-ops and the addresses of everything untouched; planned_values, prior_state, configuration and relevant_attributes are dropped. The result is still a terraform plan JSON, so the same questions get the same answers.
check_loses: planned_values, prior_state, configuration and the attributes of unchanged resources (the full JSON is the saved original); null-valued attributes of created or deleted resources

title: Cloud resource-ID grammar: hoist ARN, Azure, GCP prefixes
detail: Grammar-aware aliasing of ARN partition/region/account, Azure /subscriptions/GUID/resourceGroups/RG/providers prefixes and GCP googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/P URLs, with one legend line. Synthetic: GCP URL 29 to 13 tokens, Azure ID 40 to 16.
test: Replay aws, az and gcloud JSON outputs; count repeated prefixes; alias only when net-positive in tokens; have an agent write follow-up commands using the shortened tails.
because: grammar-aware aliasing with legend, deterministic
check: ARN (partition:service:region:account:), Azure (/subscriptions/GUID/resourceGroups/RG/providers/) and GCP googleapis project prefixes repeated in a cloud CLI's JSON become §N aliases with a one-line legend; the resource tail stays visible and decode restores the input byte for byte.

title: Rewrite [{Key,Value}] tag and env lists as maps
detail: AWS Tags [{Key,Value}], Kubernetes env [{name,value}] and similar pair lists pay braces and key names per entry; columnar encoding suits big uniform arrays, not 3-entry tag lists. Synthetic: pretty 65, minified 31, map 17 tokens.
test: Convert Tags, Labels and env lists in describe-instances and kubectl -o json samples; assert reverse conversion round-trips including duplicate keys; tokenize; test follow-up --filter commands.
because: rewrite key-value lists as maps
check: A list of {Key,Value} (or key/value, name/value) objects with unique string keys becomes an object whose first member {"§kv":"Key,Value"} names the original fields; decoding rebuilds the identical list, and lists with duplicate keys, extra fields, mixed shapes or non-string keys are left as lists.
check_loses: whitespace between tokens (output is minified)

title: kubectl describe and pod YAML: drop <none> lines, runtime IDs
detail: describe prints '<none>' fields, default NoExecute tolerations and the projected kube-api-access volume (124 tokens synthetic). Pod YAML status holds containerID and imageID hex digests (39 and 45 tokens each), likely force-kept by the classifier. Stub these; keep events and conditions.
test: Capture describe pod and get pod -o yaml from a kind cluster, including a CrashLoopBackOff pod; tokenize dropped classes; check an agent still diagnoses the crash.
because: stubs kubectl describe noise fields

title: ansible-playbook: per-task host counts, failures verbatim
detail: Each task prints 'ok: [host]' or 'skipping: [host]' per host under asterisk-padded headers. Fold to 'TASK name: ok 48, changed 2, skipped 0', listing only changed, failed or unreachable hosts; keep PLAY RECAP and failure result dicts verbatim.
test: Run ansible-playbook over 50 connection=local inventory hosts with one failing task; count host-line tokens; confirm failed and unreachable lines plus recap survive verbatim.
because: ansible per-task host-count fold
check: Within each task, bare 'ok: [host]' and 'skipping: [host]' lines become one 'ok N, skipping M' line; changed lines, fatal, FAILED and UNREACHABLE result lines (verbatim JSON), retry lines, debug output, handlers and the PLAY RECAP are unchanged, so counts, every changed or failed host and every failure message survive.
check_loses: which individual hosts were ok or skipped for each task (derivable only as 'every host that is not listed and not failed')

title: Fold health-probe access-log lines into a count
detail: Access logs seen via kubectl logs, docker logs or aws logs tail can be dominated by kube-probe, ELB-HealthChecker, GoogleHC and Route53 health-check hits on /healthz or /ready. Fold them to a count with first and last time; keep non-2xx probes.
test: Run nginx, loop curl -A kube-probe/1.28 against /healthz beside real requests; confirm only probe 2xx lines fold and failing probes stay; count tokens saved.
because: fold health-probe log lines

title: Event streams: keep terminal state per resource
detail: CloudFormation describe-stack-events emits IN_PROGRESS then COMPLETE rows per resource, each repeating StackId; ECS service events reportedly repeat steady-state messages; kubectl rollout status prints progress lines. Keep last state per resource key plus first failure reason.
test: Build a 40-resource stack-events sample and an ECS events list; fold by LogicalResourceId; ask which resources failed and why, versus raw; compare tokens.
because: keep terminal state per resource

title: Hook note names the CLI's own projection flag
detail: When a compressed output came from aws describe-/list-, az list, gcloud list or kubectl -o json, the note adds one tailored hint: --query, --format='value(...)' or -o custom-columns. Agents can shrink later calls at the source, without a model.
test: Replay recorded cloud CLI calls; count reruns of the same call with larger output; A/B note text with the hint over five tasks, comparing repeat-call size.
because: deterministic note hint on CLI projection flags
check: For a bare aws describe-/list-, az ... list, gcloud list/describe or kubectl get -o json|yaml command (no existing --query/--format/-o projection, no pipe or chain), the note of a compressed Bash output gains one constant hint naming that CLI's projection flag; the rest of the note and the output are byte-identical, nothing from the command is echoed, and the flag applied to the command parses and stops the hint.
