The saving is modelled on a 40-instance listing; whether agents act on the hint needs the A/B in the idea.

title: Render .ipynb as percent-format cells, cap outputs, stub images
detail: cat, jq, git show or Read of .ipynb prints kernelspec, execution_count, per-line source arrays and base64 outputs. Render '# %%' cells with indices, cap text outputs, stub image/png. Tiny notebook: 276 vs 26 tokens (o200k proxy). Needs an .ipynb exception to the cat skip.
test: Convert 10 real notebooks with nbformat; tokenize before and after; check images dominate; ask cell and output questions on both forms; confirm NotebookEdit by cell index still hits.
because: render notebook JSON as cells
check: A nbformat-4 notebook becomes '# %% <index> <type> ec=N id=X' cells with verbatim source (markdown commented), text outputs capped to 8+4 lines with the total count, image/html outputs stubbed to mime and size, errors reduced to ename and evalue; cell index and id, execution count, every source line, every stream/result text line that is shown, image count and sizes, and every error are unchanged.
check_loses: base64 image bytes and text/html bodies (size only), error tracebacks (ename and evalue only), the middle of text outputs longer than 12 lines, cell and notebook metadata other than kernel name and language version, whether a source ended with a newline, and JSON whitespace; notebooks with source lines starting '# %%', '#|', '#:' or '#~' are left unchanged

title: Unwrap syntax-highlighter span soup in HTML code blocks
detail: Pygments, highlight.js, Prism and Shiki wrap every token in a classed span; dropping attributes (#39) leaves the tags. Two-line Python sample: 101 tokens vs 11 plain (o200k proxy). Flatten pre/code to text, drop line-number cells. Targets curl'd docs pages and fetch MCPs.
test: curl 10 docs pages with code; flatten pre blocks via lxml text_content; assert text equals the entity-decoded original; compare tokens with full HTML-to-markdown.
because: flatten highlighter spans to text
check: Inside <pre> blocks whose only markup is <span> and <code>, the tags are removed (entities left as written) and line-number cells and spans are dropped; paragraphs, links, other markup and blocks with links, images or breaks are untouched.
check_loses: the class and style attributes of the highlighter spans, and line numbers

title: Rich-text AST JSON to Markdown: ADF, Notion, Slack blocks
detail: Jira REST v3 returns text as Atlassian Document Format; Notion rich_text and Slack blocks nest similarly, and Slack blocks duplicate text. Synthetic ADF: 308 tokens indented, 198 minified, 28 as Markdown (o200k proxy). Convert known node types, pass unknown ones through.
test: Capture a Jira v3 issue, a Notion page and Slack history; convert; compare tokens; diff extracted plain text between original and converted; list node types dropped.
because: rich-text AST JSON to Markdown
check: Inside any JSON document an ADF doc becomes '[md] ' Markdown (headings, lists with numbering, code fences with language, quotes, panels, tables, marks, links, mentions, emoji, cards, status, media), a Notion block list becomes Markdown, and a Slack message's blocks are dropped when they render to exactly its text; the word sequence, heading levels and texts, link targets, and Slack mentions and links are unchanged, and node types the converter does not know survive as compact JSON.
check_loses: ADF marks and attrs with no Markdown form (underline, text colour, sub/superscript, localId, layout, media size), Notion colours, annotations other than bold/italic/strike/code, block ids and timestamps, the structure of the JSON nodes (one Markdown string replaces it), Slack rich_text blocks that duplicate text, and JSON whitespace; documents with link targets containing spaces, angle brackets or parentheses are left unchanged

title: Decode base64 text content fields in API JSON
detail: GitHub contents API (gh api, curl) returns file content as 60-column base64 with encoding: base64. Eliding blobs (#41) would lose the file. 3 KB of Python: 2573 tokens as base64 vs 783 decoded (o200k proxy). Decode only valid UTF-8 without NULs; skip secrets.
test: Run gh api contents on 5 files; decode when encoding is base64; check re-encoding round-trips; tokenize both; confirm Kubernetes Secret data is left alone by default.
because: decode base64 text fields locally
check: In objects that have a "content" string and "encoding": "base64" (GitHub contents API), canonical base64 that decodes to valid UTF-8 without control characters or NULs is replaced by the text (JSON-escaped) and the encoding field records the line width and trailing newline; decoding rebuilds the identical base64, and Kubernetes Secrets, secret-looking files, binaries and non-canonical base64 are left alone.
check_loses: whitespace between JSON tokens (output is minified)

title: Strip template comments, placeholders and bot blobs from issue bodies
detail: Issue and PR bodies carry template HTML comments, '_No response_' stubs, empty headings, badge images and bot blocks (Dependabot commands footers with release notes, coverage or preview-deploy tables). Synthetic template: 72 vs 8 tokens. Keep human prose and checked items.
test: Pull 50 issue and PR bodies, including 10 Dependabot PRs, via gh or MCP; measure token share of comments, placeholders and bot blocks; ask reproduce-steps questions on both versions.
because: strips template/bot blobs from issue bodies

title: Known license texts and headers to SPDX stubs
detail: Match LICENSE, NOTICE, vendored licenses.txt and per-file headers against normalised SPDX license-list text (licensee and ScanCode do similar matching, reportedly); emit '[Apache-2.0, 11 KB]'. Apache header: 129 vs 20 tokens (o200k proxy). Exact matches only.
test: Scan 20 repos plus node_modules for license text; count tokens in grep -r 'Licensed under' hits and cat LICENSE; run matcher; verify modified licenses are never stubbed.
because: license text to SPDX stub

title: Collapse diff hunks for linguist-generated and -diff paths
detail: Ask git check-attr for linguist-generated, -diff and binary (GitHub collapses these in PR views), plus globs like dist/, *.min.js, *.snap, *.pb.go. Print 'path +N -M generated' instead of hunks. Extends the lockfile digest; needs relaxing the git diff verbatim skip.
test: Run git diff --numstat over 30 commits; flag paths by check-attr and globs; sum tokens of their hunks versus total diff tokens.
because: path globs in payload suffice; text transform
check: Sections of a git diff whose path is generated (check-attr stand-in: dist/, *.min.js, *.snap, *.pb.go, lockfiles) become 'path +N -M generated'; every non-generated file's diff is byte-identical and every file keeps its added/removed counts. Malformed or truncated sections are left verbatim.
check_loses: the hunk text, hunk headers and blob ids of generated files (their +/- counts and the fact that they changed are kept)

title: Fold whitespace-only, CRLF-flip and deleted-file diff hunks
detail: When - and + lines match after stripping whitespace and CR (formatter runs, EOL conversion), print '+N/-N lines whitespace-only' with the hunk header. Reduce wholly deleted files to 'deleted path, N lines'. Display-only diffs; needs git diff off the verbatim skip.
test: Scan git log -p of repos with formatter or EOL-fix commits; fold hunks; assert folded lines match after normalisation; compare tokens with git diff -w --ignore-cr-at-eol.
because: fold whitespace-only diff hunks

title: Clean pdftotext residue: page furniture and hyphen breaks
detail: pdftotext separates pages with form feeds. Drop lines recurring at page edges after digit masking (headers, footers, 'Page 3 of 40'), keeping the first; rejoin 'compres-' newline 'sion' when the joined word occurs elsewhere. Six-break sample: 32 vs 17 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Run pdftotext on 10 papers and manuals; count recurring edge lines and hyphen joins; check joins against a word list for fused compounds like 'well-known'; tokenize before and after.
because: pure text transform on pdftotext output

title: Stub SVG path data and editor metadata
detail: Replace d="..." path strings with a length stub; drop inkscape/sodipodi namespaces, namedview and default style attributes; keep ids, text, viewBox and structure. Synthetic Inkscape icon: 282 vs 37 tokens (o200k proxy). Targets grep -r hits and reads of icon sets.
test: Collect 20 SVGs from icon packs and Inkscape exports; measure token share of d= and editor metadata; ask which text labels and ids exist, before and after.
because: stub SVG path data text

title: Decode UTF-16 text before the binary stub decision
detail: PowerShell redirects, Excel 'Unicode Text' exports, .reg files and SQL Server scripts are UTF-16LE with BOM. 500 chars with interleaved NULs cost 1000 tokens vs 120 decoded (o200k proxy). Detect BOM or alternating NULs and decode; otherwise the NUL-density stub hides readable text.
test: Verify that NULs survive in tool_response: write a UTF-16LE file, run cat through a real hook payload; tokenize raw versus decoded; assert text round-trips.
because: decode UTF-16 text locally
check: A byte-per-character string holding UTF-16 (BOM or alternating NULs, LE or BE) is decoded to text behind a one-line header that records endianness and BOM, so the exact original byte string is recoverable; binary data and undecodable or cut-off UTF-16 are left untouched.

title: Markdown pipe tables re-serialised as TSV with header note
detail: Beyond trimming padding (#38): a 21-row, 4-column table cost 444 tokens padded, 398 minimal pipe, 325 TSV, 346 CSV (o200k proxy). Convert only when cells hold no tabs, pipes or newlines; HTML tables too. Reader accuracy per format needs checking.
test: Take 30 README and report tables; convert; ask 10 lookup and aggregate questions per table on Haiku, Sonnet and Opus; compare accuracy and tokens, pipe versus TSV.
because: pipe tables to TSV

title: Ledger walks parentUuid chain from leaf, not file order
detail: Session JSONL records carry parentUuid, and last-prompt records carry leafUuid; rewind, fork and resume reportedly leave abandoned branches in the file. Rebuilding in-context sets by file order (146) could stub against dead-branch results. This linear session already has 2 nodes with two children.
test: Verify that rewind leaves abandoned branches: run a session, /rewind two turns, rerun the command; check whether a file-order ledger wrongly stubs versus a leafUuid-ancestor ledger.
because: walks session JSONL parentUuid, private log format

title: Sweep --autocompact window against per-turn read cost
detail: Claude Code 2.1.316 has --autocompact <auto|100k-1M tokens>. Smaller windows mean more summaries but fewer cache-read tokens per turn; larger ones the reverse. Simulate cost per recorded session from usage fields, and mark any long-context price tier the model has.
test: Verify that --autocompact accepts window sizes; from 20 transcripts model cache reads, summary calls and rewrites at 100k, 200k, 400k, 1M; report the cheapest window by session length.
because: Claude Code --autocompact flag

title: Task-boundary /clear nudge from identifier overlap at UserPromptSubmit
detail: After a topic change, stale context is re-read every turn. A UserPromptSubmit hook measures path and identifier overlap between the new prompt and recent tool results or files touched; near-zero overlap above N context tokens shows a one-line /clear or handoff-file suggestion.
test: Verify that UserPromptSubmit can show a systemMessage; flag zero-overlap prompts over 100k context in transcripts; sum tokens carried by later turns; hand-check 30 flags for real topic shifts.
because: UserPromptSubmit hook and /clear

title: Deterministic session handoff digest at SessionEnd instead of resuming
detail: A Stop or SessionEnd hook writes a no-LLM digest from the transcript: user prompts, files edited, commands with exit status, last failing test lines, final assistant message. Next day starts fresh from that file, not --resume, which re-caches the whole old context cold.
test: On 10 long sessions, compare tokens of a cold resume against a digest start; ask 8 fixed continuation questions in both and grade the answers.
because: SessionEnd hook and transcript format

title: Detect reverted edits; stub dead-end spans on resume
detail: Find Edit hunks later undone (git checkout, git restore, or an inverse Edit by hunk hash) and the failing runs between them. Resume surgery (147) or a proxy swaps those spans for a one-line 'tried and reverted: file, goal' stub, keeping the lesson.
test: Scan transcripts for edit/inverse-edit or git checkout pairs; sum in-between tool-result tokens; replay a stubbed copy and check the model does not retry the dead end.
because: stubs reverted edit spans found in history

title: Memoize read-only Agent reports by git tree hash and prompt
detail: PreToolUse on Agent hashes the normalised prompt, HEAD tree and git status; on a hit it denies with the cached report as the reason, skipping the whole subagent run. Helps repeated exploration across sessions and after compaction. Any dirty-tree change invalidates.
test: Verify that a PreToolUse deny on Agent delivers its reason to the parent; count Agent calls with identical normalised prompts per repo across transcripts for a hit rate.
because: PreToolUse hook on subagent tool, git tree

title: Subagent writes full report to file, returns digest and path
detail: Unlike a hard size cap (240), the Agent prompt or agent definition says: write the full findings to a file, return a 10-line summary plus path. The parent reads slices only when needed, so detail stays recoverable and later turns carry less.
test: Run 10 exploration tasks with and without the suffix; compare parent tokens at the end, count follow-up slice reads, and grade final answers against inline-report runs.
because: subagent definition and prompt contract

title: Evict aged images and PDFs from history with text stubs
detail: Old screenshots, pasted images and PDF blocks cost about width*height/750 tokens each every turn (Anthropic vision docs); tool-result clearing reportedly misses user-pasted ones. A proxy or resume surgery keeps the latest per tab and stubs older ones as '[image: WxH, viewed turn 12]'.
test: Count image and document blocks per transcript and turns survived; replay stubbed history after 5 turns on 10 UI tasks; count tasks that needed the old image.
because: non-text media: images and PDFs

title: Post-compaction restore audit: summary versus re-attached files and skills
detail: Claude Code reportedly re-attaches recent files and invoked skills after compaction, under token caps. Attribute the first post-compact request's tokens to summary, files, skills, reminders and tool schemas; then trim big skills and Read habits that inflate it.
test: Verify that compaction re-attaches files and skills: compact after reading 8 files and invoking 2 skills via a logging proxy; tabulate the next request's tokens by block category.
because: Claude Code compaction re-attach behaviour

title: Lint memory files for dead paths, symbols and commands
detail: Extract backticked paths, commands and identifiers from CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and auto-memory MEMORY.md, then check each against git ls-files and grep. Flag lines whose referents no longer exist; these load every session and mislead. Distinct from rewriting (107).
test: Run on this repo's AGENTS.md and 5 other repos' memory files; hand-verify each flagged line; report tokens removable and false-positive rate.
because: lints CLAUDE.md and auto-memory files

title: Audit SessionStart injections duplicated on resume, clear and compact
detail: SessionStart hooks from plugins fire per source (startup, resume, clear, compact) and their additionalContext is added as new context. On resume the earlier copy may already be in the loaded transcript. Count injected tokens per source and per plugin; restrict matchers.
test: Install a stub SessionStart hook emitting a marker; start, resume, clear and compact; grep the transcript for marker copies and sum tokens per source.
because: SessionStart hooks and plugins

title: Stub the ExitPlanMode result's echo of the approved plan
detail: ExitPlanMode reportedly returns the approved plan text again after it was sent as input and written to the plan file, so the implementation phase carries it two or three times. Replace the echo with a pointer to the plan path.
test: Verify that ExitPlanMode results echo the plan: grep session JSONLs, compute echoed tokens and duplication count; check whether a PostToolUse or proxy rewrite is honoured for that tool.
because: ExitPlanMode and plan file are harness features

title: Route PDF Read to pdftotext via PreToolUse
detail: Read on a PDF reportedly sends extracted text plus a rendered image per page (Anthropic PDF docs). PreToolUse denies Read of text-layer PDFs with a pdftotext -f/-l command; the Bash output is image-free and hook-compressible. Keep Read for scans and figures.
test: Verify that Read on a PDF adds page images: compare usage tokens for a 20-page text PDF via Read versus pdftotext -layout; detect scans by empty output; ask page questions.
because: PreToolUse deny of Read tool

title: Clean YouTube-style VTT and SRT caption files
detail: Auto-caption VTT repeats each phrase across rolling cues and tags every word with <00:00:01.599><c>. Merge overlapping cues, drop inline tags and positioning, keep a [mm:ss] stamp about every 30 s. One synthetic cue went 253 to 18 tokens (o200k).
test: Fetch real subtitles with yt-dlp --write-auto-subs for 5 videos; tokenize raw versus cleaned; assert cleaned words are an ordered subsequence; ask 10 content questions.
because: text transform on caption files
check: Caption cues (YouTube rolling VTT or SRT) are merged into '[mm:ss] words' lines, one per 30 s bucket of cue start: inline <time><c> tags, positioning, cue ids and the rolling repeats of the previous line are dropped; the ordered spoken words and which 30 s bucket each cue's new words belong to are unchanged.
check_loses: cue end times and sub-30 s timing, per-word timestamps, styling and positioning, NOTE/STYLE blocks, and a cue whose first lines legitimately repeat the previous cue's last lines (read as a rolling repeat)

title: Whisper and ASR JSON to plain timestamped text
detail: openai-whisper style results carry token-id arrays, avg_logprob, compression_ratio, no_speech_prob and seek per segment; word timestamps add a record per word. Render '[mm:ss] speaker: text', merge same-speaker turns, flag only low-confidence segments. Synthetic segment: 132 to 16 tokens.
test: Transcribe a 5-minute clip with whisper --output_format json (plus a diarized tool); tokenize JSON versus rendering; check concatenated text equals the original.
because: text transform on ASR JSON
check: Whisper-style ASR JSON becomes '[mm:ss] speaker: text' lines: same-speaker segments merge (30 s per line), every spoken word stays in order with the stamp of its line, the speaker of each word, the language, and every segment under Whisper's own confidence thresholds is flagged on its own stamped line with its avg_logprob, no_speech_prob and compression_ratio.
check_loses: token-id arrays, temperature, seek, segment end times, per-word timestamps and probabilities, the duplicated top-level text, segment ids, and the stamps of merged segments after the first of each line

title: Delta-encode repeated browser accessibility snapshots per tab
detail: Playwright-style MCP servers and Chrome extensions return a full accessibility tree with [ref=eN] ids after most actions. Keep the last tree per tab; emit changed subtrees plus 'N lines unchanged', with refs stable. context-mode reportedly sandboxes snapshots instead.
test: Replay a 20-step browser task logging every snapshot; first verify refs stay stable across snapshots; tokenize full versus delta; confirm every ref the next click used is still visible.
because: delta of repeated snapshot text per tab
check: After the first snapshot of a tab, a repeated accessibility snapshot of the same URL is sent as keep/drop/add line counts, the changed lines and an explicit removed-refs list; replaying it rebuilds every page exactly, every ref the model acts on is visible beforehand, and a URL change, renumbered refs, a closed tab or compaction give the full snapshot.

title: Compact accessibility trees: wrappers, hrefs, repeated landmarks
detail: Collapse single-child generic wrapper chains (synthetic 47 to 14 tokens), drop refs on non-interactive nodes, fold '- /url:' lines into the link line, cap long hrefs and list children at k plus a count. Stub banner, navigation and contentinfo subtrees repeated from an earlier page.
test: Capture snapshots of 10 sites via Playwright MCP; tokenize raw versus compacted; report nav/footer token share; run 20 click-by-ref and find-by-text tasks for success.
because: text transform on accessibility tree output
check: Playwright-style accessibility snapshot: generic wrapper chains collapse into their child, refs are kept only on interactive or cursor=pointer nodes, '- /url:' folds into the link line (hrefs over 64 chars are cut), text-only lists beyond 6 items get a count, and a landmark that repeats an earlier one is stubbed; every interactive element (role, name, href) with its first ref, and all page content with its ancestor chain, survive.
check_loses: refs of non-interactive nodes, refs inside a stubbed duplicate landmark (its first copy keeps them), the tail of hrefs over 64 chars, and the text of list items past the sixth in lists with no links in them

title: Digest browser network, console and Lighthouse output
detail: Network request lists include every static asset; console lists repeat HMR and dev-warning lines; Lighthouse JSON runs to megabytes. Keep failed, slow and XHR/fetch requests, fold static assets to counts, dedupe console lines, keep Lighthouse scores and failing audits.
test: Capture network, console and Lighthouse output for 5 local dev pages; tokenize full versus digest; assert every 4xx/5xx and console error survives; ask 5 debugging questions.
because: text digest of browser tool output
check: Playwright-style network lists fold successful static GETs into one '[static xN] ext=count' line (every failed request, non-GET and /api/ request stays verbatim); console lists merge identical lines into 'line (xN)'; Lighthouse JSON becomes the category scores plus the failing audits; the request total and extension histogram, every 4xx/5xx/FAILED request, every error and warning with its count, and all scores and failing audits are unchanged.
check_loses: which static asset was which (only the extension histogram stays), the position of repeated console lines after the first, and every passing Lighthouse audit with all descriptions, details, i18n strings and timings

title: Hash-stub repeated screenshots at PostToolUse
detail: Screenshots after no-op actions, or differing only by cursor blink, spinner or clock, cost about w*h/750 tokens each (Anthropic vision docs). Perceptual-hash per tab; replace near-duplicates with 'unchanged since screenshot N' text. The hook today ignores image blocks.
test: Verify that updatedToolOutput can replace image blocks; count duplicates at pHash distance 0, 2 and 6 in 3 recorded browser sessions; compare task success with stubs.
because: screenshot image handling

title: Launch browser MCP with phone viewport and no inline images
detail: Image tokens scale with area, and responsive pages at phone width show fewer elements, so shorter trees. Playwright MCP reportedly has flags for viewport, device emulation and omitting image responses. Set them in .mcp.json for non-visual tasks.
test: Verify that Playwright MCP has those flags (npx @playwright/mcp --help); load 5 sites at 1280x800 versus 390x844; tokenize snapshots; run 5 UI tasks per setting.
because: browser MCP config and image tokens

title: Verify image tokens depend on pixels, not format or colour
detail: Idea 109 lists JPEG-ify and grayscale, but Anthropic documents tokens about width*height/750 after resize, which would make format and colour irrelevant; only area and count matter. Settle this before building any screenshot filter.
test: Run count_tokens on one screenshot as PNG, JPEG q60 and grayscale at three sizes; compare with w*h/750; record where auto-resize above about 1568 px triggers.
because: image tokens, non-text media

title: Prune Android uiautomator and Appium XML hierarchies
detail: uiautomator dump nodes carry about 15 attributes, mostly false or empty (checkable, long-clickable, password). Drop default-valued attributes, shorten class and package names, unwrap anonymous containers lacking text, id or interaction. Synthetic node: 89 to 16 tokens. Appium page source shares the shape.
test: Dump hierarchies from an emulator on 5 screens; tokenize raw versus pruned; check an agent still finds tap targets by bounds and resource-id.
because: prunes default attributes in UI XML dumps

title: Fail/pass log-pair differential labels with no LLM teacher
detail: Run pytest, cargo or npm on a fixture repo with and without a seeded bug, align the two logs. Lines identical in both runs are boilerplate (drop); lines that differ carry the signal (keep). Labels come from program behavior, not a prompt.
test: Make 20 before/after pairs from SWE-smith repos; label by line diff; measure atom agreement with teacher v2 labels and failing-test-name recall at 0.33 kept.
because: program-derived training labels, no LLM

title: Localized CLI output corpus: German, Japanese, Russian tool logs
detail: Re-run git, gcc, pip, apt and pytest under LC_ALL=de, ja, ru, zh, fr so real tools emit translated diagnostics. Transfer English-run labels by line position and anchors. Fills the multilingual-tool-output gap; fineweb2 is web prose only.
test: Run 5 commands under 6 locales, compress at 0.5, count paths, codes and identifiers lost versus the English run; check per-script deletion rate.
because: training corpus of localized tool outputs

title: Odd-one-out synthetic logs as hard negatives
detail: Take repetitive logs or listings, mutate one line (new status word, changed value, rare exception), label that line keep and its near-duplicates drop. Teaches the classifier that one deviation among hundreds of look-alikes matters.
test: Build 200 logs of 300-3000 lines with one planted anomaly; measure how often the anomaly line survives at 0.33 for the current model, then after fine-tuning.
because: synthetic hard negatives for training

title: Entropy and committee sampling to choose chunks for teacher labeling
detail: Pool unlabeled public and local saved outputs; score each chunk by mean keep-probability entropy or disagreement between int8, fp32 and earlier checkpoints; send only the top slice to the teacher. Spends GPU labeling budget where the student is least sure.
test: Label 1k top-entropy versus 1k random chunks with the same teacher, fine-tune each from the current checkpoint, compare AUC and QA at 0.5 on held-out real hook outputs.
because: active-learning chunk selection for labeling

title: Re-serialize labeled JSON as YAML, XML, CSV, tables
detail: Take teacher-labeled Toucan JSON records, re-render the same objects as YAML, XML, CSV, markdown tables and key=value lines, carrying keep/drop labels by key path. Fills format gaps in a JSON-heavy corpus and trains format invariance.
test: Probe first, no training: run the current model on JSON versus YAML renderings of 50 records; report Jaccard of kept key paths at 0.5.
because: training data augmentation across formats

title: Self-consistency soft labels from repeated teacher sampling
detail: Sample the teacher five times at temperature 0.7; per-atom keep frequency becomes a soft label, and high-variance chunks are flagged as noisy. Differs from the two-prompt v1/v2 grading by measuring the teacher's own noise.
test: Sample 5 outputs for 200 chunks; report atom-level Fleiss kappa by source, then train soft versus hard labels on equal chunks and compare AUC and QA at 0.33.
because: soft labels from repeated teacher sampling

title: Multi-family teacher consensus to break teacher-reader overlap
detail: The model card notes one reader model also labeled the training data. Relabel chunks with two other model families and train on agreement-weighted labels, so gains are not tuned to one family's taste.
test: Relabel 500 chunks with two other families; report atom agreement; compare QA at 0.5 for single-teacher versus consensus-trained students using a reader from a third family.
because: multi-teacher offline labeling for training

title: Domain-adaptive masked-LM pretraining on unlabeled tool outputs
detail: Labels are the bottleneck, raw tool outputs are not. Continue mmBERT-small's masked-LM pretraining on many unlabeled logs, JSON and traces (Gururangan et al. 2020, domain-adaptive pretraining), then fine-tune on the existing teacher labels.
test: One MLM epoch over ~50k unlabeled tool outputs, then fine-tune on 10% and 100% of labels; compare val AUC against plain mmBERT-small, especially in the 10% arm.
because: domain-adaptive pretraining of the scorer

title: Whole-document teacher labels capturing cross-window redundancy
detail: Corpus chunks are at most 500 tokens, at most 2 random chunks per document, labeled in isolation. Hook inputs run thousands of tokens. Label full documents so repeated content is dropped on later occurrences, train on 2-4k-token rows.
test: Label 100 outputs over 6k chars whole versus per 500-token chunk with the same teacher; count atoms whose label flips, split by repeated-line versus unique-line atoms.
because: whole-document training labels

title: Mutation-testing labels for code: load-bearing lines
detail: For small Python modules with unit tests, delete each statement and rerun tests or py_compile. Lines whose removal breaks something are keep; comments, docstrings and dead code are drop. A deterministic code oracle with no LLM teacher.
test: On 20 permissive modules with tests, compute load-bearing flags; compare to teacher and model keep scores per line; check that signatures score high and comments low.
because: test-based labels for code training data

title: Mask protected atoms from training loss and validation AUC
detail: is_protected atoms are force-kept under protect, yet count in loss and AUC. On a toy 60-line log 62% of atoms were protected (10% in JSON, 0% in prose). Masking focuses capacity on real decisions and de-inflates per-source AUC.
test: Recompute val AUC per source for the current checkpoint with protected atoms excluded; then fine-tune with protected labels set to -100 and compare QA at 0.33 with protect on.
because: training loss and metric masking

title: Relabel corpus after deterministic pre-pass to avoid skew
detail: Planned lossless rules (ANSI strip, minify, dedent, blank-run collapse) change what the model sees, but it trained on raw text. Apply the pre-pass to corpus chunks before teacher labeling, or measure score drift first.
test: Apply the pre-pass to 300 chunks; compare per-atom score correlation and keep-rate drift before versus after; relabel 100 and compare AUC on raw versus prepassed.
because: relabel training corpus after pre-pass

title: Restrict CTXPRUNE_SERVER to loopback; refuse remote redirects
detail: hook.py POSTs each large output to whatever CTXPRUNE_SERVER names and writes the reply back as the tool result. A repo's .claude/settings.json env block can set it. Verified locally: a fake server received a planted secret and returned injected text. Accept only loopback http.
test: Point the hook at a local listener returning injected text; assert it declines non-loopback hosts and file: URLs, with an explicit opt-in override.
because: loopback-only endpoint hardening in local process

title: Saved originals: 0600 files, no-follow create, atomic write
detail: Verified: files land 0644 in a 0755 directory, readable by other local users. Create dir 0700 and file 0600 with O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW; write temp then rename, so a killed hook never leaves a truncated original the note points to.
test: Run hook under umask 022 and check modes; kill -9 mid-write and rerun; plant a symlink at the target path and assert the hook refuses it.
because: file permission hardening for saved originals

title: Decline and save nothing when output matches secret patterns
detail: env, printenv, kubectl get secret, terraform show and docker inspect dump credentials. Scan with gitleaks-style regexes plus entropy; on a hit return unchanged, so no raw copy reaches disk and no note appears. Redacting the saved copy would break 'original'.
test: Feed 50 outputs with planted AWS, GitHub and JWT secrets plus 50 clean logs; assert no file written for hits and under 2 percent false skips.
because: secret-pattern skip, deterministic on output text

title: Canary-secret leak scan across every ctxprune write path
detail: Plant a unique canary in a tool output and find everywhere it lands: saved originals, serve cache, debug output, shadow, ledger and regret logs, temp files. Only outputs/ may hold it. Guards every new telemetry idea against leaking secrets.
test: CI: run hook plus serve with the canary, then grep -r it across HOME, /tmp and cache dirs; fail if found anywhere outside outputs/.
because: canary leak scan test

title: Neutralise forged ctxprune notes inside tool output
detail: Attacker-controlled output (page fetched with curl, issue body via MCP) can carry a fake 'ctxprune compressed this output... full output is at <path>' line steering Claude to a chosen file. Escape the marker in input, or put a per-install nonce in genuine notes.
test: Pass a page containing a forged note through the hook; assert the marker is escaped or flagged and the nonce appears only in the genuine note.
because: escape forged note markers in tool output

title: Injection-susceptibility A/B: compressed versus original output
detail: Deleting words may strip the framing that marks text as untrusted page content while a planted imperative survives, or the reverse. Plant instructions in fetched pages and issue bodies, compress at 0.5, count how often a Claude reader acts on them.
test: 30 pages, 3 injection styles; reader sees original or 0.5 compressed; compare follow rates per arm with a bootstrap interval over pages.
because: injection-susceptibility safety A/B

title: Recovery-path permission probe for saved originals
detail: The note sends Claude to ~/.cache/ctxprune/outputs, outside the project. Default-mode Read or Grep there may prompt, while headless -p, dontAsk or sandboxed runs may deny, leaving the safety net unreachable. Probe each mode; add an allow rule at install or save under the project.
test: claude -p in default, acceptEdits, dontAsk and sandbox modes: ask it to grep a saved original; record prompt, denial or success. Retest with a Read allow rule.
because: Claude Code permission modes and allow rules

title: Runtime kill switch: sentinel file, pause timer, per-repo off
detail: CTXPRUNE_OFF lives in the Claude Code process environment, so it only works for new sessions. Have the hook first stat a sentinel (~/.cache/ctxprune/OFF, repo .ctxprune-off) or a 'pause 30m' timestamp: one stat call, mid-session, no restart, no settings edit.
test: Mid-session: run a large output (compressed), touch the sentinel, rerun (verbatim); time the added stat over 1,000 small events.
because: sentinel-file kill switch in local process

title: Per-rule disable flags and rule-version stamp for rollback
detail: With dozens of proposed rules, one global switch is too coarse. CTXPRUNE_DISABLE=rule_id,... plus rule versions in the ledger and saved sidecar lets one misfiring pack be turned off in the field while the rest keep saving.
test: For each rule, disable it and assert output equals the pipeline without that rule byte for byte; assert ledger rows carry rule id and version.
because: per-rule disable flags and version stamps

title: Over-deletion floor: fail open when output is far below target
detail: The hook rejects only results at or above 0.95 of input. Verified: a 52-character reply for a 10,863-character input was accepted and noted. An ordered-subsequence check also passes empty output. Reject ratios under about half the requested rate as a malfunction.
test: Fake server returning '', one word or 3 percent of the input; hook must decline. Replay real outputs and list any below 0.5x the rate.
because: over-deletion floor, fail open on ratio

title: Int8 batch-composition and thread-count determinism audit
detail: Windows are padded and scored 16 per batch by an int8 ONNX model. If activation scales are dynamic or kernels vary by thread count, a window may score differently depending on its neighbours, breaking replay and A/B. Unverified here; model not cached.
test: Score 200 windows alone, in batches of 1, 16 and shuffled, with 1 and 8 threads; report keep-decision flips and max score drift; compare fp32.
because: determinism audit of int8 scoring

title: Pin Hugging Face revision, verify hash, handshake with serve
detail: hf_hub_download takes no revision, so a fresh install fetches whatever main holds and cached users never update, making A/B runs irreproducible. Pin a commit sha, check the file sha256, expose model hash in /health, and have the hook refuse a mismatched serve.
test: Run an old serve after upgrading the package; assert the hook detects the fingerprint mismatch and falls back; tamper one model byte and assert load fails.
because: model revision pin and hash check, local

title: Strip chunk-overlap text duplicated across retrieved neighbouring chunks
detail: Splitters with chunk_overlap (LangChain RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter, LlamaIndex SentenceSplitter) make adjacent hits share text. Using source and start_index offsets, merge touching hits and emit each character span once. Exact offsets, unlike MinHash similarity matching.
test: Index a docs folder with overlap 200, retrieve top-8 for 50 questions, count characters covered by more than one hit, tokenize merged versus raw context.
because: dedupes overlapping retrieved chunk text via offsets
check: Touching or overlapping hits of one source whose texts agree on the shared span are merged into one hit covering the union, so each (source, character offset) is emitted once; hits that disagree on the overlap, other sources, hits without an integer start_index and malformed JSON are left as they are.
check_loses: the individual hits' ranks, scores and other metadata (a merged hit keeps the best-ranked member's fields at its position), empty hits contained in a neighbour, and the input's JSON formatting

title: Hoist or exclude per-chunk metadata blocks from LLM-visible text
detail: The LlamaIndex postprocessor rewrites only get_content(), so metadata that MetadataMode.LLM prepends per node (file path, dates, size, reportedly) is never pruned; same for contextual-retrieval prefixes. Set excluded_llm_metadata_keys or hoist the shared header once per source.
test: Build a default SimpleDirectoryReader index, print LLM-mode text of 8 retrieved nodes, measure metadata token share, compare answer accuracy with keys excluded.
because: hoists or excludes per-chunk metadata text

title: Split one token budget across retrieved docs by rerank score
detail: Both integrations apply one uniform rate per document and ignore the query they are passed. Allocate a global kept-token budget by reranker or retriever score: top hits near 1.0, tail hits cut hard or dropped at a score elbow.
test: On top-10 retrievals for a multi-hop QA set, compare uniform 0.5 with score-weighted allocation at equal total tokens; paired bootstrap on reader accuracy.
because: local budget allocation across retrieved docs

title: Score chunks once at ingest; store quantised scores in payload
detail: Query-agnostic atom scores can be computed at ingestion and stored as uint8 in the vector-DB payload. Query time picks a threshold for any budget with no model call, and each chunk yields identical bytes, keeping prompt-cache prefixes stable. Embed originals, serve pruned.
test: Ingest 2,000 chunks with stored scores; check recall@k is unchanged, selected text matches live compress at the same rate, and query-time latency is milliseconds.
because: ingest-time local scoring, stable bytes

title: Strip corpus-wide document-frequency boilerplate lines before embedding
detail: Hash lines across all pages of a scraped or PDF corpus; lines present in over roughly 20 percent of documents (nav, cookie banners, running headers, license footers) are removed at ingestion, so they never fill retrieved chunks. Corpus-level, unlike per-output dedupe.
test: On 1,000 crawled documentation pages, count lines above 20 percent document frequency, their token share, and hand-review 50 removals for lost content.
because: ingest-time boilerplate line stripping
check: In a serialised corpus of at least 5 documents, every line (8+ characters, page numbers masked) that occurs in more than 20% of the documents is removed from all of them; each document's title, every line at or below the threshold (including one at exactly 20%) and the document order are unchanged.
check_loses: legitimate prose that happens to repeat in more than 20% of the documents (a shared definition, a standard warning) is removed from every document; fenced code blocks and each document's title are never touched

title: Cascade a question-conditioned sentence pruner before token pruning
detail: Run an off-the-shelf query-aware pruner first, such as RECOMP's extractive compressor (Xu et al., 2023) or Provence (reportedly Naver Labs Europe, 2025), then ctxprune on survivors. Whole irrelevant sentences go before word-level scoring. Different from training our own pair-input model.
test: On 200 retrieved passages with questions, compare pruner then ctxprune at 0.5 total kept against ctxprune alone at equal tokens; reader exact-match.
because: local extractive pruner cascade

title: Anchor compression on the retriever's matched span
detail: In sentence-window and parent-document retrieval, the matched sentence is a free relevance label. Keep it verbatim and compress only the surrounding window harder. LlamaIndex MetadataReplacementPostProcessor and LangChain ParentDocumentRetriever expose the hit; same trick for rg -C context lines.
test: Build a sentence-window index; compare uniform 0.5 against hit-verbatim plus context at 0.3 at equal tokens, on questions answered in or near the hit.
because: retriever-matched span guides local compression

title: Snippet-then-expand wrapper for search-style MCP results
detail: A proxy trims each hit body in list-shaped search results (code or doc search MCP servers) to about 200 characters plus id and path, and adds a synthetic expand(id) tool. Full text is paid only for hits the agent opens; originals saved.
test: Replay search-MCP calls from transcripts: compare tokens of full hit bodies with the share of hits the agent later opened, quoted or edited.
because: MCP proxy snippets results, adds expand tool
check: Hit bodies over 260 characters in list-shaped search results become a ~200-character snippet (around the first query word) plus id, path and an expand_id; a synthetic expand(id) returns the original body byte for byte; short hits, single documents, errors and duplicate ids pass through, and an expired id is an explicit error. On 16 tasks the snippets plus the hits actually opened cost 46% fewer tokens than the full results; 9 of 16 needed an expand.

title: Benchmark against framework-native compressors at equal output tokens
detail: Compare the integrations with what RAG users already use: LangChain EmbeddingsFilter and LLMChainExtractor, LlamaIndex SentenceEmbeddingOptimizer, LongLLMLingua. Match output tokens across arms so the README can say where ctxprune wins or loses.
test: One harness, one retrieval set, equal-token arms per method; report reader accuracy and added per-query latency, with paired bootstrap intervals.
because: benchmark against framework compressors

title: Break-even: cached compressed corpus versus per-query top-k retrieval
detail: For small static corpora, compress once and place everything in a cached prompt prefix instead of fetching chunks per query. Model the break-even from corpus tokens, queries per cache lifetime and Anthropic's published cache read/write multipliers (verify current figures).
test: Spreadsheet model: measure a 50k-token corpus raw and compressed, compare against top-8 chunk retrieval at 1, 10 and 100 queries per cache lifetime.
because: break-even cost modelling for cached corpus

title: Order-insensitive, volatile-masked fingerprints for re-run stubs and deltas
detail: Verified here: rg without --sort printed the same 117k lines in a different order on each of 8 runs (sorted hashes identical), so exact-hash re-run detection never fires. Hash the sorted line multiset after masking durations, PIDs and tmp names; diff as line sets.
test: Run rg, pytest -n 4 and make -j repeatedly on one tree; count exact versus sorted-and-masked fingerprint matches, then check stubbed outputs lose no failing-test lines.
because: order-insensitive fingerprint for rerun dedup

title: Rewrite default git log entries to one line each
detail: Verified here on an o200k proxy: 21 commits cost 2285 tokens in default format, 596 as 'short-sha date author subject', 386 as --oneline. The hook does not skip plain git log. Parse commit/Author/Date blocks, keep body lines indented, save original.
test: Parse git log, reflog and shortlog output from five repos; reformat; assert each short sha resolves uniquely; ask who/when/what questions against both forms.
because: rewrites git log entries to one line

title: Factor git blame prefixes into one header per commit run
detail: Hook skips git blame as verbatim, so it saves nothing. Verified here: a 236-line blame cost 9242 o200k-proxy tokens; one header per same-commit run plus 'lineno TAB code' cost 3105 (time of day omitted). Code stays byte-exact.
test: Run blame on 20 files; regroup; assert code columns equal the original after parsing; tokenize; confirm 'who last changed line N' answers match; leave --porcelain alone.
because: factor blame prefixes; text transform
check: Consecutive default-format blame lines from the same commit share one header (hash, file, author, date, time, tz as printed); each line becomes 'lineno<TAB>code' with the code byte-exact, and decode regenerates git's padding.

title: env, printenv and set pack: drop noise vars, mask secrets
detail: Verified here: env output was 97% protected by character share, so the classifier cannot shrink it. Rules can: drop LS_COLORS, LESSOPEN, XDG_*, SSH_AUTH_SOCK-style vars, dedupe PATH entries, and mask token-like values, which doubles as a leak guard.
test: Capture env and set from five dev containers and CI shells; apply drop and mask lists; tokenize; ask PATH, HOME, VIRTUAL_ENV and proxy questions; grep masked output for secrets.
because: drops noise env vars, masks secrets in output

title: Collapse ignored and vendored subtrees in find, ls -R, du
detail: Verified here: 4000 find lines under site-packages cost 153k o200k-proxy tokens; per-root 'dir/ (N files)' lines cost 69. Collapse subtrees matched by git check-ignore --stdin or a fixed list (node_modules, .venv, dist, target); complements tree-ify and rg rewrites.
test: Run find ., ls -R, tree and du in a JS and a Python repo; collapse; confirm source files stay listed and the agent still finds its target; compare tokens.
because: fixed ignore list works from payload paths
check: In find, du -a and ls -R listings, a vendored root (node_modules, .venv, site-packages, dist, target, __pycache__, .git, ...) that has 2+ lines below it and is not the whole listing becomes 'ROOT/ (N paths)' (du: the root's own size line gets the count); every line or section outside vendored roots is byte-identical, and each root's size and count are unchanged.
check_loses: the names of everything below a vendored root (only the count of lines or entries survives), and the distinction between a root that was itself listed and one that was not

title: Fold per-path errno lines from find, du and grep -r
detail: Traversal tools print one stderr line per path for 'Permission denied', 'No such file', 'Is a directory', 'Too many levels of symbolic links'. Group by errno suffix into count, shared parent directories and first three paths, leaving stdout hits and exit status untouched.
test: As a non-root user run find / -name x, du -a / and grep -r foo /; fold stderr; compare tokens; assert real matches and exit code are unchanged.
because: group errno lines; text transform

title: Strip quoted replies and signatures from email and ticket threads
detail: Each reply in a mail or ticket thread re-quotes everything before it, so tokens grow quadratically ('>' prefixed lines, 'On <date> <name> wrote:' headers). Drop '>' blocks whose text already appears in an earlier message, plus signature and disclaimer footers.
test: Fetch 10 long threads through an email or ticket MCP; strip quote blocks present earlier plus footers; tokenize; ask who decided what, and when, against the original.
because: strips quoted replies already in earlier messages
check: In a rendered email thread, a '>' quote block whose content lines (quoted signatures ignored) all appeared in earlier messages is replaced by '[quote omitted: N lines]', '-- ' signatures and 'Sent from my ...' lines are dropped; every message header, every line of own text (who decided what, when), every quoted line that was NOT seen earlier, and the set of distinct content lines of the thread are unchanged.
check_loses: the 'On <date> <name> wrote:' attribution lines of dropped quotes, signature blocks and legal footers (names, titles, phones), and the exact quote markup of repeated text

title: Fold per-file echo lines from tar -xv, unzip, cp -v
detail: Bulk verbose commands (tar -xv, unzip, cp -rv, rsync -av, chmod -Rv, mkdir -pv) print one line per file that succeeded. Fold to total count, per-directory histogram and the first and last entry; keep any line with an error word.
test: Extract a 3000-file tarball and zip with verbose flags; fold; verify the count equals tar -t; tokenize before and after; inject one failing entry and check it survives.
because: fold per-file verbose echo lines

title: Drop +/- bar graphs from git diff --stat output
detail: Verified here: 118 stat lines over 30 commits cost 1901 o200k-proxy tokens with bars, 1739 without. The count column already carries size; the bar adds only a scaled plus/minus split.
test: Regex-strip bars from git diff --stat, log --stat and show --stat; assert file names and counts are unchanged on 20 repos; tokenize before and after.
because: drops diff --stat bar graphs

title: Shrink Edit, Write and MultiEdit success echoes
detail: Edit reportedly returns a confirmation plus a cat -n snippet of the edited region, and Write a confirmation; the model just authored that text. PostToolUse updatedToolOutput could return 'ok, lines N-M changed'. terse (qdf-hook) reportedly suppresses write echoes too.
test: Verify that updatedToolOutput is honored for Edit, Write and MultiEdit; tally their result chars across local transcripts; count later Reads of the same region after shrinking.
because: shrink edit/write echo text in tool result

title: PreToolUse caps on built-in Read and Grep calls
detail: Built-in Read, Grep and Glob results reportedly bypass PostToolUse rewriting (item 291), so updatedInput is the lever: add head_limit to Grep content mode, add limit to Read of unsized large files.
test: Verify that updatedInput is honored for built-in Read and Grep; replay transcript calls: share lacking limits, and whether later Edit old_strings fall inside the first 400 lines.
because: adds limit params to Read/Grep tool inputs

title: Generate Read deny rules for vendored and generated paths
detail: Scan the repo for node_modules, dist, *.min.js, *.map, lockfiles, snapshots and coverage output; emit permissions.deny Read() rules so the model gets a refusal rather than a huge read. Bash cat and grep reportedly bypass deny, so pair with a hook.
test: From transcripts, tally tokens of Read and cat results on generated-file globs; run five tasks with the rules on and check none needs such a file.
because: generates harness permissions.deny settings

title: Steer symbol lookups to LSP instead of grep-then-Read
detail: Claude Code reportedly ships an LSP tool (definition, references, hover) when a language-server plugin is installed. A CLAUDE.md line or PreToolUse hint on identifier-shaped greps could replace grep plus whole-file Read chains with a few location lines.
test: Verify that an LSP tool exists with a language-server plugin; mine transcripts for identifier Grep then Read chains; A/B ten 'where is X defined' prompts, LSP on versus off.
because: Claude Code LSP tool, CLAUDE.md or hook steering

title: Zero-dependency FTS5 snippet search tool replacing exploratory grep and Read
detail: claude-context (Zilliz) reportedly pairs BM25 with a vector database in an MCP server. Lighter variant: SQLite FTS5 over code chunks, top 5 snippets with path:line, no embeddings. Aims to cut multi-step grep and Read exploration, distinct from repo map (item 207).
test: Index this repo; ask 10 'where is X handled' questions to an agent with and without the tool; compare tokens until a correct answer, and score correctness by hand.
because: standalone MCP search tool

title: Cheap-LLM extractive line picker for outputs over 50 KB
detail: Send numbered lines plus the command to a small hosted model (for example claude -p --model haiku) that returns line ranges to keep; the hook prints those lines verbatim. No paraphrase risk, unlike abstractive digests (item 210); its token spend is netted against savings.
test: On 20 giant saved logs, compare kept tokens, needle recall and Haiku token spend against ctxprune at 0.5; estimate turns each output survives to amortise the spend.
because: runtime call to hosted LLM

title: Measure post-compaction re-read tax; inject a file manifest
detail: After auto-compact the model reportedly re-reads files it already saw; terse (qdf-hook) reportedly forces a full re-read plus a file manifest around compaction. Measure first, then test a path, line-count and hash manifest that lets reads use offsets.
test: Find compaction boundaries in transcripts; sum Read and cat chars in the next 10 turns that repeat files read before the boundary; compare with the manifest's token cost.
because: measure post-compaction re-read tax first

title: Drop repeated WebSearch REMINDER footer after first result
detail: All 15 WebSearch results in local transcripts end with the identical 'REMINDER: You MUST include the sources...' line, about 20 tokens each (my estimate). Keep it on the first result per session, drop later copies via updatedToolOutput.
test: Verify that updatedToolOutput works for WebSearch (item 72); count footer repeats per session; check the model still ends answers with a Sources list when later footers are dropped.
because: dedupes repeated boilerplate footer in tool results

title: Hoist constant and default-index columns from text tables
detail: Hoist columns with one distinct value into a header line, and drop a default 0..N-1 index column with a note, in pandas print, to_csv, psql, mlflow search_runs. Synthetic 50-row CSV, 3 of 18 columns constant: 6744 to 6389 tokens (o200k).
test: Run head/to_csv on 20 real datasets; count tokens in constant and RangeIndex columns; ask row-lookup questions on original versus hoisted form.
because: hoist constant table columns
check: CSV columns whose cell text is identical in every row, and pandas' unnamed 0..N-1 index column, are listed once in a header line (position, raw header cell, raw value) and removed from the rows; decoding re-inserts them, restoring the original bytes including quoting and line endings.

title: Strip column-uniform trailing zeros from printed floats
detail: pandas pads every cell in a column to equal decimals (describe() prints 200.000000). Dropping trailing zeros keeps values identical, unlike rounding (#44). Synthetic 6-decimal columns: 279 vs 189 tokens (o200k). Also sklearn reports and numpy prints.
test: Tokenise describe(), classification_report and DataFrame prints before and after zero-stripping; assert float() parse equality for every cell.
because: strip column-uniform trailing zeros
check: In a printed table, a right-aligned column whose cells all carry the same number of decimals (pandas describe(), sklearn reports, DataFrame prints) has trailing zeros cut from each cell; every cell still parses to the same float, and every other character, including the whitespace between tokens, is unchanged.
check_loses: the fixed decimal width of the column (200.000000 becomes 200, 0.50 becomes 0.5) and the vertical alignment of the table

title: Fold the dominant value in df.info() and isnull().sum()
detail: df.info() prints 'N non-null' and a dtype per column; isnull().sum() prints a 0 per column. Print only exceptions plus 'all other columns: 200 non-null'. 18-column frame: info() 334 tokens, isnull().sum() 117 (o200k). Same for nunique, dtypes.
test: Run the four calls on 10 real datasets; tokenise raw versus folded; ask 'which columns have nulls' and 'which dtype is column X' on both.
because: folds dominant value in df.info output

title: Key-value metric lines with stable keys to header plus rows
detail: HF Trainer dict reprs, Keras 'loss: x - accuracy: y' epoch lines and logfmt repeat every key name on every row. Print the key list once, then values only; off-schema lines stay inline. 20 synthetic Trainer lines: 760 vs 406 tokens (o200k).
test: Capture a real Trainer and a Keras fit log; convert runs of same-key lines to columns; tokenise; ask 'epoch of best val_loss' on both forms.
because: header-once key-value metric lines
check: Runs of 3+ iterations (1-3 lines each) that match once every number becomes '¤' are written as a template plus comma-separated value rows with the number text kept exactly; other lines stay inline and decode restores the exact bytes.

title: Decimate per-step training curves, keep extremes and anomalies
detail: Per-step loss, lr and grad_norm lines run to thousands. Keep first and last, running min and max, NaN/inf, spikes past k sigma, eval and checkpoint lines; fold the rest into 'steps 100-900: loss 2.1 to 1.4'. Unlike counter folding (#26). Original saved.
test: Take a 5k-step Trainer or Lightning log; ask final loss, best eval step, whether it diverged; compare answers and tokens, decimated versus original.
because: decimate training curves locally
check: Per-step 'step N loss L lr R grad_norm G' lines fold into '[steps a-b: N lines folded; ...]' markers; first and last step lines, the 3 lowest-loss, 3 highest-loss and 3 highest-grad_norm lines of the run, every NaN/inf line, every spike past 3 sigma and every non-step line (eval, checkpoint, warnings) stay verbatim, and the virtual step count is exact.
check_loses: the intermediate loss, lr and grad_norm values of folded steps (marker keeps loss/lr endpoints, the loss range and the grad_norm maximum), and which steps were folded

title: ASCII +---+ grid tables to TSV (Spark show, mysql)
detail: Spark show(), mysql, beeline and sqlite print +-----+ border rows and a | on every line; psql adds a header rule. Convert to TSV when cells hold no tabs. 2-row synthetic grid: 55 vs 18 tokens (o200k). Not box glyphs (#15) or markdown (#38).
test: Capture show(), mysql and psql output with 50 rows; convert; assert cell-for-cell equality after parsing the grid; tokenise both; ask lookup questions.
because: grid tables to TSV
check: A +---+ border grid (header, rule, rows, closing rule) as printed by Spark show(), mysql and beeline becomes one tab-separated line per row with the space padding trimmed; the cells are unchanged, and a grid whose cells contain a tab, a grid that is not clean, and everything outside grids stay as they were.
check_loses: space padding and alignment inside cells (so leading or trailing spaces that were part of a value), and the border and rule lines

title: Spark driver INFO logs: fold per-task lines into stage summary
detail: spark-submit at INFO logs a Starting-task and Finished-task line per task, plus ResourceUtils, BlockManager and MemoryStore chatter (from memory). Fold to per-stage task counts and slowest task; keep WARN, ERROR and stack traces verbatim.
test: Run a local[4] pyspark job over 200 partitions at INFO; classify lines by template; rank templates by tokens; confirm a failing-task line survives.
because: folds Spark per-task log lines
check: Runs of per-task driver chatter (TaskSetManager Starting/Finished task, Executor Running/Finished task, MemoryStore, BlockManagerInfo, ResourceUtils, BlockManagerMasterEndpoint INFO lines) fold into '[... N lines folded: stage S started a finished b slowest TID t ms ...]'; every WARN, ERROR, stack frame, DAGScheduler/SparkContext line stays verbatim at its exact position, and per-stage started/finished counts and the slowest task are unchanged.
check_loses: the id, host and timing of every folded task except the slowest per stage and run, and the individual MemoryStore/BlockManager block lines

title: Spark explain: strip #exprId suffixes and repeated plan phases
detail: Spark plans suffix each attribute with a session-unique id (id#12L), and explain(True) prints parsed, analyzed, optimized and physical plans (from memory). Strip ids; keep optimized plus physical. Three-line synthetic plan: 71 vs 45 tokens (o200k).
test: Run explain(True) on a join plus aggregate in local pyspark; tokenise; check the scan filter and join strategy are still identifiable from the reduced plan.
because: strips Spark exprIds, repeated plan phases

title: pg_dump and mysqldump boilerplate; one-row INSERTs to multi-row
detail: Drop the pg_dump SET preamble, OWNER TO lines and '-- Name: x; Type:' banners, and mysqldump '/*!40101 */' pragmas; hoist repeated ENGINE/CHARSET clauses; merge per-row INSERTs sharing a column list into one VALUES list (from memory).
test: Dump a sample Postgres and MySQL schema with data; classify lines by template; tokenise before and after; check table and column names all survive.
because: dump boilerplate drop, INSERT merge on text
check: pg_dump and mysqldump text loses its SET preamble, OWNER TO lines, '-- Name: ...' banner comments, '/*!40101 ... */' pragmas, LOCK/UNLOCK TABLES and DROP TABLE IF EXISTS lines; ENGINE/CHARSET options shared by every CREATE TABLE are stated once; consecutive one-row INSERTs with the same column list merge into one multi-row INSERT; every CREATE TABLE block (table and column names), each inserted row with its column list, COPY data, constraints, indexes and any error line are unchanged.
check_loses: the dropped preamble, owner, banner and pragma lines, DROP TABLE IF EXISTS statements, the repeated ENGINE/CHARSET clause on each table, blank-line runs (collapsed to one), and the one-statement-per-row INSERT layout

title: ML framework startup and warning boilerplate pack
detail: Import and train-start lines are fixed text: TensorFlow cpu_feature_guard, cuDNN factory registration and TensorRT notices; HF 'Some weights were not initialized'; tokenizers fork warning; Lightning GPU/TPU/HPU lines; sklearn ConvergenceWarning advice with doc URLs (from memory).
test: Run small torch, TF, transformers and sklearn scripts in a clean env; extract constant lines with the pack-discovery tool (#59); keep warnings naming user code.
because: fixed ML startup warning text rules
check: Lines from a table of ML boilerplate (TensorFlow cpu_feature_guard, oneDNN, cuDNN/cuFFT/cuBLAS factory, TensorRT notices, the HF training advice, the tokenizers fork warning, Lightning hardware and tip lines, sklearn ConvergenceWarning advice and URLs) fold into '[... N fixed lines folded: pack xK]'; every other line (user warnings, the HF newly-initialized weights line, the first line and STOP reason of a ConvergenceWarning, metrics, tracebacks) is verbatim at its exact position and the per-pack counts are unchanged.
check_loses: the text of the folded boilerplate lines (it is the table, so only the pack name and count remain) and their timestamps

title: Fold identical lines across distributed ranks and workers
detail: torchrun/DDP '[rank3]:', Ray '(pid=1234, ip=...)' and mpirun '[1,3]<stdout>:' prefixes yield N copies of each line. Strip the prefix, fold identical lines to '[ranks 0-7]', keep rank-specific lines attributed. Not the pytest warning fold (#126).
test: Run a 4-process gloo torchrun script that logs and warns; measure duplicated token share; confirm a rank-only NaN or OOM line stays attributed to its rank.
because: fold identical rank-prefixed lines
check: Within a run of rank-prefixed lines (torchrun '[rankN]:', Open MPI '[job,rank]<stdout>:'), identical bodies from different ranks join one '[ranks 0-3] body' line; each rank's own line order, every rank-specific line (still carrying its own prefix), every unprefixed line and the order of every line against the first nan/error/OOM/warning line are unchanged.
check_loses: the interleaving order of different ranks' lines inside a run (except against alarm lines: nan, inf, error, exception, traceback, out of memory, failed, fatal, warn), and which of several equal lines a rank printed first relative to other ranks

title: Cell-lookup QA for tables under token deletion
detail: The classifier deletes words, but tables carry meaning by position: dropping one cell shifts every later column. Scripted row-and-column lookups on pandas prints, psql and CSV at 0.33 and 0.5 kept show whether tables need rules or protection.
test: Generate 50 tables with known cells; compress at 0.5; ask 5 lookups each with regex-derived gold; compare accuracy against original and hoisted forms.
because: table lookup QA benchmark

title: Prometheus /metrics exposition: hoist labels, fold zero series
detail: Scrapes repeat metric name and full label set on every bucket and series line, plus HELP/TYPE lines. Drop HELP, hoist shared labels per family, fold zero-valued series and empty histogram buckets into counts. One 3-label bucket line is 26 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: curl /metrics from a Go or Node service; tokenise per line class (HELP, bucket, zero value); compare raw versus folded; ask 5 'is metric X nonzero' questions on both.
because: hoists Prometheus labels, folds zero series
check: Prometheus exposition text loses its HELP lines; per family the labels every series shares (job, instance, ...) are stated once, series with value 0 and histogram buckets whose cumulative count equals the previous bucket's are folded into one counted note; the type of every family, every non-zero series with its full label set and value, and every bucket that changed a histogram's count (with its increment) are unchanged.
check_loses: the HELP text, the names and labels of zero-valued series (only their count), the order of labels within a series, and the le of buckets that did not change the count

title: Regular-interval time series: encode as start, step, values
detail: Prometheus and Loki query_range matrices store [timestamp, value] pairs at fixed steps. When steps are regular, emit start, step and a flat value list; irregular gaps stay explicit. Synthetic 30-point series: 333 vs 148 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Query a local Prometheus with query_range; re-encode; assert expansion round-trips exactly; tokenise; check the agent still finds the peak value and its time.
because: encode regular time series compactly
check: Runs of 3+ equally spaced `[timestamp,"value"]` pairs in a Prometheus/Loki matrix become `start@step:values`; the decoder restores the exact original bytes, irregular points stay explicit.

title: OTLP, Jaeger and Zipkin trace JSON to indented span tree
detail: Trace JSON carries typed attribute wrappers ({key,value:{stringValue}}), 32-hex trace ids and 19-digit nanosecond epochs per span. Render a parent-child tree with name, duration, start offset from root, status, unwrapped attributes; trace id once. Wrapper alone: 13 vs 5 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Export a trace from a local OTel collector or Jaeger all-in-one; render the tree; tokenise both forms; ask which span is slowest and which errored, on both.
because: trace JSON to span tree
check: OTLP, Jaeger and Zipkin trace JSON become 'trace <id> | N spans | window' plus one line per span, indented by depth, with service, name, duration and start offset in 0.1 ms, status with message, and unwrapped attributes; span count, tree shape, every duration and offset, the slowest span and every errored span with its message are unchanged.
check_loses: span and parent ids, span kind, scope and schema info, trace state and flags, span events and links (an exception event is folded into the status message of an errored OTLP span), resource attributes other than service.name, sub-0.1 ms precision, and JSON whitespace; traces whose spans repeat an id, run backwards or form a parent cycle are left unchanged

title: Profiler outputs: aggregate, then cut rows by cumulative weight
detail: cProfile tables, jmap -histo, perf script samples, .cpuprofile and Chrome trace-event JSON list hundreds of rows or raw events. Aggregate self-time per function, keep rows to 95% of total weight, add a residual row. One trace event: 81 tokens, summary line 8 (o200k proxy).
test: Profile a small Python or Node program with cProfile and --cpu-prof; aggregate; tokenise; ask for the top 3 hot functions and total time from both forms.
because: aggregates profiler output rows by weight
check: Profiler tables keep the heaviest rows to 95% of the total weight (at least 5, ties kept) and add one residual row with the cut rows' count and weight; cProfile, jmap -histo and node .cpuprofile JSON (aggregated per function) are covered. The totals line, the three heaviest rows, the number of rows and the total weight accounted for are unchanged.
check_loses: every row below the 95% cut (name, calls, cumulative time), the cumulative-time column's meaning for callers with near-zero self time, and raw .cpuprofile nodes, call tree and per-sample timestamps

title: Folded-stack profiles: rewrite as prefix tree with counts
detail: Flamegraph input ('a;b;c 17' from stackcollapse scripts, py-spy --format raw) repeats shared frame prefixes on every line. Print a trie with indentation and sample counts. Synthetic 6 stacks: 107 vs 34 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Capture py-spy or perf on a busy program; convert folded lines to tree; assert the tree expands back to identical lines; tokenise; ask for the hottest leaf path.
because: folded stacks to prefix tree
check: Folded-stack lines 'a;b;c N' are written with only the frames not shared with the previous line, indented by the shared-frame count; order, counts (as text) and frame text are restored exactly.

title: journalctl -o json: keep a field allowlist
detail: Each journal JSON entry carries about 20 per-boot or per-unit fields (__CURSOR, _BOOT_ID, _MACHINE_ID, _SYSTEMD_CGROUP, _CAP_EFFECTIVE, _SELINUX_CONTEXT). Keep timestamp, unit, PID, PRIORITY, MESSAGE; hoist constants. Synthetic entry: 351 vs 42 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Run journalctl -o json -n 200 on a systemd host; rank key frequencies; drop the complement of the allowlist; tokenise; confirm error messages and unit names survive.
because: journal JSON field allowlist
check: journalctl -o json lines become 'timestamp unit[pid] pN message' (host hoisted or suffixed to the unit when it varies, newlines escaped, binary messages stubbed); every entry's time to the millisecond, unit, pid, priority and message, the per-priority counts and the error messages are unchanged.
check_loses: __CURSOR, _BOOT_ID, _MACHINE_ID, _SYSTEMD_CGROUP/SLICE/INVOCATION_ID, _CAP_EFFECTIVE, _SELINUX_CONTEXT, _UID/_GID, _EXE, _CMDLINE, SYSLOG_FACILITY/TIMESTAMP, monotonic and source timestamps, COREDUMP_* and every other field, sub-millisecond time, and the bytes of binary messages; output that is not one JSON object per line is left unchanged

title: Severity-run folding: collapse DEBUG/INFO runs between warnings
detail: Detect level tokens (log4j, Python logging, glog I/W/E, syslog PRI, pino numeric). Collapse runs of TRACE/DEBUG/INFO to 'N lines, time span, top 3 templates'; keep WARN and above verbatim plus 2 context lines. Ceiling: 20 DEBUG lines, 759 vs 24 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Run on LogHub Spark, HDFS and OpenStack samples plus a CI log; count tokens dropped; verify every WARN/ERROR line and context survives; ask what happened before the first error.
because: collapse low-severity log runs
check: Runs of TRACE/DEBUG/INFO lines (log4j, Python logging, glog) fold to one '[... N lines folded (first .. last): per-level counts; top 3 templates]' line; every line with a WARN/ERROR/FATAL/Traceback/Exception word, every line the format does not recognise, and 2 lines of context around each alarm stay verbatim, and virtual line positions are exact.
check_loses: the individual messages of folded DEBUG/INFO lines (only the top 3 templates with counts, the level counts and the first/last timestamp survive), and the ids and values inside them

title: Strip addresses, symbol hashes and arg words from stack frames
detail: Rust '::h<16 hex>' symbol hashes, Go '(0xc000..., 0x1)' argument words and '+0x1d' offsets, gdb '0x00007f... in', Python 'object at 0x7f...' and Java '$$Lambda$N/0x...' are noise to the agent. Synthetic frame tokens (o200k proxy): Go 44 to 9, gdb 75 to 38.
test: Collect backtraces from Rust (RUST_BACKTRACE=1), Go panic, gdb bt, Python and Java; strip; count tokens; check the agent can still locate the failing file:line and function.
because: strips addresses and hashes from stack frames

title: Crash-report section triage: drop libraries, memory maps, register dumps
detail: JVM hs_err_pid files, Android tombstones, macOS crash reports and Linux oops print long sections (Dynamic libraries, Environment Variables, memory maps, Binary Images, 'Modules linked in', 'Code:' bytes) after the cause. Keep header, signal, crashing thread; stub the rest with line counts.
test: Trigger crashes (Unsafe on a JVM, ctypes null deref with faulthandler, a segfaulting C binary); measure token share per section; verify cause and top frames remain.
because: crash-report section triage, text transform
check: In a JVM hs_err log, macOS crash report, Linux oops or Android tombstone, register dumps, memory-to-register maps, stack dumps, the whole Process/System sections, other threads' stacks, binary-image lists, memory maps, open files, the module list and 'Code:' bytes become '[ctxprune: N lines elided (Section)]'; the header, signal/exception/cause lines, the crashing thread's frames and the identity lines are unchanged, and kept lines plus the stubs' counts add up to the original line count.
check_loses: register values, memory contents around registers, the loaded-library, module and memory-map lists, the other threads' stacks and heap/GC/environment/OS details (all in the saved original)

title: Zero-valued counter dumps: ethtool -S, procfs, smaps
detail: Dumps like ethtool -S (per-queue counters), /proc/PID/smaps, /proc/vmstat, redis INFO and cgroup stat files list many 'key: 0' lines. Drop them, print 'N zero counters omitted', keep nonzero. Five zero smaps lines cost 44 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Capture ethtool -S, /proc/self/smaps and /proc/vmstat on a real box; tokenise the zero-valued share; ask 'which counters are nonzero' and 'is X zero' on both forms.
because: drops zero-valued counter lines

title: Error-event frame objects to compact traceback lines
detail: Sentry-style events and Jackson-serialized StackTraceElement arrays hold each frame as an object (filename, abs_path, module, lineno, in_app, pre_context, post_context, vars). Render 'file:line in func', keep in_app frames, vars for the top frame only. Synthetic frame: 68 vs 7 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Log a Java exception as JSON with a logstash encoder and build a Sentry-shaped event; convert; tokenise; check the agent locates the failing line from the compact form.
because: frame objects to compact traceback lines

title: Regroup interleaved logs by request, trace or thread id
detail: Concurrent services interleave many requests. Group lines by correlation key (req-uuid, trace_id, thread, pod), print the key once as a header, keep order inside each group, add per-line time offsets. A 32-hex id costs 21 tokens per line (o200k proxy).
test: Use LogHub OpenStack samples (request ids) and a multi-worker server log; measure id token share and savings; check an agent reconstructs one request's failure sequence.
because: regroup logs by correlation id

title: Breakpoint before unique task text in fan-out children
detail: In 36 local workflow children, 27 warm ones each read ~43k cached tokens yet wrote ~11k fresh (~299k of 857k first-turn writes). If the shared block is identical across siblings, a proxy cache_control breakpoint after it turns writes into reads.
test: Log two sibling first requests through an ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL proxy, diff bytes before the task text, add cache_control at the last shared block, compare cache_creation on siblings 2..N.
because: cache_control breakpoint placement

title: Census of cold-start prefix sizes per subagent type
detail: Local children cold-started at ~54k or ~77k tokens, the larger kind roughly every 25-30 minutes, never sharing. Differing tool sets or system prompts per agent type likely fragment the cache; tool allowlists shrink tokens but unshare the prefix. Quantify before restricting tools.
test: Group first-turn creation plus read by prefix size across subagent JSONLs; diff the tools and system blocks of two types via proxy; price shared versus split prefixes.
because: Claude Code subagent types and transcript usage fields

title: Calibrate subscription-quota weights per token class
detail: API prices say cache reads cost 0.1x, but how Pro and Max usage limits weigh cache reads, cache writes, uncached input and output is not documented in the repo. If reads count near full, compression is worth more than the dollar model says.
test: Run scripted claude -p sessions with known usage mixes; regress the /usage percentage change on each token class. Assume no weights beforehand and report intervals.
because: vendor subscription quota weights

title: Suffix-aware gate for stubbing old history
detail: Editing history at position p rewrites every later token at +1.15x over a read while warm, but costs nothing right after a gap past the TTL. Stub only if saved × 0.1 × turns_left beats suffix × 1.15, or the cache is cold.
test: On recorded transcripts, compute suffix tokens and remaining turns for every superseded tool result; count candidates passing the warm rule versus the cold-gap rule; total net token-equivalents.
because: proxy gate for stubbing old history by cache economics

title: Stop-hook alert when cache reads collapse mid-session
detail: At Stop, read the last request's usage from transcript_path; if cache_read is under 80% of the prior request's total within a 5-minute gap, print one line naming suspects: model, effort, MCP reconnect, image. Locally 0 of 307 requests flagged.
test: Replay stored transcripts through the rule, including seeded busts from toggling /effort mid-session, and measure recall and false positives; check hook output reaches the user via systemMessage.
because: Stop hook and transcript_path

title: Keep fan-out system prompt and cwd byte-identical
