detail: Per-child --append-system-prompt text, or worktree paths in the environment block, change the system segment, so system and messages stop sharing across children (tools may still hit). Put per-task text in the user prompt and use one cwd.
test: Launch 5 claude -p calls with differing append-system-prompt versus fixed system plus differing prompts, in same versus distinct worktree paths; compare cache_read on runs 2-5 from JSON usage.
because: advice on configuring fan-out child prompts

title: Controlled cache-bust matrix for mid-session toggles
detail: Anthropic docs reportedly say thinking-budget changes, image additions and tool-list edits invalidate cached segments. Measure rewritten tokens for /effort, /model, MCP reconnect, plugin toggle, pasted image and CLAUDE.md edit in one 50k-token session, then publish a do-not-toggle table.
test: Through a logging proxy, run one scripted session; apply one toggle per trial from a fresh copy; record next-request cache_creation versus baseline, repeating 3 times for noise.
because: measures harness toggles (/effort, plugins, MCP reconnect)

title: Pin MCP tool list against mid-session list_changed churn
detail: Tools sit first in the cached prefix, so one edited or reordered tool after a tools/list_changed notification rewrites system and messages too. A proxy keeps the first-seen tool array and applies changes only after compaction or a cold gap.
test: Fake MCP server emits notifications/tools/list_changed every 3 minutes; verify Claude Code refetches, and measure next-request cache_creation; repeat with the pinning proxy.
because: proxy pins tools array so prefix stays stable

title: Test the 20-block cache lookback on parallel tool batches
detail: Anthropic docs reportedly say cache hits are searched only about 20 content blocks before a breakpoint. A parallel batch of Reads adds two blocks per call. Locally, 307 requests had at most 16 blocks between them and no misses, so this is unproven.
test: Issue a parallel batch of 12 Reads (24+ blocks) after a warm turn, via proxy; compare next-request cache_read to prior total; if it misses, add an intermediate cache_control breakpoint.
because: tests Anthropic-specific 20-block lookback

title: Add cold-rewrite term to per-token savings value
detail: Each cache expiry re-bills every surviving context token at 1.25x, so a saved token is worth 1.25 + 0.1 per turn + 1.15 per later cold rewrite. Users with habitual idle gaps benefit more; derive min_chars and rate from their gap history. Extends #4.
test: From 20 transcripts count requests after gaps over 5 minutes per session; recompute break-even per tool result with and without the term; count sub-6,000-char outputs that flip.
because: cost-model refinement for cache expiry

title: Thinking cost as residual of output_tokens minus visible text
detail: Claude Code transcripts keep thinking blocks with empty text (here 243 blocks held about 85 tokens), so thinking looks free. Final usage.output_tokens minus tokenised text and tool_use inputs gives real thinking spend; in one local workflow session it was most of the output.
test: Per assistant message id, subtract o200k-tokenised visible content from final output_tokens; sum by tool and by preceding tool_result class.
because: relies on Claude Code transcript thinking blocks

title: Per-request thinking budget keyed to preceding tool result
detail: A proxy sets thinking.budget_tokens (or effort) low after trivial successes (Edit ok, ls, clean test pass) and high after failures or ambiguity. Varies per turn, unlike a global effort sweep (#160). Reportedly, changing the budget invalidates cached messages, so measure that cost.
test: Size the prize with residual thinking per result class from the ledger, then A/B capped budgets on 10 golden tasks for pass rate, output tokens and cache_creation.
because: Anthropic extended-thinking budget parameter

title: Audit fixed per-call overhead: Bash description, long MCP names
detail: Every call emits optional UI-only args and a full tool name that stay in history. Locally 294 Bash descriptions cost 2,246 o200k tokens (about 7.6 each); tool names 736 over 383 calls. Test dropping descriptions and shortening .mcp.json server keys (mcp__gh__ not mcp__github__).
test: Tokenise name plus optional args per tool_use across transcripts; A/B a CLAUDE.md line omitting Bash description on 10 tasks for compliance and UI or permission-rule breakage.
because: Claude Code Bash description arg and .mcp.json keys

title: Replace whole-list TodoWrite rewrites with per-item task updates
detail: TodoWrite reportedly re-sends the full list on each status change, so output tokens grow with list length times updates, and every copy stays in history. Deny it where TaskCreate/TaskUpdate-style per-item tools exist, or steer to changing one item.
test: Verify that per-item task tools are visible to the agent; count TodoWrite calls, items per call and input tokens in transcripts; compute tokens if only the changed item were sent.
because: Claude Code TodoWrite tool, deny via hook

title: Append commit attribution trailers via git hook, not model output
detail: The model emits Co-Authored-By and session-link lines in each commit message and PR body, and the instruction text sits in context. A prepare-commit-msg hook using git interpret-trailers adds them; clearing the attribution setting (reportedly exists) removes both costs.
test: Verify that the attribution setting can be cleared; count trailer tokens in transcript commits; install the hook, make three commits, check trailers appear once and the model stops emitting them.
because: harness attribution setting and git hook

title: Expand PR body placeholder from commit log in a hook
detail: PreToolUse on gh pr create and MCP create_pull_request replaces a model-written body of '@auto' with commit subjects, diff stat and file list, after any template. The model writes only title plus one line of why, skipping text duplicated from commit messages.
test: Measure body tokens and overlap with commit subjects in recorded PR creations; verify updatedInput works for Bash and MCP tools; have a reviewer rate generated versus written bodies.
because: PreToolUse updatedInput expansion

title: Deny third identical Edit pair; steer to sed or codemod
detail: Renames and import fixes make the model emit the same old_string/new_string file after file, each a full tool call plus echo. PreToolUse counts identical pairs per session and hints rg -l | xargs sed -i, ast-grep or comby instead.
test: Scan Edit and MultiEdit calls in transcripts for repeated (old,new) pairs across files; total tokens versus one command; try the deny wording on a 12-file rename.
because: PreToolUse deny and steering

title: Measure output copy-tax: written lines already seen verbatim
detail: Write, Edit, Agent prompts and heredocs often retype text the model read earlier: code moves, extractions, pasted context for subagents. Count output tokens whose lines match prior tool_results; if large, steer to sed -n ranges, git mv and path references instead.
test: For each Write, Edit, Agent and heredoc input, find the fraction of lines over 25 chars present verbatim in earlier tool_results; report tokens by tool, split move versus new code.
because: measures output copy-tax against prior results

title: Line-range edit tool with content-hash guard, no old_string
detail: An MCP replace_lines(path, start, end, sha, new) drops old_string from every edit; the sha of the range, taken at the last Read, rejects stale edits. Anchors currently cost output tokens on every Edit; some other harnesses use line- or hash-addressed edit formats.
test: Measure old_string share of Edit input tokens in transcripts; count stale-range rejects when files changed between Read and Edit; 20 edit tasks comparing success rate and output tokens.
because: new MCP edit tool cuts output tokens
check: replace_lines(path, start, end, sha, new) applies the same non-overlapping edits (12 of 20 drawn) as old_string/new_string to real files and cuts the edit input tokens by 38% (old_string was over a third of it); the sha covers the range plus one context line each side, so a changed range or a shift above is rejected with the current text and the new position, a far-away change is not, strict file_sha mode catches shifts inside runs of identical lines, and CRLF, a missing final newline, deletion, unicode, permissions, binary files and path escapes are handled.

title: Compress aged assistant narration in request history
detail: A proxy runs the classifier over assistant text blocks older than N turns (narration, plans, recaps), which are re-read every turn. Thinking blocks are signed and left alone. Memoize rewrites and batch them at cold gaps so cached bytes stay stable.
test: Sum tokens of assistant text blocks older than 10 turns in long interactive transcripts; replay compressed history and ask 10 recall questions about earlier decisions versus uncompressed.
because: proxy compresses aged assistant text, memoized

title: Bash replay token: !N re-runs an earlier command verbatim
detail: Edit-test loops make the model retype long commands (cd, flags, pipes to tail). PreToolUse expands '!3' or '!!' to the nth earlier Bash command of the session via updatedInput, so only a few tokens are emitted and the permission prompt shows the full text.
test: Verify that updatedInput expansion works and see what the transcript stores; count Bash commands over 40 tokens repeating an earlier one; A/B whether the model uses the token.
because: PreToolUse updatedInput command expansion

title: Mine recurring command lines into short project aliases
detail: Cluster Bash inputs by normalised prefix across sessions; long recurring test, build and lint invocations, and retyped python heredoc scripts, become Makefile or justfile targets with quiet flags, named in one CLAUDE.md line. Saves output and history tokens each call.
test: Tokenise the top 20 clusters in transcripts, compute tokens saved per call by the alias minus the listing cost, report calls to break even; check the model picks the alias.
because: cross-session logs and CLAUDE.md alias line

title: Register serve as an HTTP hook, skipping Python spawn
detail: Claude Code reportedly supports hook handlers of type http that POST the event JSON to a URL. Add POST /hook to ctxprune serve running hook.run on the warm model: no process spawn, no second hop, no hook.sh or uvx. Server down fails open.
test: Verify that settings accept type http; time 50 small events and one 20k-char event via command hook versus http; stop the server and assert Claude gets the original output.
because: Claude Code http hook handler type

title: Ship a pre-optimised ORT graph to cut session creation
detail: The repo's ~2 s cold start is likely InferenceSession building (graph fusion plus a 143 MB read), since onnxruntime import is ~100 ms here. Save the optimised graph (optimized_model_filepath, or .ort) at install and load it with optimisation off.
test: Time phases (import, tokenizer, session creation) cold and warm; compare stock, ORT_DISABLE_ALL on the saved graph, and .ort; assert keep-decisions agree on 200 windows within int8 noise.
because: local ORT graph cache cuts cold start

title: Trim the embedding vocabulary to tokens seen in tool output
detail: mmBERT-small reportedly spends most of its 140M parameters on a ~256k-token embedding table (unverified). Drop rows unseen on a tool-output plus multilingual sample and remap tokenizer ids, as in 'Load What You Need' (Abdaoui et al. 2020) for mBERT. Smaller download, load, RSS.
test: Verify that the embedding table dominates parameters; count token ids hit over 1k real outputs; trim; report file size, load time, ROC-AUC and keep-decision agreement, including non-English logs.
because: trims local model embedding vocabulary

title: Do embedding lookup from np.memmap, feed ONNX inputs_embeds
detail: Export the transformer body without the Gather over the embedding table; look up only the rows each window needs from a memory-mapped array and pass inputs_embeds. Resident memory and session load shrink, no vocabulary or accuracy change. Keeps non-English intact, unlike vocab trimming.
test: Export with inputs_embeds, compare logits to the stock graph on 200 windows, and measure RSS and cold load time with a cold versus warm page cache.
because: memmap embedding lookup, local model

title: Pick int8 or fp32 per CPU with a first-run benchmark
detail: Int8 is assumed faster everywhere, but dynamic-int8 speed reportedly depends on VNNI or dot-product instructions, and users span Apple silicon, aarch64 and older x86. If int8 loses on some CPUs, a one-window timing at install can choose the file.
test: Per-window latency of int8 versus fp32 on AVX2-only x86, AVX512-VNNI, Apple M-series and aarch64 Linux; if int8 ever loses, gate the 563 MB fp32 download behind it.
because: local CPU benchmark picks model file

title: Sweep ONNX threads, spinning, arena and batch size defaults
detail: compress.py sets only the log level, so threads, spin-waiting, memory arena, batch 16 and dynamic widths are all defaults. Parallel hooks or an idle serve may steal CPU from the build just run. Try intra_op 2-4, allow_spinning=0, arena off, batch 1-4.
test: On 4 cores, time 100 windows per setting, plus serve idle CPU over 10 min and latency with 3 concurrent hooks; pick the Pareto setting.
because: ONNX runtime setting benchmark sweep

title: Self-spawn a detached serve on first large output
detail: The first over-threshold call pays the model load, so let it also fork a detached server (lock-file single-flight, port probe) that exits after N idle minutes. Sessions with no large outputs pay nothing; parallel first calls stop loading 143 MB each.
test: Fire 4 parallel large events with no server running; count model loads and peak RSS, then check later calls hit the daemon and it exits after the idle timeout.
because: self-spawned local daemon, no harness feature
check: One detached serve is spawned on the first over-threshold call under an flock the daemon inherits (4 concurrent first calls: 1 spawn, 1 model load, identical output for every caller), later calls reuse it, it exits when idle, and a failed spawn, crashing daemon, foreign port owner, disabled or remote server or crashed spawner all fall back to in-process compression with no stuck lock or spawn storm.

title: Line-aligned content-defined windows plus on-disk score cache
detail: Windows cut every ~510 tokens, so one inserted early line shifts and rescores every later window. Cut at newlines chosen by a rolling hash (content-defined chunking) and cache per-window keep-probabilities on disk by token-id hash, usable without serve.
test: Score two runs of one log differing by a line near the start; compare per-line score drift and cache hit rate, fixed versus content-defined cuts; check QA parity.
because: content-defined windows with local score cache

title: Skip model calls on windows holding only protected atoms
detail: The hook passes force_protected=True, so numbers, IDs and paths are kept whatever their score. Windows made only of such atoms (hex dumps, numeric tables) cannot change the output, yet are still scored. Skip them, still counting their chars against the budget; latency drops.
test: Count windows with zero unprotected atoms over a captured corpus, then assert byte-identical output with and without the skip and record the time saved.
because: skips scoring windows of protected atoms
check: Windows whose atoms are all forced (force_protected / keep_structure) are not scored, and compress() output, kept count and total are byte-identical to scoring them for every rate, threshold, unit and measure mode; a window with any unprotected atom is always scored.

title: Differential fuzz of the inference stack, not just rules
detail: Check _RawTokenizer offsets against the transformers tokenizer and int8 against torch on hostile inputs: lone surrogates (saved originals use surrogatepass), NUL, CRLF, ZWJ emoji, a 300k-char one-line minified JSON, empty text. Any exception makes the hook fail open silently, forfeiting the saving.
test: Generate 500 fuzz strings; run hook.run in process, logging exceptions by class; compare token ids and offsets across both tokenizers; list input classes that never compress.
because: differential fuzz of inference stack

title: Ship model weights in a PyPI wheel for locked-down sandboxes
detail: Cloud sandboxes reportedly allow package managers but may block huggingface.co, so the first-use download fails and the hook silently never compresses. A companion wheel with int8 weights avoids it; PyPI's default 100 MB file limit means trimming or splitting.
test: Verify that huggingface.co is blocked in a Limited-network cloud session; time install plus first large-output hook; build a split wheel and confirm load without any Hugging Face call.
because: packaging: ship weights in wheel

title: Streaming filter mode with a running score quantile
detail: The CLI reads all stdin before scoring, so a piped docker logs -f or long build shows nothing and holds everything in memory. Score each window as it fills and cut at a running quantile of earlier scores, approximating global top-k.
test: On 20 saved logs, compare streaming kept-atom overlap with global top-k at rate 0.5 and the achieved-rate error; pipe a 500 MB file and track peak memory.
because: streaming filter with running score quantile

title: Shape-preserving pseudonymizer for private training and eval corpora
detail: Replace secrets, UUIDs, hashes, IPs, emails, usernames and paths with random strings of the same class and length, consistent per document. Typed placeholders skew measurement: on synthetic logs (tiktoken cl100k) they cut tokens 54% and zlib size 98%; same-shape fill moved tokens under 1%.
test: Scrub 200 real outputs both ways; compare count_tokens, zlib ratio and classifier keep-probabilities against raw; accept the scrubber only if drift stays under 2%.
because: corpus pseudonymization for evals

title: k-anonymous line-template export for reviewable cross-user sharing
detail: Mask variable fields Drain-style, then export only templates seen in at least k distinct sessions or repos, with counts and token mass, filtered against a public-vocabulary allowlist. The user reviews the file before posting it in an issue. Feeds pack discovery without raw text.
test: Run on 20 local sessions with k=3; grep the export for home paths, repo names and planted canary secrets; count how many top-50 token-mass templates survive.
because: privacy tooling for sharing templates

title: Content-free deletion-class counters per command family
detail: Hook increments counters of kept and dropped atoms by class (digit, path, URL, identifier, stopword, negator, punctuation) per command family; no text stored. Shows what the model systematically deletes on real traffic, safe to paste in a bug report.
test: Run in shadow mode for a week; compare each class's drop rate per family with the training-corpus mix; flag classes dropped far more often than in training.
because: content-free deletion counters for measurement

title: Stratified reservoir sampler with per-family quotas for local corpus
detail: Raw shadow logs would grow unbounded and skew toward frequent commands. Keep a fixed byte cap using weighted reservoir sampling keyed by command family, favoring rare families and evicting oldest-within-family, so the private corpus stays small and covers the long tail.
test: Replay transcript tool results through the sampler at a 5 MB cap; compare family and format coverage against FIFO and uniform sampling at the same cap.
because: corpus sampling tooling

title: Drift monitor: local template histogram versus shipped golden corpus
detail: Weekly, compare the user's command-family and line-template histograms, plus mean keep-probability entropy, against the shipped golden corpus using Jensen-Shannon divergence. A high score means the model and noise rules are stale for this user, so raise the pass-through threshold or flag relabeling.
test: Compute divergence per week for 10 transcript sets; check whether high-divergence weeks show lower rule fire rates or more regret-log refetches.
because: drift measurement against golden corpus

title: Cost-weighted eval: weight items by tokens times surviving turns
detail: QA accuracy averages items equally, but the bill does not. Weight each source and size bucket by its transcript token-bill share (tool-result tokens times turns survived, cache-priced) and report the weighted headline plus the best keep rate under those weights.
test: Reweight the cached per-source eval_qa results by shares from the transcript ledger; check whether headline accuracy and the best keep rate change versus the unweighted mean.
because: cost-weighted eval methodology

title: Forward-chaining holdout for rules mined from private logs
detail: Pack discovery would fit rules on the same sessions that score them. Mine on the earliest weeks or repos A, freeze, then score on later weeks or repos B; report savings and false-fire decay. Guards against rules that only fit one project.
test: Split transcripts by month and by repo; mine templates on the early split; compare token savings and rule fire rates on early versus late holdout.
because: holdout methodology for mined rules

title: Near-duplicate clusters before splitting private corpus rows
detail: Public sources split by group, but private sessions repeat: reruns, forks, vendored dependencies and shared CI templates put near-identical outputs on both sides. MinHash-cluster rows first, split by cluster, and weight clusters once so reruns do not dominate training.
test: On 1,000 captured outputs, report the share of test rows with a Jaccard-0.8 neighbor in train under group versus cluster splits; compare AUC on full versus de-leaked test.
because: corpus split hygiene

title: Default-deny corpus admission with per-row provenance
detail: Corpus builder admits a repo only with an opt-in marker file and a license file, after a secret/entropy scan; rejects everything else. Each row records ctxprune version, pre-pass and rule versions, and a salted content hash, so results are reproducible without sharing text.
test: Dry-run over ~/.claude/projects; list admitted and rejected repos with reasons; assert rejected repos contribute zero bytes and manifests contain no raw text.
because: corpus admission and provenance tooling

title: Canary exposure test for classifiers tuned on private logs
detail: Plant random secret-like canaries in fine-tuning chunks (exposure metric from Carlini et al., 'The Secret Sharer', 2019). Check whether seen canaries get higher keep-probability than fresh same-shape strings. A keep/drop head may leak little; measure before releasing weights.
test: Fine-tune on a corpus with 100 canaries repeated 1, 10 and 100 times; compare keep-probability distributions for seen versus 100 unseen canaries by AUC.
because: canary exposure test for tuned classifier

title: No-egress CI test backing the no-telemetry claim
detail: AGENTS.md promises nothing leaves the machine. Run hook, serve, CLI and future analytics scripts, model pre-cached, under a network namespace or strace connect trace; fail on any non-loopback connection. The torch path's from_pretrained may query the Hub.
test: Run under `unshare -n` with the model cached; time 50 hook calls; assert exit 0, compressed output present, and zero connect() calls beyond 127.0.0.1.
because: no-egress CI test

title: Shorten GitHub URLs to org/repo#N and sha7 shorthand
detail: Release notes, issue bodies, gh pr checks and git merge text repeat https://github.com/org/repo/pull/N and /actions/runs/ID/job/ID. Rewrite to #N, org/repo#N or id pairs plus one legend line naming the base repo. Synthetic 10 release-note lines: 250 to 130 o200k tokens.
test: Run the rewrite on 20 release bodies, gh pr checks tables and issue threads; assert regex round-trip restores every URL; ask which PR fixed X versus raw.
because: URL shorthand with legend, deterministic
check: github.com/<org>/<repo>/{pull,issues,commit,actions/runs,releases/tag,compare}/ prefixes of repeated repos become §<id><kind> with a one-line legend naming the repos; numbers, run/job ids and full shas stay verbatim and decode restores the input byte for byte.

title: Steer Actions log fetches to failed-only and tailed
detail: Rewrite gh run view --log to --log-failed; add failed_only or tail_lines to GitHub MCP get_job_logs calls (parameters reportedly exist). Green-job logs are never fetched, so the hook skips multi-megabyte inputs and nothing dilutes the failing step.
test: Verify that get_job_logs accepts failed_only; on 10 failed runs compare bytes of --log and --log-failed; check the root-cause line survives and count agent requests for the full log.
because: rewrites log-fetch command and MCP params

title: Fold identical failures across CI matrix legs
detail: gh run view --log prefixes lines with job names, so a 6-leg matrix prints the same traceback and setup six times. After normalising timestamps and paths, print identical blocks once with 'also in: leg names'; legs with different failures stay in full.
test: Pull a failed run with a 6-leg matrix via gh; fold; assert every distinct failing test name survives and each leg is listed; compare tokens against raw.
because: fold identical CI matrix failures
check: A step block that is identical in an earlier leg after normalising timestamps, the leg's own name, hosted-toolcache paths, interpreter versions and pytest durations is printed once with '~ also in: leg; leg'; blocks that differ in any other way (a different assertion value, a different test) stay in full; every leg, every distinct failing test and every failure message is still present.
check_loses: the exact timestamps, interpreter versions, paths and durations of the folded legs' blocks, and the order of a leg's steps once some of them live in an earlier leg's block

title: Keep only each bot's latest comment in PR threads
detail: Some bots (coverage, preview deploys, review summaries) post a fresh comment on each push, and walkthrough comments carry details blocks and mermaid diagrams. For user.type Bot or [bot] logins keep only each login's newest comment, with details and diagrams stripped; save the rest.
test: Fetch comments for 20 PRs with active bots via MCP; measure bot share of tokens; fold; ask 'is coverage dropping, what do humans still need to change' versus raw.
because: keeps newest bot comment within one result

title: Fold resolved and outdated review threads; one diff_hunk per thread
detail: Review-comment JSON repeats the same diff_hunk on every reply in a thread. Use isResolved and isOutdated (GraphQL reviewThreads, reportedly also in MCP review output) to reduce closed threads to path:line, first comment and a count; print each hunk once for open ones.
test: Pull review comments for 10 PRs with long threads; measure token share of resolved threads and duplicate hunks; ask which feedback remains unaddressed, folded versus raw.
because: fold resolved threads from payload flags

title: Fold long details blocks in issue and PR markdown
detail: Reporters wrap env dumps, pip freeze and full logs in <details><summary>; the author already marked them as secondary. Keep summary plus first and last 5 lines when the block exceeds 40 lines, with a line count; the original stays in the saved file.
test: Sample 50 bug issues containing details; measure their token share; fold; ask for root cause and versions, and count cases where the answer lived in the folded middle.
because: fold long details blocks

title: Apply JSON rules to get_file_contents directory listings
detail: VERBATIM_MCP matches get_file|file_contents, so a GitHub directory listing is exempt like source text. Its entries reportedly carry url, git_url, html_url, download_url and _links per file. Detect the listing shape (array of {type: file|dir}) and keep name, type, size, path.
test: Call get_file_contents on 5 repo directories; check the hook skips them; apply the field strip and compare tokens; confirm file reads of real files still pass verbatim.
because: JSON listing rules on MCP tool result

title: Drop the text block that duplicates structuredContent
detail: The MCP spec says a tool returning structuredContent should also put the serialized JSON in a text block for old clients. If the host forwards both to the model, the payload is paid twice. Drop the text block when it parses to the same value.
test: Verify that both forms reach the model: build a FastMCP tool with an output schema, dump the PostToolUse tool_response, check the transcript, and count duplicated tokens.
because: MCP result transform dropping duplicate text block
check: When a tool result's structuredContent is an object and a plain text block parses (strictly: no duplicate keys, true/1/1.0 kept distinct) to the same value, that block is dropped; any differing value, annotated block, other block, error result or non-JSON text stays. Valid only if the host forwards structuredContent to the model.
check_loses: formatting and key order of the dropped text block; the model must receive structuredContent for nothing to be lost, which the idea's own test has to confirm for each host

title: Drop MCP content blocks annotated audience user-only
detail: MCP content blocks can carry annotations with audience [user] or priority. A wrapper or hook can drop blocks the server addressed only to the user, or low-priority blocks past a budget, before the model reads them. Spec-defined, so it needs no learned judgement.
test: Verify that Claude Code forwards user-only blocks: write a toy server returning audience [user] and [assistant] blocks; if it does, count tokens a drop rule saves on real servers.
because: MCP spec annotations drive block dropping

title: One ci_failure MCP tool replacing four serial gh calls
detail: Wrap gh api calls: find the failing check, job and step from steps[].conclusion, fetch only that step's log, append annotations and the matrix legs affected. One call returns root-cause lines as a compact digest instead of checks, view, log and grep turns.
test: Replay 10 CI-failure tasks; compare turns and billed tokens for the agent using raw gh versus the tool; check the digest names the same root cause as the full log.
because: new MCP tool collapsing serial gh calls
check: One ci_failure call finds the failing check, job and step from steps[].conclusion, reads only that step's log slice, appends annotations and groups identical matrix legs, returning a digest under 5% of the tokens of checks, run view, failed logs and grep; every FAILED, E and ##[error] line of each full failing log (found by an independent scan) is in the digest, and green, in-progress, expired-log, infrastructure-failure, misaligned-log, rate-limited and multi-cause runs are each reported truthfully.

title: Inject git quiet config through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT env vars
detail: Git 2.31+ reads config from env without touching ~/.gitconfig. Setting advice.statusHints=false, status.short and status.branch took a two-file git status from 349 to 20 characters here. Such outputs sit far below the 6,000-char threshold, so only source-side config helps.
test: Set the vars in Claude Code settings env; run status, checkout, rejected push, merge conflict, detached HEAD; compare bytes; check whether agents misread short status codes.
because: GIT_CONFIG env prefix on commands
check: Before a git command the hook exports GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE for advice.statusHints=false, status.short and status.branch, skipping every key the user already configured (an env override beats repo and global config) and doing nothing when the user already uses GIT_CONFIG_*; on a real repository the short status carries the same path-to-state map as the long one, but not the detached-HEAD commit id or the 'unmerged paths' notice.

title: Free ground truth for CI log packs from Actions API
detail: Job JSON lists steps[].conclusion and check-run annotations carry the error messages, so 'which step failed and why' has an answer key without an LLM judge. Build a corpus from public failed runs and score fold rules by whether those lines survive.
test: Fetch 30 failed runs with gh api; store jobs JSON, annotations and log; script a survival check of annotation text and failing step name after each rule.
because: free ground-truth corpus from Actions API

title: Project-scope install: repo-root file and portable guarded command
detail: install --scope project|local writes under Path.cwd(), so running from a subdirectory creates a dead .claude/ there. _hook_command also bakes the absolute venv path into a committable file, which fails on teammates' machines. Emit a command -v guard and use the git root.
test: Run install --scope project from a subdirectory of a temp git repo; copy the settings file to a clean container without ctxprune; replay one event; expect exit 0, no stderr.
because: settings.json hook install scope

title: ctxprune doctor: synthetic hook event, heartbeat, effective config
detail: The hook exits 0 silently when huggingface_hub is missing, and CTXPRUNE_DEBUG is off by default. A doctor command pipes a synthetic event through the installed settings.json command, checks model cache, serve and env, and reports last-fired heartbeat age.
test: Break one thing at a time (rename exe, uninstall huggingface_hub, set CTXPRUNE_MIN_CHARS=6k, delete model cache); doctor must flag each.
because: settings.json hook command and heartbeat

title: Defensive env parsing: clamp rate, accept 6k and 50%
detail: CTXPRUNE_MIN_CHARS=6k makes int() raise and the outer except disables every compression, silently. CTXPRUNE_RATE is unvalidated (50 keeps everything, 0 keeps only protected atoms), unlike the CLI's (0,1] check. Parse each var alone, clamp, fall back to defaults, warn once.
test: Feed bad values (6k, 6,000, 50, 50%, 0, -1, abc) through the hook on an 8k-char event; assert sane config or default plus one visible warning.
because: robust ctxprune's own env parsing

title: Per-call config file and named profiles instead of env-only
detail: Env vars are frozen when Claude Code starts, so rate and threshold cannot change mid-session or per repo. Read ~/.config/ctxprune.toml plus repo .ctxprune.toml on each call; ship lean, balanced and safe profiles, with measured savings and QA loss printed at install.
test: Edit the file between two calls in one headless session and confirm the second call uses the new rate; time the extra file read.
because: ctxprune's own config file and profiles

title: Lossless-only tier from 1k chars: no note, no saved file
detail: run() gates everything at 6000 chars and rejects results above 0.95, which suits lossy deletion. Byte-exact transforms (ANSI, CR, blank runs, duplicate lines) risk nothing, so apply them from about 1,000 chars, accept any gain, and omit the roughly 80-token note and disk write.
test: From transcripts, bucket Bash/MCP results of 1k-6k chars; run the lossless rules; sum tokens saved with zero note cost; compare against current gating on the same bucket.
because: lossless-only tier at lower size threshold
check: Below the 6,000-char lossy threshold, outputs of 1,000+ chars get ANSI styling stripped, CR progress frames collapsed, blank-line runs squeezed and repeated lines marked '[previous line repeated N more times]' (the only byte-exact step: dup_expand restores it, and it steps aside when the text already holds a marker); the response has no note and no saved file, any strict gain ships, verbatim commands/Read/CTXPRUNE_OFF/small/no-gain outputs are untouched. Only the duplicate step is byte-exact; colours, progress frames and blank counts are dropped by design and cannot be recovered without a saved file.

title: In-process Claude Agent SDK PostToolUse callback using ctxprune
detail: Orchestrator and workflow runs built on the Claude Agent SDK may not load settings.json hooks (reportedly SDK settings sources are opt-in). Ship integrations.claude_agent_sdk_hooks(): a callback in the long-lived process, model loaded once, returning updatedToolOutput with the same note and saved original.
test: Verify that SDK PostToolUse callbacks can return updatedToolOutput; run one SDK query whose Bash prints 20k chars and inspect the transcript tool_result for compressed text and the note.
because: Claude Agent SDK hook callback

title: Keep separator punctuation between protected atoms: 1,299 and 80,443
detail: is_protected(',') is false, so when the model drops a comma, detok leaves a space (simulated: 1,299.00 gives '1 299.00', 80,443,8080 gives '80 443 8080', 3,14 gives '3 14'). The README says numbers are kept exactly. Force-keep zero-whitespace punctuation flanked by protected atoms.
test: Count digit-comma-digit and key=value spans in saved originals; run the model; count spans split in output; add the rule and compare tokens at equal QA.
because: keeps separator punctuation between protected atoms

title: Docs-as-tests: executable checks for README and AGENTS claims
detail: Claims can drift: README says plugin download ~180 MB, install prints 143 MB; ~2 s load, ~50 ms no-op and 'seq 1 3000 left alone' have no test. prune(), CLI and integrations default protect=False despite the 'without mangling IDs' headline.
test: Put each claim in claims.toml with a command and tolerance; run in CI on a fresh venv and HF cache; fail on drift; test prune() defaults on an ID-heavy log.
because: executable tests for documented claims

title: Size-dependent keep rate instead of a constant 0.5
detail: Hook applies rate 0.5 to a 6k-char and a 30k-char output alike, but redundancy plausibly grows with length. Try target = max(floor, rate * N^0.8) or an absolute cap near 2k tokens per call; the rate parameter is already per call, so no retraining.
test: Bucket saved originals or corpus chunks by size; at equal total kept tokens compare reader QA for constant rate versus sublinear budget; report accuracy per kept token.
because: keep rate depends on output size

title: Send Accept: text/markdown on curl of docs pages
detail: Cloudflare's Markdown for Agents converts HTML at the origin when asked via Accept: text/markdown, and sends x-markdown-tokens; its blog example went 16,180 to 3,150 tokens (Cloudflare's figure). PreToolUse adds the header to curl/wget of docs URLs; fall back to .md or llms.txt.
test: Verify that sites honor the header: curl 20 docs pages with and without it; compare o200k tokens and x-markdown-tokens; check code blocks and tables survive.
because: adds Accept header to curl command

title: Show lint and typecheck findings only in git-diff-touched files
detail: Reviewdog's filter modes and diff-quality reportedly report only findings on added lines. For ruff, mypy, tsc, eslint keep findings in files git diff touched, plus a count and first three of the rest. Needs no earlier run, unlike #141 and #142.
test: Repo with 200 old findings; edit 3 files, one breaking a caller elsewhere; compare output size and confirm the cross-file break still appears in the outside-diff summary.
because: touched-file set derivable from earlier edit calls
check: Replaces the git diff section by a one-line list of touched files and, per lint/typecheck section, keeps every finding in a touched file, then states how many findings lie outside the diff (with the first three) and lists every outside finding whose message names a def/class the diff added or removed (the cross-file breaks); summary lines are unchanged.
check_loses: the diff text itself, the line-by-line detail of old findings outside the diff beyond the first three, and linked findings are matched by name only (a break that does not mention the changed name is shown only if it is among the first three)

title: Inject fail-fast limits into test runner commands
detail: pytest --maxfail=N, jest --bail and go test -failfast stop at the first failures, so a broken suite prints 3 failures, not 300. Unlike quiet flags (#76) this shortens the run itself; the note says how to rerun without the limit.
test: Break 30 tests in a sample repo; run default versus fail-fast; compare output tokens, wall time, and extra turns the agent needs to fix everything.
because: appends fail-fast flags to test commands

title: Turn off built-in git instructions, bundled skills and attachments
detail: Binary strings reportedly show settings includeGitInstructions and disableBundledSkills, and env CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_GIT_INSTRUCTIONS, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ATTACHMENTS (what attachments removes is unverified). They drop built-in commit/PR text and skill listings from every turn. Set for subagents and no-commit sessions.
test: Verify that each flag exists: run claude -p with and without each, output json; diff input and cache-creation tokens; confirm git commit via Bash and @-mentions still work.
because: harness settings and env vars

title: Probe: does a partial Read satisfy Edit's read-first check
detail: Binary text refuses a Write after a start-only Read and advises Edit, hinting offset/limit Reads count for Edit. If so, capped Reads (#400) cannot trigger 'File has not been read yet' retries; if not, each cap risks a wasted turn.
test: In a scratch repo Read lines 1-20 of a 500-line file, then Edit text at line 300 and at line 10; record success and error text.
because: probes Claude Code Edit read-first check

title: Render giant read-only logs as PNG; compare image tokens
detail: DeepSeek-OCR and Zhipu's Glyph reportedly pass rendered text to vision models at several-fold fewer tokens. Anthropic documents image cost near width*height/750 after resize. Render 20 KB logs in monospace within 1568 px, Read the PNG, and check exact-value lookup accuracy.
test: Render 5 logs at 3 font sizes; Read each PNG, compare input tokens with the text version, ask 10 exact-value questions (IDs, line numbers) and score errors.
because: depends on vendor image-token costs and vision reading

title: Gateway MCP exposing list, describe, invoke instead of N schemas
detail: mcp-compressor reportedly proxies any MCP server, swapping the upfront tool dump for a compact tool list with schemas fetched on demand. Aimed at hosts without deferred tool loading, where #250's ToolSearch route does not apply.
test: Wrap the GitHub MCP (about 50 tools); count tool-block tokens before and after; run 10 tasks for success rate and extra describe calls.
because: MCP gateway with on-demand schemas
check: A gateway exposing list_tools, describe_tool and invoke replaces 48 tool schemas by 3 plus a one-line-per-tool list; every non-blocked call returns exactly what the direct call returns, unknown names, wrong types and missing arguments return errors that name the fix, upstream failures are forwarded, and per-tool deny rules have to move into the gateway because the host only sees 'invoke'.

title: Head-to-head versus rtk, Headroom and similar agent-side compressors
detail: Item #388 covers RAG compressors only. Agent-side tools differ: rtk rewrites commands per tool, Headroom routes by content type with retrieval, other hook-based trimmers cut JSON and logs. Run each on one recorded Bash/MCP corpus at equal output tokens, scoring reader accuracy.
test: Replay 100 recorded outputs through each tool's filters; match output tokens; ask 5 questions per output; report accuracy, savings and winners by command family.
because: head-to-head benchmark against other compressors

title: Drop repeated 'Shell cwd was reset' Bash trailers
detail: Claude Code binary builds 'Shell cwd was reset to <dir>' notes for Bash after a command leaves the project directory. Repeats of the same note add nothing after the first. Trim them in PostToolUse on small outputs, if the model actually sees them.
test: Verify that the note reaches model-visible text: grep transcripts for 'Shell cwd was reset' inside tool_result; count per session times tokens; drop the idea if it never appears.
because: targets Claude Code's own cwd-reset trailer string

title: Strip comments and blank lines from exploratory source dumps
detail: rtk reportedly filters comments and whitespace; repomix offers --remove-comments. Opt-in for cat of source when no edit follows, with a note 'comments stripped; Read before Edit'. Exact-match Edit would otherwise fail on stripped lines; license headers (#327) are a subset.
test: Measure comment+blank token share in 50 cat/Read results of source from transcripts; replay 20 Edit calls against stripped text and count old_string mismatches.
because: deterministic comment stripping of source output

title: lsof: fold per-thread duplicate rows or inject -Ki
detail: Linux lsof repeats each process's fds once per thread, differing only in TID and TASKCMD. Measured here: 507 of 1,285 rows were repeats, about 22k of 49k o200k tokens. Fold into 'x N threads' rows, or rewrite to lsof -Ki.
test: Run lsof on a multithreaded server (java, node) raw, folded and with -Ki; compare tokens; confirm the same files, ports and PIDs remain visible.
because: fold lsof per-thread duplicate rows
check: lsof -K style output (COMMAND PID TID TASKCMD ...): rows identical from the USER column on across a process's threads fold into one row whose TID cell reads 'xN', and one '# threads PID [[tid,name],...]' line per pid keeps the thread list; every distinct file, port and pid with the number of task rows it stood for, and every (tid, name), are unchanged.
check_loses: the order in which the per-thread rows were printed, and which thread's row was the representative (all are identical by construction)

title: strace: collapse loader preamble, join unfinished/resumed pairs
detail: In strace -f ls /tmp, 3,050 of 3,436 o200k tokens preceded the first write: execve, ld.so, libc, locale, mmap, mprotect. Collapse successful startup syscalls to one line; keep failures (= -1 E...), connects, non-library opens, signals, exit. Join <unfinished>/<resumed> pairs.
test: Run strace -f on ls, python -c 'import json' and curl; compare tokens; assert every ENOENT/EACCES line, connect and exit_group survives.
because: collapses strace loader preamble text
check: Joins <unfinished ...>/<... resumed> pairs into one call at the resumed position and replaces each process's run of successful loader syscalls (mmap, mprotect, brk, library openat/read/fstat/close, rseq, ...) between its execve and its first other call by one '[ctxprune: N startup syscalls ok (...); libraries: ...]' line; every failed call, socket/connect/bind, non-library open, write, fork/exec/wait, signal and exit marker is unchanged.
check_loses: the arguments and addresses of the collapsed successful startup calls (including statfs probes and which fds the libraries used), and the position of a blocking call's start relative to other pids' calls (it now appears where it completed)

title: dmesg: fold OOM tables, audit denials, boot-time chatter
detail: Keep Oops, BUG, WARN and error lines verbatim. Cut OOM-killer Mem-Info and task tables to the victim line plus top RSS rows. Fold repeated apparmor/audit DENIED lines to counts per profile, operation and name. Collapse boot runs of ACPI, pci, virtio lines.
test: Capture dmesg from a fresh boot, a cgroup OOM kill and a denied apparmor profile; compare tokens; verify every error/warning line and the killed process name survive.
because: folds dmesg OOM tables and audit lines

title: Coarsen dmesg and journalctl monotonic stamps; elide repeats
detail: dmesg prefixes like '[    0.123456]' cost 3,080 of 10,410 o200k tokens in this VM's 385-line dmesg. Truncate to milliseconds or whole seconds and drop stamps equal to the previous line's. Differs from wall-clock hoisting: the microsecond digits are the cost.
test: Tokenise dmesg and journalctl -o short-monotonic with full, millisecond and elided-repeat stamps; ask 'what happened just before the first error' to confirm ordering still resolves.
because: coarsen dmesg timestamps; text transform

title: systemctl list-units and status: drop legend, fold healthy units
detail: From memory: list-units ends with a LOAD/ACTIVE/SUB legend and lists dozens of healthy .device, .mount, .slice and .scope rows; status prints CGroup trees of full command lines. Drop the legend, fold healthy rows to per-type counts, keep failed and not-found, cap command lines.
test: On a systemd host capture list-units --all, --failed and status of a busy service; compare tokens; check failed and not-found units and the main PID remain.
because: folds healthy systemctl rows

title: nmap: drop verbose duplicates, fold identical-host sweeps
detail: From memory: -v prints 'Discovered open port' lines repeating the final table, Initiating/Completed/Stats progress lines, a data-files path, and 'Service detection performed' and 'Raw packets sent' footers. Drop them; fold hosts with identical port signatures; in -oG drop 'Status: Up' lines.
test: Scan localhost and a /24 lab with nmap -v -sV and -oG; compare tokens; check open-port, version and host-up answers match between raw and folded outputs.
because: drops nmap duplicate verbose lines

title: openssl x509 -text and s_client: digest certificates
detail: x509 -text prints colon-hex modulus, signature and SCT blocks; s_client -showcerts prints full PEM chains, session ticket and Master-Key. Keep subject, issuer, validity, SANs, key and signature algorithm, verify result; replace PEM and hex blocks with SHA-256 fingerprint stubs.
test: Run s_client -showcerts against a public host and x509 -text on its leaf; compare tokens; ask expiry date, SANs and whether verification succeeded on both forms.
because: digests certificates, PEM to fingerprint stubs

title: ps aux: fold kernel threads, hash-cap very long argv
detail: Measured here: 70 of 83 ps aux rows were bracketed kernel threads (kworker, ksoftirqd, rcu_*), about 2,950 of 21,530 o200k tokens. Fold to 'N kernel threads: kworker x30, ...'; cap argv beyond a length with a hash; keep user processes verbatim.
test: Run ps aux and ps -ef on a VM and in a container; compare tokens; ask which PID runs a given script and how many kernel threads exist.
because: folds kernel-thread rows in ps output

title: ss, netstat, conntrack: aggregate socket rows by state and port
detail: From memory: busy hosts list hundreds of ESTAB and TIME-WAIT rows. Keep LISTEN and unusual-state rows verbatim; merge the rest into 'ESTAB :443 <- 10.0.0.0/24 x212 (nginx)'. Merges rows rather than dropping columns (#57), so counts answer load questions directly.
test: Capture ss -tanp and netstat -tan during a local load test (ab, wrk); compare tokens; answer 'who is connected to :8080' and 'how many TIME-WAIT' on both.
because: aggregate socket rows; text transform

title: sysctl -a: fold per-interface and per-CPU key families
detail: Measured here: sysctl -a was 10,650 o200k tokens; net.ipv4.conf.* took 2,930 and neigh.* 1,285, and 30 of 33 conf keys were identical across all six interfaces. Print 'net.ipv4.conf.{all,default,eth0}.key = v' once and list only exceptions.
test: Run sysctl -a on a host with docker bridges and many CPUs; fold; expand back with a script and diff against the original; compare tokens.
because: fold sysctl key families
check: Lines 'P.I.S = v' with the same prefix P, suffix S and value v across 3+ instance names I (interfaces, CPUs) become one 'P.{I1,I2,..}.S = v'; expanding them yields exactly the original multiset of lines.
check_loses: the order of lines: a folded family is listed once, at the position of its first member

title: Replace tree, pstree and perf call-graph rails with indentation
detail: Rails like '├── ', '│   ' and perf report -g's '|--12.3%--' cost tokens at every level. An 8-line tree sample went 55 to 28 o200k tokens using two-space indents. Convert only when depth stays recoverable; also drop perf's leading '#' header block.
test: Run tree, pstree -p, lsblk and perf report -g --stdio on real data; convert; compare tokens; ask parent-of and depth questions on both forms.
because: pure text rewrite of tree rails
check: A run of 3+ `tree` entry lines whose rails are exactly what the depths imply becomes two-space indentation (non-canonical trees stay as they are); in perf call graphs only decoration lines ('#', '# ......', '|') are dropped.
check_loses: the rail glyphs themselves (re-derivable from depth order, including the NBSP padding variant, which must be restored by the reader), and perf's decoration-only lines; perf's Samples/Event-count/column-title header lines are kept on purpose

title: Collapse git ref series in ls-remote, tag, branch, fetch
detail: GitHub remotes advertise refs/pull/N/head and /merge per PR; tag -l, branch -r and fetch '[new branch]' lines can run to hundreds. Print ranges and counts ('refs/pull/1..N head+merge x2N'); keep heads, default branch, newest tags, refs named in the command.
test: Run git ls-remote on a large GitHub repo, git tag -l, and a first git fetch --all; collapse; compare tokens; check the agent still finds a named tag or PR.
because: collapse git ref series
check: git ls-remote output: with 20+ pull refs the refs/pull/N/head and /merge series become 'pull head refs (N): ranges' lines, and with more than 18 versioned tags the older ones become one names-only line; HEAD, every branch, the 10 newest tags with their shas (and peeled shas), tags without digits, every tag name, and the exact set of PR numbers with a head and with a merge ref are unchanged.
check_loses: the shas of all pull refs and of tags older than the 10 newest, and the peeled shas of those tags

title: Minify multi-document or truncated JSON with a lexeme-preserving scanner
detail: jq '.[]' output, concatenated docs and truncated JSON fail json.loads, so parse-based minify skips them. A string-aware scanner strips whitespace outside strings and keeps number text; loads/dumps turns 1E5 into 100000.0 and merges duplicate keys. Ten pretty docs: 680 vs 340 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Run jq '.[]' output and head -c truncated API JSON through it; assert whitespace-stripped input equals output byte for byte; fuzz with 1E5, duplicate keys, 20-digit ints.
because: lexeme-preserving JSON minify
check: Whitespace outside JSON strings is removed from concatenated, `jq '.[]'` or truncated JSON by a string-aware scanner; every string, number (1E5, 20-digit ints), duplicate key and a mid-string cut stay byte-identical, and non-JSON text is returned untouched.
check_loses: indentation and spacing outside strings; a newline run between top-level documents becomes one newline; CRLF becomes LF there

title: Partition mixed-kind JSON arrays by key set, columnar per group
detail: #32 assumes uniform rows, but timelines, CloudTrail, k8s events and Slack history mix shapes. Group rows by key-set signature or discriminator (event, type, kind); emit one columnar table per group of 3+, leave singletons inline. Synthetic 36 events: 1130 vs 670 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Capture gh api issues/N/timeline, aws cloudtrail lookup-events and kubectl get events -o json; encode; assert row-for-row reconstruction; ask per-kind counting questions against minified JSON.
because: partition mixed JSON arrays, columnar
check: A compact JSON array of mixed-shape objects is regrouped by exact key list: groups of 3+ rows become one header plus value rows, singletons stay inline, and an order string restores every row in place byte for byte.

title: Render GraphQL introspection, JSON Schema and CRDs as type signatures
detail: Introspection JSON nests kind/name/ofType wrapper chains (one field: 71 tokens vs 6 as 'issues: [Issue!]!'); CRD schemas repeat type/description blocks (synthetic spec: YAML 108, signature 45). Emit SDL or 'name?: type // desc' lines, drop __ types, resolve $ref once. #248 only strips boilerplate.
test: Fetch introspection JSON from a public GraphQL API; run kubectl explain --recursive and get crd for cert-manager; convert; tokenise; ask required fields and enum values; list dropped keywords.
because: schemas to type signatures
check: GraphQL introspection JSON becomes one block per type (kind, interfaces, union members, 'field: [Issue!]!' lines with deprecation, 'arg name: Type = default' lines, enum values) without __ types, and JSON Schema or CRD openAPIV3Schema becomes 'path*: type' lines with enums, arrays, maps and $ref targets named once; every type, field, argument with its type signature and default, enum value, required flag and enum list is unchanged.
check_loses: all descriptions, deprecation reasons, directives, introspection (__) types, JSON Schema constraints (format beyond the type, minimum, pattern), default values of JSON Schema properties, and JSON whitespace; schemas with whitespace in property names are left unchanged

title: Rewrite NDJSON app logs as logfmt before line rules
detail: pino, zap, slog and bunyan lines carry quotes, braces and repeated keys that hide them from timestamp, template and duplicate-line rules. Emit 'time LEVEL msg k=v' with dotted nested keys, quoting only when needed. Synthetic 20 lines: 1220 vs 759 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Convert pino and zap samples; assert key=value parse returns the original objects; run timestamp, template and duplicate rules on both forms; compare tokens against #130 hoisting alone.
because: NDJSON to logfmt rewrite
check: Compact JSON object lines become logfmt (`key=value`, dotted nested keys, quotes only when needed, string-vs-number types kept) and decode back to the exact original line; lines the decoder cannot reproduce stay JSON.

title: Drop rendered-HTML and epoch twins of fields in records
detail: The same value stored twice in one record: Jira renderedFields HTML beside wiki text, GitHub body_html beside body, RSS content:encoded beside description, epoch beside ISO time. Detect by equality after tag-strip or instant parse; keep the plainer form. Synthetic: 82 vs 31 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Capture Jira issues with expand=renderedFields and a GitHub issue with the full+json media type; measure twin token share; check stripped-HTML similarity finds twins without dropping genuinely different text.
because: drop duplicate twin fields in records

title: Collapse all-zero counter objects such as GitHub reactions
detail: Lone zeros can matter (#33), but an object whose numeric members are all 0 (reactions: +1, -1, laugh, hooray, heart, rocket, eyes, plus url) carries no information. Fold it to {}; lone zero fields stay. One reactions object: 59 vs 5 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Count all-zero reactions objects in captured GitHub list_issues and list_pull_requests output; collapse them; tokenise; confirm non-zero reaction objects stay verbatim.
because: collapse all-zero counter objects

title: Strip indentation whitespace from pretty-printed XML: pom, csproj, manifests
detail: Generic counterpart of JSON minify (#31) for XML read by cat or curl: drop whitespace-only text nodes between elements, never under xml:space=preserve or in mixed content. Synthetic pom dependencies: 696 vs 485 tokens (o200k proxy). #40 covers only reports.
test: Take 20 pom.xml, AndroidManifest.xml, .csproj and SOAP files; strip with lxml remove_blank_text; assert trees equal ignoring blank text; tokenise before and after. Exclude files the agent will Edit.
because: strip XML indentation whitespace
check: Whitespace-only text between sibling elements is dropped from well-formed XML; text nodes with content, mixed content, leaf elements, xml:space="preserve" subtrees, CDATA, comments and PIs keep every byte.
check_loses: indentation and line breaks between elements (element-only content) and whitespace outside the root element

title: Remove unneeded quotes from quote-all CSV output
detail: Exports using QUOTE_ALL, pandas quoting=1 or spreadsheet dumps wrap every field in quotes. Re-emit with minimal quoting (only fields with comma, quote or newline); keep quotes on numeric-looking text. Synthetic 30 rows: 368 vs 336 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Collect quote-all CSVs from pandas quoting=1 and spreadsheet exports; rewrite with csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL; assert csv.reader rows equal before and after; tokenise.
because: minimal CSV quoting
check: Quote-all CSV is re-emitted so only fields that need quotes (comma, quote, line break, edge whitespace, number-like text, a row's only empty field) keep them; csv.reader returns identical rows and line terminators are untouched.
check_loses: the quoted-vs-unquoted distinction, which csv.reader does not expose (including quoted empty strings)

title: Collapse textproto map entries and hoist grpcurl @type URLs
detail: Protobuf text prints each map entry as a key/value message; grpcurl repeats the type.googleapis.com prefix per Any. Fold entries into 'labels: {a: b}' when a repeated field has only key and value; hoist the prefix. 6 entries: 90 vs 28 tokens (o200k).
test: Capture grpcurl responses and a .textproto/.pbtxt file; apply the folds; tokenise; assert expansion restores the entries; ask which map keys exist on both forms.
because: collapse textproto map entries

title: Flow-style YAML for scalar-only block sequences
detail: Lists such as container args, ports and paths cost a newline, indent and dash per item. Rewrite plain-scalar-only sequences as '[a, b, c]' when no item has a colon-space, hash, comma or bracket and no comments interleave. 12 args: 110 vs 87 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Apply to kubectl get -o yaml and docker-compose output; assert yaml.safe_load is equal before and after; tokenise; exclude Read and cat of repo files, since Edit needs exact lines.
because: flow-style YAML sequences
check: Block sequences whose items are all plain scalars become `key: [a, b, c]`; sequences of mappings, quoted or colon-bearing items, comment-interleaved lists, continuation lines and anything inside block scalars are left alone, and the loaded document is unchanged.
check_loses: block layout and per-item line structure of the rewritten sequences

title: Shape-keyed format ladder: cheapest encoding per JSON shape
detail: Measure each rung per shape: pretty, minified, unquoted keys, YAML, dotted paths, TOON-like, TSV. On a nested single object, minified JSON (85 tokens) beat YAML (96) and dotted paths (104); unquoted array keys saved about 3% (o200k proxy). Convert only when a rung wins.
test: Build 5 shapes (flat record, nested object, uniform array, ragged array, deep config) from captured output; count tokens per rung with the count_tokens API; run reader QA per rung.
because: deterministic JSON re-encoding by shape, pluggable counter

title: Seed ledger with CLAUDE.md, @-mentions, prompts and assistant text
detail: Index text the model already holds, not only tool results and own Edits: CLAUDE.md and imports, @-mentioned file attachments, user prompts, assistant messages. A later Read, cat or pasted-trace echo of those bytes becomes 'already in context: source'.
test: Mine transcripts for Reads or cats of files earlier attached via @-mention or quoted in a prompt; sum duplicated tokens per session.
because: index text already in payload, dedupe later echoes
check: A Read or Bash result containing runs of at least 3 lines that equal lines of CLAUDE.md, an @-attachment, a user prompt or an assistant message already in context gets each run replaced by a pointer naming that source and its lines; changed lines stay literal, and after compaction only CLAUDE.md remains a source.

title: Block-until-changed rewrite for repeated status polls
detail: When the model re-issues the same status command (gh run view, kubectl get, sleep then tail), PreToolUse rewrites it to loop until the output hash differs from the stored one, with a timeout. One result per state change replaces N identical polls and turns.
test: Verify that updatedInput rewrites Bash. Find runs of 3+ identical Bash commands in transcripts; replay one against a fake slow job with the wrapper; count turns and tokens saved.
because: command rewrite using stored output hash

title: Rerun only previously failing tests; defer full run
detail: Ledger keeps failed test IDs. A repeated test command is rewritten via updatedInput to pytest --lf, jest --onlyFailures or go test -run names, so passing-test output is never produced. Full suite once at green. Differs from #499 (fail-fast) and #62 (output delta).
test: Fixture repo, 200 tests, 3 failing: run five edit-test loops with and without the rewrite; compare output tokens, turns and regressions missed.
because: rewrites rerun command using ledger of failures

title: Cross-command error stubs keyed on exception signature
detail: The same traceback or compiler error reaches the model via different commands (python x.py, pytest, a node script). Fingerprint type, message and app frames with paths, addresses and line numbers masked; repeats become 'same error as turn 12'. #17 and #126 fold within one output.
test: Mine transcripts for tracebacks sharing type plus message across distinct commands; count repeat tokens; check the model still fixes the error from the stub.
because: error signature stubs across tool results

title: RFC 6902-style delta for re-fetched same-id JSON entities
detail: Polling an issue, PR, pod or job returns the whole object with two fields changed. Key by server, type and id; emit changed paths plus 'N fields unchanged'. #145 only references identical objects; #62 is line-based.
test: Fetch one GitHub issue via gh api before and after a comment; tokenise the full response versus the path delta. Repeat with kubectl get pod -o json across a rollout.
because: delta against earlier fetched entity
check: A re-fetch of the same (server, tool, id) JSON entity is rendered as RFC 6902-style ops plus a count of unchanged fields against the previous state; the model-side rebuild equals the server's object, and different ids, tools, servers, unprofitable patches or a compacted-away base get the full object.

title: Session-seen atom prior: drop-bias for atoms already in context
detail: Add a classifier feature, or post-score demotion, for identifiers, paths and phrases seen in the last K thousand context tokens, since the reader can resolve them. #164 and #200 only look within one output.
test: Offline: measure the share of atoms already present in the previous 20k tokens of recorded sessions; then QA at equal rate with and without demotion.
because: demotes atoms already in earlier context

title: Hoist files every sibling subagent reads into shared prefix
detail: In local transcripts the same idea-list output was returned 9 to 11 times across workflow agents, and one source file was read 5 times. Common content in the identical cached preamble costs one write plus 0.1x reads, instead of a private write per child.
test: Mine sibling subagent transcripts for bytes read by 2+ agents; price private 1.25x writes versus one shared write plus 0.1x reads; confirm with a 6-agent fan-out.
because: subagent prompt design

title: Stuck-loop breaker: deny repeated failed commands, nudge on repeats
detail: PreToolUse denies a Bash command identical to one that failed earlier unless an edit or install ran between, quoting the earlier error id. PostToolUse nudges on 3+ repeats of (command, output hash), repeated error signatures, A-B-A-B alternation (after OpenHands' StuckDetector). #447 covers only Edit pairs.
test: Scan transcripts for identical failed Bash inputs without intervening Edit, 3+ repeated output hashes and A-B-A-B pairs; sum tokens after the third occurrence; shadow-log would-be denials for false positives.
because: loop detection from payload history of commands

title: Rewrite repeated log commands to native --since cursors
detail: On a repeated docker logs, kubectl logs, journalctl or git log, PreToolUse adds the tool's own cursor from the ledger (--since last timestamp, lastsha..HEAD). #143 rewrites byte offsets of files; these commands read streams, not files.
test: Run docker logs on a looping container twice; compare tokens of the full second call versus the --since call; check boundary lines are neither lost nor duplicated.
because: adds native since-cursor to repeated log commands

title: Trim ToolSearch selects to schemas not yet in context
detail: ToolSearch select: re-injects full JSON schemas for tools already loaded. PreToolUse rewrites the query to the missing names, or denies with 'already loaded', using the compaction boundary from transcript_path as #242 does for Skill.
test: Verify that PreToolUse can deny or edit ToolSearch input. Count ToolSearch calls in transcripts requesting names fetched earlier in the session; sum duplicate schema tokens.
because: ToolSearch, PreToolUse, transcript_path are harness features

title: Shrink Edit not-found errors that echo old_string
detail: Edit failures reportedly echo the full old_string the model wrote one turn earlier. Return 'not found: N lines, first line X' plus the nearest matching line in the file. #399 covers success echoes only.
test: Verify that PostToolUseFailure or PostToolUse can rewrite Edit error text. Count Edit error results in transcripts and compare their size to old_string.
because: shrink echoed old_string in tool error text

title: Substitution replay: '!3 s/old/new/' patches an earlier command
detail: Edit-test loops and retyped python heredocs differ by a few tokens between calls. PreToolUse expands a short patch against the nth earlier Bash input via updatedInput, so only the delta is emitted and kept in history. #451 replays verbatim only.
test: Mine transcripts for consecutive Bash inputs sharing 70%+ text; tokenise unified diff versus full retype; try the syntax via a CLAUDE.md line on 10 tasks.
because: PreToolUse updatedInput command patching

title: Move CLAUDE.md rationale into stripped block HTML comments
detail: Claude Code 2.1.316's loader reportedly strips block-level HTML comments from CLAUDE.md content (seen in the binary; inline ones appear kept). Move rationale, changelog and maintainer notes into such comments: humans keep them, the model stops paying per turn.
test: Verify that block comments are stripped: put canary A in a standalone block comment and B mid-paragraph; ask a fresh session to quote both. Repeat in a SKILL.md body.
because: CLAUDE.md loader comment stripping

title: Canary probe: which manifest and frontmatter fields reach model
detail: plugin.json, marketplace.json, skill and command frontmatter (argument-hint, metadata, license) and agent fields may be UI-only. Put a unique canary in each field and grep logged requests, so description diets (#152) target only model-visible text.
test: Verify that each field is model-visible: install a throwaway plugin with one canary per field; capture requests via a proxy (#187); list canaries reaching the prompt, tool schemas or messages.
because: plugin manifest and frontmatter fields

title: Audit eager @import chains that expand into every prompt
detail: @path imports in CLAUDE.md inline the target file, recursively, in every session, unlike a plain path mention the model reads on demand. Walk the import graph, tokenize each node, flag @README.md or @docs/* style imports, rewrite as mentions.
test: Script resolving @imports across several real repos; report tokens per node; swap the largest import for a path mention and replay 5 tasks, checking the file gets Read when needed.
because: CLAUDE.md @import chains

title: Trim custom subagents: omitClaudeMd and explicit tools allowlist
detail: Subagent frontmatter omitClaudeMd (in 2.1.316; the built-in Explore agent sets it) skips CLAUDE.md for that agent. Omitted tools inherits every parent built-in and MCP schema. Set omitClaudeMd and a minimal tools list on delegation-only searchers and reviewers.
test: Verify that both fields are honored: spawn one custom agent with and without them via a logging proxy, diff first-request tokens; run its golden task under both and check success.
because: subagent frontmatter config

title: Run multi-step skills with context: fork
detail: Skill frontmatter context: fork (in 2.1.316) spawns a subagent, so the skill body, its tool calls and intermediate output stay out of the main thread and only the report returns. Convert audit, research and release-check skills the parent need not watch.
test: Verify that context: fork is honored. Run one such skill inline and forked; compare main-thread tokens at task end and over the next 10 turns, and grade the final output.
because: skill frontmatter context fork

title: Disable auto-memory in headless and throwaway sessions
detail: Setting autoMemoryEnabled false (or env CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY) should stop Claude reading or writing the memory directory and drop memory instructions and the MEMORY.md index from the prompt. Set it for CI, workflow subagents and scratch repos.
test: Verify that the setting exists: run claude -p 'hi' --output-format json with and without it; diff input plus cache-creation tokens; confirm MEMORY.md text is absent from the request.
because: auto-memory harness setting

title: Replace derivable CLAUDE.md sections with regeneration commands
detail: File trees, dependency lists and script tables written by /init-style generators can be regenerated by ls, git ls-files or jq. Detect blocks matching live command output and swap them for the command. Targets live-but-derivable text, unlike dead-reference lint (#343).
test: Diff each CLAUDE.md block against git ls-files trees and package.json or Makefile targets; report matching tokens; drop one block and replay 5 tasks, counting added tool calls.
because: edits CLAUDE.md memory files

title: Enforce CLAUDE.md rules by hook or config, delete prose
detail: Bullets like 'run prettier', 'never edit lockfiles', 'no trailing whitespace' or branch naming can be a PostToolUse formatter, a permissions deny rule or a git hook. Deleting the prose saves per-turn tokens and enforces the rule more reliably than asking.
test: Classify bullets from 5 real CLAUDE.md files as hook-enforceable; implement three; replay tasks and compare violation counts and prompt tokens before and after.
because: harness hooks, permissions, CLAUDE.md prose

title: Delta-debug always-on instruction bullets against replay suite
detail: Bisect-style ddmin: remove halves of the always-on bullets, replay a fixed task set, keep the minimal subset that preserves pass rate and tool-call counts. Behavioral ablation catches rules that matter without appearing in transcripts, unlike usage telemetry (#154).
test: Take a 40-bullet CLAUDE.md and 10 replayable tasks; run ddmin with 3 seeds; report tokens removed and pass-rate delta against the full file.
because: ablates always-on memory-file instruction bullets

title: Split cold skill-body sections into on-demand reference files
detail: An invoked skill's whole SKILL.md stays in history for later turns. Map later tool calls to body headings across transcripts, then move never-acted-on sections (long examples, edge cases, templates) into references/ files read only when needed.
test: For 10 invoked skills, report body tokens in sections with zero follow-on actions; split one skill and replay its task, comparing context tokens and outcome.
because: skill body restructuring

title: Census nested CLAUDE.md lazy loads; apply claudeMdExcludes
detail: Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files load when files in that subtree are read, then persist, so monorepo tasks can pull many. The claudeMdExcludes setting (in 2.1.316) skips chosen files. Count loads per session, exclude irrelevant ancestors and siblings.
test: Verify that InstructionsLoaded hook events fire: log them per session, sum tokens by file and load reason; add an exclude glob and compare first-request tokens and task success.
because: nested CLAUDE.md loading setting

title: Conformal-calibrated keep threshold with a recall guarantee
detail: Fixed rate 0.5 ignores per-call risk. Calibrate a score cutoff on held-out teacher-labelled chunks (conformal risk control, Angelopoulos et al., reportedly 2022) so expected recall of must-keep atoms is at least 1-alpha; emit the cutoff, capped by budget.
test: Calibrate alpha=0.1 on half of val rows per source; on the other half compare achieved recall and kept fraction against fixed rate 0.5 and 0.33.
because: calibrated score cutoff with recall guarantee

title: Predictive-entropy OOD gate: gentler rate on unfamiliar windows
detail: AGENTS.md says the model is weaker on code and non-English text, yet the rate is constant. Per-window mean softmax entropy of the existing logits is a free uncertainty signal; high-entropy windows get a higher keep rate or pass through.
test: Log per-window entropy on code, German/Japanese logs, JSON, English logs; check separation, then QA at equal tokens with entropy-scaled rate versus constant 0.5.
because: entropy gate on local scorer logits

title: Atom-normalised loss weights so each atom counts once
detail: Training loss runs per subtoken, so digit-split numbers, hashes and paths weigh many times a prose word. In a local cl100k proxy, protected atoms were 52-79% of tokens in ls -lR, dpkg -l and git log --stat. Weight each token 1/n subtokens.
test: Fine-tune one epoch with 1/n token weights versus plain CE on the same rows; compare atom-level AUC on unprotected atoms and QA at 0.33 kept.
because: training loss weighting

title: Select checkpoints by atom-level top-k recall, not token AUC
detail: The trainer picks the best epoch by subtoken ROC-AUC (metric_for_best_model=auc), but deployment averages subtokens per atom and cuts a char budget. Compute char-weighted recall of teacher-keep atoms at 0.33 and 0.5, protected excluded.
test: Re-evaluate saved v1/v2 checkpoints and epochs with both metrics on val; check whether the winner changes and which metric tracks stored QA results better.
because: checkpoint selection metric

title: Shape-collapsed scorer input: placeholders for force-kept atoms
detail: The hook force-keeps numbers, hashes and paths, yet the encoder spends tokens reading them (digits split one by one). Substitute a short shape placeholder in the scorer input only, so each 512-token window covers more real content and runs faster.
test: On 50 saved outputs, compare unprotected-atom scores raw versus collapsed (Spearman, top-50% overlap), window count and latency; then QA at equal tokens with existing weights.
because: shape placeholders in scorer input only

title: Cluster near-duplicate lines by encoder hidden states
detail: Export the last hidden layer as a second ONNX output from the same forward pass; mean-pool per line, cosine-cluster, keep one exemplar per cluster and fold the rest into a count. Catches paraphrased repeats that template mining and MinHash may miss.
test: On 20 logs, compare clusters at cosine 0.95 with Drain3 templates and exact duplicates; count extra foldable lines and spot-check QA on folded counts.
because: hidden-state clustering of near-duplicate lines

title: Confident-learning label-error detection from out-of-fold predictions
detail: Train k-fold models on the teacher labels; atoms where out-of-fold P(keep) strongly contradicts the label are flagged as likely teacher noise (confident learning, Northcutt et al. 2021; cleanlab). Automates the 200-label hand audit (#96) and feeds relabel or drop.
test: 3-fold on a 5k-chunk subset; hand-check 100 flagged atoms against 100 random ones for error rate; train on cleaned versus raw labels and compare QA at 0.5.
because: label-noise detection for training data

title: Auxiliary window-level keep-fraction head for learned per-window budgets
