detail: Add a regression head on the pooled encoder output predicting the share of atoms the teacher kept in the window, free from existing labels. At inference it sets each window's budget, so repetitive windows lose more and dense ones less than a constant rate.
test: Train the head on existing rows; report R-squared and correlation with zlib ratio; then QA at equal total tokens for predicted-budget versus constant-rate allocation.
because: auxiliary head, model-internal

title: Per-layer linear probes to find an early-exit truncated encoder
detail: Fit a keep/drop linear probe on each layer's frozen hidden states using existing labels. If a middle layer holds most of the final AUC, export an ONNX graph truncated there with that head, cutting per-window compute and file size.
test: Extract hidden states for 2k val windows; plot probe AUC and top-50% overlap with the full model per layer; time a truncated int8 graph at the best layer.
because: early-exit encoder, model-internal

title: Nested keep tiers with stored ranks for progressive expansion
detail: Global top-k makes the 0.33 output a subset of 0.5 and 0.8. Save one-byte atom ranks next to the original; an expand command re-renders a higher tier (optionally for a line range) without the model, cheaper than reading the full original.
test: Assert tiers nest on 20 outputs; on recovery tasks needing a cut fact, compare tokens spent on expand-to-0.8 of a line range versus reading the whole original.
because: stored ranks re-render higher tier without model

title: Value-swap augmentation: keep decisions should ignore which numbers appear
detail: Probe first: replace digits, hashes and paths in outputs with fresh random values and measure score drift on unprotected atoms. If large, retrain with label-preserving value swaps and formatting noise (ANSI codes, CRLF, indent changes) so the model stops keying on specific strings.
test: Perturb 100 saved outputs, rescore, report Spearman and top-50% Jaccard on unprotected atoms; if below 0.95, fine-tune with swaps and compare QA at 0.5.
because: augmentation for training, model-internal

title: Balance window splits to avoid tiny context-starved tail windows
detail: Greedy 510-token windows leave a remainder window of a few tokens, possibly under the 48-token training minimum (chunking.py), scored with almost no context. Split n tokens into ceil(n/510) near-equal windows at atom boundaries, or at least split the last two evenly.
test: Count tail windows under 64 tokens on saved outputs; compare tail-atom scores, kept share and top-k overlap between greedy and balanced splits; check latency is unchanged.
because: balanced window splits at atom boundaries

title: Scorer false-positive null: containment match accepts hedges and substrings
detail: eval_qa scores gold-substring-in-answer. Checked in a snippet: gold '1' matches 'unknown 10 files', 'in' matches 'main', hedged lists and 'not 404' also pass. Add a mismatched-gold null, word-boundary match, answer-length cap; report strict EM beside the headline.
test: Score each cached reader answer against another question's gold from the same chunk; report chance-level EM per method, then rescore all cached answers strictly and compare gaps between methods.
because: scorer false-positive audit

title: Gold-span survival ceiling splits QA misses: deleted versus misread
detail: Every gold answer is a verbatim span, so check deterministically whether it survives in each compressed context. Accuracy then splits into deleted (selection fault), kept but misread (reader or fragmentation fault) and guessed. Stratify survival by answer position and distance to window seams.
test: Using cached contexts_*.json, regex-match gold per method with whitespace tolerance; cross-tabulate survival against EM; report survival by source and keep rate with zero LLM calls.
because: gold-span survival analysis

title: Reader-prompt parity: eval framing versus the real hook note
detail: eval_qa tells the reader words were removed and offers 'unknown'. The live agent instead sees the hook note, which says IDs, numbers and paths are kept exactly, plus its command and task. Compare framings; the note may change over-trust or recovery.
test: Same cached compressed contexts, three READ prompts: eval text, verbatim hook note plus command, no mention. Compare EM and unknown rate per arm with a paired bootstrap over questions.
because: reader-prompt framing parity check

title: Recovery-augmented QA: accuracy against total tokens including refetches
detail: Give the reader a simulated grep-original tool returning matching lines from the uncompressed chunk. Score accuracy against context plus recovered tokens plus extra turns, per keep rate. The frontier shows whether deeper compression plus recovery beats gentler compression alone.
test: For 100 questions at keep 0.33 and 0.5, allow one grep call; log hit rate and tokens fetched; plot accuracy versus total tokens beside the no-tool curve and original.
because: recovery-augmented QA evaluation

title: Lockbox question set and look ledger against eval tuning
detail: Hundreds of rules, thresholds and rates will be tuned against the same 378 questions, inflating headlines through adaptive overfitting. Seal a fresh question set from repos and servers outside the corpus, open it once per release, and log the number of A/Bs for FDR correction.
test: Mint 200 questions from groups absent from the corpus; hold until a release; compare the headline there against the tuned set and report the shrinkage.
because: lockbox holdout against eval overfitting

title: Always-valid sequential harm test on the holdout stream
detail: With the per-call holdout (#178) running, apply an always-valid sequential test (mSPRT or confidence sequence) per rule on rerun and refetch rates against a non-inferiority margin. A harmful rule can auto-disable within days instead of waiting for a fixed-sample readout.
test: Simulate arms with 3 percent versus 6 percent refetch rates; compare days-to-detect and false-alarm rate of the sequential test with a fixed-N test at 500 calls.
because: sequential harm test statistics

title: Fork-from-prefix A/B: finish recorded runs from the compression point
detail: Copy a recorded session up to one oversized result, swap in the compressed text, resume headless and let the agent finish; repeat with the original. The shared prefix cuts variance versus fresh runs and judges end state, not just the next action (#177).
test: Take 20 oversized results from sessions ending in a test pass; 3 continuations per arm via claude -p resume; report paired pass rate, turns and tokens to finish.
because: resumes recorded sessions headless, harness resume

title: Exposure-conditioned task A/B: pick tasks where the hook fires
detail: Most small repo tasks emit no output above 6,000 chars, so an on/off A/B mostly measures nothing and dilutes effects. Pilot hook-fire counts per task, keep tasks with several firings, and regress outcome on compressed-token share (dose-response) beside the intent-to-treat result.
test: Run 40 candidate tasks once in shadow mode, count would-be firings; report how many exceed 3; estimate the power of a 25-task A/B using only those tasks.
because: exposure-conditioned A/B design

title: Fresh agent tasks by bug injection, free of memorisation
detail: Public SWE tasks may be memorised by the agent model. Inject a mutation (flipped condition, renamed import) into a green commit of a verbose-test repo, use the failing test as grader, and mint unlimited fresh tasks whose failure logs exceed the hook threshold.
test: Generate 30 mutants across 3 repos; confirm the baseline agent fixes at least half and logs exceed 6,000 chars in at least one third; use as #7's task pool.
because: fresh task generation by bug injection

title: Question-writer independence: re-author QA with another model family
detail: Qwen writes the questions and also labeled the training data, so questions may target what that teacher keeps. Regenerate questions with a different family and with scripted templates; check whether the original-versus-compressed gap widens. Distinct from reader and label diversity.
test: Write 5 questions per chunk with a second family on 100 held-out chunks; score the same reader on original and 0.5 kept; compare the gap to the Qwen-written set.
because: question-writer independence check

title: Forced-deletion probe: does the agent notice and recover missing facts
detail: Take cases where the gold fact is verified deleted (survival check), embed them in a small Claude Code task, and record whether the agent greps the saved original, reruns the command or answers confidently from a guess. Vary note wording and Claude tier.
test: Use 30 deleted-gold cases from the QA set; run claude -p with Bash; classify the first response as recover, rerun or guess; compare three note variants.
because: agent recovery probe experiment

title: Accuracy versus realised Claude tokens: frontier curves, not nominal-rate points
detail: Methods are compared at nominal rates, but realised ratios differ and are counted in the reader's tokenizer. Sweep five rates per method, count output with Anthropic's token-counting endpoint (reportedly free), interpolate accuracy at equal Claude tokens and report area under the curve.
test: Reuse cached contexts at several rates for ctxprune and LLMLingua-2; recount tokens; compare accuracy at 1k, 2k, 3k output tokens and AUC with 10k bootstrap resamples.
because: offline frontier curves with vendor token counts

title: OpenAI-compatible fake summarizer model backed by token pruning
detail: ctxprune serve gains /v1/chat/completions that answers summarize requests with the pruned history, not prose. Summariser slots (Aider weak-model history summary, OpenHands LLMSummarizingCondenser, similar) then cost no API tokens and no second model call. Lossy extractive replaces abstractive.
test: Run Aider with a tiny --max-chat-history-tokens and --weak-model on the stub; compare resent-history tokens and recall of 10 earlier decisions against the stock weak-model summary.
because: relies on harness summarizer slots and endpoint config

title: GIT_PAGER and PAGER set to a filter in pty agents
detail: Agents using a pty (OpenHands tmux, Cline and Cursor VS Code terminals, Zed terminal) make git, man, psql, systemctl act interactive. Pointing GIT_PAGER, PAGER, SYSTEMD_PAGER at a filter interposes with no wrappers. Checked here: GIT_PAGER fires under script(1), not when piped.
test: Under script -qec, run git log -p with GIT_PAGER set to a noise-pack filter; compare bytes. Check which target agents allocate a pty and preset GIT_PAGER=cat.
because: pager env vars at shell level

title: BASH_ENV stdout filter covering every command in non-interactive bash
detail: BASH_ENV pointing at a file containing exec > >(filter) streams all stdout of each bash -c through one filter, no per-binary shims. Checked here: exit code kept, no lost lines in 5 runs; stderr bypasses and reorders. Login shells skip BASH_ENV.
test: Set BASH_ENV in Codex shell_environment_policy, Zed terminal env or OpenHands sandbox env; run a failing pytest and a 20 KB command; compare bytes, exit status, login-shell behavior.
because: BASH_ENV shell-level stdout filter
check: A BASH_ENV file that execs stdout into a filter shrinks a 20 KB bash -c to under 200 bytes with the exit status (7) kept and no distinct line lost; stderr bypasses it; bash -c and bash -lc are covered here while bash -ic, dash and any bash whose stdin is a socket are not; the hook must mark itself (nested bash would otherwise change captured data) and test the filter first (otherwise a missing filter loses all stdout).

title: PreToolUse hook runs the command, denies with digest as reason
detail: For hosts whose hooks cannot rewrite results (reportedly Cursor beforeShellExecution, Gemini CLI BeforeTool, Cline PreToolUse), the hook runs the command itself, compresses, and returns the digest as the deny message. Also fits Claude Code built-ins that skip PostToolUse. Risks: side effects, denial misread as failure.
test: Verify that a deny reason reaches the model verbatim. Add a PreToolUse Bash hook that runs pytest and denies with pruned output; count reruns and misreads over 10 tasks.
because: uses per-harness PreToolUse deny hooks

title: ACP middleman compresses terminal and file responses for any agent
detail: Agent Client Protocol (Zed's JSON-RPC protocol, reportedly also in JetBrains and Neovim) lets agents delegate terminal/output and fs/read_text_file to the client. A shim in the client role compresses those replies and lowers outputByteLimit, covering every ACP agent at once.
test: Verify that agents delegate terminal/output to the client. Serve a 100 KB log from a mock ACP client to an ACP agent (gemini --experimental-acp); check the transcript for compressed text.
because: ACP is a cross-agent protocol, proxied like MCP

title: Graded age-based decay ladder in OpenHands condenser pipeline
detail: Replace mask-or-keep (ObservationMaskingCondenser) with chained condensers: full, pruned at 0.5 after k turns, 0.2 after 2k, then stub. Release in batches like AmortizedForgettingCondenser so cached prefixes stay stable. Keep rate falls with age, not only size.
test: Replay one recorded OpenHands trajectory offline; integrate resident tokens times turns under mask-only versus the ladder, counting cache-rewrite events; then ask recall questions on aged observations.
because: graded age decay; condenser is just one delivery route

title: Strip stale environment_details blocks from Cline and Roo history
detail: Cline and Roo reportedly append an environment_details block (visible files, open tabs, running terminals, time; full file listing on turn one) to each user message. A base-URL proxy keeps the newest block and rewrites older ones once at first sight, keeping prefix bytes stable.
test: Log 20 Cline turns through a passthrough proxy; tokenise every environment_details block, report the stale share, then replay stripped history and compare answers to questions about earlier files.
because: Cline and Roo environment_details block only

title: Native session-log adapters give exact token ledgers per agent
detail: Codex rollout JSONL, Gemini CLI telemetry outfile, Cline task history files, Aider llm-history and OpenHands event files reportedly hold per-request usage. Adapters emit one common row schema so the ledger and replay harness work without a logging proxy.
test: Verify that usage is logged: parse one real session from three agents into (tool, chars, usage) rows; check summed usage against the provider console to within a few percent.
because: adapters for each harness's private log format

title: Cross-agent canary-command probe: envelope tokens, caps, spill files
detail: Run one script (true, echo hi, seq 1 N, one 1 MB line) in each agent. Record fixed per-call envelope tokens (Gemini shell result reportedly lists Stderr/Error/Signal fields even when empty), truncation style and cap, and whether full output spills to a file.
test: Drive the script through codex exec, gemini -p and Cline; dump the model-visible tool result from logs; tabulate envelope tokens per call and the cap where output is cut.
because: cross-agent canary measurement

title: Fan one generated-path list out to every agent's ignore file
detail: Emit vendored, generated and lockfile globs to .cursorignore, .clineignore, .aiderignore, .geminiignore and .continueignore (reportedly all exist). Shrinks Aider's repo-map candidates, Cline's initial file listing and indexing, which Claude-only Read deny rules (#401) do not reach.
test: Verify that each ignore file is honored. Generate them for a Node repo; compare Aider --show-repo-map tokens and Cline's first file listing with and without; confirm ignored paths vanish.
because: per-harness ignore config files

title: Gemini CLI BeforeModel hook stubs aged results, no proxy
detail: Gemini CLI hooks reportedly include BeforeModel, which can edit the outgoing request in-process. Swap functionResponse parts older than N turns for stubs plus a saved id, memoized so earlier bytes repeat exactly. A request-rewrite point where base-URL proxies are awkward.
test: Verify that the installed gemini has BeforeModel and can modify requests. Stub old shell results in a 30-turn session; compare cached-token usage and whether the model re-runs commands.
because: Gemini CLI BeforeModel hook

title: Compress Reads of host-persisted oversized tool-result files
detail: Oversized results are diverted by the host to a tool-results file with a 2KB preview (seen in this session: 29.7KB). The model then Reads it whole, and the hook never matches Read. Add a Read matcher scoped to that directory.
test: Trigger a 40k-char Bash output, log the follow-up Read's size, then compress it via a path-scoped matcher; compare tokens and re-reads.
because: host-persisted tool-result files and Read matcher

title: Eval parity with the shipped hook configuration
detail: eval_quick and eval_qa score arms with measure=reader tokens, with or without ids; none combines the character budget with force_protected as the hook does, and none includes the note or the 6000-char gate. Headline AGENTS.md numbers may not describe shipped behaviour.
test: Run eval_qa through hook.run with the real note and character budget at 0.5; compare accuracy and achieved token ratio with the measure= arm.
because: eval parity with shipped configuration

title: Unwritable cache directory silently disables all compression
detail: run() saves the original before returning. A read-only HOME, sandbox or full disk raises, the outer except swallows it, and every output passes uncompressed with no signal. Fall back to TMPDIR or a project directory, and log once.
test: Run the hook with XDG_CACHE_HOME pointing at a read-only path; confirm empty output, then verify a fallback directory yields a note and compression.
because: fallback save dir keeps compression working

title: Detect truncated teacher outputs under the len//2 token cap
detail: Teacher max_tokens is len(text)//2+64 and finish_reason is never read. Digit-splitting tokenizers (reportedly Qwen) can need about one token per character on numeric or hex chunks, so cut-off outputs would label the tail as dropped.
test: Count teacher responses with finish_reason length; compare tail keep rates on digit-heavy chunks with and without those rows excluded.
because: dev-time check of teacher label truncation

title: Stream-aware rates: keep more of stderr than stdout
detail: hook._compress gives stdout and stderr the same rate. stderr tends to hold warnings and failures while stdout holds bulk progress. Use a higher keep rate on stderr and a lower one on stdout when the host reports them separately.
test: From captured events, check how often streams arrive separately, then compare QA on error questions at 0.7 stderr/0.4 stdout versus 0.5/0.5.
because: separate stdout/stderr streams are host-only, not in API payload

title: Todo completion as deterministic fold boundary for old results
detail: ReFold (reportedly) folds turns the agent calls finished; TokenPilot (arXiv 2606.17016) tracks active, completed and evictable segments. A TodoWrite or TaskUpdate completed event marks a span whose tool results become one-line stubs with saved ids, via proxy or resume surgery.
test: From transcripts, find completed-todo events; sum tool-result tokens in each span and the share never mentioned (path or identifier) afterwards. Replay stubbed copies and ask recall questions.
because: todo-completion tool call as fold boundary, payload-visible
check: When a TodoWrite event completes a todo that was the only one in progress, the tool results since it started become one-line stubs (tool, target, first line, saved id; unfold returns the original byte for byte); overlapping todos, a todo completed without a span, files named by a still-open todo, malformed payloads and sessions without todos fold nothing, and history is rewritten once per closing event.

title: Recoverability-ranked eviction: stub re-obtainable results first
detail: Context Window Lifecycle (arXiv 2606.11213) evicts the oldest and most recoverable content by dependency graph. Classify results: unchanged-file Read, git show, ls and grep are cheap to regenerate; one-shot test runs, network fetches and deleted-file output are not. Stub the first class first.
test: Label every tool result in 20 transcripts as regenerable or not; report token share per class and how often each class was re-read or re-run later in the session.
because: rank aged results by recoverability, proxy rewrite

title: Agent-callable fold tool honored by a history-rewriting proxy
detail: SWE-Compressor ('Context as a Tool', ACL 2026 Findings) and AgentFold let the agent choose when to condense history. Expose a fold(ids, note) MCP tool using the short ids in hook notes; a proxy swaps those results for the note and saved ids.
test: In an Agent SDK loop on 10 tasks, compare agent-chosen folds with fixed older-than-N stubbing: billed tokens, refetches, pass rate, and whether the agent uses the tool unprompted.
because: fold tool via proxy; plain tool call

title: Knee-point cutoff to pick how many rows to keep
detail: Headroom's SmartCrusher reportedly uses the Kneedle elbow algorithm to find where extra array items stop adding information. Score rows by novelty (deflate cost, or distance to nearest kept row), sort, and keep rows up to the knee instead of fixed first/last k (#132).
test: Take 30 recorded JSON lists, grep and find outputs over 200 rows; compare Kneedle keep counts against fixed 0.5 for rows kept and answers to count and outlier questions.
because: knee-point row selection, local algorithm

title: Mem0-style add/update/skip gate on memory file writes
detail: The Mem0 paper (2025) compares each new fact with similar stored ones and picks ADD, UPDATE, DELETE or NOOP; Zep invalidates superseded facts. A PreToolUse hook on writes to the memory dir flags near-duplicate or contradicted entries so MEMORY.md stops growing every session.
test: Run pairwise token-Jaccard over entries in 5 real auto-memory dirs; count duplicate or superseded entries and the tokens they add to every session start; hand-check 30 flags.
because: PreToolUse hook on memory directory writes

title: Reward-driven pruner training: reader-verified mask rejection sampling
detail: PCRL and TACO-RL (2024, reportedly) train a keep/drop policy with a reader-task reward plus length penalty, not teacher labels. Cheaper variant: sample several masks per window from classifier probabilities, keep the shortest one the reader still answers from, retrain on those.
test: On 200 windows with QA pairs, sample 8 masks each at p-scaled keep rates; measure how often the shortest passing mask beats the current 0.5 mask in kept tokens.
because: offline reader-verified training labels; runtime unchanged

title: SWE-agent-style syntax check after Edit and Write
detail: SWE-agent's ACI rejects edits that fail a linter (reportedly improving resolve rate), so errors surface at the edit, not in later test or build output. PostToolUse on Edit/Write runs py_compile, node --check or json.loads on the file and returns a one-line error.
test: Find Edit/Write calls followed within 3 turns by SyntaxError, ParseError or JSON decode output in transcripts; sum tokens of those outputs and the turns until the next successful edit.
because: PostToolUse on Edit/Write runs host file checks

title: pytest tracebacks: trim echoed test-body source above '>' line
detail: Default pytest failures echo the whole test function above the '>' line. Keep the def line, three lines before '>' and the E lines. Measured: 12 parametrized failures cost 1,868 tokens under --tb=auto, 968 under --tb=short (o200k proxy). Alternative: PYTEST_ADDOPTS in settings env.
test: Run pytest on 20 long-bodied failing tests; trim; tokenise; check each failing assert and fixture value stays identifiable from def line, context and E lines.
because: trims pytest traceback echoed source

title: Hoist shared source body across parametrized failures
detail: One @parametrize or test.each failing 12 ways prints 12 blocks with identical function source, differing only in the [id], param line and E lines. Print the shared body once, then one compact param plus E-line group per id. Beyond #17 and #478.
test: Generate 50 failing parametrized cases in pytest and jest; factor shared bodies; assert every id and distinct assert value survives; compare tokens; ask which params fail.
because: hoist shared parametrized-failure source

title: Playwright: fold retry attempts and Call log polling cycles
detail: Playwright reportedly reprints the full error per retry attempt, and its Call log repeats 'waiting for locator / element not stable / retrying click action' cycles with growing waits. Fold identical attempts to 'Retry #1 identical' and repeated cycles to a count.
test: Verify that retries reprint the error: run a flaky spec with retries=2 and a hidden button; fold; assert first cycle, final timeout and locator survive; compare tokens.
because: folds Playwright retry and polling text

title: Jest console.log capture stanzas to one line
detail: Jest prints each captured console call as a label line, blank line, indented message, blank line and 'at file:line:col' line (from memory). Rewrite to 'console.log src/a.test.ts:12: message' and fold identical repeats with counts. Same facts, re-encoded.
test: Run a jest suite with 100 debug prints; rewrite stanzas; tokenise before and after; ask which test printed value X from the rewritten form.
because: re-encodes Jest console stanzas to one line
check: A Jest console stanza (label, one message line, blank line, 'at ... file:line:col') becomes '<indent>console.<kind> file:line: message'; identical neighbouring stanzas fold into 'console.<kind>×N ...'; multi-line messages and anything else stay verbatim.
check_loses: the function name and the column in the 'at' line, and the blank lines between folded stanzas

title: tsc --traceResolution and --listFiles: fold successful resolutions
detail: Measured: a 2-file project's --traceResolution output is 19.6k chars (4,886 o200k-proxy tokens) against 370 chars for plain tsc. Fold each Resolving block ending 'successfully resolved' to one line, keep unresolved blocks whole, collapse lib and @types entries in --listFiles to counts.
test: Run tsc --traceResolution on a 200-import project with two broken imports; fold; assert failed blocks stay whole; compare tokens; ask why module X fails.
because: folds tsc resolution trace blocks
check: Each '======== Resolving ... ========' block that ends 'successfully resolved' becomes one '[ctxprune ok] module X from Y -> Z' line, 'not resolved' blocks stay whole, and --listFiles entries under typescript/lib and node_modules/@types become two count lines; every resolution result, every unresolved block, every user file and the lib/@types counts are unchanged.
check_loses: the candidate paths, extensions and 'directory does not exist' lines tried inside each successful resolution, and the individual lib/@types file names

title: TypeScript error elaboration chains: keep head and deepest lines
detail: TS2322 and TS2345 errors print nested 'not assignable / types of property are incompatible' lines, often with huge inlined types. Keyed on indentation, keep the first line, the deepest two lines and an 'N intermediate lines' marker. C++ sibling is #220.
test: Collect tsc errors from a Prisma, zod or react-query heavy repo; fold chains; check the deepest lines name the root cause; replay fixes from folded versus full.
because: trims TS error elaboration chains

title: npm packument and PyPI JSON API to version digest
detail: Measured: the express packument is 823 KB (310k o200k-proxy tokens) and PyPI's requests JSON 193 KB (82k). A digest of dist-tags, latest deps and engines, plus one 'version date' line per release, was 4.2k and 2.7k tokens. Targets curl and npm view --json.
test: Curl registry JSON for 10 packages; project to the digest; ask latest version, date of a 4.x release and engines.node; compare answers and tokens.
because: digest package registry JSON
check: An npm packument or PyPI project JSON becomes a digest: package, latest version, dist-tags, the latest version's dependencies and engines (or requires-python, requires_dist and vulnerability ids), then one 'version date [deprecated or yanked: reason]' line per release in registry order; latest version, tags, dependencies, engines.node, the release date of every version and every deprecation or yank reason are unchanged.
check_loses: the readme/description, per-version metadata of non-latest versions (dependencies, dist integrity and signatures, maintainers, scripts, files), PyPI file lists, hashes and sizes, time of day of a release (date only), the 'users' map and every other field; documents that are neither a packument nor a PyPI project JSON are left unchanged

title: Collapse applied migrations in showmigrations and db:migrate:status
detail: Django showmigrations prints '[X] 0001_initial' per migration per app, contrib apps alone adding dozens; Rails db:migrate:status, knex and prisma status list every applied row. Fold fully applied apps to 'auth: 12 applied' and show unapplied rows. Distinct from #124.
test: Run showmigrations on a Django project with 15 apps and db:migrate:status on a Rails app; fold; ask which migrations are pending; compare tokens.
because: collapses applied migration listings

title: rails routes and Django show_urls: drop framework-internal rows
detail: rails routes in a default app lists ActiveStorage, ActionMailbox and rails/info routes with long signed-blob paths, and blanks Prefix on repeat rows (from memory). Replace framework-owned controller rows with a count; keep app routes.
test: Run rails routes on 3 apps and show_urls on a Django project; drop internals; check an agent still finds the controller for a given path; count tokens.
because: folds framework-internal route rows

title: Python lock hashes: requirements --hash, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock
detail: Python counterpart to #121: pip-compile --generate-hashes puts several --hash=sha256 continuation lines on every pin, poetry.lock lists a file and hash per wheel, Pipfile.lock embeds hashes, and pip-compile adds '# via' blocks. Collapse each package to 'name==version'.
test: Take pinned Python lockfiles from 10 repos; strip hash and via lines; assert name==version pairs match a pip parse of the original; compare tokens.
because: collapses Python lock hashes to pins
check: requirements.txt with --hash and '# via' lines, poetry.lock and Pipfile.lock collapse to one 'name==version' line per package (environment markers and the Pipfile default/develop section kept); the set of pins equals what tomllib/json read from the original.
check_loses: every hash and wheel file name, who requires each package ('# via'), poetry's dependency graph, extras, python-versions, groups, optional flags and content-hash, Pipfile index and the _meta block, and the original file order of unrecognised comment lines is kept but their relation to a pin is not

title: Ecosystem nag-silencing env vars for JS and Python tools
detail: Extend the quiet env (#76, #193) with PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK, NPM_CONFIG_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=false, NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED, BROWSERSLIST_IGNORE_OLD_DATA, PRISMA_HIDE_UPDATE_MESSAGE and DISABLE_OPENCOLLECTIVE. Each targets a banner reprinted every run. Verify each name exists.
test: Run 10 build, install and test commands with and without the pack; diff bytes and exit codes; confirm each variable actually silences its banner.
because: nag-silencing env prefix on commands
check: pip commands get PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 and JS tool commands get the npm update-notifier, Next.js telemetry, Browserslist, Prisma and OpenCollective silencers through an export prefix, each only when the user has not set it; real output lines and exit status are unchanged.

title: Constant banners: ELIFECYCLE footers, setuptools star-bars, Sass deprecations
detail: Signature-fold recurring blocks: 'npm ERR! code ELIFECYCLE' footers and yarn 'Visit docs' lines, setuptools banners fenced by 80-asterisk bars, and Sass deprecation blocks with box-drawn code frames. Keep the first line plus URL; fold repeats per deprecation id with counts.
test: Collect failing npm test, pip install -e and sass runs; fold blocks; assert the first message and exit status survive; tokenise before and after.
because: signature-folds constant banner blocks

title: Decode JWTs to claims JSON plus signature stub
detail: JWTs (eyJ... three base64url parts) in curl -v, env dumps and OAuth responses tokenise poorly. Synthetic JWT: 144 vs 63 o200k-proxy tokens when decoded with the signature stubbed. Keep exp, sub, iss, aud; original saved.
test: Regex eyJ[\w-]+\.eyJ[\w-]+\.[\w-]+ over transcripts; decode header and payload; tokenise before and after; check expiry and audience questions remain answerable.
because: decode JWTs locally, stub signature

title: Stub QR codes, figlet banners and terminal block art
detail: Runs of 4+ lines dominated by block, braille or ASCII-art glyphs (QR from expo start, wrangler login, aws sso login; figlet; neofetch logos) carry no text. Synthetic 29x58 QR: 1,426 vs 13 tokens (o200k proxy). Stub with dimensions.
test: Generate QR with qrencode -t UTF8 or python qrcode, figlet text, neofetch; run detector; confirm prose, tables and trees never match; tokenise before and after.
because: stub text-glyph art; text transform
check: A run of 4+ consecutive lines of only block-element/braille glyphs (QR codes, ANSI colour ignored) or figlet-style ASCII glyphs becomes one '[block art omitted: R lines x C cols (kind)]' line; every other line, in place, is byte-identical, and prose, markdown and box-drawing tables, tree output, git log --graph, progress bars, diffs and code banners never match.
check_loses: the art itself (a QR code's payload, the glyph shapes) and the text a figlet banner spelled, and any art drawn side by side with words (neofetch logos), which is not stubbed at all

title: Same-length ASCII for progress bars, sparklines, braille meters
detail: Shade, block and braille glyphs cost 1-3 tokens each, while # and . runs cost about 1 token per 80 chars. Synthetic braille bar 56 vs 9, sparkline 35 vs 7 (digit levels), shade bar 20 vs 10. Preserve run lengths and levels; extends #15.
test: Capture rich, tqdm unicode-bar and btop-style output; map glyph runs and eight sparkline levels to ASCII; assert levels round-trip; tokenise; ask percent-complete questions on both.
because: glyph to ASCII text rewrite
check: Runs of 3+ block glyphs and braille cells become same-length ASCII (bar # . : =, sparkline levels 1-8, braille dot count 0-8 as . 1-7 #); the level of every glyph is kept, short runs, spinners and invisible padding are left alone, and the size saving is in bytes and tokens.
check_loses: glyph shape (block vs shade vs braille), which braille dots were set (only their count), and the difference between a level digit and an ordinary digit

title: Strip escaped and ESC-less ANSI residue in logs
detail: Raw ESC is handled (#9), but JSON-encoded logs carry literal \u001b[32m, \x1b[0m, \033[ or ^[[ text, and some captures keep bare [0;32m. Synthetic: 70 vs 6 tokens (o200k proxy). Strip with an anchored SGR regex.
test: Collect docker json-file logs, pino or bunyan output, gh run view --log and cat -v dumps; apply regex; count false positives such as array [0m; tokenise before and after.
because: regex strip of escaped ANSI text

title: Resolve backspace overstrike from man pages and spinners
detail: man or nroff without col -b (reportedly when piped), perldoc, ul and script typescripts emit X\bX bold and _\bX underline; old spinners write -\b\. Synthetic NAME header x5: 50 vs 10 tokens (o200k proxy). Apply backspaces like a terminal.
test: Run man -P cat ls | cat -v where man-db exists, or printf overstrike samples; compare a strip-regex result with col -b output; tokenise; assert identical text.
because: apply backspaces to output text
check: Backspaces are applied like a terminal (col -b): per line each character overwrites the one in its column, so man/nroff bold (X, backspace, X), underline (_, backspace, X) and spinner frames reduce to the last character written.
check_loses: the bold/underline emphasis itself, intermediate spinner frames, and display-column semantics (a tab or wide character counts as one cell)

title: Strip thousands separators from consistently grouped numeric columns
detail: Grouped integers like 1,234,567 tokenise as digit and comma pieces. Synthetic 30 large integers: 179 vs 119 tokens (o200k proxy). Apply only when every number in a column or run matches the grouping pattern; keep decimals; add a header note.
test: Scan saved outputs for \d{1,3}(,\d{3})+ runs; strip in consistent columns; assert reversal restores the original; tokenise; ask sum and max questions before and after.
because: strip thousands separators in columns

title: Canonicalise zero-padded hex words and IPv6 addresses
detail: Fixed-width 0x0000000000000001 values (gdb registers, lldb, Rust {:#018x}) and full IPv6 text cost digit-group tokens. Synthetic: register line 33 vs 22, IPv6 24 vs 13 (RFC 5952 form). Value-preserving; skip hexdump columns.
test: Run gdb info registers, ip -6 addr, ss -6; rewrite via int() and ipaddress compressed form; assert numeric equality; tokenise; check agent greps for full addresses still work.
because: canonicalises zero-padded hex and IPv6
check: Hex words of 8+ digits with leading zeros lose the zeros (0x0000000000000001 -> 0x1), and fully written IPv6 addresses become their RFC 5952 compressed form; every value is equal, hexdump columns, MACs, times and already-short forms are not touched.
check_loses: zero padding of hex words, hex-digit case inside a rewritten IPv6 address, and column alignment that relied on fixed width

title: Decode Python bytes-repr and \xNN UTF-8 escape runs
detail: print(resp.content), CalledProcessError and socket reprs show b'\xe6\x97\xa5...' at about 3 tokens per byte. Synthetic CJK plus accented string: 58 vs 7 tokens (o200k proxy). Decode only runs forming valid UTF-8; keep \n and \x00.
test: Regex b'...' literals and \x runs in saved outputs; decode valid UTF-8; assert re-encoding round-trips; tokenise before and after.
because: decode bytes-repr escape runs
check: Inside Python bytes literals, runs of lowercase \xNN escapes that form valid UTF-8 for printable characters are replaced by those characters (with a `§b` marker); the decoder re-escapes them to the exact original text; truncated or invalid bytes, ASCII escapes, \n, str mojibake and literals that already contain non-ASCII text are never decoded.

title: Lowercase shouted ALL-CAPS prose lines
detail: Capitalised prose merges less in BPE vocabularies: 32 vs 24 tokens for a 20-word shouted build error, 24 vs 20 for a pip PATH warning (o200k proxy). Lowercase runs of 4+ caps prose words only, never identifiers, constants, hex or level tags.
test: Find lines with 4+ consecutive all-caps dictionary words in 100 saved outputs; measure token share; confirm ERROR and INFO tags are already one token; QA lowercased variants.
because: text case transform, tokenizer-neutral

title: Run-length token price curves per character class
detail: Probe Claude's tokenizer via count_tokens for runs of 1..120 of each char. The o200k proxy shows 80 dashes or equals cost 1 token, 120 zeros 40, 120 block glyphs 30, CRLF nothing extra. Ranks rules and kills worthless ones.
test: Script count_tokens over run lengths for 60 characters including whitespace, digits, glyphs; compare with o200k; list classes costing over 0.5 token per char.
because: dev-time tokenizer probe of character classes

title: Gate compression on estimated tokens, not 6,000 characters
detail: Chars per token ranges from about 0.5 (braille) to 80+ (dash runs). A char-class weighted estimate calibrated on tiktoken would fire on 6k chars of braille or escaped CJK JSON and skip 6k of rule lines.
test: Fit weights on 500 saved outputs against count_tokens; compare gate misclassification of chars versus estimate near the boundary; measure added hook latency.
because: gate on estimated tokens; pluggable counter

title: Skip unchanged loop and cron wakeups at UserPromptSubmit
detail: Hook source field is reportedly loop_wakeup or schedule_wakeup for machine-fired turns. If a cheap fingerprint (git HEAD plus status, watched-file hashes) matches the previous fire, block the prompt so no model request runs. Dynamic /loop may stop re-arming; cron fires are safer.
test: Verify the source values reach the hook; count wakeup turns in transcripts whose reply was 'no change'; prototype; confirm a blocked fire makes no API request and whether /loop re-arms.
because: UserPromptSubmit hook source field

title: Filter poll_event turns: webhook and Monitor events
detail: Host-submitted events (PR activity, Monitor stdout lines, reportedly) reach a UserPromptSubmit hook with source poll_event, and a blocking verdict rejects the event. Drop duplicate status churn, superseded-SHA CI results and bot comments; rate-limit bursts to one per window.
test: Verify that poll_event reaches the hook; log envelopes from a PR-watch session; mark events whose reply did nothing; replay a drop rule, counting turns avoided and missed signals.
because: UserPromptSubmit hook poll_event source

title: SubagentStop blocks over-long reports for a digest rewrite
detail: Stop and SubagentStop hooks can reportedly return a block reason so the agent continues. If last_assistant_message exceeds N tokens, ask for a path:line digest with details in a file. A hard cap, unlike prompt contracts (#240, #340). Honor stop_hook_active.
test: Verify that SubagentStop block continues the subagent; on 10 delegated tasks compare extra subagent output tokens against parent report tokens times remaining turns, with and without the block.
because: SubagentStop hook

title: Shared size budget across parallel sibling tool results
detail: Eight parallel results of 5,900 chars each all slip under the 6,000 per-call threshold. Count siblings from the assistant message at transcript_path and divide one batch budget across them, lowering min_chars only for wide batches. Complements #196, which sums slots within one call.
test: Scan transcripts for assistant messages with 3+ tool calls where every result is under 6,000 chars but the sum exceeds 20,000; report their share of all result chars.
because: batch budget; siblings visible in assistant message

title: Compress Stop-gate and other hook feedback channels
detail: Block reasons from Stop hooks (test or lint gates) and stdout from UserPromptSubmit or SessionStart hooks reach the model without passing PostToolUse. A 'ctxprune wrap -- cmd' shim runs the user's hook and applies lossless noise packs above a size floor.
test: Wire a Stop hook running a failing pytest suite; compare reason size raw versus wrapped; confirm the model still fixes the failure and the wrapped hook fails open.
because: Stop/UserPromptSubmit hook feedback channels

title: Key keep rate on duration_ms and effort
detail: PostToolUse input reportedly carries duration_ms (tool run time) and effort. Instant read-only commands are cheap to rerun narrower, so compress harder; multi-minute builds and test runs are costly to rerun, so keep more. Policy keys on name and size only.
test: Verify those fields exist; join transcript tool timestamps to later reruns or saved-file greps; compare rerun rate by duration bucket and effort before choosing rate offsets.
because: needs hook-input duration_ms and effort fields

title: Session-hash arm assignment for whole-session cost A/B
detail: Per-call holdout (#178) measures local follow-ups, not whole-session cost. Hash session_id to an arm inside the hook, no state file, so whole sessions are compressed or untouched. Run A/A first to size noise; compare cache-weighted tokens per completed task.
test: Log arm and usage per session for two weeks; run A/A first; report minimum detectable effect on cache-weighted tokens before drawing any A/B conclusion.
because: session-level A/B arm assignment

title: Compact at the cold-cache boundary, nudged by idle gap
detail: Stop records a timestamp; UserPromptSubmit sees the idle gap. After idle beyond cache TTL the next request rewrites the whole context anyway, so compacting then may cost little extra and cuts every later read. Show a systemMessage nudge above a context-size floor.
test: From transcript usage fields, find turns after gaps over 5 minutes with 100k+ context; model cost of compact-first versus continue over the next 20 turns.
because: Stop and UserPromptSubmit hooks, systemMessage

title: Ledger-computed PreCompact instructions: live paths kept, dead results named
detail: PreCompact stdout reportedly feeds the summarizer as custom instructions. Instead of static terse-summary advice (#110), compute from the ledger which results were later referenced (edited files, failing tests, identifiers) and which never were; name saved paths for the dead ones.
test: Verify PreCompact stdout reaches the summarizer; on 5 recorded long sessions compare default versus computed instructions with probe questions (#306), counting post-compaction rereads and reruns.
because: PreCompact hook

title: One consolidated note per parallel batch via PostToolBatch
detail: Each compressed result in a parallel batch carries its own note and hook wrapper text. PostToolUse stores the note data and stays silent; PostToolBatch, which fires once per batch, emits one note listing all saved paths, if it accepts additionalContext.
test: Verify PostToolBatch additionalContext reaches the model; issue 5 parallel large Bash calls; count note tokens per-call versus consolidated and check path recall.
because: PostToolBatch hook event

title: Diff hook schema text from installed claude binary per release
detail: The claude binary embeds hook input and output schema text (updatedToolOutput, duration_ms, PostToolBatch, source values); grep -a reads it. A CI job extracts it per Claude Code version and diffs it against fields hook.py reads and writes, catching silent breakage.
test: Run strings on two Claude Code versions, extract hook field names and descriptions, diff them, and assert hook.py's keys (stdout, stderr, content, tool_use_id) still appear.
because: parses Claude binary's embedded hook schema text

title: Seen-set digest injected into recurring scheduled sessions
detail: A recurring cloud or cron task starts fresh each fire and re-lists the same PRs, issues or failures. Stop stores ids seen and verdicts; SessionStart injects them so the run examines only new items and says 'nothing new' in one line.
test: Run a daily PR-triage prompt twice over a fixed repo, with and without the digest; compare tokens in tool results and final report, and check no new item is missed.
because: Stop and SessionStart hooks

title: Strip redundant parameter descriptions: sibling duplicates and restated limits
detail: GitHub schemas repeat 'Repository owner', 'Repository name' and perPage text in every tool; perPage reads '(min 1, max 100)' beside minimum:1 and maximum:100. In a tools/list proxy keep the first copy, leave later exact duplicates bare, and strip clauses restating schema keywords.
test: Dump tools/list for 3 large servers; measure token share of duplicate and restating text; assert stripped numbers equal schema keywords; run 30 tool-call prompts comparing argument validity.
because: schema description dedupe in tools proxy

title: Lazy-load MCP server instructions on first tool call
detail: initialize.instructions blocks (four in this session) sit in the system prompt every turn, used or not. A proxy blanks the field and prepends the text to a server's first tools/call result per session; dormant servers cost nothing.
test: Count instruction tokens per connected server; with a proxy deferring them, run each documented flow as a dry run and check required order and safety rules still hold.
because: MCP-level proxy defers instructions text; deterministic

title: Strip x-mcp-header and other schema extension keys
detail: ToolSearch output shows 'x-mcp-header' on owner and repo of GitHub tools: apparently transport metadata the model cannot use. Strip all x-* keys. Also canary-test whether outputSchema, annotations, title, icons and _meta reach the prompt. Extends #248.
test: Count x-* keys across installed tools/list and tokenise them; add canaries in a toy server's outputSchema, annotations and icons, then grep a logged request for them.
because: schema key stripping in tools proxy

title: Collapse long enum lists in tool schemas to a pattern
detail: Some servers embed enums of dozens of values (timezones, currencies, locales). Replace any enum over N values with a type plus a one-line hint and a pointer to the saved full list; the server still validates.
test: Scan installed tools/list for enums over 20 values, tokenise their share of schema size, then check the model still picks valid values on 20 prompts.
because: schema enum collapse in tools proxy

title: Cross-call key factoring for repeated singleton MCP objects
detail: Each issue_read, get_commit or get_label result repeats the same key names. After the first result per tool in a session, render later singleton objects as values only under a 'same keys as call N' header. Differs from within-output columnar encoding (#32) and entity caching (#145).
test: Replay recorded MCP singleton results per tool; compute key-name tokens in calls 2+; run reader QA on the values-only form, including after a simulated compaction dropping call 1.
because: key factoring against earlier call results
check: Once a full singleton object for (server, tool) is visible, later objects with the identical key list are shown as `#same-keys call=N` plus a values array; the reader's rebuild equals the original key-to-value mapping (order included), and other key lists, tools, servers, duplicate keys, arrays, unprofitable cases and a compacted-away reference get the full object.

title: Drop response fields that echo the call's own arguments
detail: Some MCP results repeat the request: query, owner/repo, page, perPage, or a repository object per item for the repo the model just named. Compare tool_input with tool_response and delete values equal to arguments, noting the removal once.
test: For recorded MCP calls, tokenise response values that exactly equal a tool_input value; list the top keys; check the next turns never cited them.
because: compares tool_input with tool result

title: Collapse single-key wrapper objects in MCP JSON results
detail: Some servers wrap payloads as {"data":{"result":[...]}}, {"response":...} or {"success":true,"data":...}. Peel wrappers whose only informative child is one value, with a path note, saving braces, keys and indentation per call. Differs from GraphQL edges/node unwrapping (#136).
test: Survey recorded MCP results for top-level objects with one non-status key; count peelable depth and tokens; confirm the note lets a reader still locate the payload.
because: peel single-key JSON wrappers

title: Hide write tools by MCP annotations in read-only sessions
detail: Spec tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint) let a generic proxy or settings rule hide every non-read-only tool of any server for review, research or Explore subagents. Differs from hand-written allowlists (#253): works on servers never seen before.
test: Dump annotations from installed servers; count tools marked readOnlyHint true and schema tokens of the rest; run a read-only task with the filtered list and confirm it completes.
because: generic proxy filters tools by MCP annotations

title: Detect duplicate MCP servers across scopes and plugins
detail: The same server can load twice: user config, project .mcp.json, a bundled plugin and a claude.ai connector, each under another prefix. Hash tools/list descriptions per server, flag near-identical pairs, and drop one copy of every schema and instruction block.
test: Script over claude mcp list, plugin manifests and the deferred tool-name list: group tools by normalised name and description hash; report servers with Jaccard above 0.8 and their schema tokens.
because: hash tool definitions in payload, dedupe duplicates

title: Schema-edit regression suite: auto-generated tool-choice prompts
detail: Every schema-shrinking idea needs a tool-choice and argument check. Generate once, per tool, 3 prompts with expected tool and arguments from the original schema, verify they pass uncompressed, then reuse as a gate for any rewrite of descriptions or schemas.
test: Build for github tools: 3 prompts per tool using a cheap model, check pass rate on originals, apply one rewrite (title stripping), report tool-choice and argument-match delta.
because: schema-edit regression suite

title: Bidirectional cloze-redundancy score from the base MLM head
detail: Mask atoms in batches and read the MLM head of mmBERT-small, the base checkpoint ctxprune was tuned from. Atoms both neighbours predict confidently are redundant. Label-free, uses right context unlike left-to-right surprisal (#260), and is a selector, not the #171 metric.
test: On 30 mixed outputs, mask 15% of atoms per pass; compute Spearman against classifier scores, QA at equal tokens for cloze alone and blended, and CPU seconds.
because: local MLM-head selector, pure function of text

title: LLM-synthesised per-command filter programs, validated by replay
detail: Give a coding model about 10 captured outputs of one command family; it writes a small Python filter. Accept only if held-out replays keep every needle line (errors, failing names) and drop 30%+ of chars. Runs without the model; unlike #261, authored rather than mined.
test: For npm install, cargo build and pytest, synthesise from 10 runs, test on 10 held-out; report chars removed, needle recall, and QA against classifier at 0.5.
because: offline authored filters; runtime is local Python

title: Refetch grep patterns become per-family never-drop rules
detail: PostToolUse sees Bash commands that grep a saved original. Extract the pattern, find matching lines, mask digits and hex into templates, and add them to a never-drop list for that command family. A false drop is repaired once. Line-precise, unlike #270's rate bandit.
test: Replay transcripts with refetch greps; on each family's next run, count refetched templates now kept and chars given back.
because: learns from grep command strings; only later outputs change

title: Per-family linear heads on the frozen encoder, routed by command
detail: Keep one shared 140M encoder; train tiny keep/drop linear heads per family (traces, tests, JSON, prose, build logs) on frozen hidden states, selected by command regex. Far cheaper than per-family fine-tunes (#96); one ONNX graph can emit all heads.
test: Train 5 heads on frozen features with existing labels; compare per-source validation ROC-AUC and QA at 0.5 against the shared head.
because: heads routed by command string visible in tool call

title: Line-selection aggregator sweep with top-atom residue for dropped lines
detail: Line-level mode (#87) loses a line whose one rare word matters. Score lines by max, mean or top-2 atom score, and let each dropped line leave its single best atom as a trace. Sweeps aggregator and residue, which #87 leaves unspecified.
test: On 20 logs and test outputs, compare mean, max and top-2 line scores, with and without residue, on needle recall and QA at equal tokens.
because: selection post-processing on atom scores, text only

title: LexRank/TextRank sentence centrality as a model-free prose baseline
detail: Build a TF-IDF cosine graph over sentences, rank by centrality (TextRank, Mihalcea and Tarau 2004; LexRank, Erkan and Radev 2004) plus lead bias, keep top sentences verbatim. Runs in milliseconds, so it can serve prose before the 143 MB model is downloaded.
test: On 30 README, issue and docs outputs, compare QA accuracy and tokens against the classifier at 0.5 and against lead-only truncation.
because: model-free extractive text transform

title: Learned line-type tagger routes mixed outputs to per-segment compressors
detail: A tiny character n-gram tagger labels each line (JSON, table, stack trace, log, prose, code, diff); contiguous segments then get the matching rule or rate. Replaces global sniffing for mixed outputs, such as a log with embedded JSON and a traceback.
test: Label 500 lines from 40 captured outputs; train a fastText-style tagger; report line accuracy and compare per-segment against single-rate compression on QA at equal tokens.
because: local line tagger, text-only routing

title: Indentation-tree folding scored by block maximum atom score
detail: Parse any indented output (describe, plan, YAML, Debug and pprint dumps) into a block tree; fold subtrees deeper than d whose max classifier atom score is low into 'name: (14 lines)'. Generic non-JSON counterpart of depth capping (#132) and per-tool packs.
test: On 25 kubectl describe, terraform, pytest -vv and Debug dumps, compare tokens, needle recall and QA against flat atom deletion at equal size.
because: fold indentation subtrees by local score

title: Sub-line n-gram typicality prior built from earlier family outputs
detail: Keep a hashed word n-gram count table per command family, digits masked, from prior outputs. Phrases frequent across runs, even inside lines whose variable parts differ (trailing hints, shared prefixes), get demoted. Catches what #142 and #261 miss. Kilobytes, no inference.
test: Build tables from 5 runs of npm install or pytest; score the 6th; count demoted phrases the classifier kept and check needle recall.
because: local n-gram table, no inference

title: ctxprune recall: BM25-ranked windows from a saved original
detail: The note tells Claude to grep the saved file, which may return many lines. Ship 'ctxprune recall PATH query -k 3' printing top-ranked line windows with line numbers and a cap. Ranked by query, unlike #208's grep or line slices; #209 is initial selection.
test: From replayed sessions with refetches, compare tokens of the actual refetch command against recall, and whether the needed line lands in the top 3.
because: standalone BM25 recall CLI over saved originals

title: Retrieval query-source ablation: user prompt, command, assistant preamble
detail: #89 and #209 leave the query source open. Hook input includes transcript_path, so the assistant's last text before the tool call (its stated intent) is readable. Compare it with the user prompt and the bare command as BM25 query.
test: On 30 outputs with known answer spans, measure answer-chunk recall at equal tokens for each query source and their concatenation.
because: query-source ablation using payload-visible text

title: Retrospective difference-in-differences at install date from transcripts
detail: Mine existing transcripts for a natural experiment: compare billed cost per user prompt before and after each project's hook install date, using never-hooked projects as controls. Gives realised effect from history, with no new arms or tasks.
test: Pick two projects with mid-history installs; compute weekly cost per prompt from usage fields; fit difference-in-differences with a week-level bootstrap and report the interval.
because: hook install date and Claude Code transcripts

title: Note-only placebo arm: append the note, delete nothing
detail: Separate behaviour caused by the note's mere existence (curiosity reads of the saved file, extra turns) from behaviour caused by missing content. The placebo arm returns the full original plus the real note; compare recoveries and tokens against real compression and no hook.
test: Add CTXPRUNE_PLACEBO=1; run 20-50 paired claude -p tasks in all three arms; count Reads or greps of the saved path and total tokens per arm.
because: placebo arm experiment

title: Zero-token per-call savings line via hook systemMessage
detail: The hook returns only updatedToolOutput and additionalContext. Add the common hook output field systemMessage, e.g. 'ctxprune: 14.2k to 6.1k chars, about 2k tokens'. Costs the model nothing and works in headless or IDE sessions that show no statusline.
test: Verify that systemMessage renders for the user and is absent from the next API request, via a logging proxy or the transcript, using a test hook.
because: hook systemMessage output field

title: Rate-limit headroom: peak uncached input tokens per minute
detail: Tool results are new tokens, so they weigh far more on input-per-minute limits than in a read-dominated bill (one local session: 428k cache-write versus 4.13M cache-read). Subagent fan-out bursts hit 429s first. Value compression in that currency too.
test: Bucket transcript usage by minute (input plus cache_creation); subtract compressible result tokens; compare peak minutes against documented tier limits; check which usage fields the provider counts.
because: rate-limit headroom valuation analysis

title: Reconcile ledger claims against the official organisation cost report
detail: For API-key users, give hook-on and hook-off runs separate API keys or workspaces and read the provider's usage and cost report (Anthropic's Admin API, reportedly) as ground truth, instead of trusting self-computed savings.
test: Run identical scripted claude -p task sets under two keys for a week; pull cost per key per model; compare the delta with the ledger's claimed dollars.
because: reconcile ledger against provider cost report

title: Export savings ledger to git notes, OTLP counters, Actions summary
detail: Three sinks beyond a statusline: a Stop hook appends tokens, dollars and savings as a git note (refs/notes/ctxprune, hashes unchanged) for cost per PR; OTLP/HTTP counters to OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT; a table in $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for CI runs.
test: Write a git note from a fake Stop hook, confirming the hash is unchanged; send one OTLP metric to a debug collector (200 ms timeout); render a step-summary table.
because: Stop hook appends the ledger

title: Skip-reason ledger priced in tokens left on the table
detail: Every hook exit logs exactly one reason code (below threshold, verbatim regex, ratio over 0.95, server error, opt-out, unrecognised shape) with estimated tokens. Pricing the mass per reason shows which gate costs the most money to keep.
test: Add a reason enum to the debug log; replay 200 recorded events; verify one reason per uncompressed event; rank reasons by token mass.
because: skip-reason ledger priced in tokens

title: Local-model profile: threshold from prefill tokens per second
detail: With local models (Ollama, llama.cpp) cost is prefill seconds and KV-cache memory, not dollars, and laptop prefill can be slow. Derive min_chars from measured prompt-processing speed versus hook milliseconds; break-even may sit far below 6,000 chars.
test: Run llama-bench prompt processing on a small GGUF model here; compute seconds saved per 1k tokens against hook wall time with and without serve; solve for the threshold.
because: self-hosted local-model prefill economics

title: Pricing-cliff guard: compress harder just below the premium tier
detail: Some Claude models reportedly bill requests above 200k input tokens at a premium, a step not a slope (check current pricing). Tokens just under the cliff are worth the premium on every later turn, so raise the rate only in that band.
test: Verify the current tier threshold; parse transcripts for turns above 150k context; count premium crossings that a 10% smaller history would avoid, priced from the table.
because: one vendor's 200k premium pricing tier

title: Break-even harm rate from natural detour repair costs
detail: Tolerable harm rate p* = tokens saved per call divided by mean repair cost of a wrong action. Estimate repair cost from detours already in transcripts (failed Edit on stale text to next success), then require the measured harm upper bound to sit below p*.
test: Find Edit failures in transcripts; sum tokens until the next successful Edit; report median and p90 repair cost; compute p* for a 2k-token saving.
because: break-even harm analysis from tool-call traces

title: Rewrite clear_thinking keep:all to thinking_turns in proxy
detail: Claude Code's binary builds context_management edits with clear_thinking_20251015 and keep:'all' when thinking is on, so every past thinking block is re-read each turn. Proxy sets keep to thinking_turns N, batched at cold gaps since clearing reportedly breaks the cached suffix.
test: Replay one thinking-enabled session through the proxy with keep all versus thinking_turns 2; compare input, cache_creation and cache_read tokens per request, plus next-action agreement.
because: Anthropic clear_thinking context_management edit

title: Strip cache_control from requests whose prefix is never reread
detail: A cache write costs 1.25x input and is wasted when no later request reads it. One-shot claude -p runs and utility side calls may still carry breakpoints; the binary's DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU switch is per model family only. Proxy decides per request group.
test: In the logging proxy, flag requests with cache_creation>0 whose prefix hash never gets a cache_read; sum write tokens times 0.25 per model and request group.
because: strips Anthropic cache_control

title: Abort generation on degenerate repetition loops mid-stream
detail: Proxy watches SSE text_delta and tool-input deltas for a repeating n-gram, then closes upstream and ends the message cleanly. Output tokens stop accruing at disconnect (to be confirmed). Targets runaway loops that otherwise run to max_tokens.
test: Replay a mock SSE with a looping text block; assert the client gets a valid message_stop. Then cancel a real streamed call midway and compare billed output_tokens.
because: proxy aborts degenerate streaming output

title: Rewrite tool_use arguments in the response stream
detail: Proxy buffers tool_use input_json_delta (or OpenAI tool_calls arguments), applies PreToolUse-style rules such as quiet flags, head caps and dropping Bash description, then emits the edited call. Client runs and stores the edited call, covering hookless agents.
test: Mock-stream a Bash tool_use with a bare pytest command through the proxy; assert the client receives -q appended, valid JSON deltas and unchanged stop_reason; repeat with OpenAI tool_calls.
because: proxy rewrites tool_use args; client stores edited call

title: Baseline arms: history-level reducers (middle-out, trim_messages)
detail: Gateways already ship lossy history reducers: OpenRouter's middle-out transform and LiteLLM's trim_messages (both reportedly). Add them as baselines at equal token counts, so ctxprune claims are measured against what a base-URL swap gives for free.
test: On 50 recorded long sessions, shrink to ctxprune's 0.5 token budget with each reducer; score with the existing reader QA harness.
because: history-reducer baseline arms

title: Stub aged server-tool result blocks in resent history
detail: SDK loops using Anthropic web_search or web_fetch server tools resend web_search_tool_result entries (with encrypted_content) and fetched pages every turn. Proxy keeps title and URL, drops bodies after N turns; verify the API accepts edited blocks.
test: Run a multi-turn web_search conversation, resend with old results cut to titles; record API acceptance, citation errors and the input_tokens drop.
because: Anthropic server-tool blocks with encrypted_content

title: Proxy adds defer_loading to tool arrays for non-Claude-Code clients
detail: Anthropic's tool search beta (advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20 and a defer_loading flag, both in the local binary) hides schemas until discovered. Proxy marks all but a pinned hot set deferred and appends the search tool, for SDK and Cline-style clients sending 30+ tools.
test: Send a 50-tool request via the proxy with and without defer_loading; compare usage.input_tokens, then run 10 tasks counting extra search calls and failures.
because: Anthropic tool-search beta API feature

title: Exact-match reader-call cache plus Message Batches for evals
detail: QA sweeps re-ask identical (model, prompt) pairs across reruns and rate sweeps. A hash-keyed on-disk cache at temperature 0, with misses sent through Message Batches (50% discount per Anthropic docs), cuts the cost of measuring.
test: Re-run the QA sweep twice and count second-run hits; send 200 uncached prompts through batches, compare bill and wall time.
because: dev-time eval cost cache and batches

title: Ledger of tokens billed on interrupted and retried requests
detail: Transcripts omit requests that ended without message_stop: Esc interrupts, mid-stream 5xx, client retries. Their input and partial output are billed and then regenerated. Only a proxy sees them; this sizes the waste and any prefill-resume fix.
test: Log per-request terminal state in the passthrough proxy over a day; sum input and output tokens of requests lacking message_stop, grouped by cause.
because: proxy ledger of billed retried requests

title: Serve client obeys HTTP_PROXY and silently loads model
detail: urlopen in hook._compress honors http_proxy. Verified: with http_proxy set and no no_proxy, a running local server was ignored and the in-process Compressor path was taken. Proxied hosts pay about 2 s and a model copy per call. Fix: ProxyHandler({}).
test: Set http_proxy to a dead port, start a stub server, call hook._compress with CTXPRUNE_SERVER set; assert Compressor is never built. Add to test_hook.py.
because: bypass HTTP_PROXY for local serve client

title: Verbatim-skip regex holes: --patch, -pS, newlines, then/do
detail: Verified by running VERBATIM_CMD: git log --patch, -pS, -u, git stash show -p and git cat-file -p are not skipped (-p needs a word boundary). With no re.M, newline-separated cat, 'then cat' and '{ cat' also escape, so source gets pruned. Complements #292 and #194.
test: Add these ten strings to test_verbatim_commands_are_skipped in tests/test_hook.py (all fail today). Compare a shlex stage splitter on captured Bash events.
because: command-string skip regex fix

title: MCP verbatim name regex errs in both directions
detail: VERBATIM_MCP is an unanchored substring match: get_file_history, get_files_changed and get_file_metadata are never compressed (lost savings), while view_file, open_file, cat and serena find_symbol (source bodies) are compressed. Verified with the regex.
test: Run the regex over tool names from installed MCP servers and transcripts; hand-label which return file bodies; report false-skip and false-compress counts.
because: fix MCP tool-name verbatim regex

title: Hook re-prunes output of the ctxprune CLI itself
detail: AGENTS.md tells agents to run 'cmd | ctxprune --keep 0.33'. The hook has no skip for ctxprune commands (verified), so output over 6000 chars is pruned again at 0.5: uncontrolled double loss, a second note, a second saved file.
test: Feed the hook command 'x | ctxprune --keep 0.33' with 8000-char stdout; it compresses today. Add a skip for ctxprune and python -m ctxprune commands.
because: skip rule keyed on command string

title: Scan agent writes for strings spliced by compression
detail: Find 6-word n-grams in later Write, Edit, commit and PR text that occur in the compressed result but nowhere contiguous in the saved original. Counts durable repo artifacts corrupted by quoting pruned text, a downstream harm QA never sees; complements #182.
test: Join transcripts to saved originals via the note path; extract tool_use inputs after each compressed result; report spliced n-gram rate per 100 compressed outputs.
because: downstream harm audit of agent writes

title: JSON parse survival under the shipped keep_structure=False config
detail: hook.py sends force_protected only, so braces, quotes, commas and colons can be deleted; the README says LLMLingua-2 breaks JSON. Measure how often MCP JSON outputs stay parseable, and the token cost of keep_structure=True.
test: Run the hook config over 200 saved MCP JSON outputs; count json.loads successes with keep_structure False versus True; compare LLM-token ratio of each.
because: JSON parse survival measurement

title: detok flattens indentation after any dropped preceding atom
detail: Verified: when the atom before a line-leading kept atom was dropped, _merge_ws returns a bare newline and the original indentation is lost. YAML hierarchy, traceback frames and nested JSON flatten. Keeping newline-led whitespace costs few tokens.
test: Count kept line-leading atoms whose indentation changed over 100 saved outputs; ask parent-key and calling-frame questions on flattened versus indentation-preserved variants at equal tokens.
because: detokenizer fix, deterministic text transform

title: Time-budgeted windows: keep unscored tail verbatim at deadline
detail: In-process compression is all-or-nothing against the 60 s host kill; a very large output wastes the whole run and passes uncompressed. Score windows in order until about 40 s, keep the remaining windows verbatim, and still emit a note.
test: Set the deadline to 2 s via env, feed a 300 KB log; assert output returns in time, early windows compressed, tail verbatim, note names the cutoff.
because: local compute deadline; same text transform on windows

title: Ledger overcount guard: dedupe usage per message id, cross-check ccusage
detail: Claude Code JSONL repeats usage on every content-block line: here 35 assistant lines held 14 message ids, 12 repeated. Naive sums overcount. Sum once per id (last line), then compare against ccusage, a community cost reader that reportedly dedupes by message and request id.
test: Parse several real sessions; compare naive versus per-id totals, then diff daily totals against ccusage JSON output; chase gaps over a few percent, including sidechain files.
because: Claude Code JSONL message-id quirk

title: Bridge MCP servers into shell CLIs such as mcp2cli
detail: Wrappers like mcp2cli (Show HN claims 96-99% fewer tokens; author's figure) expose MCP tools as shell commands: schemas leave the prompt, and results flow through jq, head and the Bash hook. Checkly measured near-equal totals for Playwright, so benchmark per server.
test: Wrap github and one browser server; run 10 identical tasks via native MCP versus CLI bridge; compare schema tokens, result tokens and turn counts, not only per-call size.
because: MCP-to-CLI bridge, schemas leave prompt
check: A CLI bridge exposes 48 MCP tools as shell commands (list, <tool> --help, <tool> --arg value) with typed arguments that survive hostile quoting, exit status 64 for usage errors, 2 for tool errors and nothing on stdout when it fails; schemas leave the prompt, and a cache-aware accounting model (not Checkly's measurement, which it does not reproduce: ~+16% here vs ~0% there) shows a large win for a many-tool server with filterable results and a small one when every result must be read in full.

title: Run formatters in Stop hook, not per-edit PostToolUse
detail: Claude Code reportedly injects a 'file modified by user or linter' reminder with the changed lines when a file changes outside the model's edit. A per-edit PostToolUse formatter, as #549 suggests, may add one after every Edit. Batch formatting at Stop or pre-commit.
test: Grep transcripts for the reminder text; edit one file five times with formatter at PostToolUse versus Stop, via logging proxy; compare reminder tokens and extra Reads.
because: Stop hook formatter and harness modified-file reminder

title: Codex output knobs: tool_output_token_limit, model_verbosity, reasoning summary
detail: Codex config reportedly bounds stored tool output via tool_output_token_limit (community posts cite 8000-12000; a per-MCP-tool limit is unverified), and offers model_verbosity and model_reasoning_summary. Codex reportedly lacks an output-rewrite hook, so these caps are the main lever.
test: Verify key names in docs; run 10 codex exec tasks per setting (default, limits 12000 and 6000, verbosity low); compare rollout JSONL tokens, pass rate and hidden failures.
because: Codex config knobs

title: Codex auto-compact limit and compact_prompt override sweep
detail: Codex config reportedly accepts model_auto_compact_token_limit (a tuning guide's example is 64000) and a custom compact_prompt that keeps decisions and changed file paths. Codex counterpart to the Claude-side autocompact items; needs its own recall probe.
test: Replay a 60-turn Codex task at default versus 64000 limit plus custom prompt; after compaction ask 10 probe questions on earlier facts; compare recall and total tokens.
because: Codex config settings

title: Read delta for files changed outside the model's edits
detail: qdf-hook reportedly returns a unified diff against its cached copy when a file changed between reads. Own-edit hunks are covered by #144; changes from git pull, branch switch, formatters or teammates are not. Emit a diff only while the earlier Read is in context.
test: From transcripts, find re-Reads where mtime changed but no Edit touched the path; sum changed lines versus file length; check how often an Edit follows.
because: diff against earlier Read still in payload

title: Census of files every new session re-reads on orientation
detail: Each new session may re-read the same README, manifest and entry files before real work; the claude-learn tool reportedly flags files read three or more times. Census the first 15 tool calls per session by repo; frequent paths become a skeleton, pointer or digest.
test: Group first 15 tool calls per session by repo from ~/.claude/projects; rank paths by share of sessions and tokens; estimate savings if the top 5 became a 300-token digest.
because: census of re-read files from tool calls

title: Sweep CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS against truncated tool_use inputs
detail: Community guides cap CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS to trim prose, but a cap below a large Write or multi-Edit input could cut the call mid-JSON and force a retry. Set the cap from the p99 output_tokens of tool_use-bearing messages in the deduped ledger.
test: From the ledger compute output_tokens percentiles for Write/Edit versus text-only messages; run 10 file-creation tasks at three caps; count max_tokens stops, retries and total output tokens.
because: Claude Code environment variable

title: Collapse docstrings to first sentence in exploratory source dumps
detail: claude-compress (PyPI) reportedly collapses block comments to one line and multi-line docstrings to their first sentence on cat, head and tail, claiming 15-50% on source. #506 strips only comments and blanks. Docstrings carry contracts, so gate on no Edit following; keep the original.
test: Measure docstring token share in 50 Python cat/Read results from transcripts; replay 20 questions answerable only from docstring bodies and count answers lost.
because: deterministic docstring collapsing of source output

title: Route read-only subagents and utility work to Haiku
detail: Community guides (AutoScout24 blog, DEV tips) advise model: haiku in subagent frontmatter, and reportedly a CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL env var, for searchers and log triage. Token counts stay equal but price and quota weight per token fall. Risk: weaker reads cause extra turns.
test: Run 10 repo-search tasks with searcher subagents on Sonnet versus Haiku; compare billed cost or quota use, turns and answer correctness using ledger prices.
because: subagent frontmatter and env var; tokens unchanged

title: Strip JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS 'Picked up' banner from JVM launches
