detail: Every java, javac, mvn and gradle launch prints 'Picked up JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS: ...' on stderr, and forked daemons and surefire JVMs repeat it. Measured here: 788 chars, 303 o200k tokens per launch. Drop every copy and keep other warnings.
test: Run java -version, mvn -v and a 5-module mvn test with the variable set; count banner copies and tokens; strip; confirm exit codes and real warnings are untouched.
because: drops JVM Picked up banner lines

title: Inject compact diagnostic flags: cargo short, clang no-caret
detail: For build or check commands, PreToolUse appends cargo --message-format=short, clang -fno-caret-diagnostics, gcc -fno-diagnostics-show-caret or xcodebuild -quiet. Measured on a 2-error cargo check: 400 vs 184 o200k tokens. Help text is lost, so the note says how to rerun without.
test: Break 20 files in Rust, C++ and Xcode samples; compare default versus compact tokens; replay fixes to check agents still resolve errors without help text.
because: appends compact diagnostic flags to build commands

title: Dedupe Go race detector reports by access-site set
detail: go test -race prints a WARNING: DATA RACE block per goroutine pair. Measured: a small test gave 4 reports (1,768 of 1,878 o200k tokens) but 2 unique sets of top-frame file:line. Keep the first per key with a count; TSan likewise.
test: Run go test -race with 20 goroutines on 3 shared variables; count reports versus unique keys; verify every distinct racing line pair and read/write kind survives.
because: dedupe race reports by site

title: Drop expected/actual dumps when a diff follows
detail: Go testify prints expected, actual, then a Diff block; Rust pretty_assertions and gtest 'Which is:' lines add similar duplicates (from memory). Where a diff exists, keep it and elide the full dumps.
test: Fail assert.Equal on a 60-field struct and Rust assert_eq on nested Vecs with {:#?}; compare tokens; check the differing field stays identifiable.
because: elides expected/actual dumps when diff follows

title: Maven: redirect surefire test stdout to files, trim stack traces
detail: For mvn test or verify, PreToolUse adds -Dmaven.test.redirectTestOutputToFile=true and -DtrimStackTrace=true (property names reportedly). Spring Boot banners, context logs and framework frames then land in target/surefire-reports; failure summaries reportedly stay on the console.
test: Verify that failures stay visible: run mvn test on a Spring Boot sample with 10 classes and 2 failures, with and without the flags; compare console tokens and report files.
because: adds maven flags to command string

title: Cut cause messages repeated inside wrapper exception messages
detail: new RuntimeException(cause) copies cause.toString() into its own message, older Spring appends '; nested exception is', and .NET AggregateException embeds inner messages before '--->'. Each Caused by line then repeats text already printed. Replace the embedded copy with '...' when the cause line follows.
test: Collect 30 Spring bean-creation and Hibernate failures plus .NET AggregateException traces; measure the share of characters that are substring repeats; confirm the root-cause message survives intact.
because: cut repeated cause messages

title: .NET console logger: join two-line records, fold request pairs
detail: The default .NET console logger (dotnet run, ASP.NET Core, EF Core) reportedly prints 'info: Category[eventId]' then the message on an indented second line. Join to one line, then fold 'Request starting'/'Request finished' pairs and EF 'Executed DbCommand' boilerplate. The join is lossless.
test: Capture dotnet run output for a webapi sample after 20 curl requests; tokenise before and after; verify status codes, paths and SQL text survive.
because: join and fold .NET log records

title: Strip Version, Culture, PublicKeyToken tails from .NET type names
detail: Assembly-qualified names in .NET exceptions, serializer and DI errors repeat ', Version=8.0.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b77a5c561934e089' after each type, often nested in generic brackets (from memory). Strip the tail, keeping the version only for the assembly a load failure names.
test: Collect 20 .NET exceptions with generic types plus FileLoadException cases; count tokens in the tails; strip; confirm a version mismatch can still be diagnosed.
because: strips .NET assembly-name tails

title: Ninja and Bazel failures: hoist repeated compiler command lines
detail: After each 'FAILED: target', ninja prints the full compiler command (Bazel prints one too, reportedly). Measured: in a 2-file failing CMake build, commands were 278 of 674 o200k tokens, the second repeating the first's flags. Print compiler plus source and hoist shared flags once.
test: Break 5 files in a CMake project with many -I and -D flags; build with ninja -k 0; compare tokens; confirm the saved original keeps the exact rerun command.
because: hoists repeated compiler command lines
check: Flags shared by every failed compiler command are printed once as '[ctxprune: @1 = ...]', each command becomes 'compiler @1 <its own flags>' without the -MD/-MT/-MF/-o dependency flags the FAILED target already names; per failed target the compiler, source and multiset of compilation flags, every diagnostic and every ninja/bazel status line are unchanged.
check_loses: the original order of flags (shared flags move to the front), the -MD -MT -MF and -o arguments of ninja compile commands (the FAILED line names the object; the saved original keeps the exact rerun command), and whitespace inside commands

title: Fold expanded libstdc++ type names to std::string-style aliases
detail: Linker, ASan, Valgrind and gdb print expanded names like std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> >. A fixed table (string, default allocator, less, char_traits arguments) shortens them; a partial regex pass took one linker error from 182 to 93 o200k tokens.
test: Collect 20 linker errors and ASan/Valgrind traces from STL-heavy code; apply the table; check distinct symbols never collapse together and agents still locate the missing definition.
because: alias table for libstdc++ type names

title: Drop system-header regions from gcc -E and clang -E output
detail: Preprocessor output marks regions with linemarkers like '# 12 "/usr/include/..." 3'; flag 3 means system header. Measured: including <iostream> and <vector> gave 291k o200k tokens, 18 outside system headers, so Bash truncation hides user code. Keep user regions.
test: Run g++ -E on 5 files including Boost or Qt headers; drop flag-3 regions; check macro-expanded user code stays in order and tokens fall.
because: drops system-header regions from preprocessor output
check: Replaces every region of gcc/clang -E output that belongs to a file entered as a system header (linemarker flags 1 and 3) by one '// [ctxprune: N lines of system headers elided (...)]' line; user regions, their linemarkers and the macro-expanded text in them, including flag-3 markers on the user's own file, are unchanged.
check_loses: all text from system headers (declarations, inline functions and macros from <stdio.h>, <vector>, ...), and the linemarkers inside them

title: Unwrap xcresulttool typed-value JSON: _type/_value scalars
detail: Legacy 'xcrun xcresulttool get --format json' reportedly wraps every scalar as {"_type":{"_name":"String"},"_value":"x"} and arrays as _values (from memory, unmeasured). Rewrite to plain values, drop _type for primitives, keep it for objects. Newer Xcode subcommands may emit leaner JSON.
test: Verify that the installed Xcode still emits the wrappers: capture xcresulttool output from a 50-test run; unwrap; compare tokens; ask which tests failed and their durations on both forms.
because: unwrap typed-value JSON

title: Markdown links: collapse [X](X), drop relative targets, hoist URLs
detail: Bot comments render [https://...](https://...), the same string twice; collapsing that is lossless. Then drop relative and #anchor targets, move external URLs to numbered definitions at the end, optionally strip ** markers. Measured: link targets were 13% of o200k tokens over 107 markdown files.
test: Run on 30 READMEs, changelogs, PR bodies and docs pages; tokenise before and after; ask 'where is X documented' and 'which PR' questions; saved original keeps every URL.
because: collapse markdown link duplication

title: Drop contents lists that restate later headings
detail: doctoc blocks, [TOC] lists, 'On this page' sidebars, anchor-only README lists and PDF contents pages restate headings that follow. When entries match later headings, replace the list with a one-line note. Measured: TOC lines were 5,360 of 710,687 o200k tokens in 300 READMEs.
test: Take 20 READMEs, docs pages and pdftotext outputs with contents lists; drop with a title-match check; ask where-is-section questions on both versions; compare tokens.
because: drop contents lists restating headings

title: Replace image embeds and badge rows with alt-text stubs
detail: READMEs, docs pages and issue markdown carry shields.io badge rows, screenshots, linked logos and img tags the model cannot see. Replace with [img: alt] or a count. Measured: badge lines held 19,043 of 710,687 o200k tokens in 300 READMEs. Extends #326 (issue bodies only).
test: Count image and badge tokens in 30 READMEs and docs pages; replace; confirm alt text survives; ask which CI and license badges exist; keep the original in the saved file.
because: text stubs for markdown image embeds

title: Digest the HTML head: keep title, description, canonical
detail: Raw curl output opens with a head full of hreflang alternates, preload and icon links, and og:/twitter: meta. Keep title, description, canonical, robots and lang; fold the rest to counts. Synthetic 15 hreflang links: 406 o200k tokens.
test: curl 15 sites; measure head token share; keep listed fields; ask 'what is the canonical URL and page language' and a link-hunting question; check no body content is dropped.
because: digest HTML head metadata

title: Strip docs-site chrome left after HTML-to-Markdown conversion
detail: Converted docs pages keep per-heading permalink links ('Direct link to', pilcrow, #), 'Skip to main content', 'Edit this page', 'Was this page helpful?', pagers and cookie text. Drop by anchored regex and phrase list. Synthetic 10-heading page: 249 vs 70 o200k tokens.
test: Convert 15 Docusaurus, Sphinx and MkDocs pages with html2text or pandoc; count chrome tokens; strip; assert prose and code blocks unchanged; compare with #39.
because: strip docs-site chrome text

title: Keep only the project's language in multi-SDK doc examples
detail: API reference pages show one example per SDK language (curl, Python, JS, Go, Java); HTML-to-Markdown inlines all variants. Detect adjacent fences with different info strings, keep the languages in the repo's manifests, and stub the rest as '[Go, Java variants omitted]'.
test: Fetch 10 API reference pages; count runs of 3+ adjacent fences with differing languages and their token share; ask 'show the call in our language' questions.
because: project language inferable from payload paths

title: Steer HTML and docx converters to compact-output flags
detail: Converter defaults add tokens: pandoc's markdown writer wraps at 72 columns and can emit {#id .class} attributes and []{#anchor} spans; lynx -dump appends a numbered link list. For reading intent, rewrite to pandoc -t gfm --wrap=none, lynx -nolist, html2text --ignore-links.
test: Run 10 docx and 10 HTML inputs through default and rewritten commands; tokenise both; diff text to confirm only layout and link lists changed; verify Bash updatedInput honors the rewrite.
because: rewrites converter commands to compact flags

title: Office XML reads: strip rsid noise or extract text only
detail: Agents run unzip -p on docx, pptx and xlsx and read XML full of w:rsid*, w14:paraId, proofErr and repeated rPr runs. For display-only reads, drop those and merge equal runs; for content reads, extract w:t/a:t text and resolve sharedStrings. Synthetic paragraph: 620 vs 360 tokens.
test: Unpack 10 real Office files; measure attribute token share; strip with lxml; diff extracted text against pandoc output; replay string-replace edits to count old_string misses; gate display-only.
because: text transform on Office XML output

title: Replace XML closing-tag names with </> in display-only reads
detail: Indented XML (pom, Android layouts, OOXML, SOAP) repeats each element name in its closing tag. Emit '</>' and rely on nesting and indentation. Synthetic: OOXML 266 vs 194 tokens, pom 336 vs 280 (o200k). Conflicts with #525 indent stripping; choose one per file.
test: Apply to 20 XML files; tokenise; ask 'which element contains X' and 'what is the parent of Y' on both; mark failures when single-line or unindented; exclude files to edit.
because: collapse XML closing-tag names

title: Sitemap XML to prefix-hoisted URL lists
detail: sitemap.xml and sitemap indexes fetched by curl wrap each URL in loc, lastmod, changefreq and priority tags. Print a base prefix plus one path per line, optionally with lastmod only; drop changefreq and priority. Synthetic 30-URL sitemap: 2,200 vs 191 o200k tokens.
test: Fetch 10 real sitemaps; convert; assert the loc set is identical after re-expansion; tokenise; ask 'is /x/y listed' and 'newest page' questions.
because: sitemap XML to URL list

title: Token share of markup syntax classes in real outputs
detail: Before building markup rules, tokenise saved outputs and transcript results by syntax class: link targets, tags and attributes, entities, escapes, image embeds, diff signs, TOC lines. Measured here (o200k) on 107 markdown files: link targets 13%, emphasis 0.2%, images 0.9%, HTML tags 1.5%.
test: Run a regex classifier over ~/.claude transcript tool results plus saved originals; emit per-class token share per tool; rank rules by share times firing frequency; drop classes under 1%.
because: markup token-share measurement

title: Deny parent reads of subagent transcripts and task output files
detail: Models sometimes Read or tail a background agent's output file or sidechain JSONL, pulling every intermediate tool call into the parent and defeating isolation. A PreToolUse deny on those paths says 'wait for the final report'.
test: Grep transcripts for Read/tail/cat on subagent or task output paths and sum their tokens; verify the deny reason reaches the model and it waits.
because: PreToolUse deny on harness subagent transcript paths

title: Cap subagent turns with maxTurns from the observed tail
detail: Subagent frontmatter maxTurns (reportedly supported) hard-stops runaway exploration that burns tokens before any report lands. Set it per agent type from the measured turn distribution so only the long tail is cut.
test: Verify that maxTurns is honored; histogram tool calls per subagent type from sidechain transcripts; sum tokens beyond p90; run 10 tasks with the cap and compare report usefulness.
because: subagent frontmatter maxTurns

title: Steer follow-ups to continue a finished subagent, not respawn
detail: Agent results reportedly carry an agentId, and SendMessage can continue a stopped subagent with its explored context intact. A PreToolUse hook on Agent spots a new prompt overlapping an earlier subagent's paths and denies with 'continue agent X'.
test: Verify that SendMessage resumes a finished subagent; count Agent spawns sharing paths or identifiers with an earlier subagent in one session; compare tokens against a fresh spawn.
because: PreToolUse hook on subagent tool

title: Downgrade Explore thoroughness from 'very thorough' for narrow lookups
detail: The Explore subagent reportedly takes quick, medium or very thorough in its prompt, and parents often pick the highest. PreToolUse updatedInput rewrites it to medium when the ask names one symbol or path, keeping very thorough for broad surveys.
test: Verify that updatedInput can rewrite an Agent prompt; run 10 lookup questions at each level; compare subagent tool calls, tokens, report size and correctness.
because: PreToolUse rewrite of subagent tool input

title: Fan out headless children by forking a warmed parent session
detail: Instead of each claude -p child re-reading the same files, one parent reads them, then children fork its session (--resume ID --fork-session, reportedly). Children read the shared prefix at cache-read price. Differs from #303, which only shares the system prompt.
test: Verify that forking works headless; run four forks versus four fresh sessions reading the same 30k-token files; compare summed cache_creation and cache_read within the 5-minute TTL.
because: claude --resume --fork-session CLI feature

title: Delegation leakage: parent re-reads files its subagents already read
detail: Subagent isolation only pays if the parent does not redo the work. Join sidechain Read and Grep targets with later main-thread Reads of the same paths and price the repeat. High leakage means reports omit facts the parent needs.
test: Over 20 transcripts intersect sidechain-read paths with parent Reads within 10 turns; report repeated tokens per Agent call, split by agent type.
because: subagent sidechain is harness-specific

title: Stub aged skill bodies in history; allow reload on demand
detail: A Skill call adds the whole SKILL.md as a message that stays all session. After N turns with no mention of the skill's name or paths, a proxy or resume surgery swaps it for its description plus 'invoke again to reload'. Pairs with #242.
test: Sum skill-body tokens times later turns across transcripts; on 5 multi-step skills check the model re-invokes the skill when it needs it after a stub.
because: Skill invocation bodies are a harness feature

title: Route compaction summaries to a cheaper model on cold cache
detail: A proxy recognises the compaction request and swaps in a cheaper model when an idle gap already expired the cache, so the big read bills at a lower rate. With a warm cache keep the main model. Gate on summary quality.
test: Capture one /compact request, replay it to two model tiers, grade both summaries with the #306 probe questions, and price each run from usage and published rates.
because: model routing price lever, not token saving

title: Partial compaction from a rewind point keeps the cached prefix
detail: Claude Code's rewind menu reportedly offers 'summarize from here', compacting only later messages. Earlier messages stay byte-identical so their cache entry survives, unlike full /compact, which restarts from a new summary. Measure cache writes and recall.
test: Verify that the option exists; on two copies of one 100k session, run full /compact versus summarize-from-here at the midpoint; compare next-request cache_creation and answers to 8 probe questions.
because: Claude Code rewind menu

title: Resume-from-summary versus full resume on stale large sessions
detail: Claude Code reportedly offers a summary-based resume for large old sessions, while a full resume re-caches the whole transcript cold. Measure first-request tokens and continuation quality per mode, then set a policy by age and size.
test: Verify that the summary-resume option exists in the installed version; resume three 100k+ sessions both ways; record first-request cache_creation and ask five continuation questions.
because: Claude Code resume modes

title: BM25 memory retrieval at UserPromptSubmit instead of an always-loaded index
detail: Auto-memory loads the MEMORY.md index every session whether or not it matters. A hook matches the prompt against entry descriptions and injects only the top few topic entries as additionalContext, so unrelated memories never enter the context.
test: On 5 real memory dirs, replay past prompts where a topic file was Read; measure top-3 recall and compare injected tokens against index size.
because: UserPromptSubmit hook over auto-memory files

title: Share one brief file across parallel Agent prompts
detail: Parallel Agent calls often restate the same background paragraph, paid as output tokens and kept in parent history. Steer the parent to write the brief once to a file and give each prompt only 'read brief.md' plus its unique ask.
test: Compute the longest common prefix across sibling Agent prompts in transcripts, times sibling count; A/B file-brief versus inline on 5 fan-outs for result quality.
because: Claude Code Agent tool prompt steering

title: Digest HAR files to one line per request
detail: HAR 1.2 entries carry full headers, cookies, timings and base64 bodies per request. Emit 'METHOD url status ms bytes' per entry, truncate bodies only for failed, slow or XHR rows, and fold static assets to counts. Distinct from live network lists (#351).
test: Export 3 HARs from DevTools; tokenise raw versus digest; assert every 4xx/5xx and the slowest 5 entries survive; ask 5 debugging questions on both.
because: text digest of HAR output
check: A HAR file becomes one 'METHOD url status ms bytes type' row per kept entry (failed, slow, 5 slowest, XHR/fetch, documents, non-GET; 160 characters of text body on failed, slow and XHR rows) plus one 'static (N requests: ...)' line; the entry count, total bytes, every 4xx/5xx/status-0 request, the five slowest, every XHR/fetch request, the request count per resource type and every row at or above 1000 ms are unchanged.
check_loses: request and response headers, cookies, timings breakdown, initiator, IPs, base64 bodies, bodies beyond 160 characters, and the identity of individual successful static assets (only their per-type count, bytes and slowest time stay)

title: OCR engine outputs (hOCR, TSV, Textract JSON) to plain lines
detail: hOCR wraps each word in a span with bbox and confidence; tesseract TSV has 12 columns per word; Textract and Vision JSON add polygons and ids. Render text lines, flagging only words under a confidence floor. Synthetic 20 hOCR words: 787 vs 40 tokens (o200k).
test: Run tesseract hocr/tsv and pdftotext -bbox-layout on 5 scans; tokenise before and after; assert joined text equals tesseract plain output.
because: text transform on OCR engine output
check: tesseract hOCR or TSV becomes plain text lines (a blank line between paragraphs, '[page N]' before later pages) with words under confidence 60 written 'word[?NN]'; the words of every line in order, the paragraph and page structure and every low-confidence word with its confidence are unchanged (the rewrite is skipped when the hOCR parse and an independent regex parse disagree).
check_loses: word, line and block bounding boxes, baselines, font sizes, ids, the confidence of confident words, bold markup, and the image name and resolution

title: ffmpeg, ffprobe and yt-dlp banner, progress and format-list pack
detail: ffmpeg prints a configuration line of --enable flags plus a libav version table, then frame= progress; yt-dlp -J lists every format and per-language caption URL. Drop the banner (or inject -hide_banner), fold progress, keep streams, duration, chapters. Synthetic ffmpeg banner: 499 tokens (o200k).
test: Capture ffmpeg -i, ffprobe -show_streams and yt-dlp -J on 5 files; tokenise; assert codec, resolution, duration and errors survive; ask 5 stream questions.
because: drops ffmpeg/yt-dlp banner and progress text

title: Strip spoken disfluencies from ASR and meeting transcripts
detail: Drop um, uh, 'you know', immediate repeats ('the the', 'is is') and false-start fragments in speech transcripts from Whisper, Zoom or auto-captions. Synthetic sentence: 26 vs 11 tokens (o200k). A stricter mode could also drop hedges like 'basically'.
test: Run on 5 real transcripts; tokenise; hand-audit 100 sampled removals for meaning loss; ask 10 content questions on raw versus stripped text.
because: text transform on transcripts

title: Strip defaults and float noise from design-file JSON
detail: Figma REST node JSON repeats blendMode, visible, opacity 1, empty effects/strokes and 17-digit 0-1 float colours and coordinates. Drop defaults, convert colours to hex, round to 2 decimals. Synthetic node: 129 vs 38 tokens (o200k). Lottie, Sketch and Excalidraw are likely similar.
test: Fetch a real Figma file via the nodes endpoint; tokenise before and after; assert names, hierarchy and text survive; ask 10 layout and colour questions.
because: strip defaults in design JSON
check: In a Figma REST document, default-valued keys (blendMode NORMAL/PASS_THROUGH, visible true, opacity 1, empty effects/strokes/fills/exportSettings, TOP/LEFT constraints, ...) are dropped, {r,g,b,a} colours become hex, other floats round to 2 decimals; every node's id, name, type, text, children order, box, colour, non-default visibility, opacity, blend, effect, radius and font is unchanged.
check_loses: the 17th-digit noise of coordinates and sizes (rounded to 2 decimals), colour precision beyond 8 bits per channel, keys equal to Figma's defaults, whether a default was written explicitly, and JSON whitespace; non-Figma documents are left unchanged

title: Crop follow-up screenshots to the changed region
detail: After a click or keystroke, diff the new screenshot against the previous one in the same tab; send the padded bounding box of changed pixels plus an offset note, and a full frame on navigation. Image cost tracks pixel area (about w*h/750, Anthropic vision docs).
test: Record 3 browser sessions; compute changed-bbox area ratio per step; replay crops on 10 UI tasks; count tasks that needed the full frame.
because: screenshot image cropping

title: Choose screenshot scale by an OCR-stability probe
detail: Run local OCR on the screenshot at 100, 75, 50 and 35 percent scale; send the smallest scale whose recognised words match the full-scale set within a threshold. Replaces a fixed downscale (#109) with a per-image legibility floor, since cost tracks pixel area.
test: On 30 UI screenshots record chosen scale and w*h/750 saving; run 15 small-text tasks at fixed 50 percent versus adaptive scale.
because: screenshot image scaling

title: PreToolUse OCR swap for Read of text-dominant screenshots
detail: Users save PNGs of terminals, stack traces and dialogs; each Read costs about w*h/750 tokens. PreToolUse on Read of image files runs local OCR; if text-dominant and confident, deny with the extracted text and keep the path. Differs from downscaling (#109).
test: Take 20 saved error screenshots; OCR with tesseract; compare OCR-text tokens with w*h/750; hand-check IDs, paths and numbers for misreads.
because: screenshot image handling, hook-based

title: Run computer-use displays at XGA with zoom on demand
detail: Computer-use screenshots are billed by pixel area up to the resize cap. Declare a small display (display_width_px/height_px, XGA-class) in Xvfb or VM setups and use the zoom action (reportedly in newer tool versions) only for fine text. Measure per-task tokens and success.
test: Verify that the zoom action exists; run 10 desktop tasks at 1920x1080 versus 1024x768 with zoom; compare input tokens via count_tokens and task success.
because: computer-use display configuration, images

title: Fuse multi-step browser flows into one Playwright script
detail: Every browser MCP action returns a fresh snapshot or screenshot, so a ten-step login-and-navigate flow pays ten page states. Nudge the agent (hook note or skill) to write one script or evaluate call that prints only the final state's relevant text.
test: Log snapshot tokens per action over 10 recorded browser tasks; find deterministic runs of 3+ actions; rerun as scripts; compare total tokens and success.
because: nudges agent behaviour via hook note or skill

title: Select video keyframes by scene change, not fixed fps
detail: Agents sample ffmpeg -vf fps=1 frames and Read each at pixel-area cost. Use select='gt(scene,0.3)' or pHash dedupe so only changed frames pass, with timestamps in filenames; for slide-style lectures lean on transcript text instead of frames.
test: Take 3 lecture or screen-recording videos; count frames at fps=1 versus scene>0.3; ask 10 content questions on each set; compare image tokens.
because: video frame selection, non-text media

title: Cross-source split leakage: same repo in train and test
detail: The group key carries the source name, so a repo hashes independently in swe_smith, swe_rebench and github_code. Simulating split_of on 2,000 made-up repos, 12% split differently across three sources and 6.5% land in both test and train. Real overlap is unmeasured.
test: Normalise owner__repo and owner/repo across sources; count val/test chunks whose repo also has train chunks; re-run the QA eval without them and compare.
because: measures train/test split leakage offline

title: Weak-supervision label model over many cheap labelers
detail: Combine teacher v1, v2, template-constant, corpus document-frequency, compressor marginal cost and later-quote signals with a Snorkel-style generative label model (Ratner et al.), estimating each source's accuracy without gold labels. Yields probabilistic labels for a large unlabeled pool.
test: Write 5 labeling functions over 500 chunks; fit the label model; check agreement with the teacher and 100 hand labels; train aggregated versus teacher-only and compare QA at 0.5.
because: offline label model for scorer training

title: Noisy-student self-training on unlabeled local tool outputs
detail: Score a large unlabeled pool of captured outputs with the current student, then retrain with soft pseudo-labels plus noise (dropout, value swaps, ANSI injection), as in Noisy Student (Xie et al. 2020, ImageNet). Extends domain coverage without teacher calls. Differs from MLM pretraining (#363).
test: Pseudo-label 5k unlabeled hook-style outputs; train with and without them from the same init; compare AUC on held-out teacher labels and on 50 hand-labeled real outputs.
because: offline self-training of the scorer

title: Severity-word confusers: benign 'error' lines, fatal lines without it
detail: Build hard negatives and positives for lexical shortcuts: '0 errors', 'failed=0', test_handles_error and DEBUG error-handler lines should drop; 'Killed', 'exit status 137', 'panic:', 'command not found', 'Permission denied' must keep. Label by construction, no teacher.
test: Score 200 synthetic lines of each kind inside real log windows; report keep rate at 0.33 for benign-with-keyword versus fatal-without-keyword; fine-tune on confusers only if the gap is large.
because: constructed hard-case training labels, no runtime dependency

title: Position tokens: tell the scorer which window of the output
detail: chunk_doc keeps 2 random chunks per document and discards their index, so head or tail position is invisible to training. Record chunk index and relative depth; prepend a first/middle/last control token at training and inference.
test: Rebuild the corpus recording chunk index for 1k long docs; plot teacher keep rate by relative position; if head or tail differ, train with tags and compare per-position AUC.
because: window position derived from the text itself

title: Splice chunks from different formats into one training window
detail: Real hook inputs mix formats in one blob: a command echo, JSON, stack trace, table. Training chunks are single-source. Concatenate chunks from two or three sources with their labels intact, so the model learns regime switches and boundaries. Probe score drift first.
test: Build 300 spliced windows from labeled val chunks; rescore; Spearman of each half versus its isolated score. If below 0.9, fine-tune with splices and compare AUC on held-out spliced windows.
because: training data augmentation for scorer

title: Repair teacher recall with verbatim answer-span quotes
detail: Ask a stronger LLM for 5 questions per chunk with verbatim answer quotes; atoms inside quotes the teacher dropped are flipped to keep. Repairs labels where #267 would discard the chunk, and gives a per-source teacher-recall number.
test: On 300 labeled chunks, measure the share of answer-quote atoms the teacher dropped, by source; fine-tune on repaired versus original labels; compare QA at 0.33 with a different-family reader.
because: offline teacher label repair

title: Listwise teacher ranking of lines for continuous importance labels
detail: Instead of two keep/drop prompts, ask the LLM to order 15-20 lines by importance in sliding windows (RankGPT-style listwise ranking, Sun et al. 2023), then merge into a per-chunk rank. Yields labels usable at any budget, with no word-count target.
test: Rank 200 chunks of 40 lines; compare Kendall tau with v1/v2 graded labels, then train on rank-derived targets versus v1/v2 and compare needle-line recall at 0.33.
because: offline teacher labelling method

title: Machine-translate MCP issue and comment text, keep identifiers fixed
detail: Multilingual data today is web prose; the CLI-locale idea (#357) covers only terminal tools. Real MCP results (GitHub issues, Jira, Slack) can carry Dutch, German or Chinese comments beside English keys and code. Translate string leaves of Toucan-style JSON, relabel with the teacher.
test: Translate string values of 100 Toucan records into 4 languages; compare per-language drop rate and lost identifiers/numbers against the English original at 0.5, before any training.
because: offline multilingual training data generation

title: Verbosity-ladder labels: quiet output as subsequence of verbose
detail: Run one command at -q, default and -v (or LOG_LEVEL=WARNING versus DEBUG). Tool authors already chose what matters at each level, so the quiet output aligned as a subsequence of the verbose one (existing LCS aligner) gives free keep labels. No LLM teacher.
test: For 10 tools, run quiet and verbose; use align's variation_rate to find true subsequences; keep pairs under 10%; compare model scores on kept versus dropped lines.
because: free labels from tool verbosity levels, offline

title: LogChunks: human-labeled CI failure spans as keep labels
detail: Corpus tool sources are Python-centric (SWE-smith and SWE-rebench reportedly Python repos) with no CI build logs. LogChunks (Brandt et al., MSR 2020, reportedly) pairs Travis logs from many languages with human-marked failure-cause chunks. Use as keep labels and an out-of-domain recall test.
test: Verify that LogChunks is downloadable and licensed for training; on 100 logs, measure failure-chunk atoms kept at 0.33 and 0.5 per language; fine-tune on half, test on the rest.
because: public human-labelled CI spans as training labels

title: Per-project subdirectories for saved originals to scope recursive greps
detail: Saved originals share one global directory keyed by content hash. An agent that lost the note and runs grep -r over outputs/ can pull another repo's or client's output, secrets or planted instructions into this session. Use outputs/<project-hash>/<session>/ so recursive greps stay scoped.
test: From transcripts, count recovery commands using a glob or grep -r on outputs/. Plant a canary in project A's output; from project B, assert a directory grep cannot reach it.
because: scoped store; weaker payload-derived conversation key suffices

title: Reference-aware cleanup of saved originals; refresh mtime on re-save
detail: _save_original skips writing when the hash file exists, so mtime never refreshes. An age-based cleaner, or the documented rm -rf, then strands notes in live or resumed sessions, which may rerun commands. Keep files whose paths appear in recent transcripts.
test: Scan ~/.claude/projects for note paths and report the age distribution of referenced files. Save, backdate mtime, re-emit the same output, run an mtime cleaner, and assert the file survives.
because: mtime refresh and reference-aware cleanup of local store

title: Install/uninstall settings.json round-trip: backup, atomic write, byte-identical
detail: Verified here: install then uninstall on a 4-space settings.json with a foreign hook left the file reformatted to 2-space, so it is not byte-identical. Writes are non-atomic and no backup is kept, so a crash or concurrent edit can lose the user's settings.
test: Property test: random pre-existing settings (foreign hooks, permissions, env, odd indentation); install then uninstall must restore identical bytes. Kill the process mid-write and assert the original file is intact.
because: settings.json install and uninstall mechanics

title: Exact plugin version pin in lockstep with plugin.json
detail: With no CLI installed, hook.sh runs uvx --from 'ctxprune>=0.2.1', so every new PyPI release reaches plugin users automatically, cannot be rolled back by them, and makes A/B arms drift. Pin ==X.Y.Z, bumped with plugin.json; users opt in to upgrades.
test: CI asserts the hook.sh pin equals the plugin.json version. Manual: break a test release, run the plugin from a clean uv cache, and check the hook still fails open.
because: plugin.json and plugin hook packaging

title: Reject browser-origin and non-loopback Host requests at serve
detail: serve.py ignores Content-Type, Origin and Host, so any web page may be able to POST text/plain to 127.0.0.1:8719 without preflight, burning CPU behind the single model lock and queueing the hook. DNS rebinding is a second route. Require loopback Host and no Origin header.
test: curl with Origin: https://evil.example and a foreign Host; assert 403. Time hook latency while a 30 MB request holds the lock; add a smaller body cap.
because: serve request hardening in local process

title: Serve cache: digest keys, byte budget, no raw outputs retained
detail: The serve cache holds up to 512 entries keyed by the full raw text, so tool output, possibly with secrets, lingers in a long-lived process and memory is bounded by entry count, not bytes. Key by sha256, cap total bytes, expire idle entries.
test: Post 40 distinct 5 MB texts and record RSS today; after the change assert RSS stays under the byte cap and a repeated text still hits.
because: serve cache keying and byte budget

title: Print saved-original path POSIX-style and shell-quoted in the note
detail: The note prints str(path) bare. With a space in HOME, or backslashes on Windows (Claude Code reportedly runs Bash through Git Bash there), an agent's grep splits or mangles the path, finds nothing, and reruns the command. Emit as_posix() with quoting.
test: Unit test with HOME='/tmp/a b' and a Windows-style path: run a grep on the noted path via bash -c; assert it finds the file.
because: POSIX-quoted path in note text
check: The saved-original path in the note is POSIX-style (Windows drive and UNC paths via as_posix, a backslash in a POSIX name kept as data) and shlex-quoted: shlex.split recovers the exact path and `bash -c 'grep ...'` finds the file for 11 directory names with spaces, quotes, $, ;, backticks, globs, unicode and parentheses where the bare path fails for at least 7; a safe path gets no quotes, and the real hook's current note is shown to split at a space in the cache home. Git Bash itself is not available here, so the Windows form is checked as a string only.

title: Do-not-rerun clause in note for side-effecting commands
detail: The note says grep the original, but a cut fact may tempt a rerun. For apply, deploy, migrate, push and MCP tools without readOnlyHint, add 'do not rerun; side effects' to the note, or skip compression. Classify by verb list and MCP annotations.
test: Fake deploy script appends to a counter file and prints a cut-prone 8k log. Over 20 claude -p runs per note variant, count extra counter increments.
because: note wording by command verbs and MCP annotations

title: Sidecar with output hash and model fingerprint; ctxprune verify replays
detail: Only the original is saved, not what the agent saw, so post-mortems cannot tell which words were cut. A sidecar stores sha256 of the emitted text, rate and model hash; verify recompresses, flags drift between serve and in-process runs, and marks cut spans.
test: Compress 100 saved outputs via serve and in-process; store hashes; run verify in a fresh process on another CPU or ORT version if available and count byte mismatches.
because: post-mortem sidecar and replay verification tooling

title: Normative-sentence shield for MCP specs, issues and requirement docs
detail: Deleting words from requirements text can flip an obligation the agent must obey, unlike log noise. For Notion, Jira, GitHub issue and doc MCP outputs, force-keep whole sentences containing must, never, do not, required, breaking, deprecated, plus checklist lines; cost is a lower ratio.
test: Take 30 issue and spec bodies with planted obligations ('must not log tokens'); compress at 0.5 with and without the shield; count obligations lost or flipped, plus ratio change.
because: force-keep normative sentences, keyed on tool name

title: Collapse printed LlamaIndex NodeWithScore and LangChain Document reprs
detail: print(retriever.retrieve(q)) or response.source_nodes dumps each TextNode with constant fields: excluded_*_metadata_keys, relationships, metadata_template, text_template. Keep id, score, source, offsets, text. Synthetic reconstruction from memory: 8 nodes 2,916 vs 292 o200k tokens.
test: Install llama-index, index five markdown files, print source_nodes from a top-8 query, run the collapse rule, compare o200k tokens and check text and scores survive.
because: collapses printed node/document reprs
check: A printed list of LlamaIndex NodeWithScore reprs becomes one valid-Python 'NodeWithScore(id=..., score=..., start=..., end=..., metadata={...}, text=...)' line per node; the id, score, character offsets, the metadata entries the LLM is shown (not in excluded_llm_metadata_keys) and the text exactly are unchanged; embedding, excluded-key lists, relationships, templates and mimetype are dropped.
check_loses: the embedding field, both excluded_*_metadata_keys lists, the relationships (previous/next/source node ids, the source document's hash and its metadata copy), the templates and separators, mimetype, and metadata entries listed in excluded_llm_metadata_keys

title: Transpose vector DB parallel-array results into rows
detail: Chroma-style query results return nested parallel lists (ids, documents, metadatas, distances as [[...]]) plus null embeddings, uris and data keys. Emit one row per hit, drop nulls, round distances to 3 decimals. Synthetic 8-hit result: 450 vs 280 o200k tokens.
test: Run chromadb locally, query 8 hits, capture the result dict, apply the rows transform, verify id-to-document-to-metadata alignment by round trip and compare tokens.
because: transpose parallel arrays to rows

title: Force vectors off on vector DB get and scroll calls
detail: Pinecone fetch, Qdrant scroll/retrieve with with_vectors, Weaviate include_vector and Chroma get with embeddings in include return full float arrays. PreToolUse sets the exclusion flag unless the prompt mentions embeddings. Parameter names are from memory; complements #309 and output-side elision (#133).
test: Verify that the hook can rewrite the argument: start a local Qdrant or Chroma MCP server, call scroll/get with vectors on and off, and compare result tokens.
because: sets exclusion flags in vector DB tool inputs

title: Chunk-id seen-set across retrieval calls in agentic RAG
detail: Paraphrased queries to a retrieval tool return overlapping chunks in new order with new scores, so whole-output hashes miss them. Key on chunk or node id; replace chunks already in context with 'chunk X, shown in call N'. Related to #145.
test: Replay a 10-question session against a docs index; measure the share of returned chunk ids already seen in the last five calls and their token cost.
because: chunk-id seen-set across retrieval tool results
check: A retrieved chunk whose id and text hash were returned literally by the same tool within the last 5 calls is replaced by {id, score, seen_in_call}, keeping this call's score and rank; re-indexed text, a chunk last seen longer ago, another tool, malformed results and compaction stay literal.

title: LangChain content_and_artifact tools: compressed content, raw artifact
detail: A wrapper for @tool(response_format='content_and_artifact') returns ctxprune output as content and the original as ToolMessage.artifact, which LangChain does not send to the model. Gives in-process saved-original recovery without a hook.
test: Verify field semantics in current langchain-core; wrap a retrieval tool, run a LangGraph agent with a fake chat model recording prompts; assert prompt holds compressed text, artifact raw.
because: LangChain ToolMessage artifact feature

title: Strip layout geometry and confidences from document-parser JSON
detail: Unstructured, Docling and Azure Document Intelligence element dumps reportedly carry per-element coordinates or polygons, confidence scores and HTML duplicates of table text. Drop geometry and probabilities, keep text, type, page. Targets agents debugging ingestion by printing parsed elements.
test: Parse a sample PDF with one of these parsers, dump elements as JSON, measure the token share of geometry keys, then confirm text, type and page survive the strip.
because: strips geometry fields from parser JSON
check: Unstructured, Docling and Azure Document Intelligence JSON dumps lose their geometry (coordinates, bbox, polygon), probabilities, text duplicates (text_as_html, orig, words, lines, top-level content), span offsets, ids and parent links and are re-emitted as compact JSON; the type/label/role, page and text of every element, every table cell with its row and column, and the page numbers are unchanged.
check_loses: coordinates and polygons, confidences and detection probabilities, element ids and parent links (the document hierarchy), table HTML, word-level records, span offsets, page sizes and per-file constants (filename, filetype, languages)

title: Header-once table for CSV-loader row documents
detail: LangChain CSVLoader and LlamaIndex row readers emit 'column: value' lines per row, repeating every column name in each retrieved document. Group same-schema documents; print the header once, then tab-separated values. Synthetic 10 rows of 8 columns: 539 vs 277 o200k tokens. Cf. #410.
test: Load an 8-column CSV with CSVLoader, retrieve top-10 rows, convert to header plus rows, check every cell round-trips to its column, compare tokens.
because: header-once table for row documents
check: Runs of 2+ consecutive `column: value` documents with the same ordered column list become one tab-separated header plus value rows, and decode restores the exact original text; documents with tabs, a different schema or non-`key: value` lines are left as they were.

title: Document-order sort of retrieved chunks to extend cached prefix
detail: Score-ordered top-k reshuffles between follow-up questions, breaking any shared prefix. Sorting hits by source and offset makes overlapping retrievals share leading bytes and reads coherently, also feeding adjacent-hit merging. Reading-order effect on accuracy must be checked.
test: Run 30 follow-ups over one document set; compare the longest common token prefix of consecutive contexts in score versus document order, then reader accuracy.
because: deterministic reorder of retrieved chunks
check: Sorting retrieved chunks by (source, offset) keeps every chunk byte for byte and, over 30 drifting follow-ups, shares over 1.5x more leading bytes with the previous context than score order does; relevance rank survives only if a footer carries it, and some follow-ups get worse, so a per-request choice is checked too.

title: Chunk size, overlap, top-k and prune-rate Pareto grid
detail: Unknown whether pruning large chunks beats retrieving small raw ones. Grid chunk size, overlap, k and keep rate; plot reader accuracy against prompt tokens to find dominated settings and whether pruning replaces chunk overlap. Informs integration defaults.
test: One QA set and corpus; 3 sizes x 3 overlaps x k in 3,5,10 x keep 1.0 and 0.5; report the Pareto front with a paired bootstrap.
because: Pareto benchmark grid for chunking and prune rate

title: Anthropic citations instead of verbatim quoting in RAG answers
detail: Passing retrieved passages as search_result or document blocks with citations enabled lets the API return cited_text, which Anthropic's docs reportedly exclude from billed output tokens, instead of the model quoting passages itself.
test: Verify against current docs that cited_text is not billed; same 20 questions, prompt A asks for quoted evidence, prompt B uses citations; compare usage.output_tokens and cited-span correctness.
because: Anthropic citations API billing behaviour

title: Collapse near-duplicate chunks across document versions at ingest
detail: Versioned docs, mirrored READMEs and copied sections yield several near-identical chunks that fill top-k. SimHash or MinHash chunks at ingestion, keep one canonical chunk with a version list in payload, and delete the rest from the index. Chunk-level, unlike line-frequency boilerplate stripping.
test: Index a repo with v1 to v3 doc folders; count chunk clusters above Jaccard 0.9, the top-10 slots they occupy for 50 questions, and tokens recovered.
because: ingest-time near-duplicate chunk collapse
check: In a serialised chunk list, chunks of 12+ words with word 3-shingle Jaccard >= 0.9 to the canonical (newest version, else first) are merged into it: the canonical keeps its text and gains 'also=ID|PATH,...' for each merged chunk, the others are deleted; every chunk id and path stays listed and the versions each section exists in are unchanged.
check_loses: the text of every merged non-canonical chunk (its differing words, e.g. an old default), and chunks that drift beyond Jaccard 0.9 of the newest are not merged at all

title: Off-the-shelf cross-encoder reranks output chunks against command intent
detail: Split a large log or doc into 40-line chunks and score them against command plus last prompt with a small MS MARCO cross-encoder (cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2, sentence-transformers), keeping top chunks verbatim. Model-based counterpart to BM25 (#209); no training.
test: On 100 saved outputs with a known answer line, compare top-3 chunk recall for BM25, cross-encoder and ctxprune alone at equal kept tokens.
because: local CPU cross-encoder over command and output text

title: In-band Bash comment directive: agent sets rate and keep patterns
detail: hook.py already honours a CTXPRUNE_OFF=1 substring in the command. Extend it to a trailing '# ctxprune rate=0.2 keep=FAIL|panic' comment. Uses the existing Bash tool, no new MCP tool (#191); needs one CLAUDE.md line.
test: Parse directives in hook.run; on 20 recorded noisy commands compare needle recall and tokens with plain 0.5; run 10 agent tasks and count how often the agent adds one.
because: directive parsed from command string in payload

title: Retroactively prune aged results to lines the agent reused
detail: After N turns a proxy checks whether protected atoms or lines of a big tool result reappear in later assistant text or tool inputs. None: stub it. Some: keep reused lines plus two context lines. A saved copy stays. #169 only trains on this signal.
test: On 20 sessions, take tool results over 2k chars; measure the token share of lines reused in the next 5 turns; replay with stubs or trimmed results; count refetches.
because: retroactive prune of aged results by later reuse

title: Model-free atom scorer: word frequency times in-output IDF
detail: A stronger contrarian control than stopword deletion (#297), and a cold-start tier with no 143 MB download: score atoms by negative log of a bundled 20k-word frequency table plus within-output document frequency, keeping the top atoms with the same budget loop in compress.py.
test: Feed the scores into compress()'s budget loop; compare reader QA against the model at 0.5 per content type; report where it ties and its latency.
because: model-free scorer, pure text function

title: Regex-strip tool-announcing narration from aged assistant text
detail: Rule-based sibling of #450: in a history-rewriting proxy, delete sentences such as 'Let me read the file.' or 'Now I'll run the tests.' from assistant text blocks that sit directly before a tool_use and are older than N turns.
test: Count tokens of assistant text blocks under 15 words directly before tool_use in 10 transcripts, aged over 10 turns; replay with them removed and ask 10 recall questions.
because: regex strip of aged assistant narration in proxy

title: Coverage receipt in the note to cut needless refetches
detail: The note says only 'IDs, numbers and paths are kept'. Add a deterministic receipt such as 'all 9 lines matching error|fail|warn kept; 3 identical blocks folded' (about 15 tokens). It may reduce greps of the saved file, or add tokens for nothing.
test: Two note variants on 20 replayed tasks: count saved-file greps and total tokens including note; keep the receipt only if the refetch rate drops by more than its cost.
because: deterministic coverage receipt in note

title: Paired-delimiter closure after atom deletion: fences, backticks, brackets
detail: atoms.py splits '```', '**' and quotes into one-character atoms, so top-k can keep an opening backtick or fence and drop its partner; the reader then sees everything after it as code or bold. Post-pass: drop or restore the partner of each pair. Cf. #173.
test: On 100 markdown and log outputs, count outputs whose backtick, fence or bracket parity flips versus the original; add the post-pass and compare reader QA on those.
because: post-pass on atom mask, deterministic

title: Ditto marks for run-repeated cells in text tables
detail: kubectl get pods -A, ps, docker ps and git log tables repeat namespace, status or author on consecutive rows; replace repeats with a quote mark after a one-line legend. Synthetic 48-row pod table: 1,097 to 923 o200k tokens; #407 only hoists fully constant columns.
test: Apply to 20 captured kubectl, ps and git log tables; count real-tokenizer tokens; ask cell-lookup questions (#418) of a reader on ditto versus plain form.
because: ditto marks in text tables
check: A header-aligned text table (kubectl/docker style) becomes tab-separated with a `"` for each 3+-character cell equal to the cell above; expanding the marks and unescaping gives exactly the original cell matrix, and non-table or ragged input is untouched.
check_loses: column alignment padding and trailing whitespace

title: Edit old_string elision marker expanded by PreToolUse
detail: Let the model write only the first and last line of a long old_string around a marker such as '[...]'. PreToolUse updatedInput expands it to the file span when head and tail match uniquely. History keeps the short form; #449 needs a new tool.
test: Count Edit calls with old_string over 15 lines in transcripts and their token share; verify updatedInput works for Edit; replay 30 long blocks for unique-match and wrong-span rates.
because: PreToolUse updatedInput expansion

title: LongLLMLingua-style subsequence recovery for Edit anchors
detail: LongLLMLingua (Jiang et al.) repairs answers by matching them back to the original prompt. Same here: if an Edit old_string is absent from the file but is an ordered subsequence of one file span, PreToolUse expands it, saving the failed-edit retry.
test: Compress Bash reads of config and docs at 0.5, let an agent edit them 20 times, count not-found Edit failures with and without the repair, and any wrong-span matches.
because: proxy expands Edit anchors via tool_use rewrite

title: Replace grep -C context lines with enclosing-scope headers
detail: Aider's grep-ast shows matches under their enclosing def or class lines, not N raw neighbour lines. For -A/-B/-C output, drop context lines and prepend the nearest lower-indent line. In a local -C3 grep, context lines outnumbered matches 298 to 59.
test: Replay Grep calls with context flags from transcripts; compare token cost of raw versus scope-header form; check the model still locates the right function in 20 find-the-definition questions.
because: grep output rewrite using enclosing scope

title: Word-diff form for long-line modified pairs in git diff
detail: Minified JSON, lockfile entries, Markdown paragraphs and SQL changes print the whole old and new line. When a -/+ pair shares most words, emit one line with [-old-]{+new+} markers. Synthetic paragraph with two edits: 358 to 244 o200k tokens.
test: Take git diff output from doc, lockfile and config commits; count tokens under git diff --word-diff=plain versus default; ask what-changed questions of a reader on both forms.
because: word-diff form for diff lines
check: Inside a hunk, a lone '-' line followed by a lone '+' line that share most tokens becomes one '~' line in [-old-]{+new+} notation; decode restores both lines byte for byte, and an independent diff parser agrees on every hunk's lines.

title: Declarative per-command filter file with inline test fixtures
detail: rtk reportedly lets users add TOML filters (match command, strip or keep line regexes, head/tail, message on empty). A repo-level .ctxprune/filters.toml with embedded input and expected pairs lets agents add packs without Python; CI replays fixtures.
test: Express three existing noise rules (pytest, npm install, cargo build) in the DSL; check byte-identical output versus the Python versions on 30 captured runs; time rule load per hook call.
because: ctxprune's own filter file, not a harness config

title: Session-wide alias glossary shared across tool outputs
detail: #100 and #102 put a legend in every output. Instead, mine long strings repeated across a session (package prefixes, URLs, absolute paths), announce a glossary once via additionalContext, re-announce after compaction, and alias later outputs. Risk: wrong alias resolution in Edit paths.
test: In transcripts, list strings over 25 chars repeated in 5 or more tool results; sum their tokens minus glossary cost; run 10 edit tasks with aliases and count mis-resolved paths.
because: session glossary held locally; announce channel is incidental
check: A session-wide glossary of path/URL prefixes (25+ chars, 5+ sightings), announced once through the hook channel and again after compaction and referenced as §N;, lets a reader recover every output byte for byte, with append-only ids, exact Edit paths and fail-open on unreadable state.

title: Use Bash tool_input.description as a free intent query
detail: The model already writes a one-line description for every Bash call (#443 counts its cost). Feed it, with the command, to BM25 chunk selection (#209) or query-aware boosting (#89). Unlike #191 and #655, it needs no new tool or transcript read.
test: On 30 captured outputs with known answer spans, compare answer-chunk recall at equal tokens for description-only, command-only and both as BM25 query; report how often descriptions are empty or generic.
because: tool-call input field is in the API payload

title: Public code-completion sets to size the source-code weakness
detail: AGENTS.md admits weaker results on source code. LongBench's lcc and repobench-p sets (also used by LongCodeZip, reportedly) give public prompts to score pruning at 0.5 and 0.8 against head-truncation and no-op, calibrating the #75 skip gate.
test: Prune 200 lcc and 200 repobench-p prompts per arm; have one fixed reader complete them; compare edit similarity per arm against tokens kept, split by prompt length.
because: public code benchmark to size weakness

title: Diff-neighbourhood card: changed symbols with caller signatures
detail: For review prompts, a UserPromptSubmit or SessionStart hook runs git diff, extracts changed function names via ctags or tree-sitter, and injects each one's caller signatures and test files. Aims to replace the grep-then-Read fan-out. Code-graph MCP servers reportedly do this on demand.
test: On 10 recorded review sessions, sum tokens of grep and Read calls made after the diff to find callers; build the card with ctags and compare tokens and findings quality.
because: UserPromptSubmit hook injection from host git state

title: Infra CLI nag, hint and pager silencing environment
detail: Extend the quiet env (#610 covers only JS and Python) to infra tools: AWS_PAGER empty, gcloud update-check and survey prompts, AZURE_CORE_ONLY_SHOW_ERRORS, TF_IN_AUTOMATION, DOCKER_CLI_HINTS=false, GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER.
test: Verify that each variable exists and silences its banner; run 10 aws, gcloud, az, terraform, docker and gh commands with and without the pack; diff bytes and exit codes.
because: infra CLI quiet env injected into commands
check: aws, gcloud, az, terraform, docker and gh commands get AWS_PAGER='', gcloud update-check and survey, TF_IN_AUTOMATION, DOCKER_CLI_HINTS=false or GH_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER through an export prefix unless the user set them (an empty value counts as set); only banner lines disappear, except that AZURE_CORE_ONLY_SHOW_ERRORS also hides az warnings, which the sim asserts as the single content loss.

title: Terraform TF_CLI_ARGS defaults: concise, compact-warnings, no-color
detail: Set TF_CLI_ARGS_plan and TF_CLI_ARGS_apply in the launch env so -concise (reportedly drops refresh and progress lines), -compact-warnings and -no-color apply to every call without rewriting commands. Errors and the plan summary stay in full.
test: Verify that -concise exists in the installed terraform; plan and apply a 30-resource sample with and without; compare tokens; confirm errors, destroy lines and the summary survive.
because: TF_CLI_ARGS env equals command prefix rewrite

title: Steer unfiltered cloud reference-catalog calls to server-side filters
detail: aws ec2 describe-instance-types and describe-images, az vm image list --all, gcloud compute images list and kubectl api-resources return provider-wide catalogs unrelated to the user's infra. Deny or rewrite unfiltered forms with a hint naming --filters, --query or --publisher.
test: Mine transcripts for catalog commands; measure each unfiltered output in tokens; replay with filters; check the agent's lookup (instance type, AMI id) still answers.
because: detects unfiltered catalog commands from command string

title: Drop API-defaulted fields from kubectl YAML and docker inspect
detail: Pod, Deployment and Service YAML carry server-filled defaults (dnsPolicy ClusterFirst, restartPolicy Always, terminationGracePeriodSeconds 30, protocol TCP); docker inspect repeats ~60 default HostConfig keys and MaskedPaths. A per-kind default table drops equal-valued fields; #33 drops only empty ones.
test: Capture get pod, deploy, svc -o yaml from kind and 5 varied docker inspects; drop default-equal fields; verify non-default keys (Privileged, Binds, Memory, Ports) survive; tokenize before and after.
because: default-value table drops fields in YAML
check: Drops YAML fields that equal the API default for the object's kind (dnsPolicy ClusterFirst, protocol TCP, the default tolerations, an imagePullPolicy that matches the image tag's default) and docker-inspect keys that equal the daemon default, with their now-empty parents; the effective value of every field is unchanged and every non-default value (Privileged, Binds, Memory, PortBindings, an imagePullPolicy that is not the tag's default) survives.
check_loses: whether a default-valued field was written explicitly or filled in by the server; the docker inspect JSON is re-indented to 4 spaces with HTML escapes undone

title: YAML anchors for repeated label blocks within one document
detail: kubectl get List output repeats identical labels and annotations mappings per item. Emit the mapping once as an anchor and alias it; still valid YAML. Anchors are scoped per document, so they cannot cross --- boundaries. Synthetic 5-label block: 60 tokens, alias 6.
test: Render a 12-item kubectl get List; hoist mappings seen 3+ times; assert yaml.safe_load of both forms is equal; tokenize; ask which items carry a given label.
because: pure text transform on YAML tool output
check: A mapping block that appears 3+ times under the same key in one YAML document is written once with an anchor and aliased afterwards; anchors never cross `---`, and the loaded documents are equal.
check_loses: the repeated text of the aliased blocks (the loaded value is identical)

title: Fold healthy same-stem pod rows from DaemonSets and ReplicaSets
detail: kubectl get pods -A lists aws-node-x7k2p, kube-proxy-9fq4d and csi-node pods once per node, and replicas differing only in the random suffix. Collapse healthy same-stem groups to 'stem-* x40 Running 0 restarts'; keep unhealthy or restarted rows verbatim.
test: Build a synthetic 60-node pod table with 2 CrashLoopBackOff rows; fold; check the agent still finds bad pods and per-stem counts; compare tokens with ditto marks (#778).
because: fold healthy same-stem pod rows

title: Fold healthy Normal event chains in kubectl events and describe
detail: Healthy pods emit a fixed chain: Scheduled, Pulling, Pulled, Created, Started, plus SuccessfulCreate and ScalingReplicaSet. Collapse each healthy chain to one line with image and pull time; print Warning events (BackOff, FailedScheduling, Unhealthy) verbatim. #320 covers progress states, not this.
test: Capture get events and describe pod during a rollout and a CrashLoopBackOff on kind; fold; compare root-cause question accuracy and tokens versus raw.
because: fold healthy event chains

title: Terraform state reads: drop private, sensitive_attributes, repeated provider addresses
detail: Reading terraform.tfstate or state pull shows per-instance 'private' (reportedly often base64 of null), empty sensitive_attributes, schema_version, dependencies, the full provider address on every resource, and tags_all copies of tags. #314 covers plan JSON only.
test: Apply a 20-resource sample; cat tfstate; apply drop and hoist rules; check surviving attributes match terraform show; measure tokens; ask drift questions.
because: drops tfstate noise fields from output

title: Stub boto3 ResponseMetadata and tz-aware datetime reprs
detail: Scripts that print(client.call()) show ResponseMetadata (RequestId twice, HTTPHeaders, RetryAttempts) and datetime.datetime(..., tzinfo=tzutc()) reprs. Stub metadata when HTTPStatusCode is 200; rewrite reprs to ISO. Synthetic: metadata 142 tokens, datetime repr 31 versus ISO 13.
test: Run moto-backed boto3 scripts printing list and describe responses; apply stub and ISO rewrite; assert the same instants; tokenize before and after.
because: text stub of boto3 metadata and datetime reprs

title: Fold Lambda START/END/REPORT triples and per-line RequestId
detail: CloudWatch Lambda logs wrap each invocation in START, END and REPORT lines sharing a 36-char RequestId, and runtime lines repeat it. Fold to one header per invocation with duration and memory; keep errors and timeouts.
test: Capture aws logs tail output for 20 invocations including one timeout; fold; check the agent finds the failing request and its duration; tokenize.
because: fold Lambda log triples

title: Source-side cloud CLI output format: yaml or value() over JSON
detail: aws, az and gcloud list and describe default to pretty JSON. For commands with no pipe, --query or --output, PreToolUse appends --output yaml or --format=value(...). Avoids braces and quotes at the source; #529 found minified JSON can beat YAML, so pick per shape.
test: Capture 20 describe and list outputs per cloud; tokenize json, yaml, text, table; check nested-field questions answer equally; flag commands whose later jq pipes would break.
because: appends output-format flag to cloud CLI commands

title: Unwrap docker json-file and CRI log envelopes, join partial lines
detail: Raw container log files carry a ns timestamp plus 'stdout F' per line, or a JSON wrapper with escaped newline. Strip the envelope, keep a short time, rejoin CRI 'P' partial chunks. Synthetic 20 lines: 740 vs 460 o200k tokens.
test: Generate 20 CRI and json-file lines, count o200k tokens before and after; check partial-chunk rejoin round-trips on a line over 16 KB.
because: unwrap container log envelopes
check: CRI and docker json-file envelopes are stripped to 'hh:mm:ss.mmm<marker>text' (date on '§date' lines, stderr and cut-off lines marked), and P chunks are rejoined with the first chunk's time; the oracle re-reads both forms independently and compares (date, time, stream, text).
check_loses: nanosecond digits beyond milliseconds, the per-chunk timestamps of a split line (the first chunk's time is kept), the envelope text itself

title: gcloud logging read and aws logs envelope pack
detail: gcloud logging read YAML repeats insertId, logName, receiveTimestamp and the full resource.labels block per entry; aws logs filter-log-events adds eventId and ingestionTime. Hoist constant labels to a header, drop ids, keep time, severity, payload. Synthetic 5 entries: about 1005 vs 100 o200k.
test: Run gcloud logging read --limit 50 against a test project or save a sample; diff kept fields against the original and count tokens.
because: hoists constant log labels, drops ids
check: Parses a gcloud logging read YAML stream or an aws logs filter-log-events JSON document, hoists what is identical across entries (logName, resource type and labels, entry labels, logStreamName) into one header, drops insertId, receiveTimestamp, eventId and ingestionTime, and prints one line per entry with time, severity (or epoch milliseconds) and the payload; every entry, with its constants merged back, equals the original minus those four fields.
check_loses: insertId, receiveTimestamp (gcloud), eventId and ingestionTime (aws), YAML formatting and key order inside payloads, and the distinction between a missing severity and the '-' placeholder

title: Elasticsearch and OpenSearch hit envelopes to flat rows
detail: Search responses wrap each hit in _index, _id, _score, sort and a 'fields' map of single-element arrays that duplicate _source. Hoist _index, drop took/_shards/_score, unwrap singleton arrays, print one line per hit. Synthetic 5 hits: 677 vs 74 o200k.
test: Save one Kibana Dev Tools or curl _search response; run the rewrite and check every _source value and the total survive.
because: JSON envelope flattening, deterministic per message
check: An Elasticsearch/OpenSearch search response becomes '#es' header lines (total with relation, shared _index, the last sort, aggregations and other top-level keys such as _scroll_id, timed_out and failed shards when abnormal) plus one 'id TAB _source TAB extras' row per hit; every _source, _id, index, total, aggregation, highlight and non-duplicate fields entry is unchanged.
check_loses: took, max_score, _score, per-hit sort values except the last hit's (needed for search_after), normal _shards counts, `fields` entries that repeat _source, and JSON whitespace; responses without hits (count, health, bulk) and ids containing a tab are left unchanged

title: OTel Collector debug exporter: one line per record
detail: The collector debug/logging exporter prints about 10 lines per record: ObservedTimestamp, Timestamp, SeverityNumber, empty 'Trace ID:' and 'Span ID:', 'Flags: 0'. Fold to 'time SEV body k=v', drop empty and derivable fields. Synthetic 5 records: 500 vs 100 o200k.
test: Run otelcol with the debug exporter and verbosity detailed on a demo app; compare tokens and confirm trace ids are kept when non-empty.
because: one line per collector record

title: Drop Java frame file names derivable from the class
detail: In 'at com.acme.InvoiceService.charge(InvoiceService.java:212)' the file name repeats the class name. Rewrite to '(:212)' when the stem equals the outer class (strip $Inner), keep it otherwise. Synthetic 12 frames: 196 vs 148 o200k tokens.
test: Apply to 20 real Java and Kotlin traces; count tokens, then run the inverse expansion and compare byte-for-byte on the kept cases.
because: drops derivable Java frame file names
check: 'at pkg.Outer$Inner.m(Outer.java:N)' becomes 'at pkg.Outer$Inner.m(:N)' exactly when the file is the outer class's own .java file; Kotlin files, mismatched names and frames without a line number are kept, and decode restores the exact original.

title: Fold periodic sampler output (vmstat, iostat, ping, sar) to ranges
detail: vmstat, iostat -x, mpstat, sar, pidstat, ping -c N and top -b emit N near-identical numeric rows with repeated headers. Print the header once, per-column min/avg/max and outlier rows. Synthetic ceilings (o200k): 30 vmstat rows 1548 vs 42, 30 ping lines 809 vs 26.
test: Run vmstat 1 30 and ping -c 30 locally; check spikes survive the fold and compare tokens against the raw output.
because: fold periodic sampler rows to ranges
check: Runs of 5+ vmstat-style numeric rows (continued across a repeated header pair) fold to '[N samples: name min/avg/max, constant=v ...]' plus the rows whose value is above 5x the column median + 20; runs of 5+ ping replies fold to count, seq range, ttl, min/avg/max time and the sequence numbers that never answered, plus replies slower than 3x median + 10 ms; short runs and every header, summary or error line stay verbatim.
check_loses: the in-between rows that are not upward outliers (their values survive only as min/avg/max per column), dips below the median (only the minimum), and the repeated header pairs after the first

title: GC trace lines to a pause summary
detail: JVM -Xlog:gc, Go GODEBUG=gctrace=1 and V8 --trace-gc print one decorated line per collection with timestamp, uptime, cause and heap sizes. Summarise count, total and max pause, heap trend; keep Full GC, long pauses, OOM lines. Ceiling: 20 lines 1230 vs 37 o200k.
test: Run a JVM with -Xlog:gc for 60 s; compare tokens, and verify an injected 500 ms Full GC survives the fold.
because: GC trace lines to pause summary

title: Slim tcpdump and tshark lines: options, seq numbers, ACK runs
detail: tcpdump -n lines repeat both endpoints, Flags, seq ranges, win and TS val/ecr options on every packet. Rewrite to delta time, direction, flags, length; fold runs of pure ACKs per flow; keep SYN, FIN, RST and retransmits. Synthetic 10 packets: 741 vs 300 o200k.
test: Capture 5 s of local curl traffic with tcpdump -nn; apply the rewrite and check handshakes and resets are intact.
because: slims packet capture lines, folds ACK runs

title: Percentile tables and histograms to eight quantile rows
detail: HdrHistogram .hgrm files, wrk/hey/vegeta latency histograms, ab percentile tables and Prometheus _bucket series list dozens of cumulative rows. Keep p50, p90, p99, p99.9, max, total count and the mode bucket; save the rest. Not measured; target is rows with long-run repeated counts.
test: Generate a .hgrm from a 100k-sample load test, apply the cut, and compare tokens; check quantiles match the original rows.
because: histogram row folding on tool output

title: Join multi-line pretty-printed struct dumps (Rust {:#?}, pprint)
detail: Rust assert_eq 'left:/right:' dumps and {:#?} output spend a line and indentation per field. If brackets balance and the result is under 160 chars with no raw newline in strings, join onto one line. Synthetic nested struct: 69 vs 53 o200k tokens.
test: Collect 20 cargo test failures with struct diffs; join, count tokens, and verify bracket balance is unchanged.
because: join multi-line dumps; text transform
check: A multi-line bracketed dump whose brackets balance, whose strings each close on their own line and whose joined form is under 160 characters becomes one line; the sequence of strings, brackets and words is identical.
check_loses: line breaks and indentation inside the joined dump (token order, string contents and trailing commas are kept)

title: Fingerprint SQL statement logs: literals to ?, IN-lists collapsed
detail: Postgres log_min_duration_statement lines, MySQL slow logs and ORM show_sql echoes repeat the same statement with different literals and long IN lists. Replace literals with ?, collapse IN (...), group by fingerprint with count and duration range. Ceiling: 5 lines 315 vs 27 o200k.
test: Run a Django or Hibernate request loop with SQL logging on; group by fingerprint and check the slowest statement keeps its literal in the saved original.
because: fingerprint SQL log statements
check: Postgres 'duration: X ms  statement: SQL' lines whose fingerprint (string and number literals -> ?, lists of ? -> (?+), spaces collapsed) occurs 3+ times fold into '[xN min a max b total c ms] fingerprint' followed by the slowest occurrence verbatim; per-fingerprint count, min, max and total duration, the slowest statement with its literals, and every rarer, multi-line, ERROR, DETAIL and STATEMENT line are unchanged.
check_loses: the literals, durations and position of every repeated statement except the slowest one (its duration survives only in min/max/total)

title: Loghub dataset matrix: lossless-rule savings per log dialect
detail: Run the deterministic log rules (timestamp factoring, prefix hoist, dedupe, template mining) over the public logpai/loghub 2k samples (HDFS, BGL, Spark, Android, Apache and others). Report o200k and count_tokens savings per dataset per rule, catching rules tuned only to synthetic logs.
test: Clone logpai/loghub, run each rule on every *_2k.log, tabulate token deltas, and verify L rules invert exactly.
because: public log dataset benchmark matrix

title: Validate a cache simulator against recorded usage fields
detail: Replay request sequences from transcripts through a model of TTL per breakpoint, refresh-on-read, 20-block lookback and minimum cacheable length. Trust it for counterfactual pricing of stubbing, compaction and keep-alive rules only if predicted cache_read and cache_creation match recorded usage.
test: Reconstruct block sequences from 20 transcripts, simulate, report per-request error in cache_read; list mismatches and classify cause (TTL, lookback, tier, unknown).
because: simulates Anthropic breakpoint caching rules

title: Randomised prefix nonce to stop cache contamination in cost A/Bs
detail: Trials sharing a system prompt or forked prefix read each other's cache entries, so later arms look cheaper. Add a per-trial nonce at the start of the system prompt, or price from token counts times fixed multipliers, not billed usage.
test: Run the same 10-turn task twice back to back with and without a nonce; compare cache_read on run 2 and the cost gap between arms.
because: nonce to avoid cache contamination in A/Bs

title: Snap wakeup intervals out of the cache TTL dead zone
detail: A wake just past the TTL pays a full-context rewrite (1.25x or 2x) instead of a 0.1x read, with nothing to amortise it. A PreToolUse hook rewrites CronCreate or loop delay inputs to stay under ~4 minutes or jump to the next tier.
test: Verify that PreToolUse updatedInput can edit the cron string; price wake gaps of 240s, 330s and 1500s per context size at 0.1x, 1.25x, 2x from loop session usage.
because: PreToolUse rewrite of CronCreate input

title: Downgrade 1h cache writes to 5m for gap-free sessions
detail: A 1h write costs 2x versus 1.25x per published multipliers. In the one local session sampled, all 14 requests wrote ephemeral_1h tokens. Where no gap exceeds ~4 minutes (headless children, tight loops), a proxy or env setting saves 0.75x per written token.
test: Verify that usage.cache_creation reports 1h tokens; for sessions with max gap under 300s, price 1h versus 5m writes; check whether 1h is an env opt-in or a plan default.
because: Anthropic 1h versus 5m cache TTL tiers

title: Split first-request writes into shared prefix versus session-unique head
detail: In the one local session, the first request read 50,696 cached tokens and wrote 19,006; a resume hours later read the same 50,696. If the shared prefix stays warm, trimming the head (skills, MCP text, CLAUDE.md) pays the 2x write every session.
test: For every session's first request, record cache_read versus cache_creation, bucketed by minutes since the previous session start in that cwd; then rank head segments by size via a logging proxy.
