because: session usage logs, skills and CLAUDE.md trimming

title: UserPromptSubmit guard for thinking keywords that bust message cache
detail: Anthropic docs reportedly say changing the thinking setting invalidates cached message blocks. If a prompt keyword such as ultrathink changes the request's thinking parameters mid-session, a hook can warn or block it when context is large and warm.
test: Verify that the keyword changes thinking parameters: via logging proxy, send a prompt with and without it in a 50k-token session; diff parameters and next-request cache_creation.
because: UserPromptSubmit hook

title: Subagent versus inline exploration break-even by main-context size
detail: Each serial inline turn re-reads the whole main context at 0.1x, while a subagent pays a cold session-unique head at 2x plus its own small reads and a report. Compute the context size above which delegating an N-turn search wins.
test: From transcripts, take runs of 4+ Grep/Read/Glob turns; price them inline from usage versus a subagent using measured cold-start sizes; report break-even context and share of runs above it.
because: subagent delegation analysis tied to harness and cache pricing

title: Cache the document prefix across questions in reader evals
detail: QA evals send the same compressed document with each question. Put the document first with a cache_control breakpoint and the question last: one write plus N reads. Reportedly best-effort inside Message Batches, so use the 1h tier.
test: Run 20 questions on one 8k-token document with and without the breakpoint; compare summed input cost from usage fields and check cache_read_input_tokens on questions 2 to 20.
because: dev-time eval cost saving using vendor caching

title: Keep-alive ping must match thinking parameters, so max_tokens=1 may fail
detail: Anthropic docs reportedly require thinking budget_tokens below max_tokens (minimum 1024), and changed thinking settings invalidate cached messages. A ping with max_tokens=1 or no thinking field may miss the entry or error; replaying it faithfully costs output tokens.
test: Replay a thinking-enabled request via API with max_tokens=1, then with matching thinking and small max_tokens; record errors, cache_read_input_tokens and output_tokens; re-price the #284 break-even.
because: Anthropic thinking budget and cache invalidation rules

title: PreToolUse stagger of parallel Agent calls until first child warms
detail: When one assistant turn emits N Agent calls, siblings cold-write the same prefix. A hook lets the first through, waits until the first child's transcript shows an assistant record, then releases the rest. Automates #303 for interactive sessions.
test: Verify that parallel PreToolUse hooks run concurrently and can sleep; fan out 6 identical Agent calls with and without a lock-file stagger; compare summed cache_creation and wall-clock.
because: PreToolUse hook on Agent calls

title: Attribute cold-cache gaps to user, tool time, retries, permission prompts
detail: Extends #157. A gap over the TTL needs a different fix by cause: human think time suggests the 1h tier, a long build suggests background runs or keep-alive, an unanswered permission prompt suggests allow rules, retries need none. Split each gap from transcript timestamps.
test: For each gap over 300s, split into tool_use-to-tool_result time (flag permission waits), last Stop-to-prompt time and residual; tabulate next-turn cache_creation per bucket; list commands behind permission waits.
because: transcript timestamps and permission prompts

title: Continue-versus-respawn gate on subagent cache age and size
detail: Extends #718. Continuing a finished subagent after its cache expired rewrites its whole context at 1.25x to 2x. If idle gap exceeds the TTL and its context is large, respawn fresh with a short digest instead.
test: From subagent transcripts, find follow-up messages to finished agents; compute idle gap and context tokens; price cold continue versus fresh spawn with a 2k-token digest; count follow-ups above break-even.
because: subagent continuation and cache TTL

title: Drop TodoWrite activeForm duplicate via proxy schema edit
detail: Each todo carries content plus a derived gerund activeForm, and the whole list is re-sent on every update. A proxy marks activeForm optional in the TodoWrite schema and a hook fills it in. Synthetic 4-item list: 113 vs 68 o200k tokens.
test: Sum activeForm tokens across TodoWrite inputs in transcripts; verify that a proxy-edited schema is accepted and the spinner text still shows.
because: Claude Code TodoWrite schema and hook

title: Stub dead old_string text of aged Edit calls
detail: A history-rewriting proxy replaces old_string in Edit/MultiEdit tool_use blocks older than N turns with '[N lines replaced]'. That text no longer exists on disk and an earlier Read already showed it; new_string stays. Complements #288, which covers Write and heredocs.
test: Sum old_string tokens of Edit calls older than 10 turns; verify that rewritten tool_use history is accepted; replay stubbed history, ask 10 questions about previous values, count re-Reads.
because: stub aged Edit old_string in tool_use inputs

title: Proxy stop_sequences for mined closing pleasantries
detail: Mine the most frequent closing sentences ('Let me know if...') from assistant text, then have a proxy or SDK loop send them as stop_sequences so generation halts before they are emitted. Unproven that Claude Code tolerates stop_reason stop_sequence.
test: Verify that Claude Code tolerates stop_reason stop_sequence: send a mock request via proxy with one stop sequence, confirm lower billed output_tokens and unaffected tool_use turns; count mined closers per transcript.
because: steers model output style via stop_sequences

title: Hook-computed end-of-turn change receipt replaces model recap
detail: A Stop hook shows git diff --stat, touched files and last test status through systemMessage, costing no model tokens. A one-line CLAUDE.md rule then drops the model's closing recap, which restates the diff and is re-read on every later turn.
test: Measure final-message tokens in transcripts that restate diff or test results; A/B the receipt on 10 tasks for output tokens and user comprehension.
because: Stop hook, systemMessage and CLAUDE.md rule

title: Write elision markers expanded from disk by PreToolUse
detail: For rewrites of existing files, accept '# ... existing code ...' markers in Write content; a hook diffs against disk and fills unchanged spans via updatedInput. Differs from #779 (Edit old_string) and #211 (guard). Risk: wrong-span expansion.
test: Verify that updatedInput can rewrite Write content; collect Write calls over existing files, compute tokens if unchanged runs became markers, expand them and diff against original to count mismatches.
because: PreToolUse updatedInput expansion

title: Revise plans with Edit on the plan file
detail: After feedback, models re-emit the whole plan in a new ExitPlanMode input, paying output tokens for unchanged sections and keeping both copies in history. Steer to Edit the plan file, then approve by pointer (plan-file handling is reportedly version-dependent).
test: Verify that plan mode allows Edit on the plan file; find consecutive ExitPlanMode inputs sharing 60%+ lines in transcripts and total the re-emitted tokens.
because: ExitPlanMode and plan-file handling

title: Generated-comment tax in model-written code
detail: Comment and docstring lines in Write content and Edit new_string cost output tokens once and input tokens on every later Read. Compare their share with the repo's own comment density; if higher, add a steering line.
test: Tokenise comment lines in new_string and content per language across transcripts; compare with comment ratio of files at HEAD; report tokens above baseline.
because: measures comment share in model-written code

title: UserPromptSubmit answer-length hint keyed to prompt class
detail: A cheap rule classifies the prompt (yes/no question, lookup, edit task, open design) and injects a one-line length cap such as 'answer in two sentences' only for short-answer classes. Dynamic and per prompt, unlike a static terse rule in CLAUDE.md.
test: Classify 100 prompts from transcripts; A/B hinted versus unhinted on 20 short-class prompts for output_tokens and reader-graded completeness.
because: steers answer length, output style

title: Repo-relative paths and no cd prefix in tool calls
detail: Read, Edit and Write take absolute paths, so each call repeats the cwd prefix, and Bash calls often start with 'cd <repo> &&'. PreToolUse updatedInput can expand relative paths; a CLAUDE.md line steers. One short path measured 13 vs 6 o200k tokens.
test: Verify that updatedInput accepts relative file_path; tokenise path prefixes and leading cd clauses across tool_use inputs; A/B 10 tasks for compliance and path errors.
because: PreToolUse updatedInput and CLAUDE.md steering

title: Closed-schema final reports for headless subagents
detail: Workflow children and claude -p runs return through a StructuredOutput-style schema with short typed fields (enum verdict, path:line list) instead of free prose. The parent receives a bounded report enforced by the tool, not an ignorable prompt contract.
test: Run 10 delegated tasks with prose versus schema return; compare report tokens, parent follow-up reads and grader-scored answer quality.
because: harness headless structured-output subagent reports

title: Terse-reasoning instruction to shrink thinking tokens (Chain of Draft)
detail: Test whether a CLAUDE.md or output-style line asking for fragment-style drafts (Chain of Draft, Xu et al. 2025, reportedly a few words per step) lowers thinking spend, billed as output. Distinct from effort sweeps (#160, #442) and the narration diet (#111): it changes reasoning wording.
test: Use #441's residual method: same 15 tasks with and without the line; compare thinking residual tokens (output_tokens minus visible text) and pass rate.
because: prompting advice to steer reasoning style

title: Skip model load when protected share forces bail-out
detail: With force_protected, output cannot fall below the protected-atom char share, and the hook rejects ratios of 0.95 or more. Compute the share via atomize and is_protected before Compressor() loads; return early if max(rate, share) reaches 0.97. Same result, saves a ~2 s load.
test: Replay 500 recorded hook events; assert every predicted skip was an actual bail (zero false skips); report calls skipped and seconds saved, on env, ls -lR, seq and numeric tables.
because: early bail-out avoids model load; output unchanged
check: The model is skipped when a whitespace-aware lower bound on the output (protected atoms plus the whitespace they keep) is >= 95% of the input, and hook.run's result is then exactly what the full path returns (None); the idea's extra rate>=0.97 arm is refuted by a counterexample and a failing prefilter falls through to the full path.

title: Int8 keep-decision drift across CPU instruction sets
detail: scripts/export_onnx.py notes signed int8 or a quantized head drops keep agreement to 0.1-0.84, so the model is quantization-fragile. ORT reportedly picks different int8 matmul kernels per CPU (AVX2, VNNI, ARM64), so rankings, and savings, may differ by laptop.
test: Score 200 windows on CI runners (linux x64, macos arm64, windows) against an fp32 reference; compare top-50% atom overlap and max probability gap; flag outlier machines.
because: measures int8 decision drift across CPUs

title: Per-layer int8 sensitivity map and static calibrated quantization
detail: Only the head is kept fp32, though the export comment shows the model breaks easily. Quantize all but one layer in turn to find fragile layers, and try static QDQ calibrated on 256 real tool-output windows instead of dynamic activation scales.
test: Export baseline, per-layer-exempt and static variants; report MB, ms per window, ROC-AUC and top-50% atom agreement with fp32 for each; keep the Pareto winner.
because: quantising the local scorer, not the reader

title: Try CoreML, DirectML and OpenVINO execution providers
detail: compress.py hard-codes CPUExecutionProvider, so Apple Silicon and Windows users never get an accelerator. Faster windows would let the 6,000-char threshold drop (#277). Those providers reportedly lack dynamic-int8 ops, so this needs the fp32 or fp16 graph.
test: On a Mac and a Windows box time 100 windows: int8 on CPU versus fp16 or fp32 on each available provider; check keep-decision agreement and cold session-creation time.
because: optional local execution providers; CPU remains the default

title: Load tokenizer and ORT session in parallel threads
detail: compress.py says tokenizer.json loads in ~1 s, about half the ~2 s cold start AGENTS.md quotes, and the session build is independent. Create InferenceSession on a worker thread while the main thread parses the tokenizer, if both release the GIL. Output unchanged.
test: Time cold Compressor() sequential versus threaded over 10 runs with a warm page cache; check the GIL is released by comparing wall time to the sum of the two phases.
because: parallel local startup, output unchanged
check: Loading tokenizer and session on two threads returns equal objects in declared order and a Compressor with identical output, wall time falls below 0.75x the sum of the phases when they release the GIL, and a failure in either loader is re-raised as the serial path would raise it, with thread exhaustion degrading to serial.

title: Serve window scheduler: shortest request first, shared batches
detail: serve holds one global lock per request, so a 1 MB log makes 7 KB requests from sibling sessions or subagents wait until their hooks time out. One scorer thread could draw windows from all queued requests, smallest first, filling shared ORT batches.
test: Send one 1 MB and ten 7 KB requests concurrently to serve; compare p50 and p95 latency of the small ones and total throughput against the current lock.
because: local serve scheduling, no harness dependence
check: A single scorer drawing windows from all queued requests shortest-first into shared batches gives every request exactly its own results, cuts small-request p50 and p95 latency over 10x against the global lock without losing throughput, a max-wait guard bounds a long request that pure shortest-first starves, and a poisoned window fails only its own request.

title: Freeze per-atom scores so selection experiments skip ORT
detail: Compressor.atom_scores already separates scoring from selection, but each sweep reruns the model. Dump atoms, scores, token counts and model hash once per corpus item; rate, aggregator, smoothing, protect and detok experiments then run as pure Python in seconds.
test: Dump scores for 500 recorded outputs; rebuild current compress() output byte-for-byte from the table; then time a 20-setting rate sweep against rerunning ORT.
because: frozen scores for fast experiments

title: Bound peak memory with line-aligned input segments
detail: Measured here with synthetic offsets: Python glue alone took 4.3 s and 741 MB peak RSS on a 4.4 MB log before any model call; serve accepts 32 MB. Score ~256 KB line-aligned segments, keeping only scores, so one huge output cannot OOM the daemon.
test: Compare maxrss and output on 1, 4 and 16 MB real logs against the current path; assert identical keep-sets where windows align and bounded difference elsewhere.
because: bounded-memory segmented scoring in local process

title: Resolve model paths from an install-time manifest
detail: _hub_file imports huggingface_hub on every cold start just to find two cached files. At install, write absolute paths plus sizes to a small JSON; the hook checks it and imports the hub only when files are missing. Import cost is unmeasured here.
test: Run python -X importtime on the cold path with and without the manifest; compare total Compressor() time over 10 cold runs and confirm a deleted file falls back to hf_hub_download.
because: install-time model path manifest, local startup
check: With a valid install-time manifest the model files resolve to the same paths and bytes as compress._hub_file without importing huggingface_hub (0 imports in 10 cold starts versus 10), and a moved ref, deleted, truncated or rewritten file, a missing, corrupt or wrong-version manifest, or another cache root all fall back to the hub and return exactly what it resolves, on one revision.

title: Offline per-result token counts from usage deltas
detail: count_tokens sends text to an API, against local-only analytics. Instead take growth in input plus cache tokens between consecutive requests, minus prior output_tokens, on turns with one tool result. Regress on character classes. Noisy: attachments and reminders add tokens.
test: Keep single-result, attachment-free turns from a session JSONL; compare delta-derived tokens with count_tokens on 50 outputs; report error by content class.
because: offline token counts from usage deltas

title: cost-state records as offline ground truth for the ledger
detail: Local session JSONL reportedly holds cost-state entries: totalCostUSD, per-model tokens including thinkingTokens, API and tool durations. Reconcile the usage-field ledger against them offline; works on subscriptions without Admin API access. Undocumented, so stamp the Claude Code version.
test: Verify that cost-state entries exist; sum deduped usage per session at list prices; diff against the last totalCostUSD over 20 sessions; chase gaps above 5 percent.
because: undocumented Claude Code cost-state records

title: Contamination guard: corpus miner skips already-compressed results
detail: If hooked sessions store ctxprune output in the transcript (open question, #295), a miner trains on the model's own deletions. Detect the note marker, then restore the original from the saved path or drop the row.
test: Install the hook in a scratch session, run one large command, mine its JSONL; assert the row is flagged and the original restored byte for byte.
because: corpus contamination guard

title: Shell command-family canonicaliser with coverage metric
detail: Every per-family counter, quota and rate needs a family key. First word fails: 3 of 10 Bash calls in one local session began with VAR= assignments. Strip env assignments, cd, time, uv run, npx, sudo; split && chains; key pipelines by producer stage.
test: Over transcript Bash calls, compare token-mass share of the top 20 keys, naive versus canonical; hand-check 50 mappings; report the share left in 'other'.
because: command-family keying from payload command string

title: User interrupt and correction rate as local harm proxy
detail: Bash toolUseResult reportedly carries an interrupted flag, and users type corrections. Compare interrupts and corrective user turns within three turns after compressed versus uncompressed results, paired by session. Needs no model or task set; small effects need many sessions.
test: Verify that the interrupted flag exists; join the holdout or shadow arm to the next three user turns; count interrupts and 'no, wrong, revert' openers; report paired counts, clustered intervals.
because: harm proxy from user corrections

title: ddmin-minimise a bad compression into a regression fixture
detail: When compression loses something, delta-debug the saved original by line to the smallest slice that still reproduces the loss, then pseudonymise. A tiny fixture is safe to review and paste, and feeds the golden corpus.
test: Take 5 known misfires; run ddmin with predicate 'needle atom dropped at 0.5'; report slice size versus original and whether the fixture still fails after pseudonymising.
because: delta-debug fixture minimiser

title: Re-identification red team on exported templates and counters
detail: Grepping for names misses quasi-identifiers: rare package-version combinations, internal hostnames and ticket prefixes can fingerprint a project. Test exports by asking a model to guess repo, employer or stack, and by counting tokens absent from public package and word lists.
test: Export from 20 local sessions; run the guess prompt and the public-vocabulary miss count; report uniquely identifying lines per export and what the user-review step catches.
because: re-identification red team, safety tooling

title: Row egress classes restrict which teacher or judge sees it
detail: Rows already sent to Claude in a session add no new recipient when Claude labels or judges them (retention terms may differ); a third-party model or hosted service does. Tag rows claude-seen, local-only or public; route teacher, judge and consensus calls by tag.
test: Add the tag to the corpus manifest; assert a mocked non-Anthropic client refuses non-public rows; report what share of the private corpus each downstream use may touch.
because: data egress governance for corpus rows

title: ctxprune flag and show: pruned twin plus human hard negatives
detail: The hook saves only the original, not the pruned text Claude read. Keep the twin; 'ctxprune show' renders deletions inline and 'ctxprune flag [why]' copies original, pruned text and rule ids into local fixtures. Explicit labels complement implicit regret logs (#8).
test: Prune 20 saved outputs, render diffs, flag harmful deletions for a week; replay fixtures through the current build; count flags the regret log never caught.
because: labelling and fixture tooling

title: Lineage-tracked purge with per-session encrypted shards
detail: Store shadow rows in per-session shards encrypted under a key kept outside the cache directory; purging a session deletes its key. Derived templates, counters and sketches carry lineage ids, so a rebuild drops them and recomputes k counts.
test: Purge one canary session; assert its shard is unreadable, the rebuilt template export lacks the canary lines, and affected k counts drop.
because: privacy purge tooling for corpus

title: Capture-recapture estimate of scrubber miss rate
detail: Run two or more independent secret and PII scanners over the corpus. Lincoln-Petersen estimates findings all scanners missed from their overlap, a recall estimate needing no labels. Scanners correlate on easy cases, so treat it as optimistic.
test: Run gitleaks and detect-secrets on 500 outputs with 30 planted secrets; compare the estimated total with the known count and report the bias.
because: scrubber recall estimation

title: Synthetic outputs regenerated from shared templates for evals
detail: Templates plus per-slot type distributions (path, hex, integer, word) can sample new outputs shaped like a user's real ones. Share or evaluate on those instead of rows; only template constants survive. Differs from scrubbing real rows (#465).
test: From 20 sessions regenerate 200 outputs; compare token counts, zlib ratio and classifier keep-rate distributions with real rows; accept if drift is under 5 percent.
because: synthetic eval data generation

title: Drop SGR-8 concealed spans, not just the escapes
detail: Jenkins raw console logs reportedly hide ConsoleNote blobs as ESC[8m ha:////base64 ESC[0m. Stripping only the escapes (#9) leaves a visible base64 run on each annotated line. Synthetic 407-char random base64: 272 o200k tokens. Delete the text between conceal and reset.
test: Fetch a Jenkins pipeline's raw console log; run current ANSI strip, count residual ha:// tokens; then drop concealed spans and diff. Confirm no visible text is lost.
because: delete concealed span text

title: Non-GitHub CI log packs: Jenkins, GitLab, Azure, Buildkite
detail: Jenkins prints [Pipeline] structure lines per stage and block; Azure DevOps ##[section]/##[command] markers; GitLab section_start/end; Buildkite ~~~ and --- group lines. Drop structure lines and fold passing sections, as #311 does for Actions. Formats reported from memory, unmeasured.
test: Export console logs from a Jenkins pipeline and a GitLab job; strip marker lines and passing sections; assert failing stage and error lines survive; compare tokens.
because: CI log structure-line folding, text rules

title: Subtract last green run's log from a failing run
detail: Fetch the last successful run of the same job on the default branch, normalise timestamps, paths and hashes, and drop lines present in both. Differs from #142, which only sees runs the agent made itself. Needs a network call and gh auth.
test: On 10 failed runs, subtract the last green log of the same job; assert the root-cause lines survive; report percent of lines removed and tokens versus raw.
because: needs network fetch and gh auth credentials at runtime

title: Runner-side failure digest emitted as a workflow annotation
detail: Steps tee output to a file; a later if: failure() step runs it through ctxprune and emits the digest as a workflow-command annotation. Agents read it through the check-run annotations API instead of downloading the full log.
test: In a scratch repo, fail a pytest step, emit the digest annotation, fetch it with gh api; compare tokens and root-cause coverage with gh run view --log-failed.
because: CI-side digest via ctxprune, agent-agnostic
check: An if: failure() step turns the tee'd pytest log into at most ten ::error:: workflow commands (test, file:line, assertion lines, an overflow annotation naming the rest) plus a summary notice; the check-run annotations carry every failing test and location the raw failing-step log does, in under half the tokens; green runs emit nothing, an unrecognised failure falls back to the log tail, log text cannot inject commands, and a missing log or crashing digest warns and exits 0.

title: Zero-schema gh extensions for CI digest and PR card
detail: gh alias set --shell or a gh extension adds ci-digest and pr-card commands: failing step, annotations, unresolved threads, failing checks in one call. Costs one CLAUDE.md line instead of an MCP schema each turn, and output passes the Bash hook. Delivery variant of #485.
test: Count tokens of the alias line versus the #485 tool's schema; run 10 PR-review tasks with raw gh versus the aliases; compare turns and tokens.
because: compact CLI digest output via any shell tool

title: Fold green and skipped rows in check lists
detail: gh pr checks, get_check_runs and get_status list every check with name, state, elapsed and URL; large PRs show dozens of mostly green rows. Print 'N passed, M skipped' plus compact names, and keep failing, pending and cancelled rows in full.
test: Capture checks for 10 PRs with 20+ checks via gh and MCP; fold; ask which checks block merge, folded versus raw, and compare tokens.
because: fold green check rows; text transform

title: Actions debug-rerun logs: drop ##[debug] lines outside failures
detail: gh run rerun --debug (or ACTIONS_STEP_DEBUG) makes logs carry ##[debug] Evaluating, Expanded and Result lines for every expression and step. Drop them except in the failing step, where inputs may matter. Extends #311, which assumes normal logs.
test: Rerun a failed workflow with --debug, pull logs, count ##[debug] share of tokens, drop outside the failing step, check root cause survives.
because: drops debug lines outside failing step

title: Drop commit verification payload and signature blocks
detail: GitHub commit JSON carries verification.signature and verification.payload, reportedly the full PGP or SSH signature plus the signed commit text again; git log --show-signature and cat-file print the same blocks. Synthetic PGP block: 410 o200k tokens. Keep verified and reason.
test: Fetch list_commits for a repo with signed commits; measure verification field share; stub; ask who authored and whether verified, folded versus raw.
because: drops signature blocks from commit JSON text

title: Tune GitHub log tool params: get_check_run textLimit, get_job_logs return_content
detail: get_check_run pages output.text in 4096-byte windows by default (max 8192), reportedly repeating metadata per page; get_job_logs returns URLs unless return_content is true, costing a turn plus an untailed curl. Inject textLimit 8192, or return_content with tail_lines. Complements #477 and #203.
test: Verify that updatedInput works for MCP; fetch a 30 KB check run at textLimit 4096 and 8192, and a failed job with and without return_content; compare turns and tokens.
because: sets log tool params in MCP call inputs

title: Return digest plus resource_link from wrapped MCP tools
detail: The MCP 2025-06-18 spec (from memory) adds a resource_link content block. A ctxprune mcp-wrap (#188) returns the digest plus a link, and serves the full text on resources/read, so no extra expand-tool schema is added. Host handling of the block is unknown.
test: Verify that Claude Code handles resource_link: a toy server returns text plus a link; check whether the host shows the URI, auto-reads it or drops it; count tokens.
because: MCP spec resource_link in wrapper output

title: pre-commit, husky and lint-staged output pack
detail: pre-commit prints each hook as name, dot leader padded to terminal width, then Passed or Skipped; husky and lint-staged add spinner and task lines. Fold passing and skipped hooks to a count, drop dot leaders, keep Failed hooks, exit codes and auto-fix diffs.
test: Run git commit in a repo with 10 pre-commit hooks, passing and failing; fold; assert failed hook ids and diffs survive; compare tokens.
because: folds passing hook lines, drops dot leaders

title: Install canary through the real host proves replacement is honored
detail: AGENTS.md's check only looks for the note, which appears even if the host ignored updatedToolOutput, leaving full text billed beside a false claim. A one-shot headless run with a stub hook can prove the field is honored for Bash and MCP.
test: Verify that updatedToolOutput replaces the result: run claude -p with a throwaway settings file whose stub hook returns CANARY-7 for an 8k-char Bash output; check the stream-json tool_result.
because: tests Claude Code updatedToolOutput honoring

title: Refuse ephemeral interpreter paths when writing the hook command
detail: _hook_command() stores shutil.which('ctxprune') or sys.executable. Under uvx or a project venv that path reportedly sits in a cache or deletable folder; after cleanup the hook fails open forever, with no savings and no signal. Warn and point to uv tool install or pipx.
test: In a temp HOME run uvx ctxprune install claude-code, read the written command, run uv cache clean, pipe an 8k-char event to that command, and confirm a silent no-op.
because: validates hook command written to settings

title: Probe where CTXPRUNE_* reaches hooks; plugin userConfig fallback
detail: AGENTS.md says tune via the Claude Code process environment, but shell-rc exports may not reach IDE, desktop or scheduled launches, so knobs silently do nothing. Settings env blocks should reach. Plugin manifests reportedly support userConfig values exported to hooks as environment variables.
test: Stub hook logs CTXPRUNE_RATE under terminal, VS Code, desktop and claude -p launches, set in shell rc versus settings env; verify that a scratch plugin's userConfig reaches it.
because: env reach into hooks, plugin userConfig

title: Latency circuit breaker: skip the model path after slow calls
detail: Hooks run synchronously, so on a throttled laptop or busy CI box every large output stalls the agent. Time each model-path call; past N seconds, write a backoff stamp and pass outputs through (or lossless rules only) for ten minutes, then retry.
test: Inject a sleep into Compressor.compress, fire five large events, assert calls after the first slow one skip the model; assert the stamp expires and a fast call restores compression.
because: local latency breaker, pass-through when slow
check: After one call slower than the threshold the model path is skipped for the backoff window (lossless rules only, zero model time), then retried; a stamp shared by new processes persists the state and a corrupt stamp fails open.

title: Prompt-keyword raw mode: 'verbatim' in newest prompt bypasses hook
detail: The hook can read transcript_path and find the user's newest prompt. If it says 'verbatim', 'exact output' or 'full log', pass outputs through for that turn. Users get a per-turn escape hatch without editing env or settings, so they keep the hook installed.
test: Scripted claude -p runs with and without the keyword over one 8k-char command; assert passthrough only with it; time the transcript tail read over 1,000 events.
because: bypass keyed on user prompt text, in payload
check: Only the newest real user prompt decides: 'verbatim', 'exact output' or 'full log' used as a request (not quoted, negated, a substring such as 'full logging', or part of a path) makes hook.run pass outputs through for that turn only, tool results, meta and sidechain entries are ignored, the transcript is read from the tail in bounded windows, and an unreadable transcript keeps the default compress behaviour.

title: Key rate and threshold on permission_mode and headless runs
detail: Hook input reportedly carries permission_mode. Unattended runs (claude -p, bypass, auto) build long contexts that nobody reads raw, while plan mode favours exactness. Choose rate and min_chars per mode instead of one global default, starting with shadow logging.
test: Verify that permission_mode is in hook input; log it with output sizes for a week; report the share of over-6,000-char outputs per mode before choosing any mode-specific rate or threshold.
because: keys on hook-input permission_mode

title: Setup-agent eval: can a fresh agent follow AGENTS.md?
detail: AGENTS.md is itself a prompt. Give a fresh Claude Code only that file plus a user request and grade the outcome: scope flag, verification run, secrets-in-originals warning, no unrelated installs, correct uninstall hint. Doc edits become measurable instead of anecdotal.
test: Ten headless trials per request variant (user-wide, repo-only, Python-only, plugin) in temp HOMEs; grade the resulting settings.json and final message against a checklist.
because: evaluates setup docs, not token saving

title: Shorten harness-forced path prefixes: project root, temp dirs, worktrees
detail: Read, Edit and Write need absolute paths, so every call re-emits the project root as output tokens and tools echo it back. Launch from a short symlink or bind mount. o200k proxy: 108-char scratchpad path 52 tokens, /t/ideas.jsonl 5.
test: Count path tokens in Read/Edit/Write inputs of a recorded session with count_tokens; rerun one task from a /w symlink; check tools do not resolve it.
because: user launch-environment advice (symlink), not a rewrite

title: Re-price every rewrite per Claude model: tokenizer drift check
detail: Rule savings here are mostly priced with one tokenizer or an o200k proxy. Newer Claude models reportedly changed tokenizers, so digit, whitespace, glyph and hex rewrites may save less or flip sign. Re-measure each rule per model ID at release.
test: Run count_tokens (free) on a golden before/after corpus for two Claude model IDs; flag rules whose savings differ by over 20% or flip sign.
because: per-model tokenizer re-measurement

title: Phase-split billed cost and turns-to-first-edit as harm indicators
detail: arXiv 2607.12161 reportedly saw a 38.4% tool-output cut raise billed cost 6.8%: later first edit, more re-retrieval, downstream phases costing about four times the retrieval savings. Segment turns into retrieval, diagnosis, edit, test; compare arms per phase.
test: Label transcript turns by tool sequence; per arm report cost by phase, turns to first Edit, repeated-search tokens, paired bootstrap intervals; failures stay in the cost numerator.
because: harm indicators by task phase

title: Shims filter only when stdout is the agent's capture pipe
detail: arXiv 2607.12161 reportedly found a stdout-pipe incompatibility in a command-rewriting compressor that gave wrong answers without errors. PATH shims (#189) and BASH_ENV filters (#579) must pass through under $(), pipes and redirects, e.g. by comparing fd 1 with the top shell's.
test: Through the shim run git log --format=%H | xargs echo, V=$(pytest -q), and cmd > f; assert byte-identical to the real binary and exit codes equal.
because: shell-level shim must pass through pipes; harness-agnostic

title: Idle-time memory consolidation by a cheap model at SessionEnd
detail: Letta's sleep-time compute and LightMem (reportedly) move memory reorganisation off the hot path. A SessionEnd job on Haiku merges duplicate auto-memory entries, drops ones contradicted by current code and re-caps file size, leaving a git-tracked diff. Every future session loads less.
test: Run on a real memory directory; compare loaded tokens before and after, and answer 10 probe questions from each version with a fixed reader.
because: SessionEnd hook, auto-memory, cloud LLM

title: Generate .ignore files so ripgrep-backed Grep and Glob skip noise
detail: ripgrep honours .ignore and .rgignore beyond .gitignore. List tracked-but-noisy paths (vendor, snapshots, *.min.js, lockfiles, generated code) there: searches stop returning them while direct Read still works, unlike deny rules (#401). Claude Code's Grep reportedly uses bundled ripgrep.
test: Verify that Grep and Glob honour .ignore: in a repo with vendored dirs, compare result tokens before and after adding it, and confirm Read of an ignored path works.
because: ripgrep .ignore files, no harness feature

title: Rejoin backslash-wrapped pandas DataFrame column chunks
detail: With display.max_columns=None, pandas splits wide frames into backslash-continued column chunks, repeating the index in each. Rejoin chunks into one tab-separated table with the index once. Synthetic 30x14 frame: 2417 vs 2032 o200k tokens.
test: Print 10 wide frames; rejoin chunks, assert cell equality against df.to_csv, tokenise both forms, ask cell-lookup questions on each.
because: pandas chunk rejoin, pure text transform
check: Backslash-wrapped pandas column chunks are joined into one tab-separated table with the index once; every cell lands under its own header (cut at the header words' right edges) and every row reads as the same words in the same order.
check_loses: column alignment padding, the wrap backslashes and the repeated index columns

title: Decode JSON-escaped source lines in notebook git diffs
detail: git diff of .ipynb shows each code line as a quoted JSON string ending in \n, plus execution_count and metadata hunks on every re-run. Decode to plain lines, fold counter and output hunks. Synthetic hunk: 98 vs 34 o200k tokens. Reading notebooks is #322.
test: Re-run a real notebook and git diff it; render a per-cell plain diff; confirm code edits survive and output hunks collapse to counts; tokenise before and after.
because: decodes JSON-escaped notebook diff lines
check: In 'diff --git' sections of .ipynb files, JSON string element lines are decoded to 'm|text', execution_count lines are folded to one '~|execution_count -a +b' per hunk, image payloads become '<blob mime N>' stubs, and a hunk whose only changes are counters and payloads keeps no context lines; every added, removed and context source line, every hunk header, every other line and every other file's diff is unchanged.
check_loses: the trailing \n and comma of each decoded element (so which element was last in an array), the execution_count values and their context lines, image payload bytes (size only), and context lines of hunks that changed nothing but counters and images; a diff that already holds the legend or a '|' decoded-looking line inside a notebook is left unchanged

title: Print symmetric matrices as triangles, sparse ones as cells
detail: df.corr(), covariance, distance and similarity matrices repeat values across the diagonal; confusion matrices are mostly zeros. If exactly symmetric, print the upper triangle with a note; if mostly zero, list nonzero cells. Synthetic 12x12 corr: 498 tokens, 389 for triangle numbers alone (ceiling).
test: Print corr() for 10 datasets and a 50-class confusion matrix; check exact symmetry, expand back to the identical matrix, ask 'most correlated pair' on both forms.
because: matrix triangle/sparse reprint, pure text
check: A whitespace-aligned matrix whose cell texts are exactly symmetric (labels equal to the header) is printed as its upper triangle; one that is mostly a single filler token is printed as its non-filler cells; expanding either gives back the identical token matrix.
check_loses: alignment whitespace

title: Fold psql \x and mysql \G records into one table
detail: Expanded mode prints '-[ RECORD n ]-' or '*** n. row ***' then a padded name|value line per field, repeating column names every row. Parse runs of records sharing a column list into one header plus value rows. #410 covers only one-line records.
test: Run psql \x and mysql \G on a 20-row, 15-column table; convert to a table, assert cell equality, tokenise both, ask which row has the max of a column.
because: folds expanded psql/mysql records into a table
check: psql `\x` or mysql `\G` record listings become one header line plus a tab-separated value line per record (a new table where the column list changes); a parser per format yields the same (column, value) records from both forms.
check_loses: the record separator lines (numbers must be 1..N), dash widths and name-column padding

title: Prune EXPLAIN ANALYZE plan nodes by share of actual time
detail: Postgres and MySQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE trees print cost, rows, loops, Buffers and Output lines for every node. Keep nodes above about 2% of total actual time, big estimate-versus-actual row misses, and the Planning/Execution footer; fold the rest to 'N fast nodes'. Original saved.
test: Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on a six-table join in local Postgres; prune; ask slowest node, any seq scan, worst misestimate on both forms; tokenise.
because: prunes plan nodes by time share, text

title: Schemas from Spark, BigQuery, Glue, Avro as name-type lines
detail: PySpark StructType reprs, printSchema '(nullable = true)' rails, bq show prettyjson field objects, Glue get-table Columns and .avsc files spend a nested object or call per column. Emit 'name type' lines, flagging only non-default nullability or mode. Synthetic 5-column repr: 55 vs 16 o200k tokens.
test: Capture df.schema, printSchema, bq show --format=prettyjson and glue get-table for five wide tables; convert, round-trip name-type pairs, tokenise, ask one column's type.
because: schema output to name-type lines

title: dbt console pack: fold START/OK pairs, dot leaders, debug SQL
detail: dbt build prints 'N of M START ... [RUN]' then an OK line, with dot leaders and clock prefixes; --debug adds connection, BEGIN/COMMIT and SQL echoes. One line per node; keep failures and warnings. Synthetic 10 models (from memory): 600 vs 170 o200k tokens.
test: Run dbt build on jaffle-shop with DuckDB, plain and --debug; classify lines by template, fold, ask which node failed and how many tests passed; tokenise both.
because: folds dbt START/OK pairs in console output
check: dbt result lines lose their clock prefix and dot leaders and their START lines are dropped when a result line with the same 'N of M' exists; --debug blocks (a [debug] line and the SQL lines under it) are dropped unless a line in the block names an error or failure; every node's status, description and timing, START lines with no result, failure details and the Done summary are unchanged.
check_loses: the clock time of each node line, the dot-leader alignment, and the connection, BEGIN/COMMIT and SQL-echo lines of --debug runs

title: Digest dbt manifest, run_results and catalog JSON reads
detail: target/manifest.json carries each node's raw_code, compiled_code, macros, docs and checksums; run_results.json repeats timing arrays and adapter_response per node (from memory, unmeasured). On cat or jq reads emit per-node name, materialization, depends_on, status and failure message; full file stays on disk.
test: Compile a sample dbt project, cat its manifest and run_results; rank key families by token share, build the digest, ask upstream models of X and failed tests on both.
because: digests dbt JSON read output, text transform
check: A dbt manifest becomes one line per node and source (type, materialization, file, upstream nodes, test name and column), run_results one line per result with status, time, rows, failures and the message of every non-success (plus status counts and command), and catalog one line per relation with its columns; the upstream and downstream models of every node, every failing or erroring test with its message, skipped nodes and status counts are unchanged.
check_loses: raw_code, compiled_code, macros, docs, exposures, checksums, config keys other than materialized, column descriptions, parent_map/child_map (derivable from depends_on), timing arrays, adapter responses, thread ids, catalog stats and column comments, success messages, and JSON whitespace; the full artifact stays on disk

title: Fold identical idle GPU blocks in nvidia-smi output
detail: nvidia-smi prints a bordered block per GPU, so an 8-GPU idle node repeats equal fields. Fold equal-state GPUs into 'GPU 0-7 A100-80GB idle 4MiB 0% 34C'; keep busy GPUs and process rows verbatim. Synthetic 8 idle GPUs (layout approximate): 712 vs 43 o200k tokens.
test: Capture nvidia-smi from a multi-GPU box or posted samples; fold, ask which GPUs are free and which processes hold memory, compare tokens; check XID or ECC errors survive.
because: folds identical idle GPU blocks

title: Fold layer-index families in parameter and summary listings
detail: state_dict keys, named_parameters, safetensors headers, Keras summary tables and gguf-dump repeat 'layers.N.' names with identical shapes across N layers. Fold to 'layers.{0..31}.self_attn.q_proj.weight [4096,4096]' when shapes match; outliers stay listed. Synthetic 128 keys: 2560 vs 31 o200k tokens (ceiling).
test: Dump parameter shapes of a small Hugging Face model and a safetensors header; fold, expand back to the exact original lines, ask the shape of layer 7's k_proj.
because: fold layer-index families in listings
check: 3+ consecutive layers whose lines are identical apart from the index fold to '§prefix{a..b} k' plus the k lines once; layers that differ stay listed whole and decode restores the exact bytes.

title: Keep only best-improving trials in Optuna and Ray Tune logs
detail: Optuna logs 'Trial N finished with value: v and parameters: {...}. Best is trial K' per trial; Ray Tune reprints a status table. Keep best-improving trials, failures and the final best; fold the rest to counts. Synthetic 20 trials: 1340 vs 66 o200k tokens (ceiling).
test: Run a 100-trial Optuna study on a toy objective plus a small Ray Tune run; fold, ask best parameters, failed trials and trial count; tokenise both forms.
because: keep best trials; text transform

title: conda and mamba pack: solver chatter, Package Plan, build strings
detail: conda install/create prints metadata and solve chatter, a Package Plan, download tables and per-package build strings; conda list repeats a Channel column and build hashes. Keep name and version changes, conflicts and errors; steer conda env export to --no-builds (from memory).
test: Run conda or mamba create with 15 packages, then conda list and env export; classify lines by template, filter, ask which packages changed and why a conflict failed; tokenise.
because: drops conda solver chatter from output

title: Reassemble SSE and streaming-chunk JSON into final text
detail: curl -N of OpenAI- or Anthropic-style streams yields one data: JSON envelope per token, repeating id, model, created. Concatenate delta text and tool-call argument fragments; keep first-chunk metadata, finish_reason, usage, errors. Synthetic 66 chunks: 3,752 vs 48 o200k tokens.
test: Capture streamed completions with curl -N; reassemble; assert text equals the non-stream response; tokenise both; confirm mid-stream error events and truncated streams survive.
because: reassembles SSE chunks in tool output text
check: OpenAI chat-completion chunk streams and Anthropic message event streams become a header (flavour, id, model, created, chunk count), the concatenated text per choice or block (escaped), tool calls with name, id and joined arguments, finish or stop reason, usage, every error event, and 'end: done|truncated|partial' with the raw tail of a stream cut mid-event; the text, tool arguments, reasons, usage, errors and end state are unchanged.
check_loses: the per-chunk boundaries and timing, logprobs, system_fingerprint, role deltas, Anthropic ping events and block-stop events, event ids and comments, the exact interleaving of text and tool-call fragments, and the first-chunk fields other than id, model and created; streams with a bad JSON event before the last, CRLF framing, unknown fields or an unknown flavour are left unchanged

title: Unwrap DynamoDB, Firestore and Mongo extended-JSON type tags
detail: aws dynamodb scan wraps values as {"S":..}, {"N":".."}, {"M":{..}}; Firestore uses stringValue/mapValue.fields; Mongo canonical EJSON uses $oid, $date, $numberLong. A known-wrapper table gives plain values plus a legend. Synthetic 20 items: 1,319 vs 762 (DynamoDB), 1,282 vs 1,002 (EJSON) o200k tokens.
test: Run aws dynamodb scan and mongoexport --jsonFormat canonical on sample data; unwrap; assert reverse mapping restores input; tokenise; ask attribute-type questions on both.
because: unwraps type-tagged JSON, deterministic

title: Digest CycloneDX, SPDX and syft SBOM JSON to component lines
detail: Each component repeats bom-ref and purl, derivable cpe, hashes and tool properties; dependency edges repeat those refs. Emit 'name@version license' lines plus edges by short index. Synthetic 40 components: 8,382 vs 369 o200k tokens (repetitive hashes, so indicative only).
test: Run npm sbom --sbom-format cyclonedx or syft on a small repo; digest; tokenise by field class; ask licence and depends-on questions on both forms.
because: SBOM JSON digest, pure text transform

title: Group Graphviz DOT and edge-list graphs by source node
detail: terraform graph, madge --dot, go mod graph and bazel query print one quoted edge per line, repeating '[root] ' prefixes and '(expand)' suffixes. Emit 'node -> a, b, c' adjacency lines, drop quotes. Synthetic 75 edges: 1,904 vs 459 o200k tokens.
test: Capture terraform graph and go mod graph on real repos; convert; assert the edge set round-trips apart from dropped decorations; tokenise; ask reverse-dependency questions on both.
because: groups edge lists into adjacency lines

title: Plist XML key/value pairs to compact typed key: value lines
detail: Info.plist, entitlements and launchd plists spell each pair as <key>K</key><string>V</string> under a DOCTYPE header. Render type-preserving key: value lines (bool, int, date markers), round-trip checked via plistlib. Synthetic 7-key Info.plist: 246 vs 74 o200k tokens. #525 only strips whitespace.
test: Convert 20 real Info.plist, entitlements and LaunchAgents files; assert plistlib.loads equality after reverse conversion; tokenise before and after; skip files about to be edited.
because: plist XML to compact lines
check: A canonical XML property list becomes indentation-structured `key: value` lines with bare or JSON-quoted strings and typed bool/int/real/@date/@data values; decoding rebuilds the identical plist text with plistlib, and a file plistlib would not reproduce byte for byte is left untouched.

title: Fold Relay Connection and Edge boilerplate types in GraphQL SDL
detail: In schema.graphql, every object type has XConnection{edges,nodes,pageInfo,totalCount} and XEdge{cursor,node} twins. When they match the template exactly, print one legend line plus a name list; deviations stay verbatim. Synthetic 8 types: 378 vs 37 o200k tokens. #521 covers introspection JSON only.
test: Fetch a public SDL (GitHub's schema.docs.graphql); count types matching the template exactly; fold; assert unfolding reproduces the file byte for byte; tokenise.
because: folds GraphQL SDL boilerplate types
check: Relay XConnection{edges,nodes,pageInfo,totalCount} and XEdge{cursor,node} blocks that match the template character for character become one-line markers under a one-line legend; any deviating block, other type and every other byte stays verbatim, and decode restores the exact original.

title: Sparse wide CSV and TSV: emit only non-empty cells
detail: Feature matrices, exported forms and wide report CSVs are mostly empty cells: runs of commas. Past roughly 70% empty, print the header once, then rows as col=value for filled cells, keeping row order. Synthetic 40 columns, 3 filled: 609 vs 479 o200k tokens.
test: Find wide CSVs in saved outputs; compute empty-cell share; convert rows; assert reverse conversion restores the CSV; tokenise; ask which rows have column X filled.
because: sparse CSV re-encoding, pure text
check: A CSV/TSV with at least 70% empty cells becomes its header once plus one line of name=rawcell pairs per row (filled cells only, row order kept); decode restores the exact bytes, including quoted cells with commas, quotes and newlines and a missing final newline.

title: Skeleton-plus-slots fold for near-identical sibling JSON subtrees
detail: #35 needs exact equality, #32 flat rows. OpenAPI paths (CORS OPTIONS, API Gateway mock integrations), CloudFormation resources and k8s items share one nested skeleton differing in few leaves. Print the skeleton once, then per-sibling leaf overrides. Synthetic 25 paths: 4,564 vs 761 o200k tokens.
test: Export an API Gateway OpenAPI file and a CloudFormation template; cluster siblings by structural hash; fold; assert expansion restores parsed equality; measure the real foldable share.
because: skeleton-plus-slots fold of JSON siblings
check: Runs of 3+ consecutive sibling subtrees with the same key structure are replaced by one skeleton plus per-sibling slot values (dict runs keep their keys); expanding the folded JSON gives back the same parsed value, key order and number types.
check_loses: JSON whitespace, number spelling (1e2 vs 100.0, 1.50 vs 1.5) and string escape form; inputs with duplicate keys, NaN/Infinity or the sigil are left untouched

title: Strip type and length tags from var_dump and spew
detail: PHP var_dump prints string(5) "Alice" and array(3) {; Go spew prints (string) (len=5) and (main.User) per value; lengths are derivable. Rewrite to JSON-like, quotes preserving types, object ids dropped. Synthetic 24 rows: var_dump 1,238 and spew 992 vs 347 o200k tokens. #808 only joins lines.
test: Capture var_dump of a Laravel or WordPress object and spew.Dump of a Go struct; convert; verify values and nesting match; tokenise; ask field-value questions on both.
because: strips var_dump/spew type tags, text rewrite

title: Lift escaped multi-line JSON strings into raw side blocks
detail: Stack traces, diffs and file bodies inside JSON strings keep \n and \" escapes, so line rules (traceback, dedupe, templates) cannot see them. Replace with a placeholder; print the raw string after the JSON. Synthetic 24-line trace: 405 vs 376 tokens; mainly enables other rules.
test: Take pino or Sentry JSON with stack fields; lift strings; run existing line rules on both forms; assert unlifting restores parsed equality; compare tokens.
because: unescapes JSON strings into side blocks
check: A JSON string value with 3+ newline escapes whose lexeme is exactly its canonical encoding is replaced by a placeholder and printed raw (real newlines, no escapes) in a length-framed block after the JSON; decode restores the exact bytes. Keys, non-canonical lexemes (\u00e9, \/) and short strings stay in place.

title: Digest agent transcript JSONL to role, text and tool lines
detail: Claude Code, Codex rollout and stream-json logs wrap each turn in uuid, parentUuid, usage, cache and duplicated toolUseResult fields. Emit 'role: text' and 'tool(name,args) -> result' lines. One local 134-line transcript: about 87% of o200k tokens sat outside message content.
test: Digest several session JSONL files; tokenise envelope versus content; ask which command ran at turn N and its result on both; check interplay with #716 read denial.
because: depends on products' private transcript log formats

title: Compare stub back-reference formats the model can resolve
detail: Stubs like 'unchanged since turn 12' assume a turn index the model cannot see in its context. Compare pointer grammars: turn number, command text plus first-line quote, or a short tag the hook appends to long outputs. Pick the one resolved without re-running.
test: Build a 30-turn transcript with one stub per format; ask what the earlier result said about X; score correct answers and count re-runs per format.
because: compare stub pointer formats; experiment

title: Dedup ledger must store emitted text, not originals
detail: A stub saying 'lines already shown' is false for words the hook deleted from the earlier output. Record the updatedToolOutput text per call and match later lines against it; partly deleted lines count as unseen and are re-emitted in full.
test: Compress output A with the hook, then run B sharing 30 lines with A. Assert every B line stubbed as seen is byte-present in A's emitted text.
because: dedup ledger of emitted text, local state

title: Recovery view prints only deleted spans with word anchors
detail: Reading a saved original re-pays the roughly half of words already in context. Save the keep mask; a recall mode prints each deleted span between two kept anchor words, so context plus complement reconstructs the original. Differs from #562 tier re-render.
test: On 20 compressed outputs, tokenise the full original versus the anchored deleted-span view; check re-merging with the emitted text reproduces the original byte for byte.
because: recovery view of deleted spans from saved mask

title: Subtract the model's own edited files from git status
detail: A session set of Edit and Write targets is built from PostToolUse. git status, diff --stat and --name-only lines for paths the model itself edited become a count ('11 files = your edits'); only foreign, untracked or unexpected paths are listed.
test: Scan transcripts: for each git status, diff --stat or --name-only result, count paths equal to earlier Edit/Write file_path values; report lines and tokens avoidable.
because: edit targets visible in earlier tool_use inputs

title: Strip Agent report passages copied from the prompt
detail: Subagent reports often restate the task, file lists or code the parent wrote into the Agent prompt. PostToolUse on Agent compares report lines of 40+ characters against tool_input.prompt and replaces verbatim matches with a one-line marker.
test: Over transcripts, for each Agent result compute the share of lines of 40+ characters that appear verbatim in the prompt; report tokens per call.
because: dedupe result lines matching earlier call input

title: Drop Bash output lines that restate the command text
detail: tool_input already holds the command. npm run banners, make recipe echoes, set -x traces of the model's own heredoc, 'git commit' subject echoes and -v flags repeat pieces of it. Remove output lines that are substrings of the command, with a count.
test: From transcripts, count output lines of 20+ characters that are substrings of the same call's command, grouped by first word; sample 30 for information loss.
because: uses command string from tool call payload

title: Line-keyed delta for repeated git diff after further edits
detail: Hunk-hash dedup (#139) fails when a hunk grows by a few lines, the typical edit-diff-edit loop. Key each +/- line by (file, content); print only unseen lines under their current hunk header plus 'N lines as before', so patches stay readable.
test: Make 8 incremental edits to one function, running git diff after each. Compare tokens of full diffs, hunk-hash dedup and line-keyed delta.
because: line-keyed delta over earlier diff results
check: For repeated git diff after incremental edits, diff body lines already shown literally (same file, same text and marker) become 'K lines as before: turn T lines a-b' pointers under the current literal @@ headers; where hunk-hash dedup saves nothing, this saves a measured share; other files, unseen lines, hostile text and compaction stay literal.

title: Encode a Read as a unified diff against sibling file
detail: Config variants, locale catalogs, per-env Terraform, similar test files and vendored copies are read back to back. If the new file has difflib ratio of 0.7+ with a file already read, emit 'same as PATH with these changes' plus the diff. Exactly reversible.
test: In three repos, list same-directory file pairs with ratio at least 0.7; tokenise the full second file versus the unified diff; count pairs transcripts read within ten turns.
because: diff against similar earlier-read file, reversible
check: A full Read whose lines have difflib ratio >= 0.7 with a file the model already read in full is shown as 'same as PATH' plus a diff over text lines against the text the model holds; applying the diff to that text returns exactly the Read's lines, and dissimilar files, a path's own re-read, ranged reads, CRLF twins and compaction stay literal.

title: Elide outer stack frames shared with an earlier traceback
detail: Different exceptions in one session share framework and runner frames (pytest, Django, uvicorn, Node internals). Replace a frame run identical to an earlier trace's outer frames with 'N outer frames as before'; keep application frames and the exception line. #533 handles identical errors only.
test: Collect tracebacks from 10 pytest/Django failures in one repo; compute the longest common outer frame run between consecutive distinct exceptions and the tokens it holds.
because: elide frames shared with earlier traceback

title: Drop line templates seen in three distinct commands' outputs
detail: Per-family baselines (#142) miss boilerplate shared across commands: npm deprecation warnings, runtime banners, repeated table headers, Python warnings. Mask digits and ids, count distinct commands per template in a session, and fold a template from its third distinct command on, with a count.
test: Over transcripts, template-normalise output lines, count templates in 3+ distinct command strings, report their token share and check no failing-test or error lines are among them.
because: cross-command template dedup with session state

title: Learn per-host page chrome from the first fetch
detail: Raw curl and fetch-MCP pages from one docs site repeat nav, footer and cookie lines; fixed regexes age badly. After two fetches from one host, lines present in both are chrome: drop them from later pages, keeping the first page whole as the reference.
test: Fetch five pages from each of three docs sites; compute line sets shared by two pages; count their tokens; verify by hand that no shared line is body content.
because: learn page chrome from earlier fetches, local state

title: SubagentStart hook hands children the parent's read manifest
detail: Sidechain agents may re-read files the parent read before spawning. A SubagentStart hook (reportedly supports additionalContext) injects a short list of paths and one-line digests the parent holds, only when the task prompt names those paths. Net effect is uncertain.
test: Verify that SubagentStart accepts additionalContext. Find sidechain Reads of paths the parent Read earlier; compare child tokens with and without an injected manifest on 10 delegated tasks.
because: SubagentStart hook

title: Replace default system prompt in non-coding headless runs
detail: Every headless or workflow child re-pays Claude Code's coding system prompt. --system-prompt, --system-prompt-file or an output style with keep-coding-instructions false reportedly replace it. Cache hits soften the saving; measure it. Complements #155 and #500.
test: Verify that the flags exist. Compare input plus cache-creation tokens of claude -p 'hi' --output-format json, default versus replaced prompt; then run 10 non-coding tasks, checking tool calls.
because: harness system-prompt flags and output styles

title: Test exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections for cross-directory cache sharing
detail: Claude Code reportedly offers --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections, moving cwd, environment and git status from the system prompt into the first user message. Identical system blocks then share cache across repos and parallel claude -p jobs started within the TTL.
test: Verify that the flag exists in --help. Start two sessions in different cwds within 5 minutes, with and without it; compare cache_read_input_tokens on the second session's first request.
because: Claude Code CLI flag

title: Measure context left behind by /context, /cost and /mcp output
detail: Built-in local commands reportedly log their output as local-command-stdout messages that later requests may carry. Every /context check in a session could re-pay its grid each turn. Measure per command; prefer a statusline for monitoring.
test: Verify that the output persists: run /context then /cost in a fresh session behind a logging proxy (#187); check whether the next request body includes it and count its tokens.
because: harness slash-command output

title: Pass through output of commands run from skill directories
detail: Skills tell the agent to run bundled validators or generators and read the result exactly. Those commands have paths under skills/ or the plugin cache, which the hook ignores, so it may prune checker output. Match the path, then skip or force protect.
test: Collect Bash calls whose command contains /skills/ or /plugins/cache/ from transcripts; list outputs over 6,000 chars; run the hook and diff kept lines against error lines.
because: skill and plugin cache directories

title: Lint CLAUDE.md bullets restating the built-in prompt or other layers
detail: Generated or copied rules often repeat what the default system prompt and tool descriptions already say, or what ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md already says. Score each bullet's shingle overlap with a captured system prompt and the other layers; flag for deletion.
test: Capture the system prompt via a logging proxy (#187), compute shingle overlap for bullets in 5 real CLAUDE.md files, hand-check flags, then ablate them with #550's replay.
because: lints CLAUDE.md bullets

title: Audit the token tax of non-English instruction files
detail: Quick o200k proxy check of one three-sentence rule: 22 tokens in English, 30 Dutch, 32 German, 35 Russian, 45 Japanese. Always-on CLAUDE.md, skills and commands in other languages may cost 1.4 to 2x; translate them, keep reply language separate.
test: Count a real non-English CLAUDE.md and its English translation with Anthropic's token-count endpoint; replay 10 tasks to confirm rule adherence holds.
because: advice to translate instruction files

title: Map Codex AGENTS.md chain loads and project_doc_max_bytes cap
detail: Codex reportedly concatenates AGENTS.md files from repo root to cwd, capped by project_doc_max_bytes (32 KiB reported), silently dropping the tail. Monorepos repeat rules per level. Dedupe levels, lower the cap deliberately, keep critical rules above the cut.
test: Verify that the cap exists. Put a canary in each AGENTS.md level, run codex exec with a logged request; see which arrive; then dedupe, cap at 8192, compare input tokens.
because: Codex AGENTS.md loading and config cap

title: Detect duplicate skills, commands and agents across scopes
detail: The same skill can be installed as a plugin, copied into ~/.claude/skills and left in a legacy commands directory, so its name and description may be listed more than once. Extends #643 beyond MCP servers to the skill listing.
test: Walk user, project and plugin-cache directories, hash SKILL.md bodies and names, list collisions, and sum their listing tokens from /context before and after removal.
because: Claude Code skill and command listing across plugin scopes

title: Point agents at raw AGENTS.md, skipping the GitHub page
detail: A user saying 'install ctxprune' sends the agent to the repo page, where WebFetch summarizes README and AGENTS.md through a small model. A first README line linking raw AGENTS.md (plus llms.txt) gives exact steps in about 2.5 kB.
test: Ask a fresh agent to install from the repo URL with and without the link; log fetch tokens and count missed steps.
because: README and docs packaging for agent install

title: Learned protect head replacing the is_protected regex
detail: Second head trained to flag atoms a reader later needs verbatim (labels from teacher answer-span quotes and agent copy-forward). Context-aware: keeps the failing test id, drops the 500th timestamp. Frees budget now eaten by force-kept numbers.
test: Label protect=1 where a later command or answer copies the atom; train head on frozen encoder; compare copied-atom recall and QA at equal chars versus regex protection.
because: learned local protect head, text-only

title: Orphan-value coupling: keep numbers with their label words
detail: force_protected keeps numbers while their labels can drop; random stub scores turned 'Compiled 142 modules in 3.2s with 2 warnings' into '142 3.2s 2'. Post-pass keeps the nearest preceding word of each kept number, or drops numbers whose label went.
test: On 50 saved outputs, count kept numeric atoms with no kept word within two atoms on the line; run QA on 'how many/how long' questions for each variant.
because: deterministic post-pass on kept atoms

title: Mid-line crop augmentation to match inference window seams
detail: chunking.py cuts training chunks on line boundaries, but compress.py cuts inference windows at any atom every ~510 tokens. Randomly crop training chunks to mid-line starts and ends, labels kept, so seam tokens are in-distribution.
test: Measure val AUC by token position inside fixed windows; fine-tune with crops; compare first/last-32-token AUC and QA at 0.5 on outputs over 6,000 chars.
because: training augmentation for scorer

title: Group-DRO training loss over source and format groups
detail: Replace average cross-entropy with group-DRO (Sagawa et al., 2020): online exponentiated weights on per-group loss over code, non-English, JSON, logs, prose. Aims at the weaknesses AGENTS.md admits, not the average.
test: Fine-tune one epoch from the current checkpoint with group-DRO; report per-group and worst-group within-chunk AUC versus baseline, then QA on code and non-English slices at 0.5.
because: training loss change for scorer

title: Gradient-boosted rescorer over frozen scores and handcrafted features
detail: Train LightGBM LambdaRank on the classifier's atom score, neighbour scores, atom class, line position, repeat count and command family, with teacher labels. One learned rescoring replaces hand-tuned adjustments; retrains on CPU in minutes, no encoder retrain.
test: From a frozen score table of 500 outputs, train on 70% of chunks; compare top-50% atom recall and QA at equal chars versus raw scores on the held-out 30%.
because: local CPU rescorer on text features

title: Small-encoder bake-off: ELECTRA-small, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall, MiniLM
detail: Fine-tune each on the existing labels. ELECTRA's replaced-token-detection pretraining is token-level like this task, and it is reportedly about 14M parameters, so load time and latency could drop. English-only vocabularies are the risk.
test: Train each on v1 labels for equal epochs; report val AUC, top-50% atom overlap with mmBERT-small, int8 ONNX size, ms per window, and QA at 0.5.
because: swapping the local scorer backbone

title: Weight-only int8 or 4-bit ONNX with fp32 activations
detail: The export comment says signed int8 or a quantized head collapses keep agreement to 0.1-0.84. Try weight-only quantization (ORT MatMulNBits for 4-bit, reportedly available), leaving activations in fp32, for fewer rank flips at similar size. Differs from #836.
test: Export dynamic-int8, weight-only int8 and 4-bit variants; compare Spearman and top-50% atom agreement with fp32 on 500 windows, file MB, ms per window.
because: quantising the local scorer, not the reader

title: Read-only header carry-over prefix for later scoring windows
detail: Windows after the first lose the table header row, JSON parent keys and test-suite banner. Prepend the first lines plus the nearest lower-indent scope line to each later window, labels masked in training and ignored at inference.
test: On 30 multi-window tables and JSON outputs, compare window-2+ scores with and without prefix against a 4k-token whole-document pass; then QA at 0.5 and latency.
because: scorer-input context from same output, deterministic

title: Per-line sentinel tokens with a learned line keep head
detail: Insert one learnable token at each line start; pool its hidden state into a line-level keep/drop head trained on lines the teacher emptied, beside the atom head. Whole-line drops become one learned decision, not a sum of atom scores.
test: Count teacher-emptied lines in v1 labels; train the sentinel head; compare line-drop precision and recall against thresholding mean atom score (#87) and QA at 0.5 on logs and test output.
because: local scorer architecture, pure text function

title: Structured-twin labels: machine-readable output marks essential atoms
detail: Run each build or test command twice, human text and machine-readable form (cargo --message-format=json, go test -json, eslint -f json, pytest junitxml). Atoms matching the tool's own file, line, code, message and test-name fields get keep=1; the rest drop, with no LLM teacher.
test: On 20 small repos, make twin pairs for 3 tools; measure agreement with the LLM teacher; fine-tune on twin labels; compare AUC on cargo, pytest, eslint outputs.
because: labels from tools' machine-readable output, offline

title: Spillover test: holdout controls contaminated by earlier compressed calls
detail: Per-call randomization (#178) assumes no interference, yet earlier compressed results and notes may teach the agent to grep originals or rerun on later control calls. Compare control-call refetch rates by prior treated-call count; if spillover appears, move to session-level arms (#629).
test: From holdout logs, regress control-call refetch on prior treated-call count with session random effects; compare control calls in all-control sessions against mixed sessions.
because: holdout spillover test

title: Prune saturated and zero-signal QA items to raise power
detail: Many span questions are answered by every arm or by none, adding reader cost without information. Estimate per-item discrimination from cached answers across methods and keep rates, keep items whose correctness moves with keep rate, and recompute the minimum detectable effect (#174).
test: Compute per-item variance and item-rest correlation over all cached arms; select on half the chunks, compare MDE and winner ordering on the other half versus the full set.
because: eval item pruning for power

title: Agentic A/B sizing from A/A discordant-pair rate
detail: Pass/fail pairs only inform through discordant tasks. Run the baseline twice per task to measure discordance from agent randomness alone, then use an exact McNemar or Bayesian non-inferiority calculation to size the task pool for a stated margin before spending on hook-on arms.
test: Run 20 tasks twice with the hook off; count discordant tasks; compute tasks needed for a 5-point non-inferiority margin at 80% power; compare with the 25-task plan.
because: A/B sizing statistics

title: Cost per resolved task, not mean tokens
detail: A cheaper arm that fails more can cost more per solution. Report expected spend per pass (mean cost divided by pass rate, counting failed runs) with task-level bootstrap intervals, plus worst-decile task cost, and check whether arm ranking flips versus mean-token ranking.
test: From any hook-on/off task runs, compute cost per pass and mean tokens per arm; 10k task-level bootstrap; report probability that the ranking differs between metrics.
because: cost per resolved task metric

title: Joint multi-fact checklist questions over test and build logs
detail: Single-span questions let each fact survive independently. Agent decisions need several facts together: failing test, assertion, file:line, count. Score all-or-nothing against regex-derived checklists and compare joint accuracy with the product of per-fact accuracies to expose correlated loss.
test: Script 100 checklists of 3-4 spans over pytest, cargo and tsc logs; score reader on original versus 0.5 kept; report joint accuracy and the product-of-singles gap.
because: joint multi-fact eval questions

title: Multi-output contexts: vary how many of N results are compressed
detail: Evals compress one chunk per prompt, but live sessions mix several compressed and raw results. Stitch N=6 real outputs, compress k of them, and ask about one fixed output to test cumulative harm, cross-reference loss and over-trust of gaps versus the single-chunk score.
test: Build 100 questions with N=6 stitched contexts at k=0, 3, 6 compressed; compare EM across k and against single-chunk EM with a paired chunk-level bootstrap.
because: multi-output context eval

title: Answer-multiplicity audit: duplicate gold spans inflate survival and EM
detail: parse_qas accepts any answer found in the chunk, even if the span occurs several times. A surviving duplicate then counts as retaining the intended one. Count occurrences per gold span and recompute survival and EM on unique-answer questions only.
test: Count casefolded occurrences of each gold in its chunk; report the share above one; compare survival and EM between unique and repeated groups using cached contexts, zero LLM calls.
because: eval answer-multiplicity audit

title: Racing evaluation: drop losing variants after early question batches
detail: Hundreds of rule and rate variants each pay for the full question set. Evaluate in batches and eliminate variants whose paired interval falls outside the incumbent's non-inferiority band (F-race or successive halving), so reader calls concentrate on contenders.
test: Simulate on cached answers: 30 variants, 100 random question orders; compare reader calls spent and agreement of the final winner against full-set evaluation.
because: racing evaluation procedure

title: Reader reasoning on versus off across keep rates
detail: The local reader runs with thinking disabled, while Claude Code agents usually reason before acting. Reasoning may reconstruct missing words or notice gaps, shifting the best keep rate, at a thinking-token cost. Compare method gaps and total tokens with reasoning on and off.
test: Re-run cached contexts at keep 0.33, 0.5 and 1.0 with enable_thinking true via --extra-body; compare EM gap to original and output tokens per answer, paired bootstrap by chunk.
because: dev-time reader reasoning comparison

title: Session-level harm budget allocated greedily across rules
detail: Rules are judged one at a time, but users bear total loss. Rank rules by tokens saved per point of harm (QA drop or refetch rate), enable greedily until a pre-registered budget is spent, then verify stacked harm does not exceed the sum of singles.
test: For 10 rules, tabulate replay savings and parity-QA drop; pick top-5 by ratio; measure QA drop of the stacked set versus the sum of single-rule drops.
because: harm-budget analysis across rules

title: Tool-output cassettes so agent A/B arms differ only in hook
detail: Reruns of the same task see different timings, ordering and hashes in tool output, adding noise. Record raw outputs keyed by command plus tree hash in the baseline run; the second arm replays them through the hook, falling back to live execution on divergence.
