test: Run 10 tasks twice live and measure the share of repeated commands whose outputs differ byte-wise; then compare turn-count variance of live A/A against cassette A/A.
because: tool-output cassettes for A/B

title: Unexposed-task negative control for hook A/B designs
detail: Tasks whose outputs all stay under 6,000 chars should show no hook effect. Include them as a stratum: any hook-on versus hook-off difference there reflects non-compression side effects (latency, hook errors, double registration, noise) and gives a baseline to subtract. Complements #572.
test: Pick 15 tasks with zero would-be firings in shadow mode; run both arms 3 times; test on-minus-off pass-rate and turns differences against zero; use as difference-in-differences baseline.
because: unexposed-task negative control

title: Git textconv drivers shrink lockfile and generated diffs
detail: A diff.<driver>.textconv script bound in .gitattributes drops integrity, resolved and minified-line noise before git diff, show and log -p print it, with no agent hook. Checked on a synthetic repo: show and log -p honor it; textconv output will not git apply.
test: Run a real package-lock.json bump and a minified-bundle change through git diff with and without textconv; compare bytes and tokens; ask a reader which packages changed.
because: git textconv driver shrinks diff output

title: SHELL override: one wrapper shell filters every agent command
detail: Agents that spawn $SHELL -c (Aider reportedly) or take a VS Code terminal profile (Cline, Roo, Cursor reportedly) can use one wrapper that execs the real shell and filters piped output. Unlike BASH_ENV (#579) it covers login shells; a prototype kept exit code 7.
test: Verify that each agent honors SHELL. Point it at the wrapper; run a failing 20 KB command in each agent's bash tool; record exit codes and bytes returned.
because: SHELL wrapper at OS level
check: A wrapper shell passed as $SHELL execs the real shell, and for -c/-lc command strings filters stdout and keeps the exit status (7), stderr, argv and stdin; the login profile still runs, a non-bash real shell (dash) is covered, script and interactive invocations, opt-outs and a missing filter are exec'd untouched, and output is buffered until the command ends.

title: opencode plugin: port the hook via tool.execute.after
detail: opencode plugins reportedly expose tool.execute.after with a mutable output object and an experimental messages-transform hook. A small TypeScript plugin POSTs outputs over threshold to ctxprune serve and rewrites them in place, giving a native hook port with a saved original.
test: Verify the hook names in the installed opencode; write a 20-line plugin that truncates a Bash output over 6k chars; inspect the stored session JSON for the rewritten text.
because: opencode plugin API

title: Per-host matrix: can a hook rewrite, only observe, or neither?
detail: Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI reportedly ship hooks of differing schema, some observe-only. Probe each with a stub hook returning a canary; where only observation works, run ctxprune in shadow mode to forecast savings before building a proxy.
test: For each host, register a hook that tries to replace an 8k-char shell result with CANARY; check the model-visible transcript; record schema, matcher support and timeout limits in a table.
because: cross-host probe of rewrite capability, shadow forecast

title: Prune Codex, Cline and Aider history files before resume
detail: Codex rollout JSONL, Cline api_conversation_history.json and Aider chat-history markdown are plain files reloaded on resume (reportedly). A ctxprune command rewrites stale tool outputs to pruned stubs with saved originals, as #147 does for Claude transcripts.
test: Verify that resume reloads the file. Replace function_call_output bodies over 6k chars in one real rollout, codex resume it, compare first-turn input tokens, ask about three earlier results.
because: private history file formats of Codex, Cline, Aider

title: Cross-agent edit-format token census: whole, diff, udiff, apply_patch
detail: Aider's whole, diff and udiff formats, Codex apply_patch and Cline SEARCH/REPLACE all spend output and history tokens on context and anchor lines. Tally from each agent's own logs the share that is unchanged context, and which format is cheapest per edited line.
test: Run 10 identical small edits in Aider under each --edit-format with --llm-history-file; parse Codex and Cline logs for the same edits; tabulate tokens per edit.
because: tallies from each agent's private logs

title: Aider side calls: auto-commit messages and repo-map churn
detail: Aider reportedly asks the weak model for a commit message after each edit and rebuilds the repo map per --map-refresh, which can break --cache-prompts hits. Turn off auto-commits or fix --commit-prompt, set map-refresh to files, and cap --map-tokens.
test: Run a 10-edit Aider session with --llm-history-file; group tokens by call type (edit, commit, summary); repeat with the settings changed and compare cache-read tokens and totals.
because: Aider side calls and config flags

title: Roo and Cline mode tool groups shrink embedded tool docs
detail: Cline and Roo describe every tool in the system prompt, so unused browser and MCP sections are paid each request. Roo custom modes list tool groups and reportedly accept a per-mode system-prompt override file; cut browser, MCP and unused groups per mode.
test: Verify that the override file is honored. Preview the system prompt for default and read-only modes without browser and MCP groups; count tokens; compare billed input on three review tasks.
because: Roo and Cline mode config and prompt override files

title: Precomputed digest siblings for generated files, original ignored
detail: A build or post-checkout step writes small .digest files (lockfile versions, OpenAPI endpoint table) next to generated files, while ignore and deny rules hide the originals, so every agent reads the digest first. Unlike #401, deny leads somewhere useful.
test: Generate digests for a repo's lockfile and an OpenAPI file; ask five dependency or endpoint questions through an agent with ignores set; compare tokens and accuracy to raw reads.
because: digest files beside generated files, ignore-based

title: Codex execpolicy rules forbid verbose commands with a hint
detail: Codex reportedly supports Starlark rules files with prefix_rule decisions and a justification string shown to the model. Forbid bare git log, find / or npm ls with a justification naming the quiet form, steering without any hook, config only.
test: Verify rule syntax and that the justification reaches the model; run 10 codex exec tasks with and without the rules and count retried quiet commands and total tool-output tokens.
because: Codex execpolicy rules file

title: mini-swe-agent as a bash-only A/B harness
detail: mini-swe-agent reportedly has one bash tool and YAML templates controlling how observations render. That makes a hook-free, low-variance A/B bed: run ctxprune as a command wrapper or in the template, so effects are not confounded by many tools or hooks.
test: Verify the template keys; run 20 identical tasks with and without the wrapper at three seeds; compare resolved rate and total input tokens per task from trajectory logs.
because: hook-free bash-only A/B test bed

title: Pre-run install and build in setup scripts, not agent turns
detail: Cloud and sandboxed agents (Codex cloud setup scripts, Copilot setup-steps workflow, devcontainer postCreate) can run installs, builds and codegen before the agent starts, so their long logs and warnings never enter context. Agent sees a ready tree and a one-line status.
test: From recorded first-turn transcripts, sum tokens of install, build and codegen outputs; compare against the same task starting from a prepared environment; confirm the agent still finds needed failures.
because: advice on configuring agent setup scripts

title: Atomize runs of one punctuation char as a single atom
detail: atomize() emits '='*80 as 80 atoms, so rule lines, +----+ borders and |---| rows are scored per character and can be half-deleted; detok then injects spaces (synthetic mask gave '=== === ='). Keep or drop a run whole, optionally capped at 8 chars.
test: Count atoms and encoder tokens spent on punctuation runs in saved hook inputs; diff pytest and table outputs with and without run atoms.
because: atomizer change, deterministic text transform

title: Make identifier survival multiset-aware and orphan-aware
detail: idcheck.survival compares atom sets, so an ID kept once out of 50 mentions counts as survived, and under force_protected it is near 0 lost by construction. Add occurrence-weighted loss and an orphan count: kept numbers whose line label was deleted.
test: Run both versions on eval_quick outputs for ours+ids; report occurrence loss and orphan rate per source and hand-check 50 orphans.
because: identifier survival metric fix

title: Add built-in Grep and Glob results to the hook
detail: MATCHER is Bash|mcp__.* and the docstring says Grep/Glob are never matched, yet their output is not an Edit anchor (Edit requires a Read). Group Grep hits by file and hoist Glob directory prefixes losslessly, no model. Cf. #291.
test: Verify that updatedToolOutput replaces Grep and Glob results with a canary; then replay 100 recorded results through the grouper and count tokens saved with a Claude tokenizer.
because: lossless regrouping of grep/glob text output
check: Grep-style `path:line:text` runs become one `path` header plus `line:text` lines and Glob path runs one directory header plus basenames; decode restores the exact original (every hit, order, CRLF, text containing colons or paths), a leading or embedded sigil escapes or opts out, and input with no repeated file or directory comes back untouched. The real Grep/Glob tool_response shape and Claude Code's willingness to rewrite them (needs the canary in the idea) are not testable offline.

title: Match ReadMcpResourceTool, which mcp__.* misses
detail: Resource reads (docs, schemas, dumps) go through the built-in ReadMcpResourceTool, not an mcp__ name, so the hook never fires; _text_slots also only knows content[] blocks, while resource results reportedly use contents[] with text entries.
test: Log tool_name and tool_response for a resource read on an MCP server that has resources; add the name to the matcher and confirm updatedToolOutput is honored.
because: hook matcher for one harness's built-in resource tool

title: Sweep atom score aggregator: mean, first piece, minimum
detail: atom_scores averages keep-probability over every subword touching an atom, yet identifiers and URLs split into many pieces while labels were assigned per atom. First-piece or min-piece scores may rank them differently; only selection changes, no retraining.
test: Dump per-token probabilities for val chunks once (#840); compare aggregators on teacher-label F1 and reader QA at equal char rate using frozen scores.
because: score aggregation change, text only

title: Canonicalise whitespace in scorer input, not in output
detail: atom_spans rebuilds source indentation for the encoder, so pretty-printed JSON, code and aligned tables spend 510-token windows on whitespace tokens. Score a dedented, single-space form and map back by atom; output still uses source whitespace. Needs matching training inputs.
test: Measure whitespace-only share of encoder tokens and window count on 200 hook-sized inputs; compare keep-decision agreement with the original input on held-out chunks.
because: scorer input canonicalisation, deterministic text function

title: Eval takes first N rows per source in file order
detail: eval_quick.load_test keeps the first 60 rows per source as read, not a seeded sample; if the jsonl is grouped by repo or document, a source's score reflects a few groups. It also special-cases swe_smith_tool to val.
test: Count distinct group ids in each source's first 60 rows; rerun with a seeded group-stratified sample and compare per-source lost-ID rates.
because: eval sampling bias audit

title: LlamaIndex postprocessor mutates retrieved nodes in place
detail: _postprocess_nodes calls set_content on the retrieved node objects. With an in-memory docstore these may be the stored nodes, so each later query would compress already pruned text, compounding loss. Return copies instead.
test: Build a small in-memory index, run the same query three times with the postprocessor, and compare node text lengths between runs.
because: integration bug fix: return copies, not mutate

title: Switch off background requests: suggestions, recap, idle compaction, check-ins
detail: Claude Code docs list background spend: a prompt-suggestion request after every reply, session recap, idle compaction, goal check-ins (CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES=0) and inbound cross-session messages. Each re-reads the full prefix, perhaps after cache expiry. Disable per profile.
test: Verify that each setting exists. Run 15 turns plus a 150k-token session left idle past the cache TTL via the logging proxy, per setting; count unprompted requests and cache-write tokens.
because: Claude Code background request settings and env vars

title: Lean spawn prompts and idle shutdown for agent teams
detail: Claude Code docs say agent teams use about 7x the tokens of a standard session in plan mode, each teammate loads CLAUDE.md, MCP servers and skills, and idle teammates keep consuming until shut down. Test a minimal teammate profile plus a shutdown-when-idle rule.
test: Enable agent teams, spawn three teammates on one task with default versus stripped settings and a 300-token spawn prompt; compare total tokens across all teammate transcripts and task success.
because: Claude Code agent teams and subagent profile config

title: UserPromptSubmit resolves named files and symbols to path:line
detail: Docs say vague prompts trigger broad scanning. A hook extracts filenames and identifiers from the prompt, looks them up with git ls-files and rg, and injects up to five unique path:line hits as additionalContext, skipping Glob and Grep turns.
test: Take 20 recorded prompts naming files or symbols; count Glob, Grep and Read calls before the first relevant Edit, versus injected tokens and wrong-hit rate.
because: UserPromptSubmit hook injection from host search

title: Per-release empty-session token baseline canary
detail: A reported GitHub issue describes tens of thousands of tokens spent on trivial prompts in an empty directory. Log first-request input plus cache-creation tokens for each new Claude Code version, so a bloated release shows up before users pay for it.
test: Install each of the last 10 npm versions into separate prefixes, run claude -p hi --output-format json in an empty directory, and plot usage fields per version.
because: per-Claude-Code-release baseline canary

title: Net token effect of AGENTS.md: file on versus off
detail: A third-party summary of an ICSE 2026 study reportedly found AGENTS.md cut median output tokens 16.6% while total tokens stayed about equal. Measure input tax against output and turn savings on your own tasks before trimming the file.
test: Run 10 repo tasks with the file present and removed; compare input, cache-read, output tokens and turns per task, paired by task, with three repeats each.
because: AGENTS.md memory file measurement

title: Keep-the-failures A/B before stubbing dead-end attempts
detail: The Manus context-engineering post reportedly advises leaving failed actions and stack traces in context so the model updates its beliefs. Stub rules for reverted or failed spans (#338) should be tested against that claim by counting repeated identical failures.
test: Replay 15 recorded failing-then-fixed tasks with failed results kept versus one-line stubs; compare repeated failing commands, turns to green and tokens.
because: A/B test of keeping failures in context

title: Log statusline prompt_cache fields to prove no hook cache misses
detail: Claude Code docs say status line scripts can read a prompt_cache object (requests, cache share, misses, expected rebuilds, likely cause; v2.1.251+). Append it per turn to a file and join with hook events, giving a free cache-miss ledger.
test: Verify that the field exists. Run 20 turns hook on and off on the same prompts; compare miss counts and likely-cause strings; check no miss coincides with a compressed result.
because: Claude Code statusline fields

title: Probe which thinking-budget knobs bind per model
detail: Claude Code docs say adaptive-reasoning models ignore nonzero MAX_THINKING_TOKENS and use effort levels, and some 5.5 models cannot disable thinking. Verify per model before building budget-keyed ideas (#160, #442) on the env var.
test: Set MAX_THINKING_TOKENS to 1024 and 32000 on each available model for the same five prompts; compare the output-minus-visible-text residual from #441.
because: per-model thinking-budget knobs

title: Probe double loading when CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md
detail: A blog says Claude Code reads AGENTS.md directly when CLAUDE.md is absent (v2.1.277). Repos with a CLAUDE.md containing @AGENTS.md might inject the file twice. Check the request payload and keep one copy. Extends #544.
test: Verify that behavior: in a repo whose CLAUDE.md is only '@AGENTS.md', send one prompt through the logging proxy and count occurrences of a unique AGENTS.md sentence in the payload.
because: CLAUDE.md import and memory-file loading behaviour

title: strace: fold ENOENT probe storms by basename
detail: Imports, ld.so, locale and PATH lookups fail on one basename across many directories. Group failed openat/stat/access calls into 'name ENOENT x N dirs' and hoist the constant -f pid prefix. Measured: 53 of 280 lines held 2241 of 10718 o200k tokens. #508 keeps failures verbatim.
test: Run strace -f -e trace=openat,stat,access python3 -c 'import json,argparse'; group ENOENT by basename; compare o200k tokens; check no non-ENOENT failure is folded.
because: folds strace ENOENT probe storms

title: objdump and gdb disassembly: drop raw instruction-byte column
detail: objdump -d prints address, spaced hex encoding bytes, then mnemonic; agents read mnemonics. Dropping the byte column (keeping addresses for jump targets) cut 400 lines of /usr/bin/ls from 8842 to 5493 o200k tokens (-38%). Also fold nop/int3 padding runs.
test: objdump -d a binary, strip the byte column, count o200k tokens; check every branch target still matches a kept address; ask a reader which function calls a given symbol.
because: drops raw byte column from disassembly

title: Fold identical per-core stanzas in /proc/cpuinfo and lscpu
detail: cpuinfo repeats model name and a long flags line per logical CPU; only processor, core id, apicid and MHz differ. Measured: 4 cores cost 2320 tokens, 1380 in flags lines. Print one shared stanza plus per-core diff rows; cost grows linearly on 64+ core hosts.
test: cat /proc/cpuinfo on this box and a many-core CI runner; fold identical key-value lines across stanzas; compare o200k tokens and confirm per-core values survive.
because: fold per-core cpuinfo stanzas
check: When every cpuinfo stanza has the same keys in order, the common lines are printed once in a template stanza and each stanza contributes one tab-separated row of its differing values; decode restores the exact bytes.

title: journalctl -x: strip catalog explanation blocks and failure hints
detail: From memory: journalctl -x/-xe appends ░░-prefixed catalog text (Subject, Defined-By, Support URL, 'unit has entered the failed state') per entry, and systemctl failures print 'See systemctl status / journalctl -xeu' hints. Text is constant per message ID; keep Result and exit-code lines.
test: Capture journalctl -xeu on a deliberately failing unit; measure the ░░ line share in o200k tokens; verify Result and exit status lines survive the strip.
because: strips constant journalctl catalog text

title: Aggregate auth logs by source and user; fold PAM pairs
detail: sshd, auth.log, secure and lastb brute-force storms print Failed password, Invalid user and Connection closed [preauth]. Count by user class and source with first/last time, keep Accepted lines verbatim, fold pam_unix open/close, sudo and cron pairs. Synthetic 600 lines: 23400 vs about 55 tokens.
test: Replay a public OpenSSH auth log sample (Loghub reportedly ships one) through the aggregator; check successful logins and unusual sources stay verbatim; compare reader answers on 'who got in'.
because: aggregate auth log lines locally
check: A run of 6+ consecutive sshd failure lines (Failed password, Invalid user, Connection closed/Disconnected/Received disconnect [preauth], pam authentication failure) folds into one line with, per source address, the failed-password count split root/invalid/valid, the noise-line count and the first and last time; a cron session-open, CMD, session-close triple becomes the CMD line plus ' [+2 pam lines]'; every Accepted login, sudo line and unrecognised line is verbatim and keeps its position.
check_loses: the individual usernames tried, ports, PIDs and per-line times inside a folded run, and the cron session open/close lines

title: nmap NSE blocks: vulners rows, cipher grades, cert fields
detail: vulners lists CVE rows with score plus a URL derivable from the ID; ssl-enum-ciphers lists each cipher per TLS version with a grade; ssl-cert dumps fields and hashes. Drop derivable URLs, fold A-grade ciphers to counts, keep weak ciphers and high scores. See #512.
test: Run nmap -sV --script vulners,ssl-enum-ciphers,ssl-cert against a local test server or scanme.nmap.org; measure NSE token share; check weak ciphers and top CVEs survive.
because: drops derivable nmap script URLs, folds ciphers
check: In nmap NSE output the derivable vulners.com URL of a CVE/EDB/PACKETSTORM row is dropped, runs of 2+ rows scored below 7.0 without *EXPLOIT* fold to a count and the highest score, runs of 2+ A-graded ciphers fold to a count, and MD5/SHA-1 certificate hash lines are dropped; every row scored 7.0 or more or flagged *EXPLOIT*, every cipher graded B to F with its warnings, 'least strength', the certificate subject/issuer/validity and all port lines are unchanged.
check_loses: the IDs and scores of vulners rows below 7.0 (count and maximum only), the names of A-graded ciphers (count per TLS version only), the certificate hashes, and the URL of rows whose URL follows the derivation rule

title: iptables-save and nft: fold generated chain families
detail: From memory: Docker, kube-proxy, Calico and CNI plugins create hundreds of chains like KUBE-SEP-<hash> and KUBE-SVC-<hash> differing only in hash and comment, plus [pkts:bytes] counters. Fold generated families to first example plus count, drop zero counters, keep hand-written chains and rules the command filtered for.
test: Run iptables-save on a Docker or kind host; classify chains by prefix; compare o200k tokens before and after folding; check user chains and DROP rules survive verbatim.
because: folds generated firewall chain families
check: Keeps the first chain of each generated family (KUBE-SEP, KUBE-SVC, KUBE-XLB, CNI, cali) in full and replaces the rest by one '# FAMILY: N more chains like X omitted' line, never dropping a generated chain that has a non-zero counter or a DROP, REJECT or KUBE-MARK-DROP rule; zero counters are removed; every hand-written and built-in chain, its policy, its rules and every DROP or REJECT rule are unchanged.
check_loses: the endpoints behind each folded KUBE-SVC chain (which pod IP:port a service reaches, and the service name in the comments) and the rules of folded chains; only the first example and the per-family count remain

title: wget non-tty dot-progress lines: collapse or inject -nv
detail: Without a tty wget prints one dotted progress line per 50 KB, newline-separated, so CR-collapse (#10) misses it. Synthetic 400 lines: 10819 vs 89 o200k tokens. Collapse to first line plus the saved line, or add -nv in PreToolUse when no quiet flag is present.
test: Download a 20 MB file with wget piped through cat; count progress-line tokens; confirm the final 'saved' line and any error or redirect lines survive.
because: collapses wget dot-progress output; -nv injection optional

title: Web fuzzer output: fold the dominant response signature
detail: ffuf, gobuster, feroxbuster and wfuzz print a line per probe; wildcard or soft-404 responses share status, size, words and lines. Group by signature, count dominant ones, keep rare signatures verbatim. Synthetic 2000 lines: 63995 vs 108 o200k tokens. Source-side alternative: ffuf -ac.
test: Run ffuf against a local server with a wildcard route and two real paths; fold by (status,size,words,lines); verify both real hits stay verbatim and counts sum to the total.
because: fold dominant fuzzer response signature
check: ffuf and wfuzz result lines whose response signature (status, size, words, lines) occurs 10 or more times fold into one '[N more lines with ...; first word: a; last word: z]' marker; every line of a rarer signature and every banner or config line stays verbatim and in order, and the per-signature counts add up to the total.
check_loses: the words and durations of the folded lines other than the first and last, and where in the run the dominant responses fell

title: systemctl show, list-unit-files, analyze security: drop defaults
detail: From memory: systemctl show prints 100+ properties, many empty or default (infinity, no, [not set]); list-unit-files lists every enabled/static/masked file; systemd-analyze security prints a row per check. Keep non-default properties, group unit files by state with counts, keep failing checks and score. Complements #511.
test: Run systemctl show, list-unit-files and systemd-analyze security on a systemd host; count empty/default lines and passing rows in o200k tokens; check non-default values survive.
because: drops default systemd properties from output

title: df, mount, findmnt: fold pod-UUID and container-ID path families
detail: Kubernetes and containerd hosts list hundreds of tmpfs kubelet pod mounts and overlay rootfs rows differing only in UUID or 64-hex ID. Synthetic 181 df lines: 12902 vs 85 o200k tokens. Fold by path template; keep real devices, near-full filesystems and rows the command named.
test: Capture df and mount on a kind or k3s node; template-fold UUID and hex path segments; compare o200k tokens; check a full filesystem row is never folded.
because: folds UUID path families in mount listings
check: Rows (df) or lines (mount) whose mount point differs only by a pod UUID, a 64-hex container id or a kube-api-access-xxxxx name, in groups of three or more with the same filesystem, become the first row plus one '+N more like the row above' line carrying the count and highest Use%; /dev devices, rows at 90% or more and everything else stay verbatim.
check_loses: the individual UUIDs, container ids, and (for df) the sizes and used space of the folded rows; rows the user's command named cannot be recognised from the text alone

title: Unescape over-escaped Markdown punctuation from HTML converters
detail: HTML-to-Markdown converters (reportedly turndown, pandoc) emit \_ \. \( \[ \! on plain words, so snake\_case names cost extra and defeat grep. Unescape where inert; skip line-start 1\., table pipes and code spans. Synthetic sentence: 47 vs 32 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Run fetch, Notion and Confluence MCP pages through the rule; assert markdown-it HTML render is identical before and after; tokenise both; count backslash-punctuation share.
because: unescapes inert Markdown punctuation
check: Backslashes before _ . ! ( ) - [ ] ? ; , are dropped only where the character is inert (intraword underscore, period not after line-start digits, ! not before [, parens only when the paragraph has no ], hyphen not at block start, \[word\] only when the document has no reference definitions); code spans, fenced and indented code, table rows, HTML, URLs and every other escape are untouched, so a CommonMark-subset render is identical before and after.
check_loses: the backslash bytes themselves, in positions where the escaped character already renders as plain text

title: Unwrap Python scalar reprs: np.float64(), Decimal(), PosixPath()
detail: NumPy 2 scalar repr (NEP 51) prints np.float64(0.1) inside every printed list or dict; Decimal('1.5'), PosixPath('x'), UUID('..') and pandas Timestamp('..') do likewise. Unwrap single-line reprs to the inner literal. Synthetic list: 30 vs 18 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Print numpy 2 scalars, pytest assert diffs and pandas row dicts; unwrap by regex; assert inner literal text unchanged; tokenise; ask type questions to see whether the lost wrapper matters.
because: unwraps Python scalar reprs, text rewrite

title: Drop optional spaces in Python dict, list and call reprs
detail: print(d), pprint, pytest asserts and logging emit ', ' and ': ' in single-quoted reprs that JSON minify (#31) never matches. Scan outside string literals and delete the space; foo(a, b) argument lists too. Synthetic dict: 49 vs 37 tokens, args 18 vs 15 (o200k).
test: Capture 50 repr lines from Python runs; delete separator spaces outside quotes; assert ast.literal_eval equality and string-literal bytes unchanged; tokenise; leave file-read output untouched.
because: removes optional spaces in Python reprs
check: Inside balanced brackets of a single line, the spaces after ',' and ':' that sit outside string literals are removed; the per-line Python token stream (so every string literal byte) and ast.literal_eval value are unchanged, and text that looks like a Python source file is left alone.
check_loses: optional spaces after , and : inside brackets (cosmetic; a reader that wants PEP 8 spacing must re-add it)

title: Canonicalise printf-style scientific notation like 1.234560e+02
detail: C printf, Fortran, numpy and solver logs print padded mantissas with signed two-digit exponents. Rewrite digit-exact with Decimal to 123.456 or -9.87e-5, never through float. Synthetic line: 31 vs 19 tokens (o200k proxy).
test: Grep saved outputs for [0-9]e[+-][0-9]{2}; rewrite via Decimal; assert Decimal(old)==Decimal(new) for every match; skip hex-like tokens; tokenise before and after.
because: canonicalises scientific notation digit-exact
check: printf-style numbers like 1.234560e+02 (mantissa, signed exponent of 2+ digits) are rewritten to the shorter of the plain decimal (123.456) and the unpadded scientific form (9.87e-5) using digit-string arithmetic, never float; every digit is kept, zero keeps its sign, and identifier-, hex- and unit-adjacent tokens are left alone.
check_loses: the original spelling and the trailing zeros of the mantissa (1.230000e+00 and 1.23 compare equal: printed precision is not preserved), the + and leading zeros of the exponent, and the case of E

title: Fold Arabic-Indic, Devanagari and Thai digits to ASCII
detail: NFKC (#231) leaves non-Latin decimal digits alone, yet unicodedata.decimal maps them exactly and int() parses both forms. Targets LC_ALL=ar/fa/hi/th CLI output and RTL documents. Synthetic: 24 vs 11 tokens on o200k, 46 vs 11 on cl100k.
test: Generate numbers in five Nd scripts; map with unicodedata.decimal; assert int() equality; tokenise before and after; confirm is_protected still flags the resulting atoms.
because: digit folding on text
check: Every non-ASCII decimal digit (Arabic-Indic, Persian, Devanagari, Thai, fullwidth, math) in a token without ASCII letters becomes the ASCII digit with the same int() value, one character for one character; identifier-like tokens are untouched and is_protected still flags the folded numbers.
check_loses: the script of the digits (the value of every number is unchanged)

title: ASCII-fold accents in Latin-script prose, keep original saved
detail: NFD-strip combining marks on French, German, Polish, Spanish or Vietnamese prose lines from MCP issues and docs; never identifiers, paths or code. Mixed European sample: 28 vs 24 tokens (o200k), 38 vs 28 (cl100k). Lossy where accents distinguish words.
test: Fold 30 non-English issue bodies; count tokens; run reader QA on folded versus original; check quoted strings and code spans stay excluded.
because: accent folding on prose text

title: Cap combining-mark floods and collapse lone surrogate escapes
detail: Zalgo text in issue titles or chat MCP output stacks many marks per letter; Python reprs of undecodable filenames show \udce9 escapes. Keep 2 marks per base; collapse \udcXX runs. Synthetic: Zalgo 92 vs 8 tokens, escapes 17 vs 6 (o200k).
test: Craft Zalgo text and os.listdir over invalid bytes; apply the cap; assert base letters survive in order; tokenise; verify U+FFFD runs (measured token-neutral) are left alone.
because: cap combining marks; text transform

title: Strip bold and italic markers from MCP Markdown prose
detail: Issue, PR and Notion bodies and bot comments wrap words in ** and _ . Remove paired emphasis outside code fences and inline code; keep bullets, snake_case and globs. Synthetic emphasised sentence: 31 vs 17 tokens; real share unknown until #715 measures it.
test: Apply to 100 saved issue and PR bodies; count markers per 1k tokens; assert no identifier or glob changed; QA warnings like 'DO NOT' for lost emphasis.
because: strips emphasis markers from Markdown prose

title: Atomizer splits words at combining marks; add grapheme-safe atoms
detail: Verified read-only: atoms.py makes one atom per mark in Hindi, Thai, Arabic harakat, NFD accents and ZWJ emoji, since \w excludes Mn/Mc. Top-k can delete a mark or base alone, corrupting words and inflating atom counts.
test: Atomize samples from six scripts; assert each mark shares an atom with its base; run random drops and check detok output stays valid.
because: atomizer fix, deterministic text transform

title: Auto mode may block PreToolUse rewrites: probe every permission mode
detail: Claude Code 2.1.316 strings include 'A hook or plugin changed a call after auto mode reviewed it, so auto mode could not check what would run'. Every PreToolUse updatedInput idea (quiet flags, caps, aliases) may be blocked or unreviewed under auto mode.
test: Verify that a PreToolUse hook appending '| head -5' to Bash works: run claude -p under default, acceptEdits and auto modes; record executed, blocked or prompted.
because: Claude Code auto mode and PreToolUse permissions

title: Auto-mode classifier overflow: denied calls and early compaction cost
detail: 2.1.316 strings: 'Auto mode classifier transcript exceeded context window; will try to compact', and calls 'not reviewed and did not run ... issue it again'. Tool outputs fill the classifier window, so each overflow costs a reissued call plus a compaction.
test: In auto-mode transcripts count 'did not run' denials and compactions; price reissued calls; compare overflow rate with and without the hook.
because: Claude Code auto-mode classifier

title: Silent-success checks: async PostToolUse hook wakes model only on failure
detail: PostToolUse on Edit|Write with async plus asyncRewake (2.1.316 schema) runs targeted tests or typecheck in the background. Exit 0 adds nothing to context; exit 2 wakes the model with just the failure tail. Passing runs cost zero tokens.
test: Verify that async hooks work in claude -p: exit 0 stays silent, exit 2 wakes the model; replay 20 recorded edit-then-test sequences and sum tokens of passing runs.
because: async PostToolUse hook with asyncRewake

title: Block bare thank-you prompts in UserPromptSubmit when nothing awaits reply
detail: A prompt that is only 'thanks' or 'perfect' still costs a full turn: cache read of the whole context plus a reply. A Stop hook records whether the last assistant message ended in a question; UserPromptSubmit blocks only if not. Never blocks 'ok' or 'yes'.
test: Count transcript user prompts matching ^(thanks|thank you|great|perfect)[.!]*$; sum usage tokens of the following turn and count how many followed a question.
because: UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks

title: Pre/Post worktree diff receipt replaces output of mutating commands
detail: PreToolUse stores git status and tree hash under tool_use_id. PostToolUse (failures route to PostToolUseFailure) replaces the output of formatters, codegen, installs and sed -i with 'exit 0; changed 12 files +130 -40' plus the file list.
test: Bucket exit-0 Bash outputs over 1,000 chars whose commands rewrite files (black, prettier, npm install, codegen); sum their tokens and check what later turns cite from them.
because: needs Pre/PostToolUse hooks and host git state

title: Skip Stop-hook verifiers on turns that changed nothing
detail: Stop fires after every reply, including chat-only ones, so prompt or agent verifier hooks (agent hooks default to Haiku in 2.1.316 strings) and test gates run for nothing. A command wrapper runs the verifier only if the tree hash differs from the last Stop's.
test: Count Stop events in transcripts whose turn had no Edit, Write or mutating Bash; price a prompt hook's input per event; confirm the wrapper skips exactly those.
because: Stop hook verifiers are harness hook events

title: Census of hook-injected context by event, plugin and surviving turns
detail: Plain stdout from SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks, plus additionalContext from any event, becomes persistent context. Parse hook output entries in transcripts (reportedly attachments), group by event and command, multiply tokens by turns survived. Includes ctxprune's own note.
test: Run over 10 local transcripts; rank hook commands by injected tokens times remaining turns; flag any that emit text on every prompt.
because: hook-injected context by event and plugin

title: Size-forecast steering: cap commands whose earlier runs were huge
detail: PostToolUse logs output chars per canonical command signature (#846); PreToolUse adds a limit, -n, --stat or head to the next call of any signature whose earlier outputs exceeded the threshold. Learned per repo, not a static rule.
test: From transcripts, group Bash calls by signature; measure how often a signature's second call is within 2x of its first size; simulate caps and count saved chars.
because: adds limits to commands by past output size

title: Bind session-constant MCP params and hide them from schemas
detail: owner/repo and similar cloudId, project_id or org-slug params repeat on every call of GitHub-style servers. Bind from git remote at launch, drop from schemas, fill via PreToolUse updatedInput. Saves schema, output and history tokens; in github list_issues each costs 25 o200k tokens.
test: Count owner/repo/id tokens in recorded tool_use inputs and schemas across 3 servers; prototype fill-in with updatedInput; run 10 tasks checking calls still hit the right repo.
because: MCP proxy binds constant params and trims schemas

title: Drop never-used optional parameters from MCP tool schemas
detail: Tally which optional params appear in tool_use inputs across transcripts; a tools/list proxy removes never-used ones. In github list_issues, field_filters alone is 175 of 649 schema tokens (o200k proxy, one schema). Usage-driven, unlike #253's tool-level allowlists.
test: Count param keys per tool in transcripts, tokenise the never-used share on 3 servers, then rerun 20 tasks and count failures needing a removed param.
because: proxy prunes schema params; usage observable in tool_use inputs

title: Collapse the deferred tool-name roster to per-server lines
detail: The deferred-tool name list repeats mcp__server__ per tool every turn. Github's 48 names cost 434 o200k tokens; brace-factored 181; one summary line 33. A proxy rewrites the reminder; the model expands names for select:.
test: Tokenise the roster in a logged request, rewrite both ways, run 10 MCP tasks counting extra ToolSearch calls and wrong-name selects.
because: ToolSearch deferred-roster reminder is Claude Code specific

title: Evict idle loaded deferred-tool schemas at cold-cache boundary
detail: Schemas fetched by ToolSearch stay in history all session, though most tools are called once. A proxy swaps old ToolSearch results for a names-only stub once the cache is cold or at compaction; the model re-searches on demand.
test: Parse transcripts for schema tokens of tools not called in the last N turns; simulate eviction at idle gaps over 5 minutes and count re-fetches.
because: depends on ToolSearch deferred loading and cache-cold timing

title: Compact ToolSearch schemas: minify separators, then TypeScript signatures
detail: ToolSearch returns JSON schemas with a space after every colon and comma; compact separators are lossless (toy schema 91 vs 68 o200k tokens). Going further, render TypeScript signatures with prose kept as comments: github list_issues 649 vs 440 (one schema).
test: Verify that PostToolUse may rewrite ToolSearch output; dump 20 real schemas, tokenise JSON, minified and signature forms, run 30 prompts comparing argument validity and tool choice.
because: schema text compaction applies to any tool schema

title: Defer per-tool description tails to the first call result
detail: Keep one sentence of each MCP tool description in the schema; a proxy appends the rest (usage notes, cautions) to the first result of that tool per session. Differs from server-instructions deferral and offline compression: per-tool lifecycle.
test: Tokenise description text beyond the first sentence on 3 servers; run 30 tool-choice and argument prompts, flagging errors the tail would have prevented.
because: proxy defers description tails to first tool result

title: Hide MCP tools that duplicate built-in Read, Write, Grep, Bash
detail: Filesystem, shell and git-style MCP servers expose read_file, write_file, search_files, list_directory, run_command, which overlap built-ins. Each costs a schema and a roster name for no new capability. Deny them per server (overlap criterion, unlike usage-based #253).
test: List installed MCP tools, classify overlap with built-ins by description, tokenise their schemas, run 5 file tasks with them hidden.
because: tool overlap visible in payload; proxy filters tools list

title: Compact MCP input-validation errors from pydantic, zod, JSON-RPC
detail: Failed calls return issue arrays; pydantic reportedly adds input_value, input_type and an errors.pydantic.dev URL per issue (from memory). Rewrite to one 'path: message' line per issue. Needs PostToolUseFailure or a wrapper, since is_error results may bypass the hook.
test: Trigger bad calls on a FastMCP and a zod server, capture error text, tokenise, apply the rewrite, count retries needing dropped detail.
because: rewrites validation error text to path-message lines

title: CI token-budget gate for self-authored MCP servers
detail: Fail CI when tools/list tokens exceed N, or a fixture call's response exceeds M. Catches schema and result bloat at the source, before it hits every session. Existing description-lint ideas (#152) cover skills and agents, not servers.
test: Script: start the server over stdio, list tools, tokenise each, run fixture calls and tokenise results; fail on thresholds.
because: CI test of MCP schema token size

title: Probe whether MCP prompts and resources enter the request
detail: Claude Code reportedly exposes MCP prompts as slash commands and resources as readable items. Whether their names and descriptions ride in every request is unmeasured. A toy server with 20 of each would show the cost.
test: Run a toy MCP server with 0 versus 20 prompts and resources; diff logged request bodies through a proxy; tokenise any added text.
because: Claude Code MCP prompts and resources behaviour

title: kNN datastore of atom states blended into classifier scores
detail: kNN-LM style (Khandelwal et al. 2020): store last-layer atom hidden states with keep/drop labels from teacher, flags and refetch regrets, then blend a nearest-neighbour vote into the score. A user's own command families adapt instantly without retraining.
test: Export hidden states for 5k labeled atoms; hold out one source, add 50 labeled atoms from it; compare ROC-AUC and QA at 0.5 with and without the kNN blend.
because: local kNN blend; state held by local process

title: Anti-unify classifier-dropped lines into wildcard patterns, with negatives
detail: #261 keeps exact digit-masked templates, so unseen variants miss. Take lines the model drops at least 95% of the time, compute least general generalisations (anti-unification, Plotkin 1970), and reject any pattern matching a line the model kept or a needle.
test: From 150 saved pytest, npm and cargo outputs build exact-template and anti-unified tables; on 50 held-out compare lines covered, false matches on needles, and chars removed.
because: local pattern learning, deterministic per-message line filter

title: Counterexample loop that attacks synthesised filters with mutated needles
detail: Before accepting a #646 filter, a generator relocates and rewords needle lines (failing test name, error code, new warning class) in captured outputs into forms the filter drops. Survivors feed back into synthesis (counterexample-guided synthesis) until none remain.
test: Take one synthesised pytest filter; mutate 200 captures by moving the failure line and rewording its message; count needles dropped before and after two repair rounds.
because: counterexample testing of synthesised filters

title: Mine JSON key-path keep lists from fields agents later reference
detail: Across transcripts, record which MCP response key paths have values later copied into tool inputs or assistant text. Paths almost never referenced become drop candidates, referenced ones never-drop. Aggregates behaviour per schema path, unlike atom labels (#169) or classifier scores (#262).
test: On 100 captured GitHub MCP list responses plus the following turns, compute per-path reference rate; compare chars removed with #262's list; hand-check false drops.
because: offline mining of key-path keep lists from payloads

title: Error-seeded personalised PageRank over a line and identifier graph
detail: Link lines to the rare identifiers they contain (test names, symbols, paths). Seed with error or summary lines such as FAILED tests/x.py::t, run a few power iterations, and give nearby lines a keep floor. Unlike TextRank (#650), centrality is seeded, not global.
test: On 30 pytest, tsc and cargo failures, compare gold-answer line recall at equal chars against the classifier alone and TextRank; confirm runtime stays in the tens of milliseconds.
because: text-only graph selection, deterministic

title: Granularity oracle: minimal tokens that keep the gold span
detail: For each QA item with a verbatim gold span, compute the smallest budget retaining it when selecting atoms, lines, 5-line chunks or whole records. The gap bounds what line-level (#87) or span-level selectors could win over atom deletion before building any.
test: Reuse the agent-text QA set; greedy-oracle selection per granularity; report median kept tokens per granularity by source. Zero LLM calls.
because: granularity oracle ceiling analysis

title: Oracle router ceiling across selection paradigms
detail: Per QA item, record which paradigms keep the gold span (classifier, BM25, cross-encoder, TextRank, head/tail) and at what size. An oracle picking the cheapest surviving paradigm bounds routing gains before any router (#651) is trained.
test: From cached contexts for four methods, build survival and kept-token matrices; report oracle-router tokens versus the best single method at equal survival rate.
because: oracle router ceiling analysis

title: Parse-first prose islands: score only Markdown text nodes and comments
detail: Parse Markdown, docstrings and code comments; run the classifier only on paragraph, list-item and comment text, leaving fences, links, table rows and code byte-identical. Extends JSON-string-only scoring (#134); avoids post-hoc delimiter repair (#777).
test: On 50 READMEs and issue bodies, count broken fences, links and tables versus whole-text pruning at 0.5; compare QA at equal tokens.
because: parse-first scoring of Markdown text nodes

title: Fold identical token substitutions across git diff hunks
detail: Renames and API swaps print the same -/+ pair in every hunk. Detect hunks whose pairs differ by one identical token substitution, emit 's/old/new/' once with file:line locations, and keep exceptions as ordinary hunks. Original diff saved.
test: Rename one symbol across 20 files of a real repo; compare diff tokens with the rule-plus-locations form; check three arbitrary changed lines reconstruct exactly.
because: fold identical substitutions in diff hunks
check: Hunks that are a pure OLD -> NEW word substitution (every changed line pairs with one that differs only there) and occur in 3+ hunks become 's/OLD/NEW/ path:line,...' (new-side line numbers) with the hunks and their context removed; hunks that do anything else stay byte for byte, files whose hunks all fold vanish, and the exact set of (path, line) locations per substitution is unchanged.
check_loses: the text of the changed lines and the context lines of folded hunks (the working tree has them: the new line is the tree line, the old line is the tree line with NEW replaced by OLD), blob ids and file headers of fully folded files

title: Fold moved blocks in git diff into pointers
detail: Refactors that move functions print the same lines as deletions in one place and additions in another. Detect blocks of 4+ lines identical after trimming across hunks (as git --color-moved does for display), print once, and point the other side at it.
test: Make 10 extract-function and file-split refactors in a repo; compare diff tokens with and without move folding; verify added and removed line counts reconcile.
because: point moved diff blocks to one copy

title: Nearest-family transfer of learned filters to unseen commands
detail: Learned tables (#261) and synthesised filters (#646) need data per command. For an unseen CLI, fingerprint its first output by digit-masked line-shape histogram, find the closest known family by cosine, and apply that family's table with a stricter never-drop floor.
test: Hold out 5 of 20 families; for each pick the nearest family and apply its table; report chars removed and needle recall versus no table and versus the model.
because: local fingerprint matching, deterministic filter selection

title: Mine agents' own pipe-suffix filters into per-family default filters
detail: In transcripts, collect post-filters agents append to commands (| tail -40, | grep -v node_modules, | grep -A5 FAIL). Per command family, recurring suffixes are the agent's own relevance judgement; promote them to default filters when the bare command runs large.
test: Scan 100 transcripts, group by normalised base command, count suffixes; for the top 10 families check how often bare runs exceed 6,000 chars and which suffixes recur.
because: mines command strings into default filters; payload-visible

title: Ledger pricing guard: usage tier, speed and iterations fields
detail: Local transcript usage records carry service_tier, speed, inference_geo, iterations and output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens, which a flat price table ignores. Price each turn from them; sum iterations rather than top-level counts; report tokens only for unpriced combos. Refines #271.
test: List distinct (model, tier, speed, geo) tuples and iterations lengths across ~/.claude/projects; assert every tuple has a price row; compare summed-iterations totals against top-level totals.
because: ledger from local Claude Code transcript usage records

title: Count savings against host-visible output, not raw output
detail: Claude Code persists oversized results to a file and sends a roughly 2 KB preview (this session's own 61 KB Bash result arrived that way). Savings claimed against raw length overstate; if compressed output still trips persistence, the model sees the preview anyway.
test: Emit 100 KB and 400 KB via Bash, hook on and off; read tool_result lengths from the transcript; compare with the ledger's claimed saving; note which cases still persist.
because: Claude Code oversized-result persistence and preview

title: CUPED covariate adjustment for session-cost A/B tests
detail: Raw session cost is dominated by task size. Regress billed cost on pre-exposure covariates (first-prompt tokens, empty-session baseline, repo size, model) and compare residuals, as CUPED does in web experiments (Deng et al., 2013). Cuts sessions needed for a given detectable effect.
test: On local transcripts compute R-squared of log session cost on covariates; report variance reduction and implied sessions-needed ratio versus unadjusted, before running any hook arm.
because: CUPED variance reduction for A/B

title: Equal-dollar-budget resolve curves instead of cost per pass
detail: Cap both arms at the same spend (reportedly claude -p --max-budget-usd, or a mini-swe-agent cost limit) and plot tasks resolved versus dollars. Treats unfinished runs as censored; answers the real question: what gets solved for a fixed bill.
test: Run each task once at a $2 cap logging cumulative spend at resolution; derive resolved-at-$0.5/$1 curves by truncation; compare arms with paired exact tests.
because: equal-budget resolve curve methodology

title: Lever league table: dollars saved per success point lost
detail: Put ctxprune beside other cost levers (model downgrade, lower effort, MCP trimming, earlier /clear, CLAUDE.md diet) on one recorded task set. Rank by dollars saved per success point lost, so effort goes to levers that win, not just to compression.
test: Using mini-swe-agent on 20 tasks, run baseline plus four levers one at a time; plot cost versus pass rate; list which levers sit on the Pareto frontier.
because: cost-lever benchmark comparison

title: Receipt splits lossless from lossy savings, shows worst compressions
detail: Tag each rule's saved tokens L, R or M and print the split ('Xk lossless, Yk lossy') with the three costliest compressions by refetch tokens. Lets a cautious user trust the lossless floor and keeps the report from showing only wins (extends #274).
test: Add a rule-class field to the ledger; render the receipt for a recorded session; check lossless plus lossy equals total saved and the worst-three list matches a manual refetch count.
because: savings accounting split lossless versus lossy

title: Cost per retained line for natural, benchmark-free usage
detail: Real work has no pass/fail. Divide each session's billed cost by lines from its commits still present at HEAD after 14 days (git blame); compare hook-on and hook-off projects. Catches cheap sessions whose output was later reverted.
test: Join transcript session ids to commits via timestamps and branch; compute retained lines with git blame; report cost per retained line by project and hook state, with bootstrap intervals.
because: natural-usage cost metric via git blame

title: Adversarial worst-case timing and ReDoS fuzz for rule pre-pass
detail: Hundreds of regex rules will meet 5 MB minified lines, deep nesting and near-miss repeats where backtracking explodes. Generate pathological inputs per rule, fail CI above a ms-per-MB cap, and wrap the pre-pass in a wall-clock deadline that returns the original.
test: Time every rule on 1 MB of: one unbroken line, repeated near-matches, nested brackets, long digit runs; use the regex module's timeout argument to find any rule exceeding 100 ms.
because: ReDoS and timing fuzz

title: Append token-size tags to results so agents self-throttle
detail: Add '[~4.2k tokens]' to each tool result over 1k tokens via additionalContext. Seeing the price of a command may make agents add head, grep or narrower paths next time. Costs about 8 tokens a call; behavioural, so uncertain.
test: Run 12 tasks in mini-swe-agent with and without tags; compare mean tool-output tokens per call, total billed tokens and pass rate, tags counted.
because: token-size tag appended to tool result text

title: Tornado sensitivity of savings to price-book assumptions
detail: Every dollar claim bakes in ratios: cache read ~0.1x, write ~1.25x, output ~5x, TTL mix. Re-price the same ledger across plausible ranges and other vendors' books, then publish only claims whose sign and rank hold everywhere.
test: Vary each ratio over a grid (read 0.05-0.5x, write 1-2x, output 3-8x) on three local sessions; report where the tool-result bill share or install verdict flips.
because: price-book sensitivity analysis

title: Proxy aliases opaque toolu_ ids to short stable names
detail: Each tool_use id and its matching tool_use_id is a long random string; a sample costs about 19 o200k tokens (not Claude's tokenizer). If the API renders them, a deterministic per-session alias like t17 applied across history saves tokens on every request.
test: Verify that aliasing is accepted: count_tokens on one recorded 60-call history with real ids versus t1..t60; if counts match, drop the idea; else replay with prefix-stable aliasing.
because: proxy aliases tool-call ids, stable per-session mapping
check: Rewriting every tool_use.id and tool_result.tool_use_id to t<N> from a persisted append-only table keeps pairs matched and unique, has an exact inverse, never changes the bytes of earlier messages as history grows or is edited, and passes malformed requests through; that the API accepts short ids cannot be tested offline.

title: Merge adjacent text blocks inside one request message
detail: Claude Code user turns usually carry a tool_result plus separate system-reminder text blocks. Each block boundary may cost framing tokens. A proxy joins adjacent text blocks with a newline wherever no cache breakpoint sits between them.
test: count_tokens on a 30-turn history with blocks split versus joined; report tokens saved per merged boundary. If zero, close it; else check byte-stable prefixes.
because: pure payload rewrite joining adjacent text blocks
check: Adjacent plain text blocks in a message are joined with a newline unless a cache breakpoint sits between them; the reader sees the same segments and tool ids, other block types and malformed payloads are untouched, and the prefix stays byte-identical across 30 turns when the breakpoint is on a message's last block.
check_loses: the block boundary between merged texts (it becomes one newline)

title: Request-hash response replay for re-run headless agent jobs
detail: A proxy stores each upstream response keyed by a hash of the full request body. A CI re-run of the same task on the same commit replays every turn free until a tool output differs and the hash diverges. Needs volatile strings canonicalised.
test: Run one claude -p review twice on a fixed commit through a recording proxy; count replayed requests before the first miss and diff the first diverging request body.
because: proxy replays stored responses keyed by request hash
check: Keying stored responses by the hash of the request with volatile values (timestamps, tmp dirs, durations, tool ids; never user-authored text) abstracted to numbered placeholders replays all 4 turns of a re-run that differs only in those values, with the new run's own values substituted so the transcript equals the live one; real differences, changed parameters, truncated responses and corrupt entries never replay.

title: Probe features lost when ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a proxy
detail: The installed Claude Code binary gates betas on firstPartyCapabilityBetas and has an isFirstPartyAnthropicBaseUrl helper (strings seen, behaviour unverified). A localhost proxy may silently disable tool search, context management or 1h caching, costing more than the proxy saves.
test: Log the first request direct versus via passthrough proxy: diff anthropic-beta header, tools array (defer_loading) and cache_control ttl; retry with ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true and rediff.
because: probes Claude Code behaviour with custom base URL

title: Programmatic tool calling keeps bulky MCP results out of context
detail: Anthropic's advanced tool use (reportedly late 2025, from its engineering blog) lets sandboxed code call tools so intermediate results never enter the prompt unless printed. A proxy or SDK loop marks read-only tools code-callable. Not in Claude Code's binary strings.
test: Verify that the feature exists for your model; stub MCP with a 200-row list tool; compare input tokens and answer equality between plain tool_use and code-callable tools on 10 queries.
because: Anthropic programmatic tool calling API feature

title: API-native compaction edit for loops lacking their own compactor
detail: The Claude Code binary contains compact_20260112, next to clear_tool_uses_20250919 (#282). A proxy could add a compaction edit with a trigger and custom instructions for SDK or gateway-fronted agents that otherwise grow until the window errors, ideally at a cold-cache boundary.
test: Verify that the API accepts the edit; drive a 60-turn SDK loop past a 100k trigger with and without it; compare billed tokens per turn and recall of earlier decisions.
because: Anthropic API-native compaction edit

title: Property test: rewritten history prefix stays byte-stable and idempotent
detail: For any history rewriter, rewrite(msgs[:k]) must be a byte prefix of rewrite(msgs[:k+1]), and rewriting its own stubs must change nothing. Generated tool-loop histories catch rules that peek at later turns, counts or clocks and silently bust the cache.
test: Run Hypothesis over generated tool-loop histories against the proxy rewrite function; assert prefix equality at every k and rewrite(rewrite(x)) == rewrite(x), including ctxprune's own notes.
because: byte-stability property test

title: Responses API previous_response_id: compress function_call_output on arrival
detail: A client sending only new items plus previous_response_id leaves history on the server, so a gateway cannot stub old results later. Compression must hit each function_call_output once, at first sight, for example in a LiteLLM async_pre_call_hook.
test: Run Codex CLI through a logging proxy; record whether requests carry previous_response_id or full input; if stateful, apply ctxprune to function_call_output only and compare billed input.
because: OpenAI Responses previous_response_id server-side state

title: LiteLLM virtual key per arm for exact billed-cost A/B
detail: Send hook-on and hook-off sessions through two LiteLLM virtual keys or request tags (reportedly supported). The gateway's spend logs give billed tokens and cost per request, including side calls and retries that transcripts omit, with no JSONL parsing.
test: Verify that spend logs split by key; run 10 paired tasks per arm through the gateway; compare totals with ccusage on transcripts to size the side-call and retry gap.
because: gateway virtual keys for billed-cost A/B

title: Route title and summary side calls to a local model
detail: The binary reads ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL and ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL. Behind a gateway, map small-model utility calls such as titles and recaps to a local model, so they bill zero API tokens. Exclude permission-relevant classifiers.
test: Size small-model spend with #287's table, then point the Haiku alias at a local LiteLLM model for a day; compare billed Haiku tokens and broken features.
because: Claude Code title and recap side calls, env vars

title: Inject content caps into server-side web_fetch and web_search tools
detail: Anthropic's server web tools reportedly accept max_content_tokens on web_fetch and max_uses on web_search; unset, one fetch can add a whole page. A proxy injects caps per request. Absent from Claude Code's binary strings, so this targets SDK agents.
test: Verify that max_content_tokens is accepted; fetch a 100k-token docs page with caps of 5k and 15k; compare usage.input_tokens; score 10 questions against the full page.
because: Anthropic server web_fetch/web_search API params

title: Hook stdin decoding corrupts non-ASCII under C and cp1252 locales
detail: Verified: hook.py reads json.load(sys.stdin) in text mode. With LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 it returns lone surrogates as updatedToolOutput; under cp1252 it returns mojibake. The saved original is then invalid UTF-8 or double-encoded. Read sys.stdin.buffer as UTF-8.
test: Pipe a UTF-8 event with 'café 日本語' x400 into the hook under LC_ALL=C PYTHONUTF8=0 and PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252; assert output and saved file round-trip byte-exact.
because: hook stdin decoding in hook entrypoint

title: Keep mixed-character operators (!=, <=, ->, :=) as single atoms
detail: Verified: atomize splits '!=' into '!' and '=', and punctuation is never protected, so dropping '!' turns 'a != b' into 'a = b'; '2>&1' and '<=' degrade likewise. #957 only joins runs of one character. Join known operator digraphs into one atom.
test: Mutation test: on assertion, diff and set -x lines, drop each single operator-char atom in turn and count flipped semantics; compare rates before and after joining digraphs.
because: atomizer change, deterministic text transform

title: Protect backslash and UNC paths from directory-word deletion
detail: Verified: 'C:\Users\dario\proj\build\out.log' atomizes into C, :, \, Users, dario, proj, build and out.log; only out.log is protected, so the rest can be dropped despite the note's 'paths kept exactly'. Treat backslash as a path separator inside a word.
test: Run MSBuild, dotnet, PowerShell and cmd logs with backslash paths through is_protected; count paths whose directory words are droppable, then re-measure after the atomizer change.
because: protect rule on text, deterministic

title: Shield line-leading diff markers and pass/fail glyphs
detail: Verified: '+', '-', '✓' and '✗' are single punctuation atoms that is_protected never keeps, and 'OK' is too short to qualify. In compressed PR diffs or test-runner lists, a dropped marker flips added/removed or pass/fail while the line text survives. Force-keep line-initial markers.
test: On compressed gh pr diff and vitest/jest outputs, count surviving lines whose leading +/-/✓/✗ marker was dropped; run a QA 'was line X added or removed' probe.
because: protect rule on text, deterministic

title: Rerun stability: do near-identical outputs keep the same words?
detail: Windows shift when an early line changes (#460), so reruns of a test suite delete different words. The agent then sees a warning vanish from compressed run 2 though it persists, a phantom fix. Measure it; fix by caching keep decisions per line hash.
test: Compress two pytest logs differing in timings and one early line; count lines kept in run 1, deleted in run 2, yet present verbatim in both originals.
because: rerun stability measurement

title: Saved original merges stdout, stderr and MCP blocks unlabeled
detail: run() saves '\n\n'.join(originals) when several slots compress. Stream and block boundaries vanish, so a recovery grep cannot say whether a line was stderr, and jq on a multi-block JSON original fails. Write one file per slot or labeled sections.
test: Feed a Bash event with 7k stdout plus 7k stderr and an MCP event with two JSON blocks; check the saved file splits per slot or parses with jq.
because: labelled per-block saved originals

title: Hook host and Bash host may not share a filesystem
detail: The note's saved path lives where the hook ran. If hooks and the Bash tool run on different hosts or mounts (WSL, SSH remote, devcontainer, docker exec, remote sessions), the grep finds nothing and the agent reruns the command. #374 probes permissions only.
test: In each setup, have a stub hook write a marker file; run `test -f` on it from the agent's Bash tool and record which setups fail.
because: probe of shared filesystem assumption

title: Protect high-entropy lowercase IDs that carry no digit
detail: Verified: is_protected is False for 'kzxqjwmvbtnrplqd' and 'xqzjwvkmbtrplsdf'. Digit-free random tokens (nanoid alphabets, session or quote tokens, lowercase keys) are deletable although the note promises exact IDs. Add a length plus vowel-ratio or character-entropy shield.
test: Generate 1,000 random lowercase tokens of length 8-24 inside log lines; compress at 0.5 with force_protected and count survivors; repeat with the entropy shield.
because: protect rule on text, deterministic

title: Source-side git diff shrink: diff.context and noprefix config
detail: git diff, show and log -p are on the verbatim skip, so no hook trims them. Inject diff.context=1 and diff.noprefix=true via GIT_CONFIG_COUNT (as #486 does for status). Measured (o200k): 20 commits of modified files, 16,456 tokens default, 13,966 at -U1, 13,039 at -U0.
test: Replay recorded git diff/show calls with and without the config; compare tokens; run 10 edit tasks and count Edit failures caused by reduced hunk context.
because: git config env shrinks diff context

title: Symbol-addressed edit tool: replace a function by name
detail: Serena-style replace_symbol_body(path, symbol, new_body) resolves the span with tree-sitter, so the edit never emits old_string. Unlike the hash-guarded line-range tool (#449), nothing goes stale when lines shift; failure means only a missing or ambiguous symbol.
test: Measure old_string tokens in whole-function Edits across transcripts; run 15 function-rewrite tasks with the tool versus Edit; compare output tokens, failed edits and wrong-span rate.
because: symbol-addressed edit tool cuts output tokens

title: Stub inputs of errored tool calls after a few turns
detail: OpenCode's dynamic-context-pruning plugin reportedly has a purge-errors strategy: after N turns, inputs of failed calls (rejected Edit, failed Write, errored heredoc) become a stub and the error text stays. Differs from #824, which stubs old_string of successful Edits.
test: Sum tool_use input tokens of calls whose result is an error and which are older than 5 turns, across transcripts; replay stubbed history and count repeated identical mistakes.
because: stub aged errored tool_use inputs in proxy

title: Goal-hint line skimmer for source reads, SWE-Pruner style
detail: SWE-Pruner (reportedly a recent paper) has the agent state a goal hint per read; a small neural skimmer keeps goal-relevant lines and drops the rest. Line-level and learned, unlike BM25 function ranking (#305); intent comes from the agent.
test: On 30 recorded Reads over 300 lines, derive a goal from the next Grep or Edit; compare kept lines later quoted versus #305 at equal tokens.
because: local skimmer with agent-supplied goal argument

title: Static-embedding semantic dedupe for paraphrased log and doc lines
detail: Model2Vec (MinishLab) distils sentence encoders into lookup tables that reportedly embed on CPU with no transformer pass. Cluster lines by cosine to fold paraphrases that MinHash (#265) and Drain3 (#21) miss, such as retries worded differently. Unverified here.
test: Verify that Model2Vec embeds on CPU without a transformer pass; embed lines of 50 saved logs; count clusters above 0.9 cosine that template mining misses; time per 1k lines.
because: CPU static embeddings, no cloud or GPU

title: Pick noise packs by output signature, not command text
detail: Headroom reportedly routes by detected content type. npm test, make check, tox or uv run hide the real runner from command regexes. Match the first 20 lines against a signature table (pytest header, jest PASS/FAIL, cargo Compiling) to select the pack.
test: On 200 recorded wrapper-command outputs, compare pack-selection accuracy of command regex, first-line signatures and Google Magika; report wrong-pack rate and milliseconds per call.
because: content-signature routing on output text

title: Trust gate and hash pin for repo-supplied filter files
detail: A repo-local .ctxprune/filters.toml (#783) can hide failing tests, warnings or planted text from the agent. rtk reportedly gates project-local filters behind explicit trust (from memory). Require approval keyed on file hash; reset trust when the file changes.
test: Commit a filter dropping FAILED lines; confirm it is ignored until trusted; edit the file and confirm trust resets; confirm user-level filters still load without a prompt.
because: hash-pinned trust for ctxprune's own filter files

title: Mine public agent trajectory datasets as a replay corpus
detail: Hugging Face reportedly hosts agent trajectories with real tool observations (nebius SWE-agent-trajectories, SWE-Gym OpenHands traces). They offer shareable, non-private Bash, test and grep outputs for the replay harness (#6) and pack mining, though scaffold formats differ from Claude Code's.
test: Verify that the datasets exist and permit reuse; sample 2,000 observations; bucket by command family; report share over 6,000 chars and per-family savings; compare with a private-transcript sample.
because: public trajectory replay corpus

title: Terminal-Bench with real Claude Code to exercise the live hook
detail: mini-swe-agent (#955) never fires Claude Code's PostToolUse hook. Terminal-Bench reportedly offers containerised bash tasks with pass/fail checks and a Claude Code agent adapter, so hook-on versus hook-off runs the real host, note included.
test: Verify that the adapter runs Claude Code with hooks; run 20 tasks x 3 seeds per arm; compare pass rate, billed tokens and hook firing counts.
because: exercises Claude Code's PostToolUse hook

title: Classifier-compress CLAUDE.md and skill bodies once, keep backups
detail: The caveman Claude Code skill reportedly compresses memory files into telegraphic prose with a backup. Run ctxprune with protect over CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and skill bodies at install, beyond tool descriptions (#257). Every session saves the tokens.
test: Compress this repo's AGENTS.md at keep 0.7 with protect; run the setup-agent eval (#872) on both versions over 5 runs; compare tokens and task success.
because: rewrites CLAUDE.md and skill files at install

title: Rewrite find, tree and ls -R to gitignore-aware listings
detail: PreToolUse swaps find . -name, tree and ls -R for git ls-files -co --exclude-standard, tree --gitignore or fd, as rtk's ls reportedly hides noise directories. Source-side sibling of #394, which folds after the fact.
test: Count find, ls -R and tree calls and tokens in transcripts; replay with the rewrite; diff results to confirm only ignored paths vanish; log cases needing an ignored path.
because: rewrites find/tree/ls to gitignore-aware listing

title: Mine rival compressors' bug trackers for failure-mode fixtures
detail: Open issue trackers of rtk, Headroom and context-mode reportedly hold reports of filters hiding needed lines or breaking pipelines. Each closed report becomes a regression fixture before ctxprune ships a similar rule; cheaper than discovering the same bug in users' sessions.
test: Use gh to list closed bug issues mentioning wrong, missing or hidden output; classify 30 by rule type; write one fixture each for those matching our planned packs.
because: fixtures mined from rival trackers

title: Drop docs-URL hint lines that restate an error code
detail: pydantic appends 'For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.x/v/<type>' after every error, duplicating [type=...]: 83 of 213 o200k tokens in one 4-error sample. Similar lines, from memory: SQLAlchemy 'Background on this error', pytest '-- Docs:', Next 'Learn more'.
test: Collect FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, pytest and Next error outputs; drop URL lines whose slug matches an in-line code; tokenise; confirm agents still resolve the errors.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Unbox Rich and Typer tracebacks, rejoin soft-wrapped paths
detail: Rich panels pad lines to 80 columns inside box borders and wrap paths mid-word; show_locals adds per-frame tables. One sample: 764 o200k tokens versus 221 for the stock traceback. Unbox, rejoin paths, keep locals for the last frame only.
test: Crash a 5-frame Typer app with rich and show_locals on; unbox and rejoin; assert every path and line number round-trips; tokenise before and after.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Strip SSR markers and stub hydration payloads in fetched HTML
detail: A curl'd Next.js page: flight scripts held 42.8k of 90k o200k tokens, inline SVG 15k. Stub __NEXT_DATA__, flight pushes and __APOLLO_STATE__ to key list plus size; strip React '<!-- -->', Angular _ngcontent-*/ng-reflect-*, Vue data-v-* markers. Extends #39.
test: curl SSR pages from Next, Nuxt, Angular and SvelteKit apps; measure payload and marker token share; assert the visible-text DOM dump is unchanged; ask a reader to locate one prop.
because: stubs hydration payloads in fetched HTML text
check: In fetched SSR HTML, __NEXT_DATA__ keeps only its size, top-level and pageProps key lists, the run of self.__next_f.push scripts becomes one stub with count and size, __APOLLO_STATE__ keeps size, entry count and first 10 keys, and React '<!-- -->' and Suspense comments, Angular _ngcontent/_nghost/ng-reflect attributes and Vue data-v attributes are removed from markup; the visible-text DOM dump, every tag with its other attributes, every other script and style verbatim (JSON-LD, application code) and the payload sizes and key lists are unchanged.
check_loses: the values of the stubbed payloads (props, flight data, Apollo cache entries beyond the first 10 keys), the individual flight chunks, markers that carry no visible text, and Nuxt/SvelteKit payloads (window.__NUXT__ and svelte-kit data scripts stay as they are); inline SVG is not touched (that is #331)

title: Native-build failure digest for node-gyp, setuptools and extconf
detail: Failed native installs (sharp, psycopg2, nokogiri) dump gyp info/ERR blocks, gcc lines with identical flags, and extconf option lists. Keep the last compiler or 'checking for' error, tool versions once, hoisted flags. Sibling of #701 for other toolchains.
test: Install sharp, psycopg2 and nokogiri with a missing system library; compare raw and digested tokens; check the missing library or header name survives.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Collapses gyp 'spawn args' blocks, make progress runs (the last object stays), setuptools creating/copying runs, mkmf 'checking ... yes' runs and mkmf's option list into count lines, hoists the flags shared by several cc/gcc lines into one '[ctxprune: @1 = ...]', and drops the node and node-gyp versions that 'gyp ERR!' repeats; every error line, the missing header/library/tool, the tool versions, the failing object and each compiler command (expanded) are unchanged.
check_loses: the successful intermediate steps (which objects compiled, which files were copied, which configure probes passed), the order of hoisted compiler flags, and the argument list gyp passes to python and make

title: Regroup monorepo runner output: turbo, nx, pnpm -r, lerna
detail: turbo prefixes every line with 'pkg:task: ', prints package-scope headers, and replays full logs of cache hits. Move prefixes into per-package headers and fold successful cache-hit replays to one line; failing tasks stay verbatim. Like #430, for task runners.
test: Build a 6-package turbo workspace twice, once with a type error; compare second-run tokens; check the failing package's full output and exit code survive.
because: regroup runner output; text transform
check: In turbo-style 'pkg:task: line' output, a task whose log is a quiet cache-hit replay folds to its cache-hit line plus a line count, a run of 3+ lines of a quiet task moves its prefix into one 'pkg:task:' header, and any task with an error/fail/warn/exception/traceback word keeps every line verbatim; header lines, the Tasks/Cached/Time summary, ERROR run failed and unprefixed warnings are unchanged and in order.
check_loses: the bodies of quiet cache-hit replays (only the hit line, hash and line count remain) and the repeated 'pkg:task: ' prefix on quiet runs
