title: Prefix commands with PYTHONNODEBUGRANGES and a frame-dropping preload
detail: The env var PYTHONNODEBUGRANGES removes traceback carets (250 to 240 tokens on a 3-frame sample). A preload via sitecustomize or NODE_OPTIONS=--require drops site-packages and node:internal frames by real path (5 of 10 lines in a Node sample).
test: Verify that PreToolUse can prefix Bash env vars. Run failing python and jest commands with and without the preload; compare tokens; confirm failures and exit codes are unchanged.
because: env var prefix removes traceback noise

title: Dedupe pytest records printed in both stderr and log sections
detail: With a StreamHandler on stderr, a failing test prints each record under 'Captured stderr call' and again, with level and logger prefix, under 'Captured log call' (reproduced with 2 records). Drop the plain copy when each line is a substring of a log-section message.
test: Run failing tests from Django and Flask apps with stderr logging; count stderr lines matched in the log section; verify no unmatched line is dropped.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Fold pip and npm resolver backtracking to version ranges
detail: pip backtracking prints Collecting, Downloading and 'looking at multiple versions' per candidate release; npm ERESOLVE prints nested Found/peer trees. Fold runs on one package to 'foo: tried 1.9 to 1.0 (40 versions)'; keep the final conflict chain verbatim.
test: pip install deliberately conflicting pins; npm install two packages with clashing peers; tokenise raw versus folded; confirm conflicting requirement names and versions survive.
because: fold resolver backtracking lines

title: Factor pytest --collect-only IDs into a file and class tree
detail: -q prints one full node ID per test, repeating file, class and parametrize ids; default mode prints a verbose <Function> tree. Rewrite as file header, class indent, bare names, and param ids folded to a count. Different format from #27 find/ls trees.
test: Collect a 2,000-test suite with parametrized cases; rewrite; tokenise before and after; ask which tests cover module X and whether a given param case exists.
because: factor test IDs into tree

title: Fold long Tailwind class strings in component file reads
detail: Replace className literals over ~12 classes with 'cls[14]: flex items-center ...' plus an id; PreToolUse expands the id inside Edit old_string (mechanism of #779). Lossy, for exploratory reads only; share of component tokens unmeasured.
test: Tokenise class/className literals in five open-source Tailwind repos to get their share of component files; then run 10 logic-only edit tasks with and without folding.
because: reversible folding with tool_use input expansion

title: Dictionary-stub known scaffold comments and XML prologs
detail: Hash lines against a shipped table of upstream text and drop or stub exact matches only: tsc --init, jest --init, Django settings.py and alembic.ini comments; pom schemaLocation roots, SVG and plist DOCTYPEs. Pom prolog 89 vs 14 tokens; user comments survive. Like #327.
test: Generate each scaffold, scan 100 local XML files for known prologs; tokenise their share; drop exact matches only; confirm user comments survive and a reader still names the schema version.
because: hash-table stub of known scaffold comments

title: Fold ORM boilerplate in Django migrations and Rails schema.rb
detail: makemigrations repeats the same id field tuple, BigAutoField(auto_created=True, primary_key=True, serialize=False, verbose_name='ID'), per model; schema.rb repeats created_at/updated_at datetime lines per table. Fold to 'id=auto' and 'timestamps' markers on exploratory reads.
test: Generate migrations for 20 models and a 20-table schema.rb; fold; tokenise; ask an agent to write a dependent migration or model and compare correctness.
because: deterministic boilerplate folding in file output

title: Fold tool-owned marker blocks in Markdown READMEs
detail: All-contributors lists (ALL-CONTRIBUTORS-LIST:START/END), terraform-docs (BEGIN_TF_DOCS) and similar generated regions hold avatar img and href cells per person. Fold each marker pair to names plus a count. One synthetic cell: 128 vs 7 o200k tokens. Related to #707.
test: Grep 30 popular READMEs for START/END and BEGIN/END marker pairs; measure token share inside them; confirm names survive the fold and the original stays in the saved file.
because: folds tool-owned marker blocks in Markdown

title: Ditto repeated function context in diff hunk headers
detail: git prints the enclosing function after every @@ header, so ten hunks in one big method repeat the same signature ten times. Replace a suffix identical to the previous header's with a ditto mark. Derivable line counts could go too, as a separate R variant.
test: Take git diff output from 20 commits touching large functions; count tokens in repeated header suffixes; ask which function each hunk sits in, before and after.
because: ditto repeated hunk header context
check: A hunk header whose function context equals the previous header's (same file; reset at each 'diff --git') ends in a lone '"' instead; decode restores the exact bytes, and a diff parser agrees on which function each hunk sits in.

title: Drop per-line plus prefix inside new-file diffs
detail: When the header says new file mode or --- /dev/null, every body line starts with + and adds nothing. Strip the prefix, emit one '[all lines added]' marker, keep the header. Synthetic 8-line file: 39 vs 31 o200k tokens. Deleted files stay with #329.
test: Run git show on 20 commits that add files and gh pr diff on PRs with new files; tokenise with and without the prefix; ask where a given function starts.
because: drop plus prefix in new-file diffs
check: In a new-file diff (--- /dev/null, @@ -0,0 +1,N @@ with N > 18) the N added lines are printed without their '+' after one '[all lines added]' marker; decode is count-based and restores the exact bytes, and an independent diff parser sees the same added lines.

title: Strip git patch-email constants and binary patch blocks
detail: format-patch and curl of .patch URLs open with 'From <sha> Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001' (constant date) and end with '-- ' plus the git version; 'GIT binary patch' holds base85 lines. Drop constants, stub binary literals. Synthetic binary block: 570 vs 9 o200k tokens.
test: Generate patches with format-patch and git diff --binary on repos holding images; apply the rule; confirm the saved original still passes git apply --check; tokenise before and after.
because: strip patch-email constants, stub binary

title: Lossless HTML attribute minifier: booleans, quotes, defaults
detail: Complements #39's chrome stripping: disabled="disabled" to disabled, unquote simple attributes, drop type="text/javascript", method="get", empty attributes and void-tag slashes. Same parse tree. Synthetic form fragment: 53 vs 31 o200k tokens.
test: Parse 30 curl'd pages and templates with html5lib before and after; assert identical trees; tokenise; exclude edit targets; compare the gain with #39 alone.
because: lossless HTML attribute minification
check: Start tags are rewritten with boolean attributes bare (disabled="disabled" to disabled), simple quoted values unquoted, default attributes (script type=text/javascript, style type=text/css, form method=get) and empty class/style dropped and the / of void elements removed; comments, CDATA, script, style, textarea and title content, any tag the pattern does not recognise and everything after such a tag are untouched, and html.parser yields the same event sequence.
check_loses: attribute quote style, whitespace inside tags, the trailing / on void tags, and attributes equal to their HTML default or empty class/style

title: Drop icon-font private-use glyphs and variation selectors
detail: eza or lsd --icons, powerline prompts, Nerd Font git graphs and FontAwesome markup emit U+E000-F8FF characters; emoji add U+FE0F. They carry no meaning for an LLM. #15 covers emoji; #233 drops icon glyphs only inside binary stubs. Synthetic icon listing: 22 vs 11 tokens.
test: Grep transcripts for U+E000-F8FF and U+FE0F in Bash output; count tokens; strip only in display output, never file reads; check CJK and source identifiers stay untouched.
because: drop private-use glyphs from text

title: Collapse PDF extractor glyph garbage: (cid:N) runs, spaced letters
detail: pdfminer prints (cid:123) for glyphs lacking a Unicode map; letter-spaced headings extract as 'C O N T R A C T'. Stub cid runs; rejoin five-plus single capitals when the result is a known word. Synthetic: 40 vs 8 and 18 vs 4 o200k tokens.
test: Extract text from 20 varied PDFs with pdfminer, pdfplumber and pdftotext; count cid and spaced-letter runs; check joins against a word list; ask a heading-lookup question before and after.
because: text transform on PDF extractor garbage

title: Stub References sections in pdftotext and arXiv paper text
detail: Paper-to-code tasks read pdftotext or arXiv markdown ending in long reference lists and appendices. Detect a References or Bibliography heading near the end, keep an entry count and the first entries, stub the rest. Extends #264; token share untested.
test: Run pdftotext on 15 arXiv papers; measure token share after the References heading; ask 10 method questions plus 3 'which paper introduced X' lookups; count refetches.
because: text transform stubbing reference sections

title: LaTeX build log pack for pdflatex and latexmk output
detail: pdflatex prints every opened file in nested parentheses, font and package info lines, and Overfull/Underfull hbox warnings. Keep '!' errors with their l.NN source line, undefined citations and references, a hbox count and the page count. Token share untested.
test: Build 10 public LaTeX repos with latexmk plus one broken edit each; measure log tokens; ask for the error line and missing citation; assert no '!' line is ever dropped.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Keeps the TeX version line, every '!' error with its 'l.NN' line and continuation, every LaTeX/Package/Class warning block (undefined citations and references, rerun hints, including a key hard-wrapped at column 79) and the 'Output written' / 'No pages of output' lines; the nested '(file' lines, font and package Info lines, memory statistics and page markers become '[ctxprune: N log lines elided]', and Overfull/Underfull boxes become one count line.
check_loses: the 79-column hard wrap of the lines it keeps (they are joined), the names and order of loaded packages and files, the line numbers and text of each Overfull/Underfull box (only the counts survive), font and package Info lines, page markers, and TeX's memory statistics

title: Changelog digest: newest sections plus versions named in context
detail: cat of CHANGELOG.md, HISTORY, NEWS or a release body often runs years deep. Keep Unreleased and the latest N version sections plus any section whose version appears in the command, prompt or lockfile diff; fold the rest to a heading list with counts.
test: Take 30 changelogs; split by version headings; run 20 'what changed in vX' and 'when was Y removed' questions with and without the digest; count refetches.
because: changelog digest keyed on versions in payload

title: Archive auto-memory entries that are never read or date-expired
detail: Two model-free signals: an index line whose topic file no transcript Read in the last N sessions, and an entry whose every embedded date is past by N days. A session hook moves them to a git-tracked archive outside the loaded index.
test: On 3-5 projects with memory dirs, parse transcripts for topic-file Reads and regex-scan for past-only dates; report index tokens recoverable times sessions per month; hand-check none still apply.
because: auto-memory files, transcripts and session hook

title: Cross-session failed-then-fixed command table, rewritten at PreToolUse
detail: Mine transcripts for a command that failed and a variant that then succeeded (pytest, then uv run pytest). Store pairs per repo; PreToolUse rewrites via updatedInput or denies with the fix. No standing context, unlike a SessionStart note (#307).
test: Extract fail-then-succeed pairs within 3 turns over 30 transcripts; count cross-session recurrence and the tokens of the failed call, error and retry turn.
because: failed-then-fixed command pairs learned from payload history

title: Subagent frontmatter preloads: skills and memory per spawn
detail: Subagent frontmatter skills: reportedly injects full skill bodies and memory: reportedly loads the head of that agent's MEMORY.md, at every cold spawn. Attribute spawn-time tokens to each preload and trim agents whose preloads go unused.
test: Verify that both fields inject text: spawn one agent with and without each via a logging proxy, diff the first request; count preloaded skills never invoked in sidechain transcripts.
because: subagent frontmatter config

title: Route context-answerable side questions to /btw
detail: Claude Code reportedly has /btw for a side question kept out of conversation history. UserPromptSubmit flags short questions without imperative verbs whose identifiers overlap recent context and suggests /btw, so question and answer never persist. Same nudge channel as #336.
test: Verify that /btw leaves no turn in the session JSONL. Classify 200 past prompts as side questions; sum their answer tokens times remaining turns.
because: /btw slash command and hook

title: Compaction summary anatomy: tokens per section and content type
detail: Split each compact-summary message into sections (requests, files, errors, user messages, pending, next step) and into verbatim code, pasted blobs, paths and narrative. Shows which sections PreCompact instructions (#631) should shrink, instead of guessing.
test: Extract isCompactSummary messages from transcripts; count tokens per heading and fenced block; rank sections across 20 compactions.
because: Claude Code compaction summary and PreCompact

title: Saved originals vanish with cache cleaners and fresh containers
detail: Originals cannot be regenerated, yet sit under ~/.cache, which the XDG spec calls non-essential; cleaners may purge it and restored cloud sessions may lack it, stranding note paths. Use XDG_STATE_HOME or a repo-local store; a resume check validates paths.
test: Run BleachBit or systemd-tmpfiles --clean over a home holding saved originals; separately delete the cache dir and resume; count failed greps and command reruns versus ~/.local/state storage.
because: durable saved-original location

title: Orientation card at SessionStart resume and compact
detail: After resume or compaction models typically rerun git status, git diff --stat and the last test command to re-learn state. A SessionStart hook computes those cheaply and injects one card of changed files and last failing test ids, replacing several calls.
test: Count orientation calls in the first 10 turns after compaction or resume over 20 transcripts; compare their tokens with a card of the same facts.
because: SessionStart hook

title: Deny Agent spawns that are single-file or single-symbol lookups
detail: A subagent pays a cold prefix plus report overhead. PreToolUse on Agent denies prompts naming one path or one identifier, saying 'Read or Grep it directly'. A rule-based gate applying the break-even from #817; distinct from continue gate #718.
test: Mine Agent prompts naming one path or symbol; price each sidechain total against an inline Read or Grep of the same target.
because: PreToolUse gate on Claude Code Agent spawns

title: Deterministic evidence manifest appended to subagent results
detail: A SubagentStop or Agent PostToolUse hook builds, without a model, a list of paths and line ranges the subagent read plus its grep patterns, saved to a file whose path rides on the result. Parent follow-ups use offsets instead of respawning or re-reading (#721).
test: Verify that the hook can append to Agent results. On 15 delegated runs, build manifests from sidechain transcripts; count later parent Reads or respawns that offsets would have narrowed.
because: SubagentStop hook and subagent result plumbing

title: Fold identify -verbose histograms and exiftool maker notes
detail: Measured: identify -verbose on a synthetic 800x600 gradient printed 942 lines, 35,194 o200k tokens, 97% of it an 836-line Histogram; plain identify is 36. Fold the histogram to top colours plus a count; drop ICC/profile hex and exiftool maker notes.
test: Run identify -verbose, exiftool and mediainfo on 10 photos and screenshots; tokenise; assert geometry, depth, colorspace, orientation and date/GPS tags survive; ask 5 metadata questions.
because: text fold of verbose tool output

title: Caption cleanup for ASS, TTML, json3 and LRC files
detail: #347 covers only VTT and SRT. ASS carries a style header and {\an2\fad} overrides per Dialogue line; TTML wraps each cue in p attributes (synthetic 40-cue TTML: 1,948 o200k tokens versus about 520 for text alone). Extract text, keep sparse stamps.
test: Fetch subs with yt-dlp --sub-format ass/ttml/json3 for 5 videos; tokenise raw versus cleaned; assert cleaned words are an ordered subsequence; ask 10 content questions.
because: text transform on caption formats

title: Playwright MCP envelope: drop echoed code, unchanged page header
detail: Playwright MCP results reportedly start with a 'Ran Playwright code' block echoing the call just made, then page URL, title and console sections. Strip the code echo (derivable from the arguments) and fold an unchanged URL/title to 'same page'.
test: Verify that the layout exists: run @playwright/mcp through 10 actions; tokenise each section per response; report envelope share outside the snapshot; confirm error text is untouched.
because: text transform on MCP result envelope

title: Blocklist trackers, ads and consent widgets in browser MCP
detail: Playwright MCP reportedly offers blocked-origins and init-script options. Blocking ad, analytics, chat-widget and consent-manager hosts keeps their nodes out of every snapshot, screenshot and network list. Differs from viewport and image flags (#353).
test: Verify the flags via npx @playwright/mcp --help; snapshot 10 news and shop sites with and without a blocklist; tokenise; run 10 tasks and count any needing a blocked widget.
because: browser server configuration, not a text transform

title: Visual-regression failures: Read only the diff image
detail: Playwright toHaveScreenshot failures reportedly write name-expected, name-actual and name-diff PNGs, and agents may Read all three at pixel-area cost each. PreToolUse on those reads serves the diff alone plus mismatch pixel count and changed bounding box.
test: Verify that a failing toHaveScreenshot spec writes three PNGs; log which the agent Reads; compute diff-crop token cost with PIL; ask 5 'what changed' questions, diff-only versus the triplet.
because: image reads, PreToolUse steering

title: Settle-before-capture: one stable screenshot instead of retakes
detail: Agents often screenshot mid-load (spinner, skeleton, animation) and retake. A wrapper disables animations, waits for network idle and two matching frames, then returns one image. #352 stubs duplicates after the cost; this prevents the extra frame.
test: In 5 recorded browser sessions count screenshot pairs on one URL within 5 s that differ only by loading state; replay tasks with the wrapper; compare screenshot counts and success.
because: screenshot capture wrapper

title: Text probes instead of screenshots for layout and plot checks
detail: Agents screenshot after CSS edits or matplotlib plots to eyeball alignment, colours or axis ranges. One evaluate call returning getBoundingClientRect, computed styles or plot data stats costs tens of tokens versus about w*h/750 per image. A hook note nudges after the second screenshot.
test: Count image Reads following CSS or plotting edits in transcripts; on 10 layout and plot tasks compare image tokens and success for probe-first versus screenshot-first.
because: advice to agents to avoid screenshots

title: PDF outline-first: deny whole Read, offer bookmarks and page index
detail: For PDFs over about 20 pages, PreToolUse denies a full Read and returns the page count, bookmark outline (PyMuPDF get_toc or pdfinfo) and each page's first heading line. The agent then reads chosen page ranges. Differs from pdftotext routing (#346).
test: Take 5 long manuals; build outlines; for 10 lookup questions count pages read with versus without the outline; check the fallback when no bookmarks exist.
because: PreToolUse deny of Read tool

title: Transcript chaptering: timestamped topic segments with lead sentences
detail: For hour-long meeting or lecture transcripts, segment by lexical shift (TextTiling, Hearst 1997) and emit '[12:40] lead sentence, N words elided', keeping the original on disk to grep. Differs from disfluency stripping (#731) and cue merging (#347).
test: Segment 5 long transcripts; compare outline tokens with full text; ask 10 questions and count those answerable from the outline versus needing a refetch.
because: text segmentation of long transcripts
check: A timestamped transcript of 40+ lines is segmented by lexical shift (TextTiling-style, 8+ lines per chapter) and replaced by a one-line header plus '[mm:ss] Speaker: lead sentence, N words elided' per chapter; the chapter starts and leads, the word count (lead words plus elided words equal the transcript's), the time span and the speaker list are those of the segmentation of the original. Short transcripts are left alone.
check_loses: everything except each chapter's first sentence and word count (the original must be grepped or re-read for details), the stamps of lines inside a chapter, and any chapter boundary the lexical shift misses

title: Desktop accessibility-API text instead of computer-use screenshots
detail: To read dialogs or field values in desktop apps, query OS accessibility APIs (AT-SPI on Linux, AX on macOS, UI Automation on Windows) for focused-window text. Cost follows text length, not pixel area. Screenshots stay for visual judgement; steer via skill or hook note.
test: Verify that an AT-SPI or AX dump works in the sandbox; on 10 read-the-value desktop tasks compare dump tokens with w*h/750 per screenshot and answer accuracy.
because: steers away from screenshots, non-text media

title: Teacher outputs atom-index delete ranges, so rewriting is impossible
detail: Number atoms in the prompt ([17]word) and have the teacher reply only with ranges to delete, like 3-9,14. No alignment and no variation filter, so non-English chunks the model card says were dropped as rewrites survive; output tokens shrink, cutting teacher cost.
test: On 200 non-English and 200 code chunks, compare variation-filter pass rate and atom agreement of free-text v1 versus index-range output; train both on equal chunks, compare QA at 0.5.
because: offline teacher prompt design for labels

title: SWE-bench test lists as free keep labels for pytest logs
detail: SWE-style instances carry FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS test names (SWE-bench; SWE-smith and SWE-rebench reportedly too). In trajectory pytest outputs, atoms of lines naming FAIL_TO_PASS tests and their tracebacks are keep; PASS_TO_PASS pass lines are drop. No teacher needed.
test: Join 100 pytest-bearing SWE-smith tool outputs to instance metadata, label by test name, report failing-test-name and traceback atom recall of the current model at 0.33 and 0.5 versus teacher labels.
because: free offline labels from public SWE datasets

title: Gold-patch hunks as task-conditioned keep labels for code reads
detail: SWE trajectories pair file views with the instance's gold patch. Lines in or near patched functions, plus signatures, are keep for that task; distant bodies drop. Gives teacher-free code labels and training signal for pair-input scoring (#166) and goal-hint skimming (#1056).
test: For 100 file views in SWE-smith traces, derive labels from the patch; measure how many patched-line atoms the current model keeps at 0.33 versus a head-truncation baseline of equal size.
because: offline labels from gold patches

title: Failing-test coverage slices as deterministic code keep labels
detail: Run a repo's passing and failing tests under coverage.py; spectrum-based fault-localization scores (Tarantula, Jones and Harrold 2002) rank lines. Suspicious lines plus signatures are keep, never-executed bodies drop. Cheaper than per-statement mutation (#365) and task-shaped.
test: On 15 SWE-smith repos with a failing test, compute Tarantula scores; check fixed lines rank in the top 20%, then measure the current model's keep rate on them at 0.33.
because: offline labels from coverage runs

title: Dictionary word segmentation for CJK and Thai atoms
detail: Verified: atomize() gives one atom per Han or kana character, so deleting one character inside a word garbles it. Atomize with a word segmenter (jieba, BudouX or ICU break iterator) in training and inference so deletions drop whole words. Complements #993.
test: Segment 200 fineweb2 zh/ja chunks; count current model deletions that split a segmenter word; relabel with word atoms, fine-tune, compare zh/ja QA at 0.5.
because: local word segmenter in atomizer, text only

title: Teacher position-bias audit via reversed and shuffled line order
detail: For order-independent chunks (logs, listings, JSON arrays), relabel with lines reversed and shuffled. Atoms whose keep flips are position noise or lost-in-the-middle bias (Liu et al. 2023). Train on agreement-only or soft labels. Differs from temperature resampling (#361).
test: Relabel 200 log and listing chunks forward and reversed with the same teacher; map lines back, report flip rate by relative position and by duplicate versus unique line.
because: offline teacher label denoising

title: Instruction-file corpus with imperative-preserving labels
detail: No training source resembles AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or SKILL.md text, which #257, #450 and #1062 want to compress. Mine permissive public ones; the teacher prompt must protect must/never/always/only and conditions. Probe first: how often the current model deletes modal words there.
test: Score 50 public permissively licensed AGENTS.md files at 0.5; count deleted must/never/always/only/not and conditional clauses per file versus a sentence-level BM25 baseline at equal tokens.
because: training corpus of instruction-style text, offline

title: Mine fenced console output blocks from READMEs and docs
detail: Public trajectory data is reportedly Python-heavy. READMEs and docs show real outputs of cargo, go, helm, terraform, kubectl and npm in console or text fences right after the command block. Extract command and output pairs as a non-Python tool-output source; license-filter by repo.
test: On a 1,000-file markdown sample from a permissive code corpus, extract pairs; report distinct command families and median output length versus SWE-smith.
because: public docs mined as training data, offline

title: Inflate-to-label: LLM inserts filler into dense text
detail: Reverse the teacher. Give an LLM terse, human-written text (quiet logs, commit messages, API docs) and ask it only to insert verbose filler. The original is a guaranteed subsequence, so labels are exact with no alignment failures. Watch for shortcut learning on LLM-style filler.
test: Inflate 300 terse chunks (subsequence check), fine-tune mixed with real labels, compare held-out real AUC and QA at 0.5 against real-only; first score inserted filler with the current model.
because: offline synthetic label generation

title: Score-conditioned needle writer targets the pruner's blind spots
detail: Show an LLM the chunk with per-atom scores and ask for questions whose answers sit in the lowest-scored decile, quoting verbatim. Quoted low-scored answer spans become hard keep labels. Unlike random question sets (#745), sampling targets where the current checkpoint is weakest.
test: Generate 5 low-score-targeted and 5 random questions for 100 chunks; compare the share of answer spans the model drops at 0.33, then fine-tune on each set and compare QA.
because: offline hard-example label generation

title: Mine 'trim' commits for human deletion-only edit labels
detail: Git history holds human deletion-only edits: commits whose messages say shorten, trim, tighten or drop noise, with hunks that only remove words from docs, comments, logged strings or fixtures. Before/after pairs are natural subsequence labels, with no LLM teacher.
test: git log -p --grep over 20 permissive repos; keep pure word-deletion hunks, hand-check 100 for low-value versus obsolete content, score removed atoms with the current model.
because: git history mined for labels, offline

title: Leave-one-source-out ablation to tune the corpus mix
detail: DEFAULT_MIX fractions in sources.py are hand-set. Train small runs with each source removed or doubled (DoReMi, Xie et al. 2023, learns domain weights with a proxy model). Cut teacher spend on sources whose removal costs nothing; reallocate to weak slices.
test: Using existing labels, train 8 leave-one-source-out runs with fixed steps; report per-source held-out AUC and QA-at-0.5 deltas. Repeat one removal with a second seed to estimate noise.
because: offline ablation to tune corpus mix

title: Spend keep rate on unprotected atoms, with a prose floor
detail: compress() charges force-kept atoms against the budget: once protected share reaches the rate, only protected atoms survive and the 0.95 gate still ships it. Simulated: 74% protected, rate 0.5, 0 of 156 prose words kept. Budget the unprotected remainder or reserve a prose floor.
test: Replay hook events; count outputs where protected share exceeds rate and no unprotected atom survives; compare forced-only, remainder-rate and floor arms on error-line QA and total tokens.
because: budget logic change, deterministic text transform

title: Verify existing saved original's digest before skipping the write
detail: _save_original skips writing whenever the hash-named file exists, never checking content. A stale or pre-planted file (a prompt-injected agent can compute the name of a predictable output) then becomes the 'full output' the note points to. Compare digest; rewrite atomically.
test: Pre-create outputs/<hash>.txt with different text, then run the hook on the matching output; assert the file is repaired or the hook declines. Repeat with a truncated file.
because: digest check on saved originals

title: Never prune plan and dry-run outputs that authorise an action
detail: terraform plan, kubectl diff, helm diff, git clean -n and rsync -n print what the next command will destroy or replace. Lowercase 'destroy', 'replace' and 'forces' are unprotected, so deletable. Skip these by command signature, or run lossless rules only.
test: Compress 10 terraform plan and kubectl diff outputs at 0.5; count dropped destroy, replace and delete words; weigh against the tokens lost by skipping.
because: skip rule by command string protects plan outputs

title: Shield true, false, null and empty-value literals from deletion
detail: Verified: is_protected is false for true, false, null, None, yes, no, on, off, up, down and '<none>'; '[]' and '{}' are droppable, and the hook runs keep_structure=False. So '"enabled": false' can lose its value but keep its key. Force-keep literals after ':' or '='.
test: Count these literals dropped right after a kept key across 200 saved MCP JSON, YAML and kubectl outputs at 0.5; add the shield; compare tokens and 'is X enabled' QA.
because: protect rule on text, deterministic

title: Stub high-confidence secrets in the model's view only
detail: PEM private keys, AKIA keys, ghp_ tokens, JWTs and Bearer headers become '[secret kind, N chars, sha8]' in updatedToolOutput at any size; the 0600 saved file keeps originals. Keeps credentials out of the transcript and provider. Differs from #370, which declines.
test: Plant ten secret kinds in command outputs; assert the model view holds only stubs and the file holds originals; run a task needing one value and count recovery tokens.
because: deterministic secret stubbing in tool output text

title: Probe whether agents present pruned output as verbatim to users
detail: Asked 'show me the exact output' after a compressed call, an agent may paste spliced text as the real thing, an honesty failure no QA metric sees. Compare note variants (e.g. 'abridged; quote only from the saved file') and price the added words.
test: Run 20 prompts asking for the exact output of compressed commands; score replies that show spliced text without a caveat or a refetch, per note variant.
because: agent honesty probe

title: Identical command rerun passes through uncompressed once
detail: A repeat of the same command soon after a compressed result signals the agent distrusts it. Keep a small stamp keyed by session_id and command hash; return the full output once. Per-call and stateful, unlike family-level breakers (#270).
test: In transcripts, count identical Bash reruns within five turns of a compressed result and the tokens their second compression wasted; with the stamp, confirm the rerun is verbatim.
because: local state keyed by command hash

title: Install should detect settings layers that stop hooks running
detail: Claude Code reportedly honors disableAllHooks and managed-policy options such as allowManagedHooksOnly, and project hooks wait for folder trust. Install writes settings.json and reports success while no compression ever happens. Read every layer and warn at install.
test: Verify that disableAllHooks silences the hook: set it locally, run install, then a 10 KB Bash output via claude -p; confirm no note appears and install stays silent.
because: checks harness settings layers at install

title: LangChain 1.0 wrap_tool_call middleware port of the hook
detail: LangChain 1.0 AgentMiddleware (verified in the 1.0.0 wheel) exposes wrap_tool_call, which can return a replaced ToolMessage. A CtxpruneMiddleware compresses any tool result over a threshold, MCP-adapter tools included, saves the original, and appends the note.
test: Build create_agent with a fake chat model and a tool returning 20k chars; assert the ToolMessage the model receives is compressed and the original file exists.
because: LangChain middleware API

title: LangGraph llm_input_messages stubs aged ToolMessages, state untouched
detail: In create_react_agent, a pre_model_hook can return llm_input_messages (present in langgraph-prebuilt 1.1.1) so the model sees stubs for old ToolMessages while graph state keeps full text. Stub text is a head line plus a saved-file pointer.
test: Run a ReAct agent with a fake model over 8 retrieval calls; compare tokens of model input with and without the hook; confirm state.messages stays intact.
because: LangGraph pre_model_hook is one framework's feature

title: Rank on pruned candidates before LLM listwise rerank
detail: LLM rerankers (LlamaIndex LLMRerank, RankGPTRerank; LangChain LLMListwiseRerank; names from memory) read every candidate in full. Show them a 0.3-kept view to order candidates, then pass the chosen few at higher fidelity.
test: On 100 HotpotQA queries with 30 BM25 candidates, run a listwise LLM rerank on raw versus 0.3-pruned text; compare NDCG@10 and rerank prompt tokens.
because: pruned view shown to LLM reranker

title: Retriever-native MMR and score threshold before any compression
detail: LangChain search_type='mmr' (fetch_k, lambda_mult) and 'similarity_score_threshold', or LlamaIndex MMR query mode, drop near-duplicate and weak hits at query time at zero model cost. Set them before choosing a prune rate.
test: On a docs index, compare top-8 similarity against MMR (fetch_k 24, lambda 0.7): pairwise chunk overlap, tokens, and answer-chunk recall over 50 questions.
because: advice on configuring retriever settings

title: Drop LlamaIndex _node_content JSON blob from raw vector DB reads
detail: LlamaIndex stores each whole node as a JSON string in payload metadata (verified in llama-index-core 0.12.0 source), plus doc_id, document_id and ref_doc_id copies; Qdrant may keep the text inside too. Agents reading the DB directly pay per hit. Keep text, file, offsets.
test: Repeat the synthetic check (571 metadata vs 169 chunk tokens) on a real LlamaIndex Chroma or Qdrant collection; strip the blob; confirm text, file and offsets remain.
because: text transform dropping redundant DB payload JSON

title: Pruning lets refine-mode synthesis collapse into one call
detail: LlamaIndex refine and LangChain refine/map_reduce chains make one LLM call per chunk batch, resending question, template and the running answer each time. If pruned chunks fit one window, use compact or stuff mode.
test: With a fake LLM that logs prompts: run refine on 10 chunks, then compact on 0.5-pruned chunks; compare total prompt tokens and call count, then answer agreement on 30 questions.
because: advice on choosing synthesis mode

title: Slim RAG-server MCP envelopes: Context7 snippets, qdrant entries
detail: Context7-style servers reportedly return snippet blocks (title, description, source URL, code) split by long dash rules; mcp-server-qdrant wraps hits as <entry><content/><metadata/></entry>. Drop rules, fold description equal to title, dedupe identical code, hoist URL prefixes and shared metadata keys.
test: Verify the formats: capture 10 Context7 and 8 qdrant find results; count tokens in separators, wrappers, repeated prefixes; apply the rewrite; check every code block and metadata value survives.
because: text transform on RAG MCP output envelopes

title: RAGBench sentence-level utilization labels as reader-free pruner eval
detail: RAGBench (Galileo, 2024; reportedly on Hugging Face) annotates which retrieved sentences were relevant and utilized per question. Measure how much of those sentences survive each keep rate, with no reader model; the same labels could train a query-aware pruner.
test: Load the dataset, run ctxprune at 0.5 and 0.33, report token recall of utilized sentences against random, head and BM25 baselines at equal kept tokens.
because: reader-free eval with public labels

title: Multi-hop bridge-entity survival audit under pruning
detail: In HotpotQA or MuSiQue style questions, hop two depends on an entity named in a hop-one passage. Pruning one passage at a time can drop that bridge. Measure bridge-mention survival and answer accuracy per hop at each keep rate.
test: Use HotpotQA distractor-setting items with gold supporting facts; prune each passage independently at 0.5; count questions whose bridge entity string is deleted, and the accuracy gap versus intact ones.
because: multi-hop survival audit

title: Mean pruner score as a chunk-quality prior for filtering
detail: Mean atom keep-probability per chunk is a query-free density signal; low-percentile chunks may be boilerplate or filler (to be verified). Exclude them at ingest or demote them in top-k, before spending any prune budget.
test: Score 2,000 chunks of a docs crawl; hand-label the lowest 10 percent as filler or content; then compare recall@8 on 50 questions with those chunks excluded.
because: local pruner score as chunk-quality filter

title: Embed pruned chunks to cut embedding-API tokens
detail: Idea #383 embeds originals and serves pruned. The opposite saves embedding-API tokens at ingest: embed a 0.7-kept version of each chunk and serve that same text. Risk: query words deleted from the embedded text lower recall.
test: On a BEIR subset, embed raw versus 0.7- and 0.5-pruned chunks with one embedding model; compare recall@10 and total embedded tokens.
because: prune text before embedding-API calls

title: Glue path sigils, signs, percent and units to protected atoms
detail: Verified: atomize('~/proj') gives '~' and '/proj'; '../x' gives '.', '.', '/x'; '+5' splits into '+' and '5', '50%' into '50' and '%'. Only the core is protected, so a dropped sigil, sign or percent changes meaning. Atomize affix plus core as one atom.
test: Mutation test: on 200 saved outputs with relative paths and signed or percent values, drop each lone affix atom and count changed meanings; recount after gluing; QA 'how much slower'.
because: atomizer change, deterministic text transform

title: Re-glue punctuation, CJK and tabs after deletions in detok
detail: Verified: detok treats a zero-whitespace dropped atom as a space, so kept punctuation gains one: 'log.txt .', 'Retrying ( 2 .'; Chinese '你好世界很好' became '你 世界 好'. Tabs collapse to spaces. Keep source adjacency unless two word atoms would fuse.
test: Compare Claude token counts of detok output before and after on 100 outputs and 20 CJK files (cl100k showed no change on one sample); assert no word atoms fuse.
because: detokenizer fix, deterministic text transform
check: After deletions a kept atom that was glued to the deleted atoms before it stays glued unless the output would then read back as different atoms, and a deleted run keeps newline over tab over space, so CJK, kept punctuation and tab columns are not padded with spaces; checked against the real atomize/detok on 480 random keep masks (token effect on a real tokenizer not measured).

title: Fold content-free issue comments: +1, bump, thanks, LGTM, emoji
detail: In GitHub MCP issue and PR comment lists, replace comments whose whole body is +1, bump, thanks, LGTM, 'any update?' or only emoji with a per-author count and a date range. Author and timestamp JSON per comment is the real cost. Original saved.
test: Fetch comments for 20 busy public issues via gh api; count tokens in bodies matching the regex; spot-check 50 matches for a hidden maintainer decision.
because: folds MCP tool result JSON, payload-only

title: Protect precision: prose compounds like and/or and e.g. cost budget
detail: Verified: 'e.g' and 'i.e' are protected as dotted atoms; by the same rule 'and/or' counts as a path, and CamelCase brand names like GitHub count as identifiers. They eat budget meant for IDs. Require path or identifier shape. Precision side of #92.
test: Count protected atoms in saved prose outputs that fail a path or ID shape check; relax and compare kept useful words and QA at equal output characters.
because: protect rule precision, text only

title: Single-atom ablation fuzz with parse oracles ranks unprotected atoms
detail: Delete each unprotected atom alone from golden outputs; flag deletions that break a cheap oracle (bash -n on commands, json.loads, yaml, shlex, path resolution, number parse). Rank atom classes by breakage rate to prioritise protect rules (#1046, #494, #924).
test: Run on 500 saved outputs; report breakage per atom class; check the top classes include the verified cases (~, %, +, false); ship rules for the rest.
because: ablation fuzz with parse oracles

title: Lexical-overlap strata for QA, NoLiMa-style latent questions
detail: NoLiMa (Adobe, ICML 2025, reportedly) shows long-context retrieval degrades when question and needle share no literal words. Teacher-written questions likely reuse output words, flattering any selector. Bucket existing items by overlap and add paraphrased latent versions.
test: Bucket the 378 QA items by question-to-gold-span word overlap; report original versus 0.5-kept accuracy per tercile; rewrite 50 high-overlap items with no shared words and rerun.
because: lexical-overlap eval strata

title: Next-action-invariant mask search as training labels
detail: CoACT (arXiv 2607.02911, reportedly) compresses observations while preserving the agent's next action. Use that as acceptance: sample masks per recorded result, keep the shortest one where a cheap policy repeats the same next tool call, train on them. Differs from QA-verified #598.
test: On 50 recorded results, sample 8 masks each; Haiku repeats the next call 3 times; report share where the shortest action-safe mask keeps fewer tokens than the uniform 0.5 mask.
because: offline mask search for training labels

title: Intent-to-output attention maps from a 0.5B local LM
detail: Reportedly AttentionRAG-style work scores context by attention from the query tokens. Run a tiny causal LM over command, output and an intent prompt; sum mid-layer attention per line as relevance. Differs from surprisal #260, ablation #266 and encoder-pair #166.
test: On the QA set with gold spans, compare gold-line recall at equal kept tokens against current classifier scores and BM25; time it per 10k chars on CPU.
because: small local CPU LM scoring command and output text

title: Fault-history pinning: stop re-stubbing re-requested paths
detail: Pichay (arXiv 2603.09023, reportedly) detects a page fault when a model re-requests evicted content and pins that page for the session. Apply to dedup stubs (#60, #140): after one re-read of a stubbed path or hash, never stub it again.
test: Replay 20 transcripts through a stub simulator; count re-reads within 10 turns of a stub and the tokens spent; compute what pin-after-first-fault would have avoided.
because: pin re-requested paths, never stub again

title: Generic-compressor headroom map per command family
detail: Log-compression research (Logzip, LogReducer, reportedly) shows template coding beats generic compressors. Per command family, compare lossless-rule byte ratio with xz and a trained zstd dictionary on the same corpus; big gaps flag missing rules. Bytes are not tokens, so ranking only.
test: Group saved outputs by family; tabulate rule ratio versus xz and zstd -D ratio; pick the five largest gaps and read their lines for missed repetition patterns.
because: compressor headroom comparison analysis

title: Classical Chinese rewrite of always-on rules, kill-test first
detail: Reverse of #919: translate English CLAUDE.md rules into dense Classical Chinese. A quick o200k proxy on one rule sentence gave 25 English versus 26 Chinese tokens, so a win is doubtful; Claude's tokenizer may differ. Cheap to kill.
test: Run Anthropic count_tokens on 20 rule paragraphs in English versus Classical Chinese; continue only if at least 25% fewer tokens, then replay 10 tasks for rule adherence.
because: CLAUDE.md rule rewriting; also tokenizer dependent

title: CMake cache listings: drop help comments and blank lines
detail: cmake -LAH and CMakeCache.txt put a '//' help sentence and a blank line before every variable. One-file project: 1321 o200k tokens, 678 without them. Keep NAME:TYPE=value; help stays in the saved original.
test: Run cmake -LAH on three real repos; count o200k tokens before and after; ask a reader which option controls a feature; compare accuracy.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Drop empty and default rows from toolchain config dumps
detail: go env, xcodebuild -showBuildSettings, mvn help:effective-pom and gradle properties print hundreds of default-valued entries (go env here: 389 tokens, 319 after dropping empty rows). Use per-tool default tables or an empty-project baseline; keep overrides and keys the command named.
test: Capture each dump on a real project; diff against an empty-project baseline; measure tokens saved; check a reader still finds the JDK, SDK or proxy setting.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Linker undefined-reference floods: group by symbol, drop offsets
detail: GNU ld prints an 'in function' line plus 'src.cpp:(.text+0x2e): undefined reference to X' per call site; MSVC LNK2019 repeats the decorated name after the readable one (synthetic 52 vs 33 tokens). Group by symbol with caller list; drop offsets and decorated twins.
test: Link objects missing 20 symbols with GNU ld, lld and MSVC; compare tokens; check a reader can still name the missing symbol and library.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Dedupe header-origin compiler warnings repeated per translation unit
detail: A warning inside a shared header prints once per .cpp that includes it; only the 'In file included from' line differs (two TUs under g++ -Wall gave identical 5-line blocks). Key on header path:line:col plus message; print once with TU count.
test: Compile 30 TUs sharing one noisy header via make -j; count tokens before and after; verify one warning per distinct site remains.
because: dedupe repeated compiler warnings
check: A warning in a header (.h/.hpp/...) that repeats with the same context line and echoed code in several translation units is printed once, followed by '[ctxprune: this warning also occurred in N more translation units]'; the include-chain and context lines of fully duplicated blocks go with them. Every distinct header warning site with its translation-unit count, every error and every warning in a non-header file, and every make command line are unchanged.
check_loses: which translation units reported a header warning (only how many) and the include chains of the dropped repeats

title: Alias toolchain-owned path roots and hashed directories
detail: Fixed per-ecosystem prefixes: /rustc/<40hex>/library, GOROOT, JDK, Xcode SDK, DerivedData/<Proj>-<hash>, Gradle files-2.1/.../<sha1>/, cargo target/debug/deps/name-<16hex>. Synthetic: SDK path 44 to 19 tokens, Gradle cache path 79 to 29. A legend maps aliases back.
test: Collect failing builds from five toolchains; apply a prefix table; measure token drop and whether the agent can still open the aliased file.
because: toolchain path aliasing with legend, deterministic

title: Audit inherited verbosity env defaults such as RUST_BACKTRACE=1
detail: This sandbox exports RUST_BACKTRACE=1: a two-failure cargo test printed 1142 o200k stdout tokens versus 210 with RUST_BACKTRACE=0 (aliasing /rustc/<hash>/ alone gave 806). Scan inherited env for such defaults (GOTRACEBACK, RUST_LOG, MAVEN_OPTS) and set quiet values for test runs.
test: Run one failing cargo test with RUST_BACKTRACE 0, 1 and full; compare tokens, and replay whether an agent still fixes the bug.
because: quiet env prefix on test commands
check: A PreToolUse rewrite prefixes a cargo test or go test command with the quiet value of an inherited RUST_BACKTRACE, RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE, GOTRACEBACK or RUST_LOG when the environment has a noisy one and the command does not set it itself; on real cargo output the failed tests, panic sites, messages and totals are identical at a quarter of the tokens, only the call chain is lost, and non-test commands, explicit settings, quiet or missing variables and a broken audit leave the command untouched.

title: Xcode pbxproj and .sln: alias opaque IDs, collapse config matrices
detail: project.pbxproj repeats 24-hex object IDs beside name comments; .sln lists four configuration rows per project GUID. Synthetic 40 build-file rows: 2275 to 1272 tokens with short aliases; 12-project .sln matrix: 2304 to 486. Edits must use the saved original.
test: Run on a real pbxproj and .sln; check a reader can answer which target builds X.swift; confirm edit anchors from the saved original still apply.
because: aliases opaque IDs in pbxproj/sln text
check: In a project.pbxproj every 24-hex object id becomes a short '§N' alias in order of first appearance (structure, names, comments and build settings kept), and in a .sln the ProjectConfigurationPlatforms rows of every project whose matrix is exactly the identity collapse to one '{GUID} = identity' line; the object graph (which target builds which file, groups, settings) and every project, configuration and mapping are unchanged.
check_loses: the 24-hex object ids themselves (no legend: an edit must anchor on the saved original file, not on the aliased text) and, in a .sln, the verbatim identity rows (restored exactly by the one-line rule); a .sln whose matrix is not identity for a project keeps that project's rows verbatim

title: Spring Boot logs: drop padding and PID, fold repeated banners
detail: Default Boot lines carry a fixed PID, '---', a 12-wide thread slot and a 40-wide logger column; every context boot repeats the ASCII banner and startup block. Synthetic 30 lines: 1709 to 839 tokens. Normalise columns, hoist PID, fold repeated startup blocks.
test: Run a Spring Boot suite booting several contexts; apply the normaliser; compare tokens and check ERROR and WARN lines survive verbatim.
because: normalise Spring log columns; text transform
check: Spring Boot records 'TS  LEVEL PID --- [   thread] logger   : msg' lose the column padding and '---' and the shared PID moves to one '[pid N]' header (kept per record as pid=N when several JVMs log); the second and later identical banner blocks fold to one marker; timestamp, level, thread, logger and message of every record, and every non-record line (stack frames), are unchanged.
check_loses: the fixed column widths (thread slot of 15, logger column of 40), the literal '---', and the repeated banner block after the first

title: Benchmark harness logs: fold warmup and iteration lines
detail: JMH, BenchmarkDotNet, criterion and go test -bench -count reportedly print per-iteration and warmup lines before a summary table (from memory). Keep the header once, the table and flagged outliers; fold iterations into min, mean, max per case.
test: Run JMH or criterion on a five-case suite; compare tokens of full log versus table; ask a reader which case regressed.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Steer log readers to cheapest native format and bounds
detail: adb logcat -v brief with -t N, a *:W filter or --pid; journalctl -o short with -p warning; dmesg -l err,warn: flags change per-line cost before output exists. Synthetic: logcat threadtime 850 vs brief 565 tokens; journalctl short-iso 600 vs short 480.
test: Capture the same 200 lines in every -v and -o variant on a real device or host; tokenise; confirm timestamps survive at the needed resolution.
because: log command flag rewrite to cheaper format

title: Fold simctl and xcodebuild destination lists; bound bare dumpsys
detail: 'xcrun simctl list' and xcodebuild destination errors reportedly print dozens of devices and unavailable runtimes; fold to counts plus matches. adb dumpsys with no service name dumps everything: inject the service name or a head cap.
test: Run each on a dev machine and record sizes; check agents still find the right simulator UDID or dumpsys section after folding.
because: text folding and command bounding
check: Folds the devices of unavailable simulator runtimes, the Device Types and Device Pairs listings, unavailable runtimes and xcodebuild's ineligible destinations to counts, and bounds each dumpsys section to 3 lines plus a '[N more lines omitted; run: dumpsys NAME]' marker; every available runtime's devices with name, UDID and state, every eligible destination with its id, the dumpsys service list and section names are unchanged.
check_loses: the identity of devices in unavailable runtimes, the device type identifiers, ineligible destinations (including their error text), and everything in a dumpsys section after its third line (re-run with the service name)

title: Mine compiler test suites as free real-diagnostic fixtures
detail: rustc's tests/ui holds thousands of expected .stderr files; Go's cmd/go testdata scripts and clang diagnostic tests hold more (from memory; verify layout and licences). Use them as multi-version golden outputs for diagnostic rules instead of hand-written samples.
test: Clone rust-lang/rust, count .stderr files and tokens; apply the dedupe and path rules; report savings per file and any breakage.
because: compiler test suites as fixtures

title: SwiftPM and CocoaPods resolution: one line per package
detail: swift package resolve reportedly prints Fetching, Fetched, Computing, Computed and Working copy lines per dependency, repeating the URL (from memory; no swift installed here). pod install prints per-pod lines. Collapse to name, version, URL; keep errors verbatim.
test: Run swift package resolve on a 20-dependency manifest on macOS CI; count tokens before and after; confirm failures are untouched.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: CloudTrail and cloud audit events to one-line digests
detail: Each CloudTrail event repeats userIdentity.sessionContext, tlsDetails, additionalEventData, requestID, eventID and recipientAccountId. Emit time, principal, action, resource, error code per event; keep full JSON for denied or failed calls. Synthetic S3 GetObject record: 502 vs 36 o200k tokens.
test: Fetch 50 events with aws cloudtrail lookup-events; digest; ask who deleted resource X and from which IP; check AccessDenied events keep every field.
because: CloudTrail JSON to one-line digests
check: Each CloudTrail event (from Records or from lookup-events) becomes one line with time, principal, source IP, service:action and its request parameters; an event with an errorCode also keeps its complete record, so who did what to which resource from which IP, and every field of every denied call, are unchanged.
check_loses: userIdentity.sessionContext, tlsDetails, additionalEventData, requestID, eventID, userAgent, responseElements, resources and recipientAccountId of successful events; the lookup-events envelope fields (EventId, ReadOnly, AccessKeyId, Username, Resources) that repeat the record

title: OTLP logs and metrics JSON to logfmt rows
detail: Collector file-exporter JSON carries timeUnixNano plus observedTimeUnixNano, severityNumber beside severityText, empty traceId, typed attribute wrappers and startTimeUnixNano per datapoint. Emit logfmt per log record and a table per metric. One synthetic log record: 129 vs 34 tokens. Sibling of #421.
test: Run an OTel collector with the file exporter for logs and metrics; convert; assert counts and severities match; ask which service logged the most errors.
because: OTLP JSON to logfmt rows
check: OTLP logs and metrics JSON (one document or one per line) become one logfmt line per log record (time to the millisecond, level, service, trace and span ids when present, body, unwrapped attributes) and one line per metric data point under a '# metric' header (value, or count/sum/min/max/buckets/bounds); record and data-point counts, severities, bodies, attributes, metric values and the service with the most errors are unchanged.
check_loses: severityNumber when severityText is present (and the reverse), observedTimeUnixNano, sub-millisecond time, startTimeUnixNano of data points, resource and scope attributes other than service.name, metric descriptions, droppedAttributesCount and flags; documents with attribute keys containing whitespace, '=' or quotes, or metrics other than sum, gauge and histogram, are left unchanged

title: Access logs: user-agent legend and dash-field removal
detail: nginx/Apache combined, IIS W3C and ALB lines repeat a 40-50 token user-agent plus '- -' and '"-"' placeholders. List the few distinct agents once in a legend and drop empty fields. Synthetic 20 lines: 1554 vs 838 o200k tokens.
test: Tokenise a real access log by column; build the legend; check the agent still answers top client agent and which paths returned 5xx.
because: user-agent legend for access logs
check: Combined-format access-log lines are rewritten with their user agent as a legend entry ('§k UA' once, then '§k' per line) and, when ident, user and referer are all '-', without those three placeholders; decode restores every byte, including lines with a real user or referer, malformed lines and text that already contains the sigil.

title: macOS log show and log stream: drop activity columns
detail: Default style prints thread hex, type, activity ID, PID, TTL and microsecond dates with offset per line. Render time, process, subsystem:category and message, with date and PID hoisted. Synthetic 20 lines: 1088 vs 459 o200k tokens.
test: Run log show --last 5m on a Mac; tokenise by column; compare against --style compact; confirm error-type lines keep subsystem and PID.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Each default-style log show line becomes 'time [E|F|I|D ]process[pid]: message' with date and zone in '# date' lines, a legend of unique pids, and the type letter and inline pid kept for Error and Fault lines; thread, activity and TTL columns are dropped, so every line's date, time, zone, type, pid, process and message (including its subsystem and category text) survive.
check_loses: the thread id, activity id and TTL columns of every line

title: Python traceback frames to path:line function form
detail: Rewrite 'File "p.py", line 212, in charge' as 'p.py:212 charge', dropping boilerplate words per frame; path text unchanged. Synthetic 3-frame trace: 100 vs 85 tokens. Differs from #56 and #118, which drop frames or source lines.
test: Collect 50 real tracebacks from pytest and scripts; rewrite with a regex; count tokens; ask the agent for failing file, line and function.
because: pure text rewrite of traceback frames
check: Each traceback line '<indent>File "path", line N, in func' becomes '<indent>@path:N func'; every other line, including SyntaxError locations without 'in', is untouched, and decode restores the exact original (text that already contains '@path:N func' lines is escaped).

title: Strip ephemeral client ports from log addresses
detail: Client addr:port in nginx error, Postgres, HAProxy, Java '/10.0.0.5:52814' and sshd ' port N' lines carries a dynamic-range port (32768+) that rarely matters. Drop it, keep listening ports. Synthetic 20 lines: 299 vs 239 tokens; skip when ports pair connections.
test: Apply to sshd and nginx samples; verify listening ports survive; ask which client IP failed most; count lines where the port was needed.
because: strip ephemeral ports; text transform

title: Decode JSON arrays of byte values to text
detail: journalctl -o json emits MESSAGE as an int array when text has ANSI or non-UTF-8 bytes; Node Buffer.toJSON gives {type:'Buffer',data:[...]}. Valid UTF-8 byte lists become strings. Synthetic 36-byte message: 77 vs 19 tokens. #325 and #619 cover base64 and bytes-repr only.
test: Log a colored line via a systemd unit, read journalctl -o json; decode; assert re-encoding reproduces the original bytes; tokenise before and after.
because: decodes byte-value arrays to text
check: A canonical compact array of 8+ byte values under "MESSAGE" or {"type":"Buffer","data":...} that is strict UTF-8 text becomes a sigil-prefixed JSON string; decode regenerates the exact array, so the original bytes come back. Arrays elsewhere, invalid UTF-8, binary-looking data and non-canonical spellings stay as numbers.

title: Flame graph SVG to folded stacks via rect nesting
detail: inferno, flamegraph.pl and py-spy SVGs store a rect (x, y, width, fill) plus title and text per frame. Rebuild stacks from y-depth and x-extent, emit 'a;b;c N' folded lines, then apply #422 and #423. #331 stubs SVG paths but ignores this.
test: Generate an SVG with inferno from a perf sample; convert; check totals match the original folded input; ask for the hottest leaf and its callers.
because: flame graph SVG to folded stacks, text
check: A flamegraph.pl/inferno SVG (normal or inverted) becomes folded stacks 'a;b;c N' rebuilt from the rect nesting (parent = the frame one row down whose x-extent holds the midpoint, self = samples minus children); the stack table reproduces the folded input the SVG was drawn from, and the total, hottest leaf, its callers, per-function self and inclusive samples are unchanged.
check_loses: colours, pixel geometry, the script, search and zoom machinery, percentages, the exact frame order inside a row beyond drawing order, and frames narrower than the generator's minimum width (their samples were already folded into the parent when the SVG was drawn); SVGs that are not well-formed XML, have titles that are not 'name (N samples, P%)', or names containing ';' are left unchanged

title: Delta and run-length encode metric value lists
detail: Monotonic counters and flat plateaus in matrix values and series arrays. Print counters as first value plus deltas and repeats as 'v x N'. Synthetic 60 counters: 239 vs 124 tokens; 60 plateau values: 119 vs 9. #420 only handles regular timestamps.
test: Query Prometheus counter series over 1h; encode; assert exact round trip; tokenise; ask peak delta and when values flatlined.
because: delta/run-length encodes metric lists
check: Canonical compact numeric arrays of 8+ items (bare or quoted), and Prometheus [[ts,"v"],...] matrices (as two series), are rewritten as first value plus signed deltas with 'x*N' runs, or as raw tokens with runs, whichever is shorter; decode rebuilds the exact array text, including quotes and decimals.

title: Windows Event XML to one flat key=value line
detail: Get-WinEvent ToXml and wevtutil /f:xml wrap events in Provider GUID, Correlation and Execution boilerplate plus <Data Name=...> tags. Emit time, channel, EventID, computer, then Name=value for non-dash data. Synthetic 4625 logon failure: 470 vs 73 tokens.
test: Export 30 Security events as XML; flatten; check EventData names and values survive via a parser diff; ask the failing username and source IP.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Each Windows event XML becomes one line with time, channel, EventID, computer, provider, the level when it is not 0 or 4, and Name=value for every Data or Binary element whose value is not '-' or empty (quoted when needed); parsing the original and the line gives the same time, channel, id, computer, provider, level and Name/value set, including the failing user and source IP of a 4625.
check_loses: provider GUID, Version, Task, Opcode, Keywords, EventRecordID, Correlation, Execution, the Security element and Data elements whose value is '-' or empty

title: gdb bt full: drop optimized-out and deep-frame locals
detail: bt full prints every local per frame; '<optimized out>' lines and locals of frames below the top few rarely help. Keep locals for the top 3 frames and app-code frames. Synthetic one frame: 92 vs 25 tokens. #426 only strips addresses.
test: Crash a debug C program and open its core; run bt full; filter; check the faulting variable stays; count tokens per frame.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Read Claude Code's built-in cache-break diagnosis labels
detail: Installed claude binary embeds a cache-break diagnoser with labels such as 'message history mutated at index', 'tools changed', 'effort changed', 'overage state changed (TTL flip expected)'. If surfaced in debug logs or telemetry, it classifies busts without a proxy or transcript heuristics.
test: Verify that claude --debug logs these labels: seed toggles (effort, MCP reconnect, CLAUDE.md edit), grep logs, compare with usage-field classification from #157.
because: Claude Code binary diagnoser labels

title: Probe segment-split and overage-sensitive cache TTL env vars
detail: Installed binary names CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL, CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGES_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL and FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M (semantics unverified); its diagnoser says 'overage state changed (TTL flip expected)'. If they split or pin TTL, pay 2x writes only on stable prefixes.
test: Verify that each variable changes usage.cache_creation ephemeral_5m versus ephemeral_1h in 3-turn claude -p runs; start a second session 10 minutes later and compare cache_read.
because: Claude Code environment variables

title: Inventory spare cache_control slots in real Claude Code requests
detail: The API allows four breakpoints per request. #283, #290, #431 and checkpoint ladders all want slots. Count how many Claude Code already uses on tools, system and messages, and where, before building any breakpoint-injecting proxy.
test: Log 50 requests from a normal session through a passthrough proxy; tally cache_control blocks, positions and TTL; report free slots and whether positions move each turn.
because: Anthropic cache_control slot inventory

title: Measure how much cache survives an edit deep in history
detail: #434 prices a stub as a suffix rewrite. But hits search only about 20 blocks back from a breakpoint, and Claude Code reportedly marks only tools, system and the tail, so a stub 40 blocks back may force rewriting all messages, changing the break-even.
test: Via a logging proxy, take a warm 100-block history, stub one tool_result at depths 5, 25 and 60 blocks back, and record cache_read and cache_creation on the next request.
because: Anthropic lookback window measurement

title: Cache checkpoints before big tool results for cheap later stubbing
detail: A proxy puts a spare cache_control breakpoint on the block just before each large tool_result when it first appears (should add no write tokens). Later, stubbing that result still reads the prefix before it at 0.1x. Needs free slots; keep the newest few.
test: Replay a 30-turn history through a proxy with and without checkpoints, stub the third-oldest big result, and compare next-request cache_read and cache_creation. Needs the depth probe first.
because: cache_control breakpoints

title: Stub history on forced prefix mutations, not just idle gaps
detail: A tool-list, system or model change already rewrites the cache from the changed point. A logging proxy detects the changed tools or system hash and runs the pending stub pass in that same request, when it costs no extra rewrite. Extends #434's cold-gap rule.
test: Replay recorded sessions with seeded toggles (MCP reconnect, model switch); count stub candidates fireable free on the toggle request versus waiting for an idle gap; price with #811's simulator.
because: proxy stubs history when prefix already mutated

title: Does a new user prompt rewrite earlier turns' cache?
detail: Anthropic docs reportedly say non-tool-result user messages strip earlier thinking blocks (newer models may keep them), which would change the prefix. A miss at prompt starts, but not in tool loops, would make prompt boundaries free rewrite windows for stubbing.
test: Over local transcripts, ratio cache_read to previous total, split by request type, model and thinking on/off, gaps under 300 seconds only; report the fraction below 0.8 per class.
because: Anthropic thinking-block stripping behaviour

title: Lint SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks for volatile bytes
detail: Hook additionalContext lands early in messages; timestamps, PIDs, random ids or unordered listings change the prefix every session, so cross-session cache sharing past that point never hits. Run each configured hook twice and diff the output.
test: Parse hooks from all settings layers and plugins, feed a saved sample payload twice five seconds apart, byte-diff additionalContext, then confirm via cache_read on two consecutive same-repo session starts.
because: lints SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hook output

title: Probe Claude Code's own context-management flag, not a proxy
detail: Installed binary lists a USE_API_CONTEXT_MANAGEMENT env flag and clear_tool_uses strings. If it sends context_management edits, #282's server-side clearing needs no proxy; check trigger, keep and exclude_tools defaults, and the effect on cache reads.
test: Verify that the flag exists: set it, run a 40-turn tool loop via a logging proxy, inspect requests for context_management and responses for applied_edits; compare cache tokens versus flag off.
because: probes Claude Code's internal flag and Anthropic API edit

title: Zlib-ratio gate sends repetitive Write content to generator scripts
detail: PreToolUse on Write measures compressibility of the content. Highly repetitive literal data (fixtures, enum tables, near-identical test cases) is denied with a hint to emit a short generator script instead, so output tokens fall from file size to script size.
test: Replay Write inputs from transcripts, compute zlib ratio, count files above 3x and 2 KB; hand-write generators for five and compare o200k token counts.
because: PreToolUse deny on Write

title: Steer new-file Writes to cp plus Edit of a sibling
detail: PreToolUse on Write to a new path finds the most similar tracked file (difflib ratio 0.7+) and denies with 'cp SIBLING NEW, then Edit the differing lines'. Output-side twin of #909; targets config variants, locale files, parallel test files.
test: For new-file Writes in transcripts, compute best difflib ratio against git ls-files at that commit; sum tokens saved if replaced by cp plus the diff hunks.
because: PreToolUse deny on Write

title: Normalise-then-match healing of failed Edit anchors
detail: When old_string is absent verbatim but matches exactly once after normalising tabs versus spaces, trailing whitespace, CRLF, curly quotes or leaked cat -n prefixes, PreToolUse rewrites it to the file's real text, skipping the failed turn and retry. Cousin of #780.
test: Mine 'string to replace not found' errors in transcripts; replay old_string against the file as it was; report heal rate and false-unique rate.
because: PreToolUse rewrite of Edit input

title: Offload counting, sorting and diffing from reasoning to commands
detail: Thinking and prose burn output tokens on mechanical work: counting matches, comparing lists, summing, date arithmetic. A steering line with examples (wc, sort, comm, python -c) swaps long reasoning chains for one short call and removes arithmetic slips.
test: Build 20 mechanical tasks (diff two 40-item lists, count occurrences); compare billed output tokens and correctness with and without the line.
because: steering advice on offloading work to commands

title: Assistant prose redundancy: echoed tool results and repeated drafts
detail: Agents restate output before the next call ('The output shows...') and re-emit whole tables, drafts or plans with small changes. Measure n-gram overlap with the preceding tool_result and 70%+ line overlap with earlier assistant blocks; sizes don't-restate and changed-lines-only rules.
test: Script over ~/.claude/projects jsonl: 5-gram overlap per text block plus difflib against earlier blocks; sum o200k tokens of overlapped spans as a share of assistant text.
because: measures assistant prose redundancy

title: Closed-loop narration governor via PostToolUse feedback
detail: A hook reads the last assistant text from transcript_path; if it exceeded a prose budget before a tool call, PostToolUse additionalContext adds a one-line nudge. Static terse rules may decay over long sessions; feedback re-anchors them for roughly 15 tokens.
test: Replay-run the same task set with the static rule versus the governor; compare assistant prose tokens per turn, net of nudge tokens.
because: PostToolUse hook and transcript_path

title: Deny new report-style markdown files at Write
detail: PreToolUse denies Write of new SUMMARY, REPORT, NOTES, ANALYSIS, FINDINGS or PLAN markdown or text files unless the user's prompt asked for a document. Each costs hundreds of output tokens and tends to be re-read later.
test: Grep transcripts for Write file_path matching those names; sum content tokens and count how many the user prompt actually requested.
because: PreToolUse deny on Write

title: Delegate bulk code generation to a cheaper model, file-out
detail: Main model writes a five-line spec; a Haiku subagent generates boilerplate (tests, fixtures, docs, CRUD) straight to disk and returns only path plus test status. Premium output shrinks to the spec. Differs from routing read-only work to Haiku (#692).
test: Take five large past Write calls; regenerate from specs with Haiku; compare billed cost including spec and review turn, and whether tests pass.
because: Haiku subagent delegation

title: Batch independent Edits into one assistant message
detail: Chains of single-Edit turns each pay a thinking block, narration and a full cache read of the context. Steering, or a nudge, to emit independent Edits in parallel in one message removes those per-turn costs. Edit-side sibling of #213.
test: Count consecutive assistant messages holding one Edit to different files with no dependency; price saved turns as cache-read context plus output overhead.
because: advice on batching edits

title: Short alias keys for built-in tool parameters via proxy
detail: A proxy renames file_path, old_string, new_string, run_in_background and output_mode to shorter aliases in the tools array and translates tool_use back in the stream. Keys recur in every call and history copy; the per-key saving may be only a token or two.
test: Tokenise parameter keys across transcript tool_use blocks and sum the possible saving; run a small tool-call accuracy suite with aliases.
because: proxy aliases tool parameter keys deterministically

title: Denser reasoning language test: Chinese or symbolic shorthand
detail: Test whether instructing narration or reasoning in a denser notation (Chinese, arrows, logic symbols) cuts billed output per solved task on Claude's tokenizer. Targets output language; related ideas cover input rule rewrites (#1147) and draft length (#833).
test: Translate 30 narration paragraphs, compare count_tokens per version; drop the idea if under 25% fewer tokens, else run a small task A/B.
because: steers model reasoning language

title: Score the short tail window unpadded, not padded to 510
detail: atom_scores pads every window in a 16-window batch to the widest, so a short remainder window (can be tens of tokens) is computed at full 510 width. Run it as its own call, or bucket widths 64/128/256/512. Input text is unchanged.
test: Count real versus padded tokens on 50 saved outputs; time batched versus tail-separate runs; assert probabilities match within int8 noise (#378).
because: speed-only batching change, output unchanged
check: Running a batch in width buckets (each padded to its widest real row) gives atom scores and token counts identical to the real atom_scores on a padding-invariant fake scorer, for 30 outputs and edge cases (tiny windows, oversized atom, CJK, empty), at never more padded compute; int8 noise on the real model cannot be tested offline.

title: Pool windows across documents into shared ORT batches
detail: compress_documents, the LlamaIndex postprocessor and serve 'texts' call compress() once per text, so each 300-token chunk runs as a batch of one. Add compress_many: atomize all, sort windows by length, fill 16-window batches. Unlike #839 this is one sequential caller.
test: Time 20 retrieved 300-token chunks per-document versus pooled on 4 cores; assert identical kept text within int8 noise; report windows per ORT call.
because: speed-only batching change, output unchanged
check: compress_many (plan all texts, sort all windows by length, fill batches across documents, then the real compress per document) gives scores and kept text identical to compressing each document alone, in any order and for every compress mode, with a fraction of the ORT calls and a fallback to batches of one; wall-clock time needs the real model.

title: Confidence-gated cascade: cheap scorer first, transformer for uncertain windows
detail: Run a hashed-feature or IDF scorer (#263, #774) over every window; send only windows with atoms in an uncertain band to ORT and reuse cheap decisions elsewhere. The transformer stays authoritative; target is giant boilerplate-heavy logs.
test: On saved logs over 50 KB, measure the share of windows the cheap scorer settles; compare kept-atom overlap with all-ORT scoring at 0.5, plus latency.
because: local two-stage scorer, deterministic on text

title: Memory-mapped ORT external-data weights shared across hook processes
detail: Parallel tool calls spawn parallel hook processes, each reading 143 MB into private memory. Saving initializers as ONNX external data lets ORT reportedly memory-map them, sharing page cache and cutting load time and RSS with the graph unchanged. Differs from #456.
test: Verify that ORT memory-maps external data: export it, start 4 concurrent Compressors, compare summed PSS and session-creation time against the single-file model; assert identical logits.
because: local ONNX weight mmap, model-internal
