check: A stand-in model whose weights sit in a separate read-only mmap'ed file gives bit-identical logits to the single-file build, three real processes mapping it have a summed PSS of about one copy instead of three, session creation copies nothing up front, and a missing, truncated, empty, wrong-content or unmappable file falls back to the single-file model with equal logits.

title: PreToolUse warm-up: load the model while the command runs
detail: A PreToolUse hook sees the command before it runs. For likely-large ones (test suites, installs, docker logs, find, gh api) it starts a detached warm-up or serve, so the ~2 s load overlaps tool runtime. Cheap commands trigger nothing.
test: From transcripts, label commands whose output exceeded 6,000 chars; score a command-prefix predictor's precision and recall; compare tool duration_ms with load time.
because: needs PreToolUse hook event for warm-up

title: Authenticate serve: unix socket or token against port squatting
detail: hook._compress trusts any process answering on 127.0.0.1:8719 and substitutes its text for the tool output. On shared hosts another user can bind that port first and inject content into the agent's context. Use a 0700 socket or 0600 token; #379's fingerprint is spoofable.
test: As a second user, bind 8719 with a stub returning canary text; assert the hook accepts it today and rejects it after socket or token auth.
because: serve authentication in local process

title: Cancel abandoned serve work when the hook client disconnects
detail: After a hook timeout or kill, serve keeps scoring the abandoned request under its global lock, so later small requests queue behind it. Poll the client socket between ORT batches and drop the remaining windows. Differs from #839's scheduling.
test: Send a 2 MB request, close the socket after 1 s, then a small one; compare small-request latency and CPU use with and without cancellation polling.
because: local serve scheduling on client disconnect
check: Polling the client socket between batches drops the remaining windows of an abandoned 2 MB request (small-request latency 30 s to 0.5 s, rows scored 1002 to 34), a cancelled request's partial result is never cached and a retry is computed in full, and a connected client, a late close or a failing probe change nothing.

title: Derive ORT threads and memory guard from cgroup limits
detail: compress.py leaves intra-op threads at ORT defaults. In containers and cloud sandboxes the visible core count can exceed the cpu.max quota or affinity mask, risking oversubscription, and a low memory.max could kill the load silently. Read sched_getaffinity, cpu.max, memory.max first.
test: In docker --cpus=2 --memory=1g on a larger host, time 100 windows with default versus derived thread counts; record whether session creation gets OOM-killed.
because: local ORT thread and memory tuning
check: Intra-op threads become min(affinity, floor(cpu quota)) (at least 1) and the memory guard refuses an in-process load that would not fit, parsed from sample cgroup v2, v1 and hybrid files including 'max', -1, the v1 LONG_MAX sentinel, zero periods, garbage and nested cgroups (tightest ancestor wins); with no limits nothing is reduced and unreadable files fall back to the affinity mask.

title: Re-export with fused or banded attention, not eager opset 17
detail: export_onnx.py forces eager attention, opset 17, dynamo off, so ORT may run dense 512x512 attention even if mmBERT keeps ModernBERT's local-window layers (reportedly). Try SDPA export, ORT transformer-optimizer fusions or the opset 23 Attention op, then re-quantize.
test: Export each variant and rerun the script's parity and ms_per_chunk report; require keep agreement near the current int8 build and lower latency at 512 tokens.
because: local model export speed work, output unchanged

title: ORT per-op profile of the int8 graph before optimising
detail: Speed ideas (#836, #561, #929, #455) assume where time goes: activation quantisation, MatMulInteger, embedding Gather, softmax or Python glue. Run ORT profiling on one 16x512 batch and rank ops so sweeps target the real bottleneck.
test: Profile one batch of saved windows; sum time per op_type; compare with numpy and Python glue time per window; record the top five ops.
because: ORT profiling of local model

title: Reuse hook-time atom ranks to shrink aged results without ORT
detail: Hook scores are paid for once. With stored ranks (#562), a proxy or compaction step at a cold-cache boundary (#630) can re-render results older than N turns at 0.25 instead of 0.5, with no model call. Mirror of expansion.
test: Store ranks for 30 hook outputs; simulate shrinking those older than 10 turns from 0.5 to 0.25; count tokens saved and ask questions about old results.
because: re-renders aged results from stored local scores

title: Mine host-persisted tool-results files as the large-output corpus
detail: The host diverts oversized results to tool-results/*.txt; the transcript keeps a pointer (seen in subagent logs here), so JSONL-only mining misses the biggest outputs. Locally: 101 such files, 5.4 MB, all mode 0644 versus 0600 transcripts. Join by pointer path; treat as raw and sensitive.
test: Count transcript pointers, join to files, compare the size histogram with a JSONL-only corpus, check whether files hold pre-hook text, and report file modes.
because: host-persisted tool-results file layout

title: Mirror content-free digests before host transcript retention purge
detail: Claude Code reportedly deletes old transcripts after cleanupPeriodDays (default about 30). Every ledger, replay, drift (#469) and difference-in-differences (#656) idea built on ~/.claude/projects silently loses history. A Stop hook appends a text-free digest (sizes, families, usage, hashes) to ctxprune's own store.
test: Verify that the retention key exists: check oldest transcript mtime and the setting in each settings layer; after a simulated purge, check digests reproduce ledger totals for three sessions.
because: Stop hook and Claude Code transcript retention

title: Per-install HMAC pseudonyms for cross-session path and repo joins
detail: Analytics like the orientation re-read census (#689) must recognise the same path across sessions. Store HMAC(install key, path, host or repo) instead of names; deleting the key unlinks all history. Differs from per-document random fill (#465).
test: Compute the re-read census with raw paths and with HMAC ids and assert identical counts; grep the store for path substrings; rotate the key and confirm joins break.
because: privacy-preserving analytics pseudonyms

title: Hash-assigned train/dev/test splits stable under growth and purge
detail: Seeded random splits reshuffle whenever rows are added or a session is purged, leaking old test rows into train. Assign each near-duplicate cluster (#472) to a split by HMAC(cluster id) modulo 100, so membership never changes across rebuilds.
test: Build the corpus at week 1 and week 4 with 10 percent of sessions purged; count surviving rows that changed split, seeded shuffle versus hash assignment.
because: stable eval split assignment

title: Exclude corpus rows by tool-call path before content scan
detail: Secret regexes (#370) miss confidential prose. Gate on the call instead: Read or cat of .env, *.pem, id_rsa, .aws/credentials, .npmrc, kubeconfig, or repos with a private remote are never admitted, whatever the content scan says.
test: Over local transcripts count Bash and Read calls matching the denylist; run a gitleaks-style scan on their outputs; report rows only the path rule caught, plus false exclusions.
because: corpus admission gating by tool-call path

title: Scrub the conditioning side: commands and prompts in corpus rows
detail: Command-conditioned training (#166) and query boosts store the command and last user prompt beside the output. Commands carry tokens in curl headers, connection strings and -p flags; prompts carry names. Keep argv shape (flags, value classes) and keyword-overlap features, not text.
test: Scan local Bash commands and user prompts with the secret scanner; count hits absent from outputs; compare classifier AUC under raw versus argv-shape conditioning.
because: corpus scrubbing of commands and prompts

title: Append-atomic content-free ledger with schema-allowlist lint
detail: Parallel tool calls can fire several hook processes at once (#237). Write one sub-PIPE_BUF JSON line per event with O_APPEND and no lock; CI lints that the schema holds only numeric, enum and hash fields, so free text cannot creep into analytics.
test: Spawn 16 hook processes writing 1,000 records each and assert 16,000 parseable lines; add a free-text field and assert the lint fails.
because: content-free ledger with schema lint

title: Run-length kept-mask per call for positional deletion profile
detail: Log each call's keep decisions as a run-length mask with no text. Aggregate deletion rate by relative position and line index per command family, to see whether tails, where summaries and exit lines sit, are over-deleted. Differs from class counters (#467).
test: Replay 100 saved outputs through the compressor, store masks, and plot kept rate per position decile per family; flag families whose last-decile keep rate falls below the mean.
because: positional deletion profile analysis

title: Wrapper shell functions captured by Claude Code's shell snapshot
detail: Claude Code's shell snapshot holds rc-defined functions and aliases (checked here: nvm, rbenv) and is reportedly sourced per Bash call. Define git, gh and pytest functions that filter only when stdout is a pipe, keeping PIPESTATUS. No PATH shims or SHELL override.
test: Verify that rc functions reach the Bash tool: put a gh() filter function in ~/.bashrc, restart; compare exit status and bytes versus plain gh.
because: Claude Code shell snapshot mechanism

title: AGENTS.md pipe recipe masks failing exit codes
detail: The recipe 'some_command 2>&1 | ctxprune' returns ctxprune's status, so a failing build reads as success (checked: 'false | cat' gives 0, with pipefail gives 1). Document 'set -o pipefail', or add a 'ctxprune run -- cmd' wrapper that exits with the command's status.
test: Pipe a failing pytest through the recipe in claude -p with and without pipefail; check whether the agent reports failure and whether Claude Code prints an exit-code line.
because: run wrapper preserving exit status; shell-level

title: Drop runner-generated boilerplate annotations from check runs
detail: Each job gets generic annotations such as 'Process completed with exit code 1.' and, reportedly, Node.js-deprecation or set-output warnings, repeated across legs and runs. Drop a known-text list from check-run annotations and get_check_run output; keep annotations that carry file and line.
test: Fetch annotations for 20 failed runs via gh api; count the share matching the list; check no annotation with a path or line is dropped.
because: drops known boilerplate from MCP tool result

title: Strip echoed step script and env block from failing step
detail: After failed-only fetches (#477) or passing-step folding (#311), the remaining failing step still opens with the echoed Run script, env: block and shell: line, often duplicating the workflow YAML. Replace with step name and a pointer; original stays saved.
test: Take 10 failed-step logs; measure tokens in the Run header and env echo; strip; ask for root cause versus raw; check no env value needed for diagnosis is lost.
because: pure text transform on CI log output

title: Fold empty-body COMMENTED reviews in get_reviews output
detail: Each single inline comment on a PR creates a review with state COMMENTED and empty body, so review lists carry many metadata-only entries with full user objects. Fold to a count per author; keep reviews with a body, APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED.
test: Fetch reviews for 15 PRs with inline comments via pull_request_read; count empty COMMENTED entries and their tokens; confirm the review-comments call still returns the comment text.
because: folds metadata-only entries in MCP tool result

title: Fold release asset arrays to names and sizes
detail: list_releases and release JSON carry assets[] per release: one object per binary, checksum and signature, each with an uploader user object and URLs. Fold to name and size with a hoisted shared prefix; drop download counts and uploader. Original saved.
test: Capture list_releases for five projects with many assets; tokenise the assets share; fold; ask which asset fits linux-arm64 and its size, versus raw.
because: folds JSON arrays in MCP tool result

title: Composite Action: cache model, start serve, upload originals
detail: Ephemeral runners re-download the 143 MB model and lose saved originals when headless Claude Code runs in CI. A setup action restores the Hugging Face cache by revision, starts ctxprune serve, and uploads the outputs directory as an artifact (private repos only; may hold secrets).
test: In a scratch repo, run a hook-enabled claude -p job with and without the cache step; compare hook latency, download time and whether originals are retrievable afterwards.
because: CI packaging recipe, not a token transform

title: MCP wrap conformance suite: capabilities, progress, cancellation passthrough
detail: A stdio proxy that rewrites results must forward everything else unchanged: initialize capabilities, tools/list cursors, list_changed, progress, cancellation, resources, prompts, sampling and isError flags. Diff scripted-client transcripts of the wrapped and unwrapped server.
test: Drive a reference server directly and through the MCP stdio proxy (#188) with one scripted client; diff every JSON-RPC message except tools/call text blocks over the threshold.
because: MCP wrapper conformance suite

title: Compress BashOutput background-shell polls via id-to-command map
detail: run() returns for any tool but Bash, so polls of background shells (dev servers, watchers, long tests) pass raw. Record shell id to command at the originating Bash call, then apply the verbatim skip and compression to polls. Tool name reportedly varies by version.
test: Verify that polls reach PostToolUse: start a build with run_in_background, poll it, dump the event (tool_name, response shape, missing command); compress a 20k-char poll and diff tokens.
because: shell-id to command map from payload history

title: Shrink AGENTS self-check fixture and make it pre-pass-proof
detail: The AGENTS check prints one 76-char sentence 120 times (9,120 chars) just to trigger the hook; 80 repeats (6,080) clears the threshold. Being pure repetition, it would silently stop showing the note once a repeat-collapse pre-pass exists. Use non-repeating generated words.
test: Run both fixtures through hook.run with the real model: confirm the note appears for each at default threshold and count output chars; rerun after any repeat-collapse rule is added.
because: docs self-check fixture for AGENTS.md

title: Project-vocabulary protect list from repo symbols and filenames
detail: Verified here: is_protected is false for validate, Config, Users, handler, render, timeout and localhost. Plain lowercase or Capitalized names the agent will grep for stay deletable. Build a cached per-repo set (git ls-files basenames, ctags symbols) and force-keep matches.
test: On saved outputs from one repo, count droppable atoms found in the symbol set; compress at 0.5 and count how many are deleted; compare byte cost of keeping them.
because: vocabulary from payload identifiers would do; repo listing host-only

title: ctxprune launcher: per-session settings overlay, env and serve
detail: A wrapper runs claude --settings with the hook JSON (flag present in local claude --help), sets CTXPRUNE_* in the process environment so knobs surely reach hooks, starts serve for the session and stops it on exit. Nothing persistent to uninstall.
test: Verify that --settings accepts hooks: launch via the wrapper with CTXPRUNE_RATE=0.3, run a 20k-char command; confirm the note shows a 0.3 ratio, serve answered, and settings.json is byte-unchanged.
because: claude --settings launcher overlay

title: Install flags bake rate and threshold into hook command
detail: ctxprune hook accepts only the agent name; tuning is env-only. Let install take --keep and --min-chars and write them as argv in the settings command. Reaches hooks however Claude Code was launched, and project scope can share tuned values with a team.
test: Install with --keep 0.3 --min-chars 8000, launch Claude Code from a GUI without shell exports; run 7k and 20k-char outputs; confirm only the 20k one is compressed at 0.3.
because: bakes options into settings.json hook command

title: Did-you-mean paths on ENOENT misses to save retry turns
detail: When a Bash or Read call fails with No such file, a failure hook appends up to three nearest git ls-files paths by edit distance. Prior art: thefuck and git help.autocorrect. Saves the find/ls detour turns, not output bytes.
test: Verify that PostToolUseFailure additionalContext reaches the model. Replay transcripts: count ENOENT results followed within two calls by find, ls or rg; check the later-used path's edit distance.
because: failure hook plus host git ls-files lookup

title: Package inventory dumps: direct dependencies plus a transitive count
detail: pip list, npm ls --all, cargo tree, go list -m all, gem list and brew list print hundreds of rows (300 synthetic pip-list rows: 3.3k o200k tokens). Keep manifest-direct packages and ones named in the command or prompt; fold the rest to a count.
test: Capture in two real repos; ask a reader for versions of direct and transitive packages, folded versus raw.
because: fold inventory rows; manifest optional, command/prompt keys suffice

title: Drop man-page and --help footers: AUTHORS, COPYRIGHT, SEE ALSO
detail: Section triage for man output keeps NAME, SYNOPSIS, OPTIONS, EXAMPLES and drops AUTHOR, COPYRIGHT, SEE ALSO, REPORTING BUGS. Same for --help footers such as coreutils 'online help' and 'Full documentation' lines. tldr-pages is an alternative source of examples.
test: Render 20 common man pages with col -bx; measure o200k tokens in dropped sections; confirm no flag description sits under those headings.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Silence shell-startup and env-manager chatter in command output
detail: direnv documents DIRENV_LOG_FORMAT= to silence its loading and export lines; nvm, pyenv, conda activate and rc-file banners can also print into the persistent shell. First prove they appear in results, then set variables in settings env or strip their fixed line shapes.
test: Grep transcripts for lines starting 'direnv:', 'Now using node', '(base)'; run a no-op Bash call; if nonempty, set vars and compare token counts.
because: env vars or stripping fixed banner lines
check: A command that changes directory or sources a file gets DIRENV_LOG_FORMAT='' (an empty value is written as '' and a value the user set, even an empty one, is kept), 'nvm use' gets '--silent'; explicit direnv commands are not touched; the sim asserts that nvm's 'Now using node' line, which names the active version, is the one piece of content this drops.

title: Pin LC_ALL and LANGUAGE so tool diagnostics print in English
detail: On non-English systems git, gcc, pip and apt print translated messages. A hand-translated sample git fatal line cost 16 o200k tokens in English versus 23 German, 27 Russian, 30 Japanese. Pin the locale in launch env, keeping UTF-8 so filenames survive.
test: Run git, gcc, apt under LC_ALL=de_DE.UTF-8 and C.UTF-8; count tokens on real messages; verify filenames with accents still print correctly.
because: locale env pinned via command prefix
check: Commands that run git, gcc, make, pip or apt get 'export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 LANGUAGE=en;' so a gettext tool prints its English message (fewer tokens than de, ru or ja) in a UTF-8 charset; the pair is skipped whenever the user set LC_ALL, LANGUAGE or LC_MESSAGES.

title: Docker config.json psFormat and imagesFormat as source-side column trim
detail: Docker's client config.json accepts psFormat and imagesFormat templates, so plain docker ps and docker images can drop COMMAND, CREATED and ID columns with no command rewriting. Names stay usable for logs and exec. Source-side, unlike post-hoc column dropping (#57).
test: Set psFormat on a host with 30 containers; compare o200k tokens of docker ps -a before and after; confirm the agent still runs logs and exec by name.
because: docker client config, no agent harness feature

title: Adapters: Pydantic AI, OpenAI Agents SDK, Vercel AI SDK
detail: Reportedly each has a pre-model message hook: Pydantic AI history_processors, OpenAI Agents SDK call_model_input_filter, Vercel AI SDK toModelOutput and prepareStep. Wrap prune() there, as the LangChain item does, so non-Claude-Code agents get the same savings.
test: Verify that each hook name exists in the installed package versions; run one 20-turn tool loop per framework with and without the adapter and compare provider-reported input tokens.
because: per-framework hook adapters

title: Per-turn growth slope of a no-op chat exposes re-injected context
detail: A claude-code GitHub issue (number 50998, reportedly) shows attachments re-sent every turn, growing payload linearly. Send N trivial prompts, subtract new-message tokens from input_tokens plus cache reads; any positive residual slope is re-injection. Complements the first-request baseline (#968).
test: Run 10 'reply ok' turns through the logging proxy per Claude Code version; regress total input tokens on turn index; flag slopes beyond the typed text.
because: generic no-op chat growth-slope measurement

title: Canary for harness-induced duplicate tool executions
detail: A claude-code GitHub issue (number 41750, per its title) reports all tool calls executing twice when context management fired with empty edits. Flag adjacent identical tool_use inputs with near-equal timestamps; duplicate side effects and outputs both cost tokens.
test: Scan local transcripts for consecutive identical Bash inputs under two seconds apart, excluding model-issued retries; report rate per Claude Code version.
because: duplicate tool_use detection analysis

title: Security-group, NACL and firewall rules to one-liners
detail: aws ec2 describe-security-groups prints each rule as an object with empty Ipv6Ranges, PrefixListIds and UserIdGroupPairs arrays. Rewrite to 'tcp 443 10.0.0.0/8' lines; same for NACLs, route tables, gcloud firewall-rules. Synthetic 3-rule group: 313 vs 67 o200k tokens.
test: Capture describe-security-groups, describe-network-acls and gcloud firewall-rules list --format=json from a real account; check every rule's protocol, ports, CIDR and source group survive the digest.
because: pure text rewrite of JSON tool output

title: docker compose config: re-shorten long-form ports and volumes
detail: docker compose config expands ports, volumes and depends_on to long form (mode, target, published, protocol, create_host_path, condition, required). Rewrite to short syntax when no non-default sub-field exists, else keep long form. Synthetic service: 141 vs 67 o200k tokens.
test: Run compose config on 5 real projects; feed each shortened output back through compose config and diff the resolved model against the original; compare tokens.
because: re-shortens compose long-form syntax
check: In docker compose config output, long-form ports (mode ingress, protocol tcp/udp, optional IPv4 host_ip), bind and named-volume mounts (default bind/volume options only, optional read_only) and depends_on entries with the default condition become short syntax; any item with a non-default sub-field (mode host, propagation, nocopy, tmpfs, condition service_healthy) stays in long form, and the resolved model is the same.
check_loses: long-form defaults that short syntax implies: mode: ingress, protocol: tcp, create_host_path: true, an empty volume: {}, condition: service_started and required: true

title: Digest cloud CLI debug traces: kubectl -v, aws --debug, TF_LOG
detail: Agents add kubectl -v=6/8, aws --debug, az --debug or TF_LOG=debug when stuck. Keep each request line with status and latency, the final error and auth or retry events; fold discovery GET storms and header or body dumps to counts. Original saved.
test: Run kubectl get pods -v=8 and aws s3 ls --debug against kind and localstack; compare tokens and confirm an injected failure's status and message survive.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: For kubectl -v=8 output, each request becomes one 'time METHOD url -> status in Nms' line, header dumps and 2xx bodies are dropped, the request and response bodies and the final error of a failed request stay verbatim, and runs of three or more discovery GETs become one count line; for aws --debug, requests become one digest line while HTTP status lines, credential and retry events, the failed response body, tracebacks and the final error stay verbatim and hook, loader and signing noise becomes one count line.
check_loses: request and response headers, 2xx response bodies, per-request detail of discovery GETs, the botocore signing, hook and loader records and 'No retry needed' lines; TF_LOG output is not handled

title: IaC synth output: strip CDK path metadata and asset hashes
detail: cdk synth and cdk diff print CloudFormation with Metadata aws:cdk:path per resource, a CDKMetadata resource, 64-hex asset S3Keys and 8-hex logical-ID suffixes. Drop metadata, alias hashes with a legend; try the same for sam, serverless package, pulumi preview.
test: Synthesize a small CDK app with Lambda, S3 and IAM; measure tokens by field class and whether a reader can still map diff entries to construct paths.
because: pure text transform on tool output

title: Cross-document label legend for helm template and kustomize
detail: Each rendered resource repeats the same helm.sh/chart and app.kubernetes.io/* label set in metadata, selector and pod template. YAML anchors (#792) cannot cross --- boundaries, so emit a one-time legend 'L1={...}' and reference it per document. Reversible.
test: Run helm template on 3 popular charts with 10-30 resources; count label-line tokens, then ask a reader which resources carry a given label from the legended form.
because: label legend on YAML text, deterministic
check: Label/annotation blocks of 2+ lines that recur across the YAML documents of helm template or kustomize output (at any indent) are defined once in a legend and referenced by a one-line §L<id>; decode restores the input byte for byte, including CRLF files and lines that already start with the sigil.

title: Ansible setup facts: keep a curated subset
detail: ansible -m setup and gather_facts debug output dump hundreds of ansible_facts keys (env, mounts, devices, ssh host keys, python, interfaces). Keep distribution, kernel, CPU, memory, default IPs and keys named in the command; fold the rest to key names and sizes. Original saved.
test: Run ansible -m setup on a container host and a VM; measure tokens by top-level key; check 10 questions about OS, memory and IP remain answerable.
because: pure text transform on tool output
check: Keeps the distribution, kernel, CPU, memory, default-IP and similar facts verbatim and folds every other fact value over 40 characters of JSON to a '<folded dict, 38 keys, 2412 chars>' placeholder, so every fact name stays and the OS, memory and IP questions are answered from the same values.
check_loses: the values of environment variables, mounts, devices, interface features, ssh host keys, python and date facts (the original is saved); only their names, types and sizes remain

title: Ansible env defaults: hide ok and skipped hosts, deprecations
detail: Launch env ANSIBLE_DISPLAY_OK_HOSTS=false, ANSIBLE_DISPLAY_SKIPPED_HOSTS=false, ANSIBLE_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS=false and ANSIBLE_LOCALHOST_WARNING=false drop per-host ok lines at the source; changed, failed, unreachable and PLAY RECAP stay. Source-side counterpart of #318.
test: Verify that the env is honored: run one playbook over 20 containers with and without it; compare bytes and confirm changed, failed, unreachable and recap lines are identical.
because: ansible env defaults as command prefix

title: kubectl diff and helm diff: fold generation and last-applied churn
detail: Diffs against live objects show a bumped metadata.generation and a rewritten last-applied-configuration annotation beside the real change. Fold only these known non-semantic hunks to one line; keep spec hunks and every destroy or replace line, respecting #1120.
test: Change one Deployment image on a kind cluster; run kubectl diff; count tokens in churn lines versus the spec hunk, then verify the spec hunk is untouched.
because: pure text transform on diff output

title: Terraform plan count/for_each siblings: delta against first instance
detail: A count or for_each resource prints one near-identical block per index. Print the first block in full, then each sibling as only its differing attributes. Synthetic 3 instances: 354 vs 96 o200k tokens; gap grows with N. Text-plan cousin of #265 and #898.
test: Plan a module with count=20 instances and a for_each subnet map; verify a reader can reconstruct each instance's attributes from the delta form.
because: delta terraform sibling blocks
check: For count and for_each resources the first block of a family is printed in full and each later 'will be created' sibling with the same attribute names keeps its header and only the attribute chunks whose text differs, behind a '# as <first address>, except:' line; every instance's full attribute set can be rebuilt from the delta form, and siblings with a different attribute set or action stay in full.
check_loses: nothing a reader cannot rebuild, except the position of the unchanged attributes inside a sibling (they are implied by the first block)

title: Kind-aware healthy-row fold for any kubectl get table
detail: #793 folds pods only. Parse column tables for deployments (READY a/a), PVC Bound, jobs Complete, certificates Ready True, nodes Ready, plus argocd and flux rows Synced/Healthy; fold all-healthy rows to counts with name stems and keep any abnormal row verbatim.
test: Capture get all -A, get pvc,job,node -A and argocd app list on a populated cluster; check no row with a non-healthy status column is folded.
because: pure text transform on table output

title: Suppress stock cluster objects in kubectl listings
detail: Fresh clusters ship dozens of stock objects: system:* ClusterRoles and bindings, kube-root-ca.crt ConfigMaps per namespace, default ServiceAccounts, kube-public. Fold names matching a shipped stock list to 'N stock objects' and keep anything else; EKS, GKE and kind need separate lists.
test: Run kubectl get clusterrole,clusterrolebinding,cm,sa -A on kind, EKS and GKE clusters; count rows matched by the stock list and check custom near-name objects survive.
because: pure text transform on listing output

title: Drop derivable selfLink, kind and fingerprint from gcloud, az
detail: gcloud compute describe YAML carries selfLink (a URL rebuilt from project, zone, name), kind: compute#..., fingerprint and labelFingerprint; az show repeats subscription and resource group inside id beside separate fields. A per-API derivable-field table drops them. Bash-side counterpart of MCP #131.
test: Run gcloud compute instances describe and az vm show on one resource; count tokens in the listed fields; confirm they can be rebuilt from the kept fields.
because: derivable-field table drop on CLI output

title: Drop redundant xmlns redeclarations on child elements
detail: .NET XmlSerializer and SOAP stacks can repeat the same default xmlns on every nested element. Remove declarations that equal the in-scope binding; the infoset is unchanged. Synthetic 10 orders, three redeclarations each: 580 vs 280 o200k tokens.
test: Canonicalise (C14N) before and after with lxml and compare bytes; count tokens on a captured SOAP response or WSDL-generated client log.
because: drops redundant xmlns redeclarations
check: An xmlns or xmlns:prefix declaration whose non-empty value equals the binding already in scope is removed from the start tag (the scope stack is rebuilt per element); every other byte, including comments, CDATA, text and attribute layout, is kept, and the parsed infoset (element and attribute names, in-scope namespace map of every element, text, comments) of both texts is identical.
check_loses: redundant namespace declarations only (they are not part of the infoset); documents with a DOCTYPE or that are not well-formed are left untouched

title: Peel SOAP envelopes and prefix noise from XML reads
detail: When no Fault is present, drop soap:Envelope, empty Header and Body wrappers and ns2:-style prefixes, printing the prefix-URI map once. Synthetic 5 responses: 326 vs 141 o200k tokens. Differs from #40 report stripping and #525 whitespace.
test: Run against saved SOAP captures and a Fault case; check a reader answers field-lookup questions equally and Faults pass through untouched.
because: peels SOAP envelope noise from XML text

title: Render XSD and WSDL as type-signature lines
detail: xs:element, complexType and wsdl:message markup repeats name, type and minOccurs attributes with closing tags. Emit 'Order { id: int, total?: decimal }' and 'op GetOrder(req) -> resp' lines, like #521 does for GraphQL and JSON Schema.
test: Convert a public WSDL with xsd imports, count o200k tokens both ways, then ask a reader which fields are optional or repeated.
because: XSD/WSDL to signature lines, text transform

title: Column-oriented dict-of-dicts (pandas to_json) to table
detail: df.to_json() and df.to_dict() default to {column: {index: value}}, repeating every index key in every column. When all columns share one index key set, emit TSV with an index column. Synthetic 3 columns x 40 rows: 527 vs 245 o200k tokens.
test: Round-trip with pandas.read_json(orient='columns') versus parsing the TSV; compare frames. Also handle the Python repr form with int index keys.
because: dict-of-dicts JSON to TSV table
check: A pandas {column: {index: value}} document (compact JSON, or the Python repr with ', ' and ': ') in which every column has the same ordered index keys becomes a TSV with an index column and raw cell lexemes; decode rebuilds the exact original text, including a trailing newline, null, escaped strings and nan.

title: Group sorted dotted-key listings by shared prefix
detail: git config -l, Spring env and configprops, .properties and flat_settings print the full dotted prefix on every line. Emit 'prefix: leaf=v leaf=v' blocks, exceptions inline. Synthetic: Spring keys 111 vs 83, git config 446 vs 407 o200k tokens. Generalises #516.
test: Invert the grouping back to flat keys and compare for equality; run on git config --list --show-origin, application.properties and actuator /env captures.
because: groups dotted keys by shared prefix
check: Runs of 2+ consecutive 'a.b.c=value' lines with the same prefix and whitespace-free values become one '§a.b: c=value d=value' line; lines with spaces in the value, comments and everything else stay verbatim in place, and decode re-expands to the exact original lines.

title: Canonicalise ISO timestamps: drop .000 fractions, use Z
detail: JS toISOString, Jira and Python isoformat() emit '.000Z', '.000000+00:00' or '+0000'. Rewrite to 'Z' (same instant); unlike #258 nothing is truncated. 20 synthetic stamps: 319 or 399 vs 279 o200k tokens.
test: Parse each stamp before and after with datetime and assert equal instants; only rewrite when every fraction in the output is zero. Measure on Jira and Graph MCP lists.
because: canonicalises ISO timestamps, same instant
check: ISO-8601 timestamps with seconds lose an all-zero fraction (.000, .000000) and have +00:00, +0000 or +00 spelled Z; non-zero fractions are kept digit for digit, offsets other than UTC (+02:00, -08:00, +0530, -00:00) are never touched, and the exact instant of every timestamp is unchanged.
check_loses: the printed fractional-second precision when it is all zeros, and the +00:00 / +0000 spelling of UTC

title: Strip comments from JSONC config reads (tsconfig, devcontainer)
detail: tsc --init writes a tsconfig dominated by commented-out options with trailing /* */ descriptions. Remove // and /* */ comments in .json files that use them, original saved. Synthetic tsc --init-style sample: 276 vs 49 o200k tokens. Not for files to be edited.
test: Run tsc --init in a scratch dir, cat the file, count tokens before and after; parse stripped output with json5 and compare option values to the live keys.
because: strips JSONC comments from tool output

title: Digest cargo metadata and go list -json output
detail: cargo metadata prints per-dependency source/req/kind/features and per-target src_path/edition/doctest flags; go list -json prints Deps, Imports and file lists per package. Emit name, version, path, workspace deps and targets. Per-tool pruning like #120.
test: Run both on a mid-size workspace, count tokens raw versus digest, check the agent still answers 'which crates depend on X' and 'where is target Y's entry file'.
because: pure text transform on JSON tool output

title: Detect HAL, JSON:API and OData link boilerplate by shape
detail: HAL _links, JSON:API links and relationships.*.links, and OData @odata.context/etag/id annotations can repeat per entity in Graph, SharePoint and hypermedia MCP servers. Detect the envelope shape, not the server name (#34); keep next-page links.
test: Count token share of these keys in captured results from one OData, one HAL and one JSON:API server; check pagination still works from the retained next link.
because: shape-based link boilerplate detection in JSON

title: Compact GraphQL error extensions: stack traces and tracing
detail: Apollo Server in non-production mode returns extensions.stacktrace arrays, and its tracing plugin adds per-resolver timings. Keep message, path, locations and extensions.code; reduce the stack to three frames, drop tracing. Complements #136, which unwraps data only.
test: Fire a failing query at a local Apollo dev server via curl; count tokens of the error JSON before and after the rule.
because: compacts GraphQL error extensions text

title: Minify JSON leaves but keep one record per line
detail: Full minify (#31) yields one multi-kilobyte line, which per-line caps (#45), line-level selection (#87) and agent grep treat as a single unit. Put newlines only at depth 1-2 and minify below. Adds one newline per record.
test: Feed fill-mode versus full-minified JSON through the line rules and classifier; compare tokens, truncation events and answer accuracy on lookup questions.
because: JSON minify keeping one record per line
check: A pretty-printed (or loosely spaced) JSON document is re-emitted with each child of the top-level container, and each child of a container-valued top-level member, on its own line and everything deeper compact; the parsed value, key order and number types are identical, and text that is not JSON, or for which the result would not be shorter (already compact, empty), is returned unchanged.
check_loses: JSON whitespace, number spelling (1e2 vs 100.0) and string escape form; inputs with duplicate keys or NaN/Infinity are left untouched

title: Measure JSON-escape tax on model-written tool_use inputs
detail: Code with quotes, backslashes and newlines grows when JSON-escaped: 220 raw vs 300 escaped o200k tokens on a synthetic regex snippet. Whether Claude's prompt renders tool_use inputs escaped is unknown. Probe with count_tokens; if real, steer quote-heavy edits.
test: Send count_tokens requests holding Edit tool_use blocks of equal character length, one quote and backslash heavy and one neutral; compare input_tokens deltas against the o200k proxy.
because: JSON-escape token tax measurement

title: Fold aged results at git commit and ExitPlanMode boundaries
detail: A commit makes earlier diffs, Edit echoes and Reads of the committed files re-obtainable from git; plan approval makes exploration reads redundant with the approved plan. Treat each event as a fold boundary, stubbing those results at the cold-cache or resume point.
test: Replay transcripts: sum tokens of tool results touching committed files before each commit, and exploration results before ExitPlanMode; check how often later turns refetch them.
because: commit and plan-approval tool calls as fold boundaries

title: Red-to-green fold: stub failing-run logs once tests pass
detail: When a test or build command first goes green after a red streak, the middle failing logs are dead history. Stub all but the first and last red outputs, keeping the final error-signature line. Trigger is the status flip, not todo state.
test: Replay transcripts for red-then-green runs of one command family; total middle-red tokens and check whether later turns quote anything from them.
because: stub middle red outputs after status flip

title: Output-handle macros expanded in Agent prompts and comment bodies
detail: Let the model write [[out:N:10-40]] instead of retyping earlier tool output inside Agent prompts, PR or issue comment bodies and Write content; PreToolUse expands it from the saved original. Targets output tokens, which cost more than input.
test: From transcripts, find Agent, add_issue_comment and Write inputs holding 200+ char spans copied from earlier results; total those output tokens as the ceiling.
because: PreToolUse macro expansion

title: Speculative next-command prefetch via PostToolUse additionalContext
detail: Learn per-repo command bigrams (git status then git diff --stat, rg then Read). When P(next | this) is high and next is read-only, append its capped output now, skipping a turn's tool_use and prefix re-read. Turns #213's detector into action.
test: Mine transcripts for read-only bigrams with conditional probability above 0.8; estimate turns saved against tokens wasted when the prefetched output goes unused.
because: hook runs predicted commands on host

title: Repetition-indexed keep schedule per command family
detail: First sighting of a command family in a session keeps the normal rate; each repeat lowers the keep rate, since the reader already knows the layout. Call-level, unlike atom-level #164 and #200 and refetch-driven #270.
test: Replay recorded sessions with rates 0.5, 0.4, 0.3 for repeats 1, 2, 3+; compare reader QA on later outputs and refetch counts against flat 0.5.
because: keyed on command string plus earlier session content

title: Relative ages against the session date in MCP timestamps
detail: Rewrite *_at ISO stamps as ages from the date already in context ('4d', 'today 12:34') rather than date-only truncation (#258). o200k proxy: full stamp 13 tokens, date 6, '4d' 2. Original stays in the saved file.
test: Tokenize synthetic list_issues-style items before and after (28-item set: 1204 vs 588 tokens); check a reader still answers oldest and newest questions.
because: ages from date in context; stable if frozen

title: Host-native dedup baseline probe before building stubs
detail: Find what Claude Code already collapses itself: repeated unchanged Read, Glob, Grep, WebFetch (some versions may emit short unchanged notices). Avoids double-counting savings or stacking a second stub on a host stub.
test: Verify that host dedup exists: headless script per installed version reads a canary file twice, Grep twice, WebFetch twice; compare tool_result sizes in the transcript JSONL.
because: probes what Claude Code itself collapses

title: Narrowing searches as path:line keys when hits already shown
detail: When a refined grep, rg or test filter returns lines all present in an earlier result, emit only the path:line keys ('subset of earlier hits') and drop the text, which is already in context. Concrete form of #63.
test: Replay transcripts for consecutive same-family commands where line set B is a subset of A; compare B's tokens with the key-only form.
because: emit path:line keys for hits already shown
check: A refined search whose every hit line was already shown (same path, line and text, unambiguous) is replaced by the ordered list of path:line keys; a new hit, changed text under a known key, line-number shifts or compaction show the full output.

title: Seed read-shadow from Write and Bash heredoc contents
detail: Content the model writes via Write, cat > f <<EOF, tee or printf is already in context as tool_use input. Record it as the shadow so a verification Read of the unchanged file becomes 'unchanged since your write'. Extends #144 beyond Edit pairs.
test: Count Reads of a path within five turns of a Write or heredoc to it where the returned text equals the written content.
because: seed shadow from earlier Write/heredoc tool_use inputs
check: Content the model wrote with Write, a quoted or expansion-free heredoc, tee or printf is kept as a shadow; a later Read whose numbered lines equal it exactly becomes 'unchanged since your write at turn N'; expanding heredocs, printf directives, failed commands, appends to unknown files, foreign changes, an Edit and compaction give the full read.

title: Cross-call redundancy ceiling: exact, line and entity, by lag
detail: For every tool result, measure the share of bytes duplicated by an earlier result in the same session as exact match, long-line match and entity match (path, sha, id), bucketed by tool and turn lag. Ranks which dedup mechanism is worth building.
test: Run over all session JSONL files; table per tool family and lag bucket; flag results above 50 percent duplicate bytes as dedup targets.
because: cross-call redundancy ceiling analysis

title: Replace skill-body code blocks the model retypes with scripts
detail: Skills often embed snippets the model copies into Bash or Write calls, paying body tokens once and output tokens every run. Detect shingle overlap between SKILL.md code fences and later tool_use inputs; move the code to scripts/ and call it by path.
test: Over transcripts that invoked Skill, measure shingle overlap between body code fences and following tool_use inputs; convert three skills to scripts, compare output tokens per run and success.
because: skill bodies and scripts directory

title: Lint skill bodies that restate their own frontmatter description
detail: The model has already seen the listing description, yet bodies often open with an H1 of the name, an intro paraphrasing the description, and a 'When to use' section. Delete these by shingle overlap with the frontmatter; fully deterministic.
test: Scan installed plugin SKILL.md files; tokenize intro and When-to-use sections with over 0.6 shingle overlap with the description; trim ten and replay trigger prompts for unchanged behavior.
because: skill frontmatter linting

title: Switch off claude.ai account-synced skills in coding repos
detail: Account-synced skills (anthropic-skills:* office files, browsers, research) list 13 entries with long descriptions in a coding repo. They are not bundled skills (#500), plugins (#151) or connectors (#156); find the setting or account toggle that omits them.
test: Verify that a toggle or env removes them: capture the /context skill-listing tokens with and without; confirm a document request still works when the skill is invoked manually.
because: account-synced skills toggle

title: Shorten plugin names that prefix every skill and tool
detail: Plugin skills list as plugin:skill and plugin MCP tools as mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__tool, so the manifest name repeats in the listing, deferred roster and every tool_use. Rename long plugin and marketplace names; complements #443 server keys.
test: Verify that plugin names appear in tool names: tokenize skill lines and tool names under a long and a 2-letter plugin name; check enabledPlugins keys still match.
because: plugin manifest naming

title: Census of text repeated across prompt parts in one request
detail: Skill descriptions, MCP server instructions, tool descriptions and deferred rosters can restate each other (one docs workflow appears in both a skill and a server block). Shingle-dedupe a captured request prefix to rank harness-fixed duplicates a proxy could drop.
test: Capture a session's first request with a logging proxy (#187); compute repeated 8-gram shingles across system, tool and reminder blocks; report tokens covered by cross-part repeats.
because: repeated text census in request prefix

title: Does an explicit agent tools allowlist lengthen the Agent listing?
detail: The Agent tool description lists each custom agent with its description and tools. #545 advises explicit minimal tool lists to cut schemas, but a long list of MCP tool names per agent may add more listing text than it saves.
test: Verify that the listing shows tools: capture the Agent tool description for one agent with tools omitted, with 3 tools and with 20 MCP tools; count tokens against #545's savings.
because: subagent definitions and Agent tool listing

title: Output tokens added by output styles and style-injecting plugins
detail: Built-in Explanatory and Learning output styles, and plugins that inject similar instructions at SessionStart, reportedly add insight blocks to replies. Output tokens cost most and also stay in history. Audit which active styles raise reply length.
test: Run 10 identical tasks under default and each active style; compare mean assistant output tokens per turn and total billed tokens; list SessionStart hooks mentioning style or insight.
because: Claude Code output styles and plugins

title: Lowercase shouted emphasis in instruction files, with compliance check
detail: IMPORTANT, CRITICAL, MUST and NEVER in caps tokenize worse and reportedly make newer Claude models over-apply rules. Toy o200k proxy: 15 tokens versus 8 for the same two sentences in plain case. Differs from tool-output rule #620.
test: Rewrite shouted lines in a CLAUDE.md to plain case; replay 20 rule-sensitive prompts; count rule violations and tokens before and after.
because: instruction-file editing; model-compliance claim

title: Collapse near-duplicate few-shot examples inside skills and CLAUDE.md
detail: Skill and rule files often carry three or four same-shaped examples or code fences. Cluster fenced blocks and example tags by shingle Jaccard, keep the most central, replace the rest with one line naming the variation. Deterministic; file backed up.
test: Run the clusterer over installed skills; report tokens in non-central members; collapse them in five skills and replay prompts that exercise the removed variants.
because: edits skill and CLAUDE.md files

title: Output-language tax of the language setting
detail: The language setting makes replies come in the user's language, and non-English prose costs more tokens (#919 saw 1.4 to 2x on input). Measure narration share versus final answer, then test English narration with a localized final summary.
test: Count tokens of 20 recorded replies and their English renderings with count_tokens; estimate the output share of narration between tool calls versus the final message.
because: Claude Code language setting

title: Attribute tool calls induced by CLAUDE.md directives
detail: Imperatives like 'always run tests first', 'read README before starting' or 'run git status' trigger fixed tool calls every session, costing far more than the sentence. Match directives to early tool calls and price their results. Differs from usage telemetry #154.
test: Extract imperative lines from CLAUDE.md; match to Bash/Read calls in each session's first five turns; sum result tokens times surviving turns per directive.
because: CLAUDE.md directives memory file

title: Consolidate sibling skills behind one router skill
detail: Sibling skills (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx here) each pay a listing entry plus cross-referencing 'do NOT use for the others' clauses. One router skill with a short description, a routing table in its body and per-format reference files cuts listing text.
test: Build a router for four related skills; compare /context skill-listing tokens; replay 40 prompts for correct file-format routing versus the original separate skills.
because: skill consolidation, plugin skill structure

title: Learn keep-masks end-to-end through a frozen reader LM
detail: Relax the keep decision to a Gumbel-sigmoid or HardKuma gate on the input embeddings of a frozen 0.5B reader; train the head to minimise reader next-token loss plus an L0 budget penalty. Rationale-extraction style (Lei 2016; Bastings 2019), gradient-based rather than #598 rejection sampling.
test: Fine-tune on 2k cached rows with a 0.5B reader; compare reader perplexity of kept text and QA at equal chars versus the teacher-label head.
because: offline mask training through frozen reader

title: Pool atom scores per template slot, column or JSON key
detail: Mask digits and hex to get line templates, table columns or JSON key paths, then average each slot's atom scores over all members before top-k. Keep/drop becomes consistent per field, so objects share surviving keys. Differs from #164, which only decays repeats.
test: On 30 saved logs, ps/df/docker-ps tables and 20 MCP lists with 100+ objects, count slots or key sets with mixed keep/drop before and after pooling; QA on column-value questions.
because: score pooling on text, deterministic

title: Global skeleton pass scores every line before detail windows
detail: For outputs beyond a few windows, concatenate the first 8 atoms of each line into one long input (ModernBERT-family backbone, reportedly 8k context), score line importance with a global view, then spend detail-window budget per line.
test: On 10 logs over 50 KB, compare kept-line overlap and needle recall of skeleton-then-detail versus independent 512-token windows at 0.5.
because: local global-view scorer pass, text only

title: Small cross-window BiGRU over frozen atom embeddings
detail: Export pooled last-layer atom vectors per window (as in #558), then train a 2-layer BiGRU across the whole output's atom sequence on the existing labels. Gives global context without retraining the encoder or lengthening windows.
test: Cache embeddings for 1k rows over 1000 tokens; compare AUC and top-50% recall on tokens past position 512 versus the encoder alone.
because: small local CPU scorer head, text only

title: Choose keep count from score-distribution elbow or mixture
detail: Fit a two-component mixture (or Otsu threshold) to each window's logit margins and keep the high component, clamped between rates 0.3 and 0.7, so dense windows keep more and padding-heavy ones less. Uses only model outputs, no redundancy proxy.
test: Check bimodality on 100 saved outputs per type; compare kept fractions and QA at equal total tokens versus constant 0.5.
because: threshold choice from model outputs, deterministic

title: Per-atom-class isotonic calibration before global top-k
detail: Digits, punctuation, lowercase words, paths and capitalised tokens may sit on different probability scales, so one global sort favors a class. Fit a monotone map per class on validation labels, preserving within-class order. Lighter than the #927 rescorer.
test: Plot reliability curves per class on val rows; compare class mix of kept atoms against the teacher's mix at 0.5, then QA at equal chars.
because: score calibration on text classes, deterministic

title: Cap near-duplicate templates in the training corpus
detail: Hash digit-masked line templates per row and downsample rows whose templates exceed a cap, so repetitive build and server logs do not dominate gradients. Works within a source, unlike source-level mix weights (#926, #1117).
test: Count template concentration in the current corpus; retrain a small subset capped versus uncapped and compare val AUC on held-out sources.
because: training corpus dedup, offline

title: Quantization-aware fine-tune so int8 matches fp32 decisions
detail: Post-training int8 shifts scores; fine-tune a few hundred steps with fake-quant (torch.ao QAT or ORT QDQ) on the training mix before export. Differs from #836 (calibration) and #929 (weight-only), which stay post-training.
test: On 200 held-out outputs compare Jaccard of kept sets at 0.5 versus fp32 for PTQ int8 and QAT int8, plus val AUC.
because: quantisation-aware training of the local scorer

title: Per-token early freezing inside the encoder (PoWER-BERT style)
detail: Tokens whose layer-4 probe margin is already extreme skip layers 5 to N and copy their decision; only uncertain tokens continue. Adapted from PoWER-BERT (Goyal et al., 2020) and Learned Token Pruning (Kim et al., 2022). Differs from whole-model exit #561.
test: Fit layer probes on cached hidden states; measure decision agreement and compute share saved at margin cutoffs on 100 outputs; prototype only if agreement exceeds 99%.
because: local encoder speedup, model-internal

title: Teacher-label oracle arm measures the distillation gap
detail: Run selection and reader eval with the teacher's keep labels as scores on held-out rows, beside the student's scores at the same char budget. A small gap means gains need better labels; a large gap means a better scorer.
test: On 200 val rows, QA at the teacher's own keep rate using teacher labels versus top-k student scores at the same budget, paired bootstrap.
because: teacher-label oracle eval arm

title: Question-before-context order: match live reading order
detail: eval_qa READ puts context first, question last. In a live session the agent's intent precedes the tool output, so it reads the output already knowing what it needs. Order may change how well gaps are tolerated and how methods rank.
test: Reuse cached compressed contexts; ask with question before versus after context; compare EM and unknown rate per method with a chunk-clustered paired bootstrap; check whether method ranking flips.
because: eval prompt-order parity

title: Order, recency and final-state questions over folded logs
detail: Folding repeats, dedupe and deletion can erase which event came first, last, or how a run ended. Programmatic-gold questions: first failing test, last error before exit, final status line, which retry succeeded. Distinct from count and absence questions.
test: Script 100 regex-gold order questions over pytest, build and retry logs; score reader on original, 0.5 kept and collapsed-duplicates output; report accuracy by question class.
because: order and final-state eval questions

title: Exit-code gold: false-green rate when output is compressed
detail: Ask the reader 'did this command succeed, and which phase failed' with gold from the recorded exit code and failing step. False-green (says success on nonzero exit) is the costliest error and needs no span gold or LLM question writer.
test: Run 100 fixture commands recording exit codes; compress at 0.5 and 0.33; ask the outcome question 3 times per output; report false-green and false-red rates versus original.
because: exit-code false-green eval

title: Planted-harm ladder: verify the eval detects known losses
detail: Before trusting a null result, delete the gold span from a fixed 1, 2, 3, 5 percent of items in the compressed contexts and rerun the full pipeline, scorer and bootstrap included. Confirms the paired test recovers known drops, end to end.
test: Strip gold from random items in cached 0.5-kept contexts to plant 1-5 point drops; rescore; report the smallest drop flagged at alpha 0.05 and false-alarm rate with none planted.
because: planted-harm eval sanity check

title: Provenance census: kept, original-only or invented strings
detail: For cached reader answers, and for IDs, hashes, paths and numbers in the agent's later messages and tool inputs, classify each string as in the compressed view, only in the saved original, or nowhere. Separates lucky inference from invention; no new LLM calls.
test: Tokenise cached answers and transcript text; bucket wrong and right ones by provenance per method and keep rate; report invented share at 0.33 versus 0.5 versus original, session-clustered.
because: provenance census of reader strings

title: Grader audit: reference passes, empty patch fails, repeats agree
detail: Before spending on A/B arms, run each task's reference patch and an empty patch five times in a clean container. Drop tasks whose grader flakes, passes on empty, or depends on test order; grader noise otherwise masquerades as hook harm.
test: For the candidate 25-task pool, run reference and empty arms 5 times each; report per-task pass variance and the count dropped; recompute the A/A discordant rate on the cleaned pool.
because: task grader audit

title: Template-overlap leakage: test lines already seen in training
detail: Mask digits and hex in test and train chunks, then measure what share of each test chunk's lines have an identical template in training. Boilerplate memorised by the classifier inflates scores; report metrics by overlap tercile.
test: Hash masked train lines, probe held-out chunks, bucket by overlap share; compare lost-ID rate and cached QA accuracy at keep 0.5 for the top versus bottom tercile.
because: train-test template leakage audit

title: Tool-version holdout: classifier on newest and oldest releases
detail: Public-dataset logs are frozen in time. Run the same failing fixture under a two-year-old and the current pytest, cargo or npm, then check whether failure lines survive equally. Tests the classifier's time generalisation, not the rules.
test: Create two venvs per tool with pinned old and latest versions; run one seeded failure; compress at 0.5; compare failure-line and path survival between versions.
because: tool-version holdout eval

title: Risk-stratified holdout with inverse-probability weights
detail: A uniform 15 percent holdout spends most controls on safe compressions where harm is near zero. Hold out aggressive or low-confidence calls at 50 percent and safe ones at 5, log the probability, and weight outcomes by its inverse.
test: Simulate 2,000 calls with a 10 percent high-risk stratum carrying all harm; compare variance of the IPW harm estimate against uniform sampling at equal control counts.
because: risk-stratified holdout statistics

title: Final-patch similarity between arms as a high-power endpoint
detail: Pass/fail needs many tasks. Compare each task's final git diff across hook-on and hook-off runs (normalised line diff), against the on-versus-on similarity as ceiling. Continuous, so it can show behaviour shifts that pass rates miss.
test: On 20 tasks with 2 runs per arm, compute pairwise diff similarity within and across arms; test whether across-arm similarity is lower than within-arm via task-level permutation.
because: final-patch similarity endpoint

title: Stub superseded final_file_content echoes in Cline and Roo
detail: Cline and Roo reportedly echo the whole updated file as <final_file_content> after every replace_in_file or write_to_file. Ten edits to one file leave ten full copies. A base-URL proxy keeps the newest per path and stubs older ones once, at first sight.
test: Log one Cline task with 10 edits to a large file through a proxy; count tokens in superseded echoes, then replay with stubs and compare later edit success.
because: Cline and Roo final_file_content echo format

title: RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH with max-columns for every rg-backed agent
detail: One shared ripgrep config (--max-columns=200, --max-columns-preview, optionally --max-filesize) caps minified-bundle hits at the source for any agent that shells out to rg, hooks or not. The agent can rerun with --max-columns=0 for the full line.
test: Verify that Claude Code's Grep honors the env; replay real transcript grep calls with and without the config and review which cut hits mattered. Synthetic 100 KB hit: 300 bytes.
because: ripgrep config via env, any agent

title: Windows PowerShell pack: CLIXML progress blobs, table padding, _x000D_ escapes
detail: Windows-hosted agents (Codex, Cursor, Cline) run PowerShell, where redirected stderr can carry '#< CLIXML' progress records and _x000D__x000A_ escaped errors, and Format-Table pads columns. Drop progress objects, decode escapes, trim padding. No current pack targets PowerShell.
test: On a windows-latest CI runner run powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command with Install-Module, Get-ChildItem and a failing cmdlet; capture 2>&1 and count o200k tokens per artifact class.
because: pure text transform on PowerShell output

title: Read-only digest view of the repo for hookless agents
detail: Mount a FUSE or rsync-mirror view where lockfiles, minified bundles, snapshots, big fixtures and notebooks appear as digests and source stays real. It sits beneath every agent's tools, so Cursor, Zed, Aider and Codex need no hook.
test: Build the mirror with symlinks plus digests for a real repo; run one scripted rg, cat and ls exploration in both trees; compare o200k tokens and answers to five questions.
because: filesystem-level digest view beneath any agent
check: A mirror of the repo with hard-linked source and digest files for the lockfile, minified bundle, snapshot, big JSON fixture and notebook cuts a scripted ls/find/cat/grep session to under 15% of the tokens, answers four of five questions identically (lockfile version, functions, snapshot names, record keys) and misses the fifth (a string inside the bundle) while every digest announces itself with the real path; real grep -r cannot see a symlink mirror, edits through hard links reach the real file, digests are mode 0444, stale digests are detected and refreshed.

title: git sparse-checkout worktree hides noisy trees from every agent
detail: Give agents a git worktree with sparse-checkout excluding vendor, generated output, fixtures and doc archives. ls, find, du, rg and IDE file trees never see them, unlike agent-specific ignore files or Claude-only deny rules. Commits still work normally.
test: git worktree add --no-checkout, then sparse-checkout set --cone; run identical ls -R, find and rg exploration in full and sparse trees and compare token counts.
because: git sparse-checkout, agent-agnostic filesystem view
check: A git worktree with a cone sparse-checkout of src, tests and docs/current cuts the same ls -R, find, grep and du exploration to under 40% of the tokens with identical answers for the code that stays; git status stays clean, new paths outside the cone are refused with a hint, a commit made there carries the whole tree and only the agent's changes, it fast-forwards into the main checkout, and a grep for a vendored symbol silently finds nothing (sparse-checkout add brings it back).

title: Gemini CLI summarizeToolOutput as baseline arm or ctxprune backend
detail: Gemini CLI has a summarizeToolOutput setting giving run_shell_command a token budget, enforced by an extra LLM call. Measure that call's cost and loss against ctxprune on the same outputs; if a base-URL override exists, point it at a local endpoint.
test: Verify that the setting exists; replay 30 recorded shell outputs through it and through ctxprune at equal output tokens; count extra requests and tokens, and score one question per output.
because: baseline measurement against summarizer arm

title: Gemini CLI BeforeToolSelection hook narrows the tool menu per turn
detail: Gemini CLI hooks include BeforeToolSelection, which can restrict which tools the model may call. If restricted declarations also leave the request, schema tokens shrink per turn by intent, which static allowlists cannot do. Whether the API still counts them is unknown.
test: Verify that the hook exists; log usageMetadata.promptTokenCount for one identical prompt with all tools versus a hook restricting to read_file and shell; check whether prompt tokens drop.
because: Gemini CLI BeforeToolSelection hook

title: Cross-vendor bulk reader: headless gemini or codex answers questions
detail: An ask_file(path, question) tool shells out to another vendor's headless CLI (gemini -p, codex exec read-only) or a local model to read a huge log; only its short answer enters the main context. The bulk read moves to a separate quota.
test: Take five logs over 100 KB with known facts; compare main-context tokens and accuracy of direct read plus grep versus the delegate's answer, and note the delegate's own token bill.
because: runtime call to another vendor's cloud CLI

title: Continue HTTP context provider serves pruned files for @-attachments
detail: Continue supports custom HTTP context providers, and Zed has extension slash commands. A ctxprune serve route returning pruned file or log text makes a user's deliberate @-attachment of a big reference cost fewer tokens than @file.
test: Verify that the provider type exists; attach one 50 KB log via @file and via the provider, compare request-log token counts, and ask three questions about it.
because: Continue and Zed context provider extensions

title: Errors-only diagnostics profile for agent edit-feedback loops
detail: Cline, Cursor and Copilot agents reportedly append editor diagnostics after edits. A dedicated VS Code profile for agent sessions disables spellcheck, hint and info diagnostics and noisy extensions, so the feedback block carries only real errors.
test: Run the same 10-edit task in the default and agent profiles; extract diagnostic blocks from the request log; compare token counts and check true errors still appear.
because: VS Code profile settings

title: Standalone JS port of the classifier for TypeScript agent plugins
detail: The int8 ONNX model could run in onnxruntime-node or WASM, with a JS tokenizer and atom rules ported. Plugins for opencode, Gemini CLI extensions, Cline hooks and VS Code extensions then compress in-process, with no Python install or serve daemon.
test: Run model_quantized.onnx in Node on 200 saved inputs; diff per-token logits against Python onnxruntime and time cold load. Port atom logic only if parity holds.
because: JS port of local classifier, no harness feature

title: Compress embedded resource and structuredContent-only MCP results
detail: _text_slots matches only type=text blocks, so payloads carried as resource.text, or as structuredContent beside an empty text block, bypass compression entirely. Add those shapes as slots, saving the originals once. #201 only logs them.
test: Replay captured results from fetch, filesystem and GitHub MCP servers; total characters in non-text shapes above 6,000, then run the extended hook and compare sizes.
because: compress additional MCP result text shapes

title: Revert individual slots that barely compress despite passing total
detail: run() applies the 0.95 gate to summed characters, so a stderr or MCP block at ratio 0.98 still gets its lossy version next to a well-compressed stdout. Restore any slot whose own ratio exceeds about 0.9 to its original.
test: Replay recorded multi-slot events; count slots above ratio 0.9 and words deleted from them, then run reader QA on those slots with and without the revert.
because: per-block ratio gate on tool output

title: Aligner ground-truth test with known deletions; line-aware duplicate ties
detail: _lcs_pairs matches the earliest equal atom, so when a repeated atom (comma, quote, 'the') is deleted later, the keep label lands on an earlier copy. A quick local run, random 50% deletions on prose, mislabeled about 2% of atoms (partly irreducible).
test: Delete known masks from corpus chunks, run align(), report mismatch by atom frequency; try same-line-first tie-breaking and compare mismatch plus student AUC after a short retrain.
because: ground-truth test of the label aligner

title: Noise pack for dnf, yum, apk, composer, bundler, nuget, flutter
detail: Drop repo-metadata refresh lines, per-package download and verify rows and progress counters; keep errors, version conflicts and the final transaction summary. Existing packs cover npm, pip, cargo, apt, brew and conda, not these.
test: Capture installs for each manager in containers, apply the pack, check reader QA on versions and failures, and count Claude tokens before and after.
because: pure text transform on package-manager output

title: Merge many MCP text blocks into one in updatedToolOutput
detail: Search-style MCP servers return one text block per hit. Joining blocks with a newline may drop per-block framing tokens and lets one compression pass see cross-hit context. Hook-level counterpart of proxy idea #1035; probe the framing cost first.
test: Use count_tokens on a tool_result with one block versus the same text split into 40 blocks; if the delta is zero, drop the idea.
because: merge result text blocks, payload-level rewrite
check: Runs of adjacent plain MCP text blocks (exactly {type, text}) are joined with a newline in the same call that compresses them; image, resource and annotated blocks, sibling keys like isError, block order and all text survive, and because the joined block crosses the size threshold the hook compresses 40 small hits that it ignores today. The per-block boundary becomes a newline (lost if hits contain newlines); whether framing tokens drop needs count_tokens, as the idea says.

title: SWE-smith eval rows double as checkpoint-selection rows
detail: eval_quick.py scores swe_smith_tool on the val split because test is empty, but train.py picks the best epoch by val AUC. That source's numbers are selection-biased; the other sources use untouched test rows.
test: Report swe_smith_tool numbers from a repo-level holdout excluded from both training and val, or re-select the checkpoint without that source's val rows, and compare the gap.
because: eval selection-bias audit

title: Shrink search result caps as same tool repeats
detail: context-mode reportedly returns 2 results per query for calls 1-3, 1 for calls 4-8, then blocks and redirects to a batch call. PreToolUse could lower Grep or search-MCP head_limit by call index within a turn window, pushing the agent to fuse queries.
test: Count runs of 4+ Grep or search-MCP calls within 10 turns in transcripts; sum tokens of the 4th-and-later results as the ceiling.
because: lowers search limits by call count in payload

title: Stub repeated WebFetch of same URL and prompt
detail: context-mode caches fetched pages 24 h and answers a repeat with a ~0.3 KB hint, not 48 KB+. Keep a session ledger keyed on URL plus prompt for WebFetch and fetch-style MCP tools; a repeat returns a pointer to the earlier result.
test: Count duplicate (URL, prompt) and duplicate-URL fetches per session in transcripts; sum their result tokens as the ceiling.
because: session ledger on URL and prompt, stub repeats

title: Trigram and identifier-split index for BM25 recall
detail: context-mode fuses Porter BM25 with an FTS5 trigram index by reciprocal rank fusion, plus proximity rerank. Word-level BM25 misses partial camelCase, snake_case and path tokens. Add trigram and identifier-split channels to recall over saved originals (#654) and code search (#403).
test: Use agents' later grep patterns as queries and the grepped line as gold; compare top-3 hit rate for word BM25, trigram and fused ranking on saved originals.
because: local retrieval index improvement

title: Per-glob Read levels: full, signatures, tree-only, processors
detail: Repomix lets each glob choose full, compressed or tree-only content and run external processors such as JSON to TOON or SVG minify. Ship a project table mapping globs to a level or processor, applied to Read and cat results, beyond one-off deny rules (#401).
test: Draft a 5-glob table for one repo; replay its Read and cat calls from transcripts and tally tokens each glob rule would have saved.
because: glob-keyed processing of Read results by path argument

title: Repo token-weight tree joined with agent access counts
detail: Repomix --token-count-tree reports tokens per directory but not usage. Compute exact tokens per path, join Read, Grep and Glob hits from transcripts: large-and-hot paths become skeleton or digest candidates, large-and-cold ones deny or ignore candidates.
test: Run on one repo and its last 20 transcripts; list top 20 paths by tokens times reads and check which existing deny or ignore rules already cover them.
because: joins Claude Code transcripts, deny/ignore settings

title: Fold markers carry value counts and min/max of dropped rows
detail: Headroom's SmartCrusher reportedly keeps errors, outliers and boundary rows. Extend any row fold marker with per-column summaries of what was dropped: categorical counts such as status ok 40, failed 7, numeric min/max, date range. Aggregate questions then need no refetch.
test: On JSON lists and tables, ask count, min, max and status questions over folded output with and without the summary; compare accuracy and refetch rate.
because: richer fold markers in text output

title: PreToolUse denial of unchanged Read using line-range ledger
detail: qdf-hook reportedly denies a Read whose mtime and size are unchanged, so nothing enters context, and lets windowed reads bypass its cache. Variant: deny only when requested lines fall inside ranges already returned. Concrete form of #60.
test: Replay Read calls from transcripts: count re-reads with unchanged mtime and range subset; verify that Edit still passes its read-first check after a denied Read.
because: line-range ledger stub; host mtime has weaker payload key
check: A PreToolUse gate denies a Read only when mtime, size, inode and content hash are unchanged since the executed Reads that returned the requested lines (clamped to EOF); across 120 random sessions every Edit outcome equals the run without the gate, every denied range is still in context, and ablations without hash, without mtime, or ignoring compaction are caught.

title: Contrast-based column selection: keep fields that separate failing rows
detail: Honeycomb BubbleUp compares anomalous and baseline rows to surface attributes whose distribution differs. For record lists with a failing subset (CI runs, pods, test results JSON), keep identifiers plus the top-lift fields, hoist the rest as constants.
test: On kubectl and CI-run JSON with failing items, compute per-field lift, keep top 5, then ask why-failing questions; compare accuracy and tokens against full records.
because: column selection on record-list output

title: Rank aged tool results by relevance to current prompt
detail: A history-rewriting proxy needs a rule for which old results to stub. Score each by BM25 overlap with the latest prompt plus recent assistant text, not by age alone, as the cloud.reduce Reducer reportedly does with prior turns.
test: On transcripts, label each aged result reused or not by later identifier overlap; compare AUC of age versus BM25-to-latest-prompt as reuse predictors.
because: BM25 relevance ranking of aged results in proxy
check: Aged tool results are ranked for stubbing by BM25 against the latest prompt instead of by age: on seeded synthetic sessions the AUC as a reuse predictor and the reused results kept at an equal budget both beat age (two independent AUC algorithms agree), a result whose path the prompt names, an error result and everything when the prompt is empty are handled by pin and fallback rules, and a vocabulary mismatch ('config' vs settings.py) is shown to be stubbed.

title: IPython, nbconvert and PySpark failures: keep user frames, fold runtime
detail: IPython tracebacks add ANSI codes, multi-line and Cython frames; nbconvert echoes failing cell source first. PySpark errors repeat the message, then constant Driver stacktrace and py4j reflection frames. Keep failing cell and line, user frames, deepest cause. Hand-made IPython sample: 778 vs 46 tokens (o200k).
test: Run nbconvert --execute on a notebook with a pandas KeyError, and a local PySpark job whose UDF raises ValueError; compare o200k tokens; confirm failing line, exception and UDF source survive.
because: pure text transform on traceback output
