check: Strips ANSI colour, folds each run of library frames (site-packages, Cython .pyx/.pxi, pyspark/py4j, stdlib) of an IPython or classic traceback into '[ctxprune: N library frames folded]', replaces a Python traceback that repeats an earlier one by a 'same as above' line, and replaces runs of 3+ Java 'at' frames by a count; the failing cell's source, every user frame (Cell In[N], project files) with its pointer line, every distinct exception line and the counts of library and Java frames are unchanged.
check_loses: ANSI colour, the names and source excerpts of library frames, the second and later identical copies of a Python traceback, and the individual Java frames (the saved original keeps them)

title: Unicode box tables (DuckDB, polars, Keras, Rich) to TSV
detail: #412 covers only ASCII +---+ grids. DuckDB duckbox, polars frames, Keras 3 summary and Lightning ModelSummary draw box-drawing borders plus a dtype row. Emit TSV with dtypes folded into header cells. Hand-made 20-row duckbox: 468 vs 245 o200k tokens.
test: Print the same 200-row frame via duckdb and polars; convert to TSV; round-trip cells against the source frame; compare o200k tokens.
because: box-drawing tables to TSV
check: A Unicode box table (top border, header rows, a header separator, body rows, bottom border) becomes TSV with one header line (name, or name:dtype when a dtype row follows; polars' --- row dropped) and one line per body row, cells trimmed; ragged, separator-less or tab-containing tables and text around the table are left verbatim.
check_loses: cell padding and alignment (cells are trimmed, so a cell with intentional leading/trailing spaces changes), border characters, extra row separators, and column width

title: sklearn search verbose: fold CV START/END pairs per candidate
detail: GridSearchCV(verbose=3) prints '[CV 2/5; 7/24] START' and END lines per fold and candidate, plus joblib '[Parallel]' progress; cv_results_ repeats params beside param_* columns. Fold to per-candidate mean scores; keep failures. Hand-made 24x5 grid, upper bound: 9,599 vs 491 tokens (o200k).
test: Run GridSearchCV(SVC, verbose=3) on a toy dataset with 24 candidates and 5 folds; compare o200k tokens with a per-candidate fold; confirm best params survive.
because: pure text transform on verbose training logs
check: For each GridSearchCV(verbose=3) candidate whose folds all finished with a finite score, the START/END lines (even interleaved by n_jobs) become '[CV c/N] params: scores s1..sF mean m total Ts'; per-candidate parameters, every fold score, the mean and the best candidate are unchanged, and a candidate with a nan or missing fold keeps all its lines, as do warnings and the final result lines.
check_loses: the START lines, per-fold times (only their sum), the fold-by-fold interleaving order, and joblib '[Parallel]' backend and 'Done N tasks' progress lines

title: Fixed-line packs for W&B, Comet, ClearML and Airflow logs
detail: W&B, Comet, Neptune and ClearML print login banners, run URLs, sparkline history and 'Synced N files' footers; Airflow task logs open with fixed dependency, runner and AIRFLOW_CTX_* lines. Fold to one header; keep run URL, metrics, task output and failures. Samples: 293 and 748 tokens.
test: Run a toy wandb offline script and a local airflow tasks test; strip via fixed-line tables; count tokens removed; confirm final metrics and a failing task's traceback remain.
because: pure text transform on log banners
check: W&B boilerplate (login, version, local path, offline hint, 'Syncing run', project URL, 'Waiting for W&B process', 'Synced N file(s)', 'Find logs at', the sparkline history block) and Airflow task-log boilerplate (dependency, executor, process, command, job, running-on, downstream and exit-code-0 lines) fold into '[... N fixed lines folded (wandb|airflow)]', the Airflow env-var line shrinks to its dag_id, task_id, try and run_id; run URLs, 'Run summary' metrics, task output, state lines, tracebacks, exit codes other than 0 and every unlisted line are verbatim.
check_loses: the W&B login name, version and local run path, the sparkline history of each metric, the Airflow dependency and command lines, the DAG owner and logical date (the run_id carries it), and the line timestamps of the folded lines

title: Fold per-row-group column stats in Parquet and ORC metadata
detail: pyarrow ParquetFile.metadata, parquet-tools meta and orc-tool meta list every column chunk of every row group with codec, encodings, min/max and null counts (from memory). Collapse groups sharing a layout into one table plus overall min/max, rows and nulls; list anomalous groups. Unmeasured.
test: Write a Parquet file with 50 row groups and 20 columns using pyarrow; print metadata; compare o200k tokens with the folded form; check codec and null-count questions remain answerable.
because: folds Parquet/ORC metadata row groups
check: A pyarrow metadata dump (file, row groups, column chunks) with 3+ row groups becomes one 'parquet: ...' line, one table line per column for the row groups that share the modal layout (overall min/max, null and value totals, sizes), the row count of every row group and full per-column lines for row groups whose codec, encodings or dictionary flag differ; the file facts, per-column codecs, encodings, overall min/max and totals, row counts and the odd row groups are unchanged.
check_loses: per-row-group min/max and null counts of the conforming row groups (only their overall min/max and totals remain), file and page offsets, per-chunk sizes (sums only), the statistics flags and the object addresses

title: DB settings dumps: keep only non-default rows (pg_settings, SHOW VARIABLES)
detail: SELECT * FROM pg_settings lists hundreds of rows with description, unit and category columns; boot_val and source let a filter keep only rows differing from boot_val or with non-default source. MySQL SHOW VARIABLES and redis CONFIG GET * need a defaults table. Extends #1149.
test: On a local Postgres run SELECT * FROM pg_settings; count rows with source='default'; compare o200k tokens before and after the filter; check every tuned parameter is kept.
because: pure text transform on settings dump
check: In 'SELECT * FROM pg_settings' output a row with source=default and setting=boot_val is dropped, in MySQL 'SHOW VARIABLES' a row equal to a known default is dropped (unknown names are kept); header, separators, footer, every other row with all its columns and the count of omitted rows (one note line) are unchanged.
check_loses: the name, description and category of every setting that is at its default (only their count survives), and the column padding is not re-aligned

title: Drop spark.sql.sources.schema JSON that duplicates the column list
detail: SHOW CREATE TABLE, DESCRIBE FORMATTED and Glue get-table output for Spark-written tables carry spark.sql.sources.schema.part.N, JSON restating every column, plus Parquet serde class names and transient_lastDdlTime (from memory). Drop the JSON when it matches the columns; stub class names.
test: Create a 30-column Parquet table in local PySpark with Hive support; run SHOW CREATE TABLE; compare o200k tokens with and without the property JSON; verify columns remain.
because: drops duplicated schema JSON in table output

title: EXPLAIN FORMAT JSON plans to indented text without zero counters
detail: Postgres EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) emits about 25 keys per node, mostly false flags and zero Blocks counters; MySQL FORMAT=JSON and Mongo explain('executionStats') nest similarly. Render a text tree of nonzero fields. #883 covers text plans only. Hand-made node: 235 vs 52 tokens (o200k).
test: Capture EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) of a 4-join query in local Postgres; convert; compare o200k tokens; check a reader still finds the slowest node and its row misestimate.
because: EXPLAIN JSON to indented text tree
check: A PostgreSQL EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) plan becomes one 'Node Type key=value ...' line per node, indented by depth, without false flags, empty values, zero buffer counters and zero 'Rows Removed' counts; every other field of every node (costs, rows, loops, times, conditions, sort details, non-zero buffers), the top-level fields, the slowest node by exclusive time and the worst row misestimate are unchanged.
check_loses: which false flags and zero counters were present in the JSON (a missing key reads as zero or false), JSON key order is kept but whitespace and nesting syntax are gone

title: PreToolUse: add --csv or -B to bare SQL client calls
detail: When psql -c, mysql -e, sqlite3 or duckdb -c carries no format flag, rewrite via updatedInput to psql --csv, mysql -B, sqlite3 -csv or duckdb -csv, avoiding padded grids at the source. Skip meta-commands and EXPLAIN. Differs from #412, which parses grids afterwards.
test: Replay 20 saved SELECTs through psql default and --csv on a local database; compare o200k tokens; run NULL-versus-empty-string and quoted-comma questions on both outputs.
because: adds format flag to SQL client commands

title: Fold passing checks in Great Expectations, pandera and Soda reports
detail: Great Expectations validation-result JSON repeats expectation_config, empty meta and null exception_info for every expectation, passing or not (from memory); Soda and dbt tests print per-check pass rows. Fold passes to a count; keep failures with unexpected_count and sample values. Unmeasured.
test: Build a 40-expectation validation result with 3 failures in Great Expectations; compare o200k tokens raw versus folded; check failed expectation names and unexpected counts survive.
because: folds passing checks in report output

title: Pack one-per-line short-item lists into space-joined rows
detail: BPE folds a space into the next word token but bills each newline separately. Re-flow lists of whitespace-free items (git ls-files, ls -1, pip freeze, rg -l) into space-joined rows. o200k proxy: 375 to 316 and 339 to 290 tokens; comma joins gained nothing.
test: Re-flow 20 saved list outputs; compare count_tokens for per-line, 80-column and 160-column rows; ask membership, count and Nth-item questions on each form.
because: reflow one-per-line lists; text transform

title: Strip leading ./ from find, grep -r and tar listings
detail: find ., grep -rn pat . and tar -tf prefix every path with ./, which names the same file without it. Dropping it keeps later commands valid. Measured on 59 repo paths, o200k proxy: 435 to 375 tokens.
test: Strip leading ./ in 50 saved find, rg and grep outputs; compare count_tokens; replay later Read and cat calls to confirm stripped paths resolve.
because: pure text transform on path listings
check: When every line of a find, grep -r or tar -t output is a path starting with './' (or '.' or '--'), the leading './' is removed from each line; names starting with '-', '/' or '~', a bare './', and any output that is not wholly such a listing stay untouched.
check_loses: the './' prefix, so './x' and 'x' printed by the same command become indistinguishable

title: Deterministic wordy-phrase table for README, issue and docs prose
detail: Replace multi-word padding phrases: 'in order to' to 'to', 'due to the fact that' to 'because', 'a large number of' to 'many'; drop 'it is important to note that'. Single-word swaps like utilize gain nothing. Measured 2-5 o200k tokens saved per phrase hit.
test: Count phrase hits per 1k tokens across 30 READMEs, issue bodies and doc pages fetched via MCP or WebFetch; apply the table; compare count_tokens; run reader QA before and after.
because: deterministic phrase rewrite of prose

title: Collapse ZWJ, skin-tone and flag emoji; drop decorative emoji
detail: Measured o200k proxy: a ZWJ family emoji costs 11 tokens versus 2 for the base glyph; skin-tone thumbs-up 3 versus 1; flag 4 versus 'NL' 1; warning sign with VS16 3 versus 'WARN' 1. Collapse sequences, drop decorative heading emoji in bot-written Markdown.
test: Grep 30 saved GitHub and Slack MCP outputs for U+200D, skin-tone modifiers and regional indicators; measure token share; collapse; confirm reader QA on status questions is unchanged.
because: collapse emoji sequences in text

title: Strip DCS, APC and PM terminal-graphics strings, not just CSI
detail: Sixel (DCS), kitty graphics (APC) and tmux passthrough wrap opaque payloads that CSI/OSC-only regexes may leave behind. Synthetic 710-char sixel: 530 o200k tokens; real image output from chafa or timg can be far larger. Delete through the ST terminator and leave a stub.
test: Emit sixel via chafa -f sixel, kitty icat and a tmux passthrough; run the current ANSI strip; count surviving payload tokens; add ST-terminated string removal and diff text lines.
because: strip terminal graphics escape strings

title: Decode cat -v meta notation and octal UTF-8 escapes
detail: cat -v and cat -A render UTF-8 as M-bM-^@M-^Y; ls -b, sed -n l and od -c use octal escapes. Extends #619 and #227. Typographic sample, o200k proxy: 54 versus 11 tokens (M- notation), 11 versus 3 (octal). Decode valid UTF-8 runs; keep ^I.
test: Run cat -A and ls -b on files named with accents and curly quotes; decode runs forming valid UTF-8; assert re-encoding matches the bytes; compare count_tokens before and after.
because: decode cat -v notation; text transform

title: Alias-label token ladder: single words versus sigil plus digit
detail: Alias labels cost differently: o200k proxy ' Alpha' 1 token, ' $1' 2, ' [1]' 3, ' <A>' 3, '{{p1}}' 4. A 3-token label can erase the gain from shortening a path. Rank label styles by tokens and reader accuracy before building aliasing (#100, #784).
test: Run count_tokens on 30 label styles in context ' X/file.py'; pick the cheapest 3; test whether Claude resolves each back through the legend on 20 path-edit prompts.
because: offline ranking of alias label styles

title: Collapse double spaces after sentence-ending periods in prose
detail: Reportedly nroff man pages, RFC text and older docstrings put two spaces after a period; the second space costs a token (3 sentences: 20 versus 17 o200k tokens). Collapse only in prose lines of 8+ words, never code, tables or indentation.
test: Count period-plus-two-spaces-plus-capital hits per 1k tokens in man, --help, RFC and docstring outputs; apply the guarded collapse; compare count_tokens; diff to confirm code and table lines are untouched.
because: collapse double spaces in prose
check: Two or more spaces after . ! or ? and before a capital letter become one space, only inside prose lines (8+ words, mostly plain words, no tab, pipe or alignment gap); indentation, code, tables and option lists are byte-identical.
check_loses: the second space after a sentence end in prose lines

title: Drop long timezone names and monotonic tails from date strings
detail: JS Date.toString appends '(Central European Standard Time)' after GMT+0100 (23 versus 17 o200k tokens); Go time.Time String appends 'm=+0.012345678' (28 versus 19). Both tails are redundant or noise. Strip them, keep offset and instant.
test: Grep saved Node, Go test and Java logs for GMT offsets followed by a zone name, and for ' m=+'; strip; verify parsed instants match; compare count_tokens.
because: strips redundant timezone names from date strings

title: Unicode block token-fertility atlas via count_tokens batches
detail: Probe Claude's tokenizer over BMP blocks in 64-char batches and record tokens per char. Yields a table of expensive blocks (rare scripts, symbols, presentation forms) to prioritise rules, price non-ASCII text in the hook gate, and find cheaper equivalents. Extends #621 beyond ASCII classes.
test: Batch 64 chars per count_tokens call with a one-token delimiter, subtract the delimiter baseline, run 200 blocks; compare with the o200k proxy; list blocks above 2 tokens per char.
because: dev-time tokenizer fertility atlas

title: Lowercase uppercase-hex runs in addresses, thumbprints and GUIDs
detail: Uppercase-hex producers (PowerShell Get-FileHash, keytool fingerprints) merge worse in BPE. Measured o200k proxy: 16-digit addresses 246 to 234 tokens, SHA-1 478 to 473, GUID and MAC about flat. Gate on 8+ digit runs; the saved original keeps the case.
test: Generate matched upper and lower hex sets of 8 to 64 digits; count_tokens on Claude; if the gain is under 3% drop the idea, else grep a corpus.
because: lowercases hex runs; tokenizer-general, tiny gain

title: SessionStart and CwdChanged write toolchain-specific quiet env via CLAUDE_ENV_FILE
detail: Claude Code sources $CLAUDE_ENV_FILE before Bash commands (seen in binary strings). A SessionStart hook, and reportedly CwdChanged, detects package.json, pyproject.toml or Cargo.toml and appends only matching quiet exports. Static settings env cannot vary per repo or directory. Differs from #193.
test: Verify that a fresh Bash call sees exports written to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE and that cd updates them. Per toolchain, run 10 common commands with and without; diff bytes and exit codes.
because: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE and SessionStart hook

title: ConfigChange hook defers mid-session edits that rewrite the cached prefix
detail: ConfigChange fires when settings or skills files change, with source and file_path. A git branch switch or plugin sync may alter the skill list or tools mid-session and force a cold cache write. Hook logs it and, if blocking is honored, defers it.
test: Verify that ConfigChange fires. At 100k context, edit a skill file and a settings file mid-session; read next-turn cache_creation tokens (#437). Then test whether exit code 2 stops the reload.
because: ConfigChange hook

title: UserPromptExpansion gate for slash-command bodies already in context
detail: Typed slash commands re-expand their whole body every time; UserPromptExpansion receives command_name, args and source. Hash expanded bodies per session; when unchanged and still in context, block with a pointer to the earlier turn. #242 covers only model-called Skills.
test: Verify that UserPromptExpansion fires and can block. Census transcripts for slash commands expanded twice in a session; sum repeated body tokens. Check the user keeps a cheap way to proceed.
because: UserPromptExpansion hook and slash commands

title: Probe which hook events see user-typed bash-mode commands
detail: User ! commands enter context as bash-input and bash-stdout tags (strings in the binary), reportedly with no PostToolUse event. #158 and #916 cover related channels only. Find any event that sees their output and whether it can be rewritten.
test: Verify that a 10k-line ! command is visible to a logging hook on every event; record which events fire and whether next-request tokens change after any rewrite.
because: probes which hook events see bash-mode commands

title: Hook-supplied sessionTitle to skip the title-generation side call
detail: SessionStart and UserPromptExpansion output accept sessionTitle (schema text in the binary), and the binary also contains a small-model title prompt. A title from branch name or ticket id may let the host skip that call; #1043 only reroutes it.
test: Verify that sessionTitle is honored. With the logging proxy (#187), count small-model requests across 20 new sessions with and without a hook-set title; confirm the title shows.
because: SessionStart hook output field

title: PreToolUse appends a brevity clause to WebFetch prompts
detail: WebFetch returns a small model's answer to the prompt Claude wrote, so its size follows that prompt. updatedInput can append 'omit navigation, boilerplate and marketing; keep code verbatim'. Shrinks at the source, unlike #1317 stubs for repeats.
test: Replay 30 recorded WebFetch URL and prompt pairs with and without the clause; compare result tokens and whether the needed facts survive versus the unclipped answer.
because: relies on WebFetch's internal small-model summarizer

title: Move tool-specific CLAUDE.md bullets into once-per-session PreToolUse hints
detail: PreToolUse output accepts additionalContext. Bullets like 'run pytest with -x -q' ride in every request; a hook can inject each on the first matching command, tracked by a seen-set. Bullets for tools never run cost nothing. Differs from skills or scoped rules (#153).
test: Verify that PreToolUse additionalContext reaches the model. Take 5 tool-specific bullets from a real CLAUDE.md; compare input tokens over 10 sessions and whether the agent follows each rule.
because: CLAUDE.md bullets moved into PreToolUse hook hints

title: Map context segments by which hook event can rewrite them
detail: Classify every transcript segment (Bash/MCP result, Read, Agent result, bash-input, local-command, system-reminder, skill body, attachment) as rewritable at PostToolUse, steerable only at PreToolUse, observe-only, or unreachable. Totals show the savings ceiling left outside the hook.
test: Parse 20 transcripts, count tokens per segment class with count_tokens, then check each class against the hook schema in the installed binary.
because: maps segments by harness hook event

title: Budget feedback hook: tool-call counter and one-shot token nudge
detail: Budget-Aware Tool-Use (Google, 2025) reportedly finds that showing calls used and remaining makes agents stop earlier or pick cheaper tools. A PostToolUse additionalContext line ('calls 7/30') does this in headless runs; a per-prompt meter can add one nudge past a token threshold. Differs from #1032.
test: In 15 headless claude -p tasks, compare no line, a calls counter, and a one-shot nudge at 300k tokens: tool calls, billed tokens and pass rate, counting the added tokens.
because: call-counter line appended to tool results

title: Incremental transcript tailer so stateful hooks stay under 50 ms
detail: Ledger, fill-aware and cold-cache ideas each re-parse the session JSONL on every call (#146), and it grows to tens of megabytes. Persist a per-session byte offset, inode and running state; read only appended lines; rebuild on truncation or branch rewind.
test: Time full parse versus tail-read on a 50 MB transcript; fuzz truncation, rewind and concurrent appends, asserting state identical to a full rebuild.
because: tails product's private session JSONL transcript

title: Hoist repeated subschemas in tool schemas into $defs
detail: Jet Cab request_booking repeats its entire ride-field schema inside additionalRides.items, enums and patterns included. Hoist nested, cross-tool and template-family duplicates into one $defs entry referenced by $ref in a tools/list proxy. Unlike #635, this targets structure, not description text.
test: Dump both booking servers' schemas, tokenise nested duplicate subtrees, rewrite with $defs, run 20 booking prompts including multi-ride, and compare argument validity and tool choice.
because: tools/list proxy hoists duplicate subschemas

title: Validation-keyword diet with error-triggered constraint restore
detail: Drop pattern, min/maxLength, minimum/maximum, uniqueItems and zero-value defaults that servers re-check; booking schemas repeat the HH:MM regex several times. A synthetic email regex cost 65 o200k tokens versus 5 for format:email. A proxy re-adds the violated constraint to validation errors.
test: Count validation-keyword tokens across 3 installed servers, strip them, send 30 boundary-value prompts (overlong note, bad time) and count calls where the error text lets the model self-correct.
because: proxy trims validation keywords, restores on error

title: Round-trip aliases for long opaque tokens in MCP results
detail: Signed quote tokens can reach 2,048 chars; a 400-char random base64 token cost 263 o200k tokens against 2 for an alias, paid in the result, echoed call argument and history. A hook aliases it; PreToolUse updatedInput expands it. Unlike #101, covers the call round trip.
test: Capture get_quote results, tokenise the tokens, prototype alias plus expansion against a stub server (never real place_order), run 10 quote-to-booking flows checking the server receives the identical token.
because: proxy aliases tokens and expands them in call arguments
check: A PostToolUse hook replaces opaque 64+ char tokens in MCP results with ⟦tN⟧ (stable per token, state in a file, literal ⟦ doubled) and a PreToolUse hook expands them in call arguments, so a stub server receives the identical token in 10 quote-to-booking flows; unknown aliases are denied and unreadable state fails open to raw results.

title: Fill token-bound request fields from the previous call
detail: A signed quoteToken binds journey, vehicle, passengers, options and fare, yet request_booking demands the ride fields again, costing output and schema tokens. Servers could take token plus contact only; otherwise PreToolUse copies fields from the get_quote input. Unlike #1002, the source is the previous call.
test: Count output tokens and schema tokens of ride fields in recorded booking calls; on a stub server verify token-only or hook-filled requests produce identical bookings across 10 flows.
because: PreToolUse copies fields between tool calls

title: ToolSearch recall at k under schema and description edits
detail: Deferred tools are reportedly found by keyword ranking over names and descriptions, so shrinking descriptions can hide a tool. Gate #644 assumes the tool is already loaded and cannot see this. Measure whether the intended tool still ranks in the top 5 per edit.
test: Write 3 natural queries per tool, run ToolSearch keyword mode on a toy server with original versus edited descriptions, compare recall@5 and count wrong-schema fetches.
because: Claude Code ToolSearch deferred-tool ranking

title: Hide tools the credential or account type cannot call
detail: Org-only, scope-gated or feature-gated tools (teams, issue types and fields, secret scanning, Actions) still cost a schema for a personal repo with a narrow token. Probe get_me and token scopes at launch; deny what cannot succeed. GitHub's server reportedly filters by PAT scope already.
test: List GitHub tools, map each to required scope or org-only, tokenise the unreachable schemas, then call each read-only tool once on a personal repo and count 403 or 404 results.
because: proxy hides tools the credential cannot call

title: Sentence-level dedupe across server instructions, tool and parameter text
detail: The booking servers state consent rules in instructions, the request_booking description, and the quoteToken and acceptedTerms text. Keep one canonical copy of each sentence per server, with consent guards pinned at the call site; drop paraphrased repeats. Rule counterpart of census #1271.
test: Shingle-overlap three servers' instructions plus schemas, remove repeats, then run 20 prompts where the customer has not approved the total and check the model still refuses to book.
because: sentence dedupe across instructions and tool text

title: Delta-debug tool schemas against a generated tool-choice suite
detail: Run ddmin (Zeller's delta debugging) over a tool's description sentences, properties and keywords: delete a span, rerun the #644 prompt suite with a cheap model, keep deletions that change no tool choice or argument. Yields the smallest passing schema per tool instead of hand-written rules.
test: Apply to one 15-parameter tool with 20 generated prompts; report minimal schema tokens and which deleted spans a larger held-out prompt set flags as regressions.
because: offline ddmin yields smaller static schemas

title: Concept-coverage greedy line selection, classifier-free extractive summariser
detail: Gillick and Favre (2009) and Lin and Bilmes (2011) summarise by greedily maximising idf-weighted coverage of digit-masked word bigrams per character cost, with diminishing returns. A knapsack selector for repetitive logs and docs; unlike MMR-decayed classifier scores (#164) or centrality (#650).
test: On 40 saved logs with planted needle lines, compare needle recall and QA at equal chars against the classifier at 0.5, TextRank and head/tail; report milliseconds per 10k chars.
because: classifier-free extractive selection, deterministic

title: Round-trip-verified synthesised encoders for MCP and CLI output
detail: A coding model writes an encode/decode pair from about 10 captures of one tool; accept only if decode(encode(x)) equals x byte for byte on held-out captures and tokens drop. Lossless counterpart of lossy synthesis (#646); the decoder is only a proof.
test: For 10 MCP tools or CLIs, synthesise from 10 captures; report held-out round-trip pass rate, tokens saved against hand-written columnar encoding (#32), and reader QA parity.
because: offline-synthesised encoders; runtime is local code
check: The acceptance gate takes an encode/decode pair and held-out captures and accepts it only if decode(encode(x)) equals x byte for byte on every capture (deterministic, no exceptions, enough captures) and tokens drop by at least 10%: it accepts a correct pair and rejects one that mangles a rare input (a float spelled 2.0) when that input is in the held-out set; a per-call round-trip check protects live traffic when the held-out set missed it.

title: Maintainer reply-quote labels from GitHub issues with pasted logs
detail: In public issues, fenced log or error blocks followed by replies that quote lines give human-chosen relevance labels, independent of the LLM teacher. Quoted lines become keep labels. Different from LogChunks CI spans (#749) and agent-derived labels (#169). Check licences first.
test: Sample 300 issues with fenced blocks over 1,000 chars; count replies quoting a line, then compare classifier line recall on quoted versus random lines at 0.5.
because: public issue replies mined as labels, offline

title: Notebook cell outputs labelled by values reused in later cells
detail: Public permissively licensed notebooks pair code with real stdout, tracebacks and DataFrame prints. Atoms an author later retypes in code or markdown become keep labels; never-reused spans become drop evidence. A data source with natural command-output pairs, outside the agent-trajectory sets.
test: Sample 500 notebook outputs over 2,000 chars; report share with reused spans, and classifier recall of reused atoms at 0.5 versus length-matched random atoms. Check dataset licences.
because: public notebooks mined as labels, offline

title: Universal line-drop decision list distilled from classifier line decisions
detail: Fit an interpretable rule list or shallow tree (RIPPER, Cohen 1995) on line-shape features: digit share, indent, first-token class, severity word, repeat count, position. Labels are classifier line-drop rates across all families. Model-free fallback for unseen commands, unlike per-family tables (#261, #1013).
test: Leave one command family out per fold; report rule precision on needle lines, chars removed, and agreement with classifier line drops, against the classifier at 0.5 and the family table.
because: model-free rule list on line features

title: Column-name-annotated scorer input for tables, CSV and logfmt
detail: Build a virtual twin of a table where each cell is prefixed by its column header (status=Running), score that, and map scores back to the original atoms; output text stays untouched, so bare cells carry meaning. Differs from #557, #962, #1280.
test: On 30 docker ps, kubectl get, ps and CSV outputs, compare column-value QA and per-column keep consistency at 0.5, annotated versus plain scoring, zero-shot and after a short fine-tune.
because: scorer input twin built from the text, deterministic

title: Keyphrase sketch inside elision markers for deleted line runs
detail: Where whole lines vanish, insert '[-37 lines: ECONNRESET, retry, 3 hosts]' listing the top idf-weighted terms of the deleted block. The agent can judge relevance and grep an exact term. Beyond counts-only markers (#269) and column stats on row folds (#1321).
test: Ask questions about deleted facts on 30 logs: compare refetch rate, confident-wrong rate and total tokens for no marker, count-only and keyphrase markers at equal marker budget.
because: deterministic elision marker text

title: Clause and parenthetical units for prose deletion, not atoms
detail: For READMEs, issue and PR text, delete whole syntactic constituents (parentheticals, appositives, trailing clauses, per Filippova and Strube 2008 dependency-tree compression) ranked by mean atom score. Avoids ungrammatical splices and flipped negations. Lightweight option: punctuation-delimited clauses, no parser.
test: On 50 issue and PR bodies, compare splice-error rate (LLM judge) and QA at equal tokens: atom deletion versus clause units versus spaCy-subtree units; note latency.
because: clause-level deletion on text, deterministic

title: Mine log templates and levels from tool source code
detail: Parse logger and printf format strings from an installed CLI's package source to get exact line templates with severity, no sample outputs needed. Debug and info templates become drop candidates, error ones never-drop. A quick scan of pip found about 470 logger calls with levels.
test: For pip, black and one npm CLI, extract templates, match 30 captured runs; report line coverage, level accuracy against observed severity, and chars removable without touching error templates.
because: dev-time template mining feeding deterministic local filters

title: Reader-cited spans from Claude's Citations feature as keep labels
detail: Feed a tool output as a document with citations enabled in the Anthropic API plus a real question; the character ranges the reader cites are production-reader attribution labels. Differs from small-LM ablation (#266), later-quote behaviour (#169) and teacher-written deletions.
test: Verify that cited ranges map back to character offsets. On 100 contexts with questions, collect cited spans and check classifier survival at 0.5 versus gold-span survival; record API cost.
because: dev-time labels via a vendor feature; runtime unaffected

title: Synthesised per-family keep-shield predicates, lower rate for remainder
detail: Instead of full drop filters (#646), a coding model writes a small must-keep predicate per command family (failure lines, summaries, counts) from about 10 captures. Shielded lines are exempt; the classifier then runs at a lower rate on the rest. Unlike generic shield (#91).
test: For pytest, cargo and npm test, synthesise from 10 captures; on 10 held-out measure shield needle recall, then QA and tokens for shield plus rate 0.3 versus plain 0.5.
because: dev-time LLM authored predicates; runtime local and deterministic

title: TTL-edge guard: skip model path when hook latency flips cache
detail: A command ending near the 5-minute cache TTL plus a 2 s hook can push the next request past expiry, rewriting the whole context at 1.25x to save a few thousand tokens. Read last-request time from transcript_path; near the edge, pass through or run lossless-only.
test: From transcripts, collect gaps between consecutive assistant requests; count those within hook latency below 300 s; price each flip's rewrite against that call's saved tokens.
because: vendor 5-minute prompt cache TTL

title: Oracle last-reference eviction ceiling for aging and stub rules
detail: Rent on a tool result after its last later mention (shared path, id or number in assistant text or tool inputs) is pure waste. Summing 0.1x per remaining request bounds every age-based stub or decay idea before any is built.
test: For each tool_result in session JSONLs, find the last later request sharing a rare identifier; sum 0.1x tokens times requests after it; report dollars and share of bill.
because: last-reference eviction ceiling analysis

title: Yield-per-millisecond scheduler for the deterministic pre-pass rules
detail: With hundreds of lossless rules, run time adds up on every large output. Profile bytes saved per millisecond per rule, run in that order under a fixed budget, and gate each rule behind a cheap sniff so non-matching ones cost near zero.
test: Time each rule on a 200-output corpus with perf_counter; compute savings per ms; simulate a 30 ms budget in yield order versus run-all and report lost savings.
because: local rule-engine scheduling optimisation

title: Learned bail-out predictor gates the model path from ledger
detail: Outputs whose ratio lands at 0.95 or above are rejected after seconds of model work. Log the ratio with cheap features (command family, zlib ratio, unique-line share, char classes); a small tree predicts bail-outs and skips the model, going beyond protected share (#834).
test: Record ratio plus features for 500 hook runs; fit a depth-3 tree; report false-skip rate (predicted bail-out but model would cut over 10 percent) against seconds saved.
because: local predictor skips model path
check: A depth-3 tree over cheap features, fitted on a canonically ordered ledger, gives a byte-identical model for any row order and skips the model only in a pure all-bail leaf for a command family seen 30+ times (never for unseen or rare families, a thin ledger, the audit sample or on any error), with zero false skips on held-out inputs, and after drift the first audited contradiction vetoes the family until 30 consecutive bails are logged.

title: Evidence grade stamped on every reported saving figure
detail: Each number in a receipt or README carries a grade: A measured by count_tokens or usage delta, B tokenizer proxy such as o200k, C chars divided by four. Headline shows grade A only, with B and C as bracketed extras, so claims cannot silently inflate.
test: Compute one recorded session's savings at all three grades; report the spread, and list result types where chars/4 misses the measured count by over 25 percent.
because: evidence-grade labelling of savings figures

title: Price-book drift canary: dated ratios checked against published pricing
detail: Every dollar claim rests on cache read, write, TTL and output multipliers. Store them in one dated table; doctor and CI parse the published pricing page and warn on a mismatch or a table older than 60 days, instead of silently reporting stale dollars.
test: Parse the current pricing page into ratios, unit-test that a perturbed ratio fails the check, and test that a table dated 90 days ago warns.
because: price-book staleness check

title: Week-over-week bill movers: decompose spend into drivers
detail: Split each week's transcript spend into session count, requests per session, static prefix size, tool-result tokens, cache-miss rewrites and model mix, then name the biggest mover. Shows whether the next saving is compression, config trimming or cache habits. Time-series counterpart of #271.
test: Bucket local transcripts by ISO week, run a log-ratio decomposition, and check that a known change (MCP server added, CLAUDE.md edited, per git log) appears as the static-prefix mover.
because: spend decomposition from Claude Code transcripts

title: Prevalence-first triage: detector per idea over local transcripts
detail: Give each listed idea a three-line detector (regex or predicate on a tool result). Run all detectors over saved transcripts to get hit rate times token mass, rank the build order by measured prevalence, and park zero-hit ideas.
test: Write detectors for 20 [L] and [R] ideas, scan ~/.claude/projects results, and check the top-ranked three save more tokens on replay than three picked at random.
because: detectors over local Claude Code transcripts

title: Break-even size above which a small-model digest beats pruning
detail: A cheap model reading raw output costs once at input price plus digest output; pruning leaves about half the tokens to be re-read every turn. Solve for the size and survival turns where an opt-in query-conditioned digest wins, keeping the saved original.
test: Price both paths from the published price table over 20k to 200k chars and 5 to 50 surviving turns; mark where digest wins and the share of real outputs there.
because: break-even cost analysis, no runtime mechanism

title: Drop volatile billing-header line from system prompt behind gateways
detail: Binary builds an x-anthropic-billing-header system line with cc_version and, on first-party, a per-turn cc_prev_msg id. Unknown whether gateways or local servers strip it; if not, byte-level prefix caches (KV, Bedrock) miss every turn. Proxy removes it, or set CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0.
test: Verify that the env var exists. Diff system[0] of two consecutive requests via a passthrough proxy; run a llama.cpp or vLLM backend with and without the line; compare cache hits.
because: proxy strips volatile system-prompt line
check: Removing the x-anthropic-billing-header line (strict format, system[0] only, never for a first-party upstream) lets a prefix cache reuse the shared history instead of nothing, whether the header varies per turn or per session, and leaves the other system blocks, tools and messages unchanged; whether a given gateway strips it is not testable offline.

title: Wire-format matrix: Bedrock and Vertex routes versus proxy rewrites
detail: Binary supports ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL and Vertex routes, whose bodies and streams reportedly differ from /v1/messages (model in URL, AWS event-stream framing, betas in body). Mark which proxy ideas need per-route adapters, and whether context-management and 1h caching exist there.
test: Set CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK with ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL on a logging server; capture one turn; diff path, headers, body fields and stream framing against a first-party capture.
because: wire-format compatibility matrix

title: Proxy fail-open: replay original body after upstream 400
detail: History rewrites can orphan a tool_result or break thinking-block signatures, giving a 400 that stalls the session. Claude Code itself resends once without the context-1m beta on rejection (binary string). Proxy replays the unmodified body once and disables the failing rule for that session.
test: Make the rewriter emit an orphaned tool_result on purpose. Assert the client gets a normal response, the log shows exactly one fallback, and later requests skip that rule.
because: proxy fail-open; disabling a rule changes earlier history

title: Buffering rewrite proxy versus client idle timeouts and billed retries
detail: A proxy that buffers a message to edit tool_use arguments delays bytes. The binary has API_TIMEOUT_MS, API_FORCE_IDLE_TIMEOUT and CLAUDE_BYTE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS. A timeout makes the client resend the whole prefix, possibly billed again. Measure time-to-first-byte added and retry rate per rule.
test: Add 5, 30 and 90 second artificial buffering delays in a passthrough proxy; count client retries and requests whose usage appears twice in the upstream log.
because: proxy latency and retry measurement

title: Extended prompt-cache retention for OpenAI-format agents via gateway
detail: Reportedly OpenAI offers prompt_cache_retention up to 24h, and Gemini explicit cached content with a TTL, against default caches lasting minutes. For Codex or Aider sessions with long idle gaps a gateway injects them, extending #289's key pinning to retention, as #283 does for Claude.
test: Verify that prompt_cache_retention is accepted. Send one 5k-token prefix to a GPT-class model after a 15-minute gap with and without retention set; compare cached_tokens in usage.
because: OpenAI and Gemini cache retention API features

title: Team gateway on one workspace key shares cached prefixes
detail: Anthropic caches are reportedly isolated per workspace. Developers in separate workspaces each pay a cold write of system prompt, tools and CLAUDE.md for the same repo. A team gateway on one key, with canonicalised env block and date, lets the second developer read it.
test: Verify that caches are workspace-scoped. Two machines, same checkout: compare cache_read_input_tokens on the second machine's first request via a shared gateway key versus separate workspaces.
because: Anthropic workspace-level cache isolation

title: Audit gateway cost fields for 1h writes and premium tiers
detail: #1042 trusts gateway spend logs as billed truth. Gateways may price every cache write at the 5m rate, collapse write and read splits, or ignore premium tiers (reportedly in some versions). Recompute cost from raw usage and published rates first.
test: Send one request with a 1h cache write and one over 200K input through the gateway; compare its logged cost with a hand computation from the raw usage JSON.
because: gateway cost-field audit

title: Set hook threshold from the backend's real context window
detail: Agents behind gateways on Ollama, llama.cpp or vLLM may run with far less context than hosted models; Ollama reportedly defaults small and truncates from the front. Set CTXPRUNE_MIN_CHARS and keep rate from the served window, not constants.
test: Serve a small-context model; run one agent task with and without the hook; log prompt_eval_count against tokens sent, and note silent truncation and task success.
because: threshold config from context window, no server control

title: Run non-urgent headless agent turns through Message Batches
detail: A price lever, not a token cut: Batches reportedly bill half, and #673 uses them only for evals. SDK loops for nightly review or cron agents tolerate latency; each turn becomes a one-request batch with tool execution between. Cache discounts reportedly stack, best effort.
test: Run a 10-turn SDK task both ways; compare wall time, cache-read share and billed cost from usage fields.
because: Anthropic Message Batches API, price lever

title: Atomizer is quadratic on long trailing whitespace runs
detail: Verified here: atomize() on 1,500 words plus 2k, 4k and 8k trailing spaces took 0.10, 0.36 and 1.5 s, about 4x per doubling. The leading-whitespace group of the atom regex rescans the tail from every start, so 64k would pass a 60 s hook timeout.
test: Time atomize on 'word '*1500 plus N trailing spaces, N up to 64k; assert under 0.5 s after rstripping the tail before the regex and re-adding it as one atom.
because: atomizer performance fix, output unchanged

title: Probe hook stdout size caps and ensure_ascii inflation
detail: hook.py writes json.dumps(out) with ensure_ascii on, so CJK or emoji text grows 6x or more on stdout. Claude Code reportedly caps hook-injected text near 10,000 chars. Whether updatedToolOutput has a cap is unknown; large replacements may be truncated or ignored.
test: Have a stub hook return updatedToolOutput of 8k, 12k, 50k, 200k chars, ASCII and CJK; log what the model receives. Repeat with ensure_ascii=False.
because: hook stdout caps and encoding

title: Shield host truncation markers from word deletion
detail: If the host or a tool inserts a marker such as '[N lines truncated]' or '... output truncated' before the hook runs, words like 'truncated' and 'omitted' are unprotected and can be deleted. The agent then believes the output is complete. Force-keep marker lines.
test: Run a Bash command printing 40k chars so the host truncates, apply the real hook, check the marker text survives; add marker regexes to the protect set.
because: force-keep truncation marker lines

title: Note-to-output attribution when several results are compressed
detail: The note says only 'this Bash output' plus a hash path and arrives as separate additionalContext. With three large parallel results the agent may grep the wrong original or assume the note refers to the last result. Check placement, then consider a command stub.
test: Fire three parallel Bash calls with distinct large outputs, ask a question answerable only from output two's original, and record which saved file the agent opens.
because: hook additionalContext note placement issue

title: Atoms no subword touches default to score 0.0, dropped first
detail: compress.py gives atoms with zero token hits a score of 0.0, so characters the tokenizer normalises away or emits no offsets for always rank last and are deleted first, even when meaningful. Unverified for the real tokenizer. A fail-safe default would keep them.
test: Run atom_scores over saved real outputs; list atoms with no token touching them and their characters; check whether pass/fail glyphs or box rails land there; try default 1.0.
because: fail-safe default in scoring, deterministic

title: Gate on output shape for diffs and numbered source
detail: In a hand-made sample of 26 agent-style commands, VERBATIM_CMD skipped 6, yet 'git -C x diff', 'diff -u', 'tail', 'rg -C' and 'grep -A' still reach compression. Gate on output shape instead: diff hunk headers, path:line: runs. Complements regex fixes #292 and #676.
test: Replay recorded Bash outputs; count those with 3+ '@@ -a,b +c,d @@' headers or mostly 'path:NN:' lines that the command regex let through to compression.
because: gate on output shape instead of command regex

title: Contrastive conditional perplexity: command-conditioned small-LM atom scoring
detail: LongLLMLingua (Jiang et al., 2023) scores tokens by how much prepending the question lowers perplexity. Run a ~135M causal LM twice, with and without the Bash command plus description as question; keep atoms the command makes likelier. Unlike #260 and #1144.
test: On 30 recorded outputs, compute the log-ratio score on CPU; compare kept-line recall for lines later quoted in Edit or Grep versus the classifier at equal tokens; log seconds.
because: small local CPU LM scoring with command string

title: Param and field pack for Tavily, Exa, Firecrawl, Brave MCPs
detail: Web search and scrape MCP servers reportedly return per-hit raw page text, images, favicons, scores and dates by default. PreToolUse sets cheap params (no raw content, small result count, main-content-only, highlights not full text); PostToolUse drops image, favicon and score fields.
test: Verify param names in each server's tools/list. Run 10 queries per server with defaults versus trimmed; compare response tokens and whether the answer-bearing sentence survives; count follow-up fetches.
because: field dropping generic; param rewrite via proxy on tool_use

title: Cache cost of per-turn tool-menu narrowing versus masking
detail: Manus's context-engineering post (2025) warns that adding or removing tools mid-run invalidates the KV cache since tool definitions sit at the prefix start, and masks logits instead. #1305 does not price this; weigh the cache rewrite against schema tokens saved.
test: Simulate with recorded usage: 40-turn session, tool set changed every turn versus every 10 turns versus never; compute cache_creation at 1.25x versus tokens saved from the smaller schemas.
because: cost analysis of tool narrowing versus cache rewrite

title: Workflow cards induced from green runs, Agent Workflow Memory style
detail: Agent Workflow Memory (Wang et al., 2024) induces reusable workflows from successful trajectories. A SessionEnd job extracts ordered tool-call skeletons ending in a passing test or commit, replaces paths with slots, and keeps recurring ones as skills matched by description, so later tasks skip exploration.
test: From 30 transcripts of one repo, extract skeletons and count recurrence across sessions; for recurring ones, sum tokens of exploration calls before the first Edit that a card would replace.
because: SessionEnd job and skills

title: Delta-merge memory edits with counters, not full LLM rewrites
detail: Agentic Context Engineering (Zhang et al., 2025) reports wholesale LLM rewrites of a playbook lose detail (brevity bias, context collapse). Store CLAUDE.md or memory as id-tagged bullets; consolidation emits only keep, merge or drop ops by id. Guards #877, #1062.
test: Take a 150-line CLAUDE.md; have Haiku produce a full rewrite versus id-level ops; compare tokens kept and accuracy on 20 probe questions about commands and paths in the original.
because: CLAUDE.md memory file consolidation

title: Drop the derivable [ NN%] column from pytest -v result lines
detail: pytest -v ends every result line with a right-aligned '[ 12%]' that equals distinct node ids reported so far x 100 // the 'collected N' total, padded to the width of the '=== test session starts ===' rule (a teardown ERROR repeats an id and does not advance the count). Strip the padding and percent when each line matches that formula and let the decoder recompute it; a mismatching line stays verbatim and a result line with no percent blocks the transform. Measured on a real capture (pytest 9.2, 28 tests, one failure): 795 vs 669 o200k tokens for the whole output, 525 vs 376 for the 29 result lines. Differs from #46, which drops PASSED lines.
test: Capture 20 real pytest -v runs at COLUMNS=80, 120 and 200 (plain, -x, --lf, parametrized, fixtures that error at teardown); encode each; assert decode is byte-exact and count the runs the encoder refuses (xdist, -s, custom plugins); compare o200k tokens; ask the agent which tests failed before and after.
because: re-encodes pytest's derived progress column with no information loss
check: Drops the right-aligned '[ NN%]' column from pytest -v result lines when each equals distinct-ids-so-far*100//collected padded to the width of the session rule, and the decoder recomputes it byte for byte; a result line with a different or missing percentage stays verbatim or blocks the transform.

title: Drop ninja's consecutive [N/M] step counters on pipes
detail: ninja on a non-tty prints '[12/340] Building CXX object ...' where N counts finished steps one by one, so only the first N and M carry information. Write them once in a legend, drop the prefix from step lines and mark the few other lines (warnings, FAILED, errors) with '· '; decode renumbers, and a gap or a restarted counter leaves the text untouched. Measured on real cmake+ninja captures: a clean 33-step build 639 vs 513 o200k tokens, a rebuild with a gcc warning between steps 702 vs 581.
test: Capture 15 real ninja builds from CMake and Meson projects, including -k 0 runs with several FAILED steps and a cancelled build; assert byte-exact decode and that the encoder refuses when the counter restarts or skips; compare o200k tokens; ask which target failed and the first compiler error.
because: re-encodes ninja's running step counter with no information loss
check: ninja's non-tty '[N/M] ' step prefix is dropped (first number and M in the legend, other output marked '· '); decode renumbers the step lines, and a gap, a repeated run or a changed M leaves the text untouched.

title: ctest results: fold Start lines, drop k/M counters and dot leaders
detail: ctest prints 'Start  9: name' and then ' 3/12 Test  #9: name ........   Passed    0.01 sec': the Start line repeats the result line below it, k/M is the running count and the dot leader pads the name to one width W. Fold an adjacent pair into '#9 name   Passed ...', keep M and W in the legend and re-derive the rest; Start lines separated from their result by -j keep their place. Measured on real captures (cmake 3.28, 12 tests, one failing): serial 500 vs 300 o200k tokens, ctest -j4 500 vs 446.
test: Capture ctest runs of 10, 100 and 500 tests with and without -j, --output-on-failure and --repeat; assert byte-exact decode, that a missing line or restarted counter makes the encoder refuse, and the o200k saving per mode; ask which tests failed and their times.
because: re-encodes ctest's Start line, counter and dot padding with no information loss
check: ctest result lines lose the 'k/M' counter and the dot leader, and a 'Start N: name' line directly above its own result line is folded into it; decode re-pads and renumbers exactly. Start lines that are not directly above their result (-j) keep their place, and a counter gap or restarted counter leaves the whole text untouched.

title: unittest -v: print the dotted id once, ditto the class
detail: Python 3.11+ unittest -v prints 'test_add (tests.test_math.TestMath.test_add) ... ok', spelling the method name twice, and repeats the class on every line; FAIL:/ERROR: headers repeat it again. Write 'tests.test_math.TestMath.test_add ... ok' and '~.test_sub ... ok' for the class of the line above; decode restores the name and the exact layout, and the pre-3.11 'name (pkg.Class)' layout is left alone. Measured on a real capture of 24 passing tests: 429 vs 258 o200k tokens (-40%); with one failure and one error in the run, 619 vs 437.
test: Run unittest -v and Django manage.py test -v 2 on 10 real suites of 20 to 500 tests; encode; assert byte-exact decode; count tokens on passing and failing runs; ask which test failed and which class it belongs to.
because: re-encodes unittest's repeated method name and class with no information loss
check: unittest -v lines 'name (pkg.Class.name) ... status' become 'pkg.Class.name ... status' ('~.name' when the class equals the previous line's), and FAIL:/ERROR: headers likewise; decode restores the repeated name, and lines whose id does not end in the name, or the python <=3.10 layout, stay verbatim.

title: cargo test list lines: drop wrappers, ditto the module path
detail: libtest prints 'test parser::lexer::tests::scans_ident ... ok' for every test, repeating 'test', ' ... ' and the module path; threads reorder neighbours only slightly, so runs from one module are common. Write 'parser::lexer::tests::scans_ident ok' and '~::scans_number ok' for the module of the line above; names with spaces (doc-tests) and test lines with no '::' stay verbatim, and decode restores the wrappers. Measured on a real 30-test capture: the 31 'test ...' lines 430 vs 317 o200k tokens; the whole output (one panic with a backtrace) 1,060 vs 947.
test: Run cargo test on 5 real workspaces (100 to 2,000 tests, default threads and --test-threads=1, with --show-output and --report-time); assert byte-exact decode; measure the share of lines that get a ditto and the o200k saving; ask which tests failed.
because: re-encodes libtest list lines with no information loss
check: cargo test list lines 'test P::n ... status' are written 'P::n status' ('~::n' when the module path equals the line above's); decode restores the 'test' and '...' wrappers and the path exactly, and doc-test names with spaces or top-level tests with no '::' stay verbatim.

title: Rust backtraces: join 'at' lines, hoist the /rustc/<hash> prefix
detail: RUST_BACKTRACE=1 prints each frame as '  3: core::option::unwrap_failed' plus a 13-space-indented 'at /rustc/<40 hex>/library/core/src/option.rs:2248:5' line, and the toolchain commit hash repeats on every std frame. Join them as '  3: sym @ loc' and write the prefix as §R/ with the hash in the legend once; decode splits the lines and restores the prefix, and the RUST_BACKTRACE=full layout is left alone. Measured on a real cargo run panic (rustc 1.97): 524 vs 381 o200k tokens for the whole output, 417 vs 275 for the 9 frames.
test: Collect 30 real panics and failing cargo tests with RUST_BACKTRACE=1 from tokio, serde and CLI projects (std and app frames); assert byte-exact decode and count refusals; compare o200k tokens; ask for the first app frame and its file:line.
because: re-encodes Rust frame lines and the repeated toolchain prefix with no information loss
check: Each RUST_BACKTRACE=1 frame '  N: symbol' plus its '             at path:line:col' line(s) becomes one line '  N: symbol @ path:line:col', with the repeated '/rustc/<40 hex>/' toolchain prefix written §R/ and the hash given once in the legend; decode splits the lines and restores the prefix byte for byte, and the RUST_BACKTRACE=full layout is left alone.

title: Maven transfers: join Downloading/Downloaded, show coordinates not URLs
detail: A fresh Maven build prints 'Downloading from central: URL' and then 'Downloaded from central: URL (8.2 kB at 16 kB/s)' for every artifact, and the URL is BASE/group/artifact/version/artifact-version.ext, a function of the coordinates. An adjacent pair becomes one 'Downloaded from central: org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api:5.10.2@pom (...)' line (BASE per repository id in the legend); lone and non-standard lines stay verbatim and decode rebuilds both original lines. Measured on a real first build of a JUnit 5 project (176 downloads, 390 lines): 17,931 vs 8,604 o200k tokens. Lossless counterpart of the drop in #50.
test: Run 10 real mvn builds into empty local repositories (Spring Boot, plain JUnit, multi-module) with -B and without; assert byte-exact decode and count URLs that stay verbatim (snapshots, other layouts); compare o200k tokens; ask which artifact failed to resolve when one is made to 404.
because: re-encodes Maven transfer lines and artifact URLs with no information loss
check: Maven 'Downloading from R: URL' + 'Downloaded from R: URL (size at speed)' pairs become one 'Downloaded' line with 'group:artifact:version@ext' coordinates (BASE per repository id in the legend); a lone Downloading line is shortened in place, a lone Downloaded line and URLs that do not follow BASE/group/artifact/version/artifact-version.ext stay verbatim, and decode restores every URL and both lines exactly.

title: node:test TAP: fold six-line passing-test blocks to one line
detail: node --test (the tap reporter, the default when stdout is not a terminal on node 22) prints '# Subtest: NAME', 'ok N - NAME', '  ---', '  duration_ms: X', "  type: 'test'", '  ...' for every passing test; the Subtest line repeats the name and the YAML frame is constant. Fold to 'ok N - NAME (X ms)' at the same indent and rebuild on decode; failing tests, skips and suites keep their blocks. Measured on real node 22.23 captures: 18 passing tests 746 vs 376 o200k tokens, a mixed run with a failure 591 vs 512.
test: Run node --test on 8 real projects (nested describe, async, 20 to 400 tests) and keep the stdout; assert byte-exact decode; count blocks left unfolded; compare o200k tokens; ask which tests failed and their messages.
because: re-encodes node:test's constant passing-test block with no information loss
check: A passing node:test TAP block of six lines ('# Subtest: N', 'ok k - N', '---', 'duration_ms: X', "type: 'test'", '...') becomes 'ok k - N (X ms)'; decode rebuilds the six lines at the same indent exactly, and failing tests, skips, suites and non-TAP reporters keep their full text.

title: pip 'Requirement already satisfied' runs: group, hoist location and parent
detail: pip install -r on an installed environment prints 'Requirement already satisfied: iniconfig>=2 in /usr/local/lib/python3.13/site-packages (from pytest->-r req.txt (line 1)) (2.3.1)' per package. Group a run into a count header and '  iniconfig>=2 2.3.1' entries, writing 'in LOCATION' and '(from PARENT)' only where they change from the entry above; decode rebuilds every line. Measured on a real 168-line capture: the 31 satisfied lines 1,489 vs 973 o200k tokens, the whole output 5,910 vs 5,448 (Collecting and Downloading lines are untouched). Lossless counterpart of the drop in #49.
test: Capture pip install -r and pip install -e .[dev] on 10 real environments (venv, system, --user); assert byte-exact decode; report the share of lines in runs of two or more and the o200k saving; ask which packages were newly installed.
because: re-encodes pip's already-satisfied lines with no information loss
check: Runs of two or more 'Requirement already satisfied: SPEC in LOCATION (from PARENT) (VERSION)' lines become a header with the location and count plus one '  SPEC VERSION' entry each, '(from PARENT)' written only when the parent changes; decode rebuilds every original line byte for byte, single lines and other pip output stay verbatim.

title: Surefire: fold Running/Tests run pairs into one row per class
detail: Surefire prints '[INFO] Running a.web.AuthFilterTest' and then '[INFO] Tests run: 4, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0, Time elapsed: 0.018 s -- in a.web.AuthFilterTest' per class: the class is spelled twice and the five labels repeat. Fold the pair into '[INFO] 4 0 0 0 0.018s a.web.AuthFilterTest' (level and '<<< FAILURE!' flag kept) with the column names in the legend; decode rebuilds both lines. Measured on a real 7-class surefire 3.2.5 run: the 14 pair lines 371 vs 197 o200k tokens, the whole output (one failure with a stack trace) 1,227 vs 1,053.
test: Run mvn test on 8 real Java projects (JUnit 4 and 5, 20 to 300 classes, some with failing and erroring classes); assert byte-exact decode and count pairs left alone (stdout between the lines); compare o200k tokens; ask which classes failed.
because: re-encodes surefire's per-class pair of lines with no information loss
check: A surefire '[INFO] Running X' line plus the '[LEVEL] Tests run: R, Failures: F, Errors: E, Skipped: S, Time elapsed: T s [<<< FLAG!] -- in X' line right after it become one row '[LEVEL] R F E S Ts X [<<< FLAG!]'; decode rebuilds both lines exactly, and pairs with output in between, a different class name or the surefire 2.x layout stay verbatim.

title: terraform plan/apply -json: rebuild each resource object from its address
detail: terraform plan -json and apply -json print one JSON object per line, and every planned_change, apply_start, apply_progress, apply_complete and refresh line embeds a 7-field resource object (addr, module, resource, implied_provider, resource_type, resource_name, resource_key) of which only addr carries information. Replace each object that follows the address grammar with "resource":"@addr" under a one-line legend; decode regenerates it byte for byte, and an object that does not follow the grammar stays verbatim. Measured on a synthetic fixture (line shape reconstructed from memory of Terraform's machine-readable UI docs): 3,829 vs 2,812 o200k tokens for an 8-resource apply (-27%).
test: Run terraform plan -json and apply -json on 5 real configs (count, for_each, nested modules, data sources, one provider outside the hashicorp namespace); assert decode(encode(x)) == x byte for byte and count the objects left verbatim; compare o200k tokens; ask a reader which resource failed and why from the encoded stream.
because: re-encodes the derivable resource object with no information loss
check: In terraform plan/apply -json lines, each resource object {addr,module,resource,implied_provider,resource_type,resource_name,resource_key} that follows from its addr (module path, data.type.name, [index] or ["key"]) becomes "resource":"@addr" under a one-line legend, and decode rebuilds it byte for byte; an object that does not follow the grammar, and any text with a marker-like "resource":"@, stays verbatim.

title: docker ps, compose ps and docker port: write IPv4 and IPv6 published-port twins once
detail: Since Docker 20.10 a port published on all interfaces prints twice in docker ps, docker compose ps and docker port: '0.0.0.0:8080->80/tcp, [::]:8080->80/tcp' (older engines print ':::8080'). Write the pair as {0.0.0.0,[::]}:8080->80/tcp; decode expands it back exactly, and a lone IPv4 entry, a specific host IP or a mismatched pair stays as it is. Measured on a synthetic fixture (the twins are reconstructed, this host has no IPv6 to capture them): 619 vs 547 o200k tokens for an 8-container docker ps (-12%) and 72 vs 58 for docker port lines; small because the other columns dominate the table.
test: Capture docker ps -a, docker compose ps and docker port on 3 dual-stack hosts (Docker 20.10 to 29); assert decode(encode(x)) == x byte for byte; compare tokens; ask a reader which host ports are reachable over IPv6 from the encoded table.
because: re-encodes duplicate IPv4/IPv6 port entries with no information loss
check: In docker ps, docker compose ps and docker port output, a published port listed on both 0.0.0.0 and :: ([::] or the older :::) with the same host and container port and protocol (ranges included) is written once as {0.0.0.0,[::]}:host->container/proto; decode expands it back byte for byte, and a lone IPv4, a specific host IP, a mismatched pair or any input already containing {0.0.0.0, stays verbatim or escaped.

title: docker compose up and down: one state-chain line per resource
detail: In a non-tty, Compose v5 prints every transition as its own line (' Container shop-db-1 Creating ', Created, Starting, Started, Waiting, Healthy), with resources interleaved and even the network lines repeated. Regroup each run into one line per resource with its states in order joined by '>': ' Container shop-db-1 Creating>Created>Starting>Started>Waiting>Healthy'. Every resource's own sequence and all other lines are unchanged; only the relative order of lines of different resources is lost. Measured on a captured docker compose up -d (Compose v5.6.1, 4 services, one healthcheck): 146 vs 67 o200k tokens (-54%); the matching docker compose down: 130 vs 63 (-52%).
test: Capture compose up, down, start, stop and restart for 5 real stacks (one with a failing healthcheck, one pull-heavy); assert every resource's state sequence is identical before and after; compare tokens; ask a reader which service never became healthy and what waited on it, from the chain form.
because: re-encodes per-resource state lines as one chain, keeping each resource's order
check: In docker compose up/down/start/stop progress (' Container shop-db-1 Creating ' lines), the lines of a run are regrouped into one line per resource with its states in order joined by '>'; every other line and each resource's own sequence of states is unchanged.
check_loses: the relative order of lines belonging to different resources inside one run (which container reported Created before which)

title: CloudFormation JSON: Fn::Join of literals, Ref and GetAtt as one Fn::Sub string
detail: cdk synth --json and aws cloudformation get-template print {"Fn::Join": ["", ["arn:", {"Ref": "AWS::Partition"}, ":s3:::", {"Fn::GetAtt": ["Bucket", "Arn"]}]]} with one part per line. When the delimiter is empty and every part is a non-adjacent literal, a Ref or a two-part GetAtt, write {"Fn::Sub": "arn:${AWS::Partition}:s3:::${Bucket.Arn}"}, which CloudFormation defines as the same value; other Joins stay as they are. Measured on a synthetic cdk-style template (reconstructed from memory): 1,481 vs 1,236 o200k tokens pretty-printed (-17%) and 915 vs 829 minified (-9%); the saving scales with the number of Joins.
test: Run cdk synth --json on 5 real stacks; expand every Sub string back to a Join and diff the parsed templates; count the Joins left untouched and why; compare tokens; ask a reader which resources an IAM statement allows, from the shortened template.
because: re-encodes Fn::Join into the equivalent Fn::Sub with no information loss
check: In pretty or minified CloudFormation JSON, an Fn::Join with an empty delimiter whose parts are non-empty, non-adjacent literals, Ref and two-part Fn::GetAtt becomes {"Fn::Sub": "arn:${AWS::Partition}:...${Bucket.Arn}"}; Joins with other delimiters, Fn::Select or nested parts, adjacent literals or a literal containing ${ stay as they are, and a Sub and the Join it abbreviates compare equal.
check_loses: nothing in the CloudFormation value; JSON layout is rebuilt with the same indent (non-canonical layouts are left untouched), and an Fn::Join and the Fn::Sub string that spells the same value are treated as the same

title: aws s3 sync and gcloud storage cp -r: print the relative path once per file
detail: aws s3 sync, cp and mv print 'upload: dist/assets/a.js to s3://bucket/assets/a.js' per file and gcloud storage cp -r prints 'Copying file://dist/a.js to gs://bucket/a.js': the relative path appears on both sides and both roots repeat on every line. Put the two roots in a one-line header and write 'upload: assets/a.js'; CR progress frames and trailing padding are kept, and lines whose paths differ, failures and delete lines stay verbatim. Measured on a synthetic 12-file sync (line shapes reconstructed from memory): 312 vs 131 o200k tokens (-58%); the same files with CR progress frames: 671 vs 480 (-28%).
test: Capture aws s3 sync, cp --recursive and gcloud storage cp -r for 5 real deploys (200+ files, one with a failure and one with --delete); assert decode(encode(x)) == x byte for byte; compare tokens; ask a reader which files failed to upload from the encoded log.
because: re-encodes the duplicated source and destination paths with no information loss
check: In aws s3 sync/cp/mv and gcloud storage cp output, the source and destination roots shared by the lines are written once in a header, and every 'verb: SRC to DST' line whose two paths end in the same relative path is reduced to 'verb: REL' (CR progress frames and trailing padding kept); lines with a different relative path, failures, delete lines and any text a decoder could misread stay verbatim.

title: Terraform diagnostic boxes: strip the rail from every line
detail: terraform validate, plan and apply print each error and warning in a box that opens with ╷, closes with ╵ and starts every line, blank ones included, with '│ '. Remove the rails and mark the opener '╷:' so decode puts them back byte for byte; a box with an unrailed line is left alone. Measured on a synthetic fixture of four validate boxes (reconstructed from memory): 285 vs 248 o200k tokens (-13%), 920 vs 870 characters; a box with one very long summary line saves less.
test: Collect 20 real terraform validate, plan and apply error outputs (including AWS provider errors with long summaries); assert decode(encode(x)) == x byte for byte; compare tokens and characters; ask a reader which file and line each error points at.
because: re-encodes box rails with no information loss
check: In Terraform diagnostics, a box that opens with a '╷' line, closes with '╵' and has the '│ ' rail on every inner line is rewritten with the rails removed and the opener as '╷:'; decode puts the rails back byte for byte, and a box with an unrailed or doubled-up inner line is left as it is.

title: docker build failure: back-reference the repeated RUN command and log tail
detail: When a BuildKit step fails, plain progress prints the RUN command five times (step header, '#N ERROR: process', ' > [i/m] RUN ...:', the Dockerfile excerpt and the final 'ERROR: failed to build') and prints the last 10 log lines again without the '#N ' prefix. Keep the header and the streamed log, replace the repeats with §N and '§last K lines of #N'; decode expands them byte for byte, and anything that does not match exactly (escaping, a tail that is not the end of the stream, a multi-line RUN excerpt) keeps its text. Measured on two captured failed builds (Docker 29.9.2, buildx 0.38.1, short test commands): 1,379 vs 991 and 791 vs 559 o200k tokens (-28% and -29%); real RUN lines are longer, which this does not measure.
test: Capture 10 real failed docker build and docker compose build runs (apt, npm, pip, multi-stage, heredoc RUN); assert decode(encode(x)) == x byte for byte; count steps left unfolded and why; compare tokens; ask a reader for the failing command and the last error line from the encoded text.
because: re-encodes repeated command and log-tail text as references with no information loss
check: In a failed docker build (BuildKit plain progress), the command of the failing RUN step is written once, in its '#N [i/m] RUN ...' header; its repeats in '#N ERROR: process ...', ' > [i/m] RUN ...:', the Dockerfile excerpt and the final 'ERROR: failed to build' line become §N, and the block of last log lines that duplicates the end of the step's streamed output becomes '§last K lines of #N'; decode expands both byte for byte, and any step that does not match exactly (escaping, tail, multi-line RUN excerpt) keeps its original text.

title: terraform providers schema -json: attribute objects as one-line flag strings
detail: terraform providers schema -json describes every resource attribute as {"type": "string", "optional": true, "computed": true}, plus description and description_kind when the provider has docs; aws_instance alone has about 40 attributes and 3 blocks. Rewrite each leaf made only of those keys as "§string optional computed|description", keeping blocks, nested types, object types and every other key as they are; the parsed document is identical after expanding. Measured on a synthetic aws_instance schema (reconstructed from memory): 2,251 vs 1,159 o200k tokens pretty-printed (-49%) and 1,290 vs 841 compact (-35%).
test: Run terraform providers schema -json for 5 real providers (aws, google, azurerm, random, datadog) and pipe single resources through jq; assert the expanded document equals the original after parsing; count leaves left unfolded and why; compare tokens; ask a reader which attributes of a resource are required and which are computed.
because: re-encodes attribute leaf objects with no information loss
check: In terraform providers schema -json (compact or pretty), each attribute object made only of type (a primitive or list/set/map of one), description, description_kind plain/markdown and true flags (required, optional, computed, sensitive, deprecated) is rewritten as one string '§string optional computed|description'; blocks, nested types, object types, false flags and every other key stay as they are.
check_loses: JSON text layout (re-serialised with the same indent, or minified, and string escapes such as \u003c written as the character) and the order of the flag keys inside a leaf; the parsed document is otherwise identical

title: kubectl config get-contexts: ditto marks for cells equal to the cell on the left
detail: kubectl config get-contexts prints the same long identifier in NAME, CLUSTER and AUTHINFO on EKS (arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:123456789012:cluster/prod), GKE (gke_project_zone_cluster), kind and minikube. Replace a cell equal to its left neighbour by a double quote and keep all spacing; decode copies the left cell back byte for byte. #778 marks repeats down a column; this marks equality along a row. Measured on a synthetic 8-context table (reconstructed; kubectl is not installed here): 242 vs 146 o200k tokens (-40%); a single EKS context 75 vs 39.
test: Collect get-contexts output from 10 real kubeconfigs (EKS, GKE, AKS, kind, minikube, k3d); assert decode(encode(x)) == x byte for byte; compare tokens; ask a reader which context is current and which namespace it targets.
because: re-encodes repeated cells with no information loss
check: In kubectl config get-contexts output, a CLUSTER cell equal to the NAME cell and an AUTHINFO cell equal to the CLUSTER cell are written as a ditto mark ("), with all spacing kept; decode copies the cell on the left back byte for byte, and a table that already uses a literal " cell, or any other text, is left alone or escaped.

title: kubectl get pods --show-labels: replace labels derivable from the pod name or a twin label
detail: Deployment pod rows print pod-template-hash=5d8f7c6b9 beside the name web-5d8f7c6b9-4xk2p; StatefulSet rows add statefulset.kubernetes.io/pod-name and apps.kubernetes.io/pod-index; Job pods carry job-name and controller-uid beside their batch.kubernetes.io twins. Replace each by ~h, ~n, ~i, ~j or ~u in place, only when its value is the derived one; decode restores the line byte for byte. Measured on a synthetic 12-pod table (reconstructed from memory of kubectl's format): 698 vs 579 o200k tokens with the namespace column (-17%) and 589 vs 478 without (-19%).
test: Capture get pods --show-labels (with and without -A and -o wide) on 5 real clusters; assert decode(encode(x)) == x byte for byte; count labels kept because the value was not the derived one; compare tokens; ask a reader to build the selector that matches one Deployment's pods.
because: re-encodes derivable labels as markers with no information loss
check: In kubectl get pods --show-labels output, labels derivable from the pod name or a sibling label are replaced in place by ~h (pod-template-hash equal to the name's middle part), ~n (statefulset.kubernetes.io/pod-name equal to the name), ~i (apps.kubernetes.io/pod-index equal to the name's number), ~j and ~u (the legacy job-name and controller-uid beside their batch.kubernetes.io twins); a label whose value is not the derived one is kept, and decode restores the line byte for byte.
