title: GitHub REST user, repo and comment objects: elide template-derived URLs, node_id and _links twins
detail: gh api and curl payloads (pulls/N, pulls/N/comments, issues/N/comments) embed user objects whose 13 URL fields and node_id are fixed functions of login and id, repository objects (head.repo, base.repo) whose 42 URL templates are functions of full_name, a _links object that restates sibling url fields, and all-zero reactions. Replace each run that matches its template exactly with one marker pair under a '§ghrest' header (node_id is base64 of 'NN:Type<id>' or a msgpack form, checked per object); decode regenerates the bytes and any object that does not match stays literal. Measured on a reconstructed fixture (written from memory of the documented responses, not captured from the live API): a 22.5 KB pulls/N payload 6,344 vs 2,225 o200k tokens, review comments 2,660 vs 1,514. #34 and #131 drop these fields as rules; this keeps them re-derivable.
test: Capture gh api repos/O/R/pulls/N, pulls/N/comments and issues/N/comments from 5 public repos (fork PRs, bot authors, old and new accounts); encode; assert decode(encode(x)) == x byte for byte; count how many user and repo objects fail the templates (GHES hosts, bots, custom avatars); compare o200k tokens; ask a reader who reviewed which file, who is requested to review, and the head repo's full name.
because: re-encodes URL fields that are fixed functions of login, id and full_name with no information loss
check: In a GitHub REST document, a user object whose 13 URL fields (and legacy or msgpack-style node_id) are the fixed functions of login and id, a repository object whose 42 URL fields are functions of full_name, a _links object that restates sibling url fields, and an all-zero reactions summary are each replaced by one short marker; a '§ghrest' header marks the encoding and decode restores the exact bytes.

title: GitHub REST file entries: derive blob_url, raw_url, contents_url and changes
detail: pulls/N/files and commit file lists repeat, in every entry, blob_url, raw_url and contents_url, each embedding the same owner/repo, 40-hex head sha and URL-encoded filename, plus changes equal to additions plus deletions. The first entry keeps blob_url as the reference; later entries drop all three URLs and every entry drops changes, under a '§ghfiles' header; decode rebuilds them and anything that does not follow the template stays literal. Measured on a reconstructed fixture with small patches: 7 entries 1,749 vs 827 o200k tokens, 8 entries without patches 1,595 vs 535; real patches dilute the saving.
test: Capture pulls/N/files for 10 real PRs (renames, spaces and non-ASCII in names, binary files, 3000-file PRs); encode; assert byte-exact decode; check how GitHub percent-encodes unusual filenames against urllib quote; compare tokens with and without the patch field; ask which files were added, renamed or removed.
because: re-encodes URLs that repeat the filename, sha and repo already in the entry with no information loss
check: In an array of GitHub file entries, the first entry keeps blob_url as the reference and every later entry drops blob_url, raw_url and contents_url (derived from the filename and the reference's owner, repo and head sha); every entry drops changes (additions plus deletions); a '§ghfiles' header marks the encoding and decode restores the exact bytes.

title: GitLab commit JSON: fold twin fields (short_id, created_at, committer, message, web_url)
detail: GitLab v4 commit objects (repository/commits, merge request commits) restate fields: short_id is a prefix of id, committed_date and created_at usually equal authored_date, committer_* equal author_*, message is title plus a newline, and web_url is a fixed prefix plus the 40-hex id again. Replace each twin with a '=source' string under a '§gitlab' header; decode resolves them in dependency order. Measured on a reconstructed fixture: 20 commits 4,381 vs 3,361 o200k tokens (-23%) but only -16% of characters, because hex ids are cheap in characters; merge request objects and change entries saved only 2-6% of tokens and are left out.
test: Capture glab api projects/:id/repository/commits?per_page=100 from gitlab.com and a self-managed instance; encode; assert byte-exact decode; count commits whose created_at differs from both dates; compare o200k tokens; ask who authored each commit and when it was committed.
because: re-encodes fields that repeat another field of the same object with no information loss
check: In GitLab v4 commit objects, a field that repeats another field of the same object (short_id as a prefix of id, committed_date and created_at as the author or committed date, committer_* as author_*, title as message's first line or message as title, web_url as the first entry's prefix plus id) is replaced by a '=source' marker; a '§gitlab' header marks the encoding and decode restores the exact bytes.

title: git blame --line-porcelain: keep each commit's metadata block once
detail: git blame --line-porcelain repeats the full metadata block (author, mail, time, tz, committer x4, summary, previous, filename) before every source line, even for consecutive lines of one commit. Keep the block on a commit's first line only: later lines keep 'sha orig final' and the tab-led source line, which is exactly git's own --porcelain layout, so the encoding can be checked against git itself and re-expanded. Measured on a real git 2.43 capture (18 lines, 3 commits): 2,073 vs 935 o200k tokens, byte-identical to what --porcelain printed for the same range. #392 covers the default human format.
test: Capture git blame --line-porcelain on 10 real files (boundary commits, renames with previous, -C moves, 2000+ lines); encode; assert the result equals git blame --porcelain for the same range and that an independent expander restores the input; compare o200k tokens; ask who last changed line N and in which commit.
because: re-encodes repeated per-commit metadata blocks with no information loss
check: In git blame --line-porcelain output, the metadata block of a commit is kept on its first line only and later lines of the same commit keep just the 'sha orig final' header and the tab-led source line (the layout --porcelain prints); a repeated sha whose block differs keeps its own.
check_loses: nothing: the repeated author, committer, summary, previous and filename lines are re-derived from the first block of the same sha (they are identical by construction)

title: git reflog and stash list: drop ref@{N} counters that equal the line position
detail: git reflog and git stash list number every line ref@{N}, where N is just the line position and the ref is the same on every line (HEAD or stash). A '§seq HEAD' header names the ref once and the counters go; decode renumbers, and offset starts (--skip), gaps, dates (HEAD@{2 hours ago}) and mixed refs (reflog --all) are left alone. Measured on a real capture: a 20-entry reflog 349 vs 253 o200k tokens, a 3-entry stash list 48 vs 37.
test: Capture git reflog, git reflog show BRANCH, git stash list and git log -g --oneline from 10 repos (decorated first lines on a tty, rebases, resets); encode; assert byte-exact decode; compare tokens; ask which commit HEAD was on before the last reset.
because: re-encodes counters that equal the line position with no information loss
check: In git reflog and git stash list output the ref name and the @{N} counters (which equal each line's position) are dropped from every line and named once in a '§seq REF' header; decode restores the exact text.

title: Rewrite long-form git status as the short form's XY codes under git's own branch line
detail: git status in its long form spends section headers, hint lines and 'modified:   ' labels on every path, where the porcelain short form carries the same index and worktree state in two letters. Rewrite to '## branch...upstream [ahead N, behind M]' plus 'XY path' rows (a path both staged and modified becomes MM, renames stay 'R  old -> new', names with spaces get git's quotes), '(clean)' for a clean tree, and leave anything unrecognised (rebase in progress, unknown labels) untouched. Measured on real git 2.43 captures: a mixed-state status 240 vs 94 o200k tokens, clean 23 vs 8, conflicted merge 114 vs 23, checked against git status -sb of the same state. #29 strips hints only and #486 injects status.short through config; this works on output any harness already holds.
test: Capture git status from 30 repo states (clean, ahead, behind, diverged, detached, conflicted, mid-rebase, submodules, ignored); transform; assert the facts equal those of git status --short --branch for the same state; compare tokens; ask which files are staged, which are modified only in the worktree, and whether the branch is behind.
because: re-encodes section prose and labels as two-letter state codes with no information loss
check: Long-form git status becomes the short form's two-letter codes under git's own '## branch...upstream [ahead N]' line: staged and unstaged entries of one path merge into one XY line, renames keep 'old -> new', untracked and ignored paths get '??' and '!!', and a clean tree gets '(clean)'; unknown lines or labels make it leave the text alone.
check_loses: the hint lines and section headers, and the prose summary line (all derivable from the entries); order inside sections (tracked paths are sorted by path as in the short form, untracked and ignored keep their order)

title: diff -rq: name the two roots once and drop the second path
detail: diff -rq prints the second path of 'Files A/p and B/p differ' as the first with its root swapped, and every 'Only in' line repeats a root. A '§drq A<TAB>B' header names the roots once (inferred from the first Files line) and each line keeps its relative path ('~ p', '< d/n', '> d/n', '! p: regular file -> directory'); decode restores the exact text and lines that do not follow the roots stay verbatim. Measured on real captures: relative roots 110 vs 63 o200k tokens, absolute roots 201 vs 76.
test: Capture diff -rq for 10 directory pairs (build outputs, node_modules, trailing slashes, names with ' and ' or ': ', symlinks, fifos); encode; assert byte-exact decode; compare tokens; ask which files differ and which exist on one side only.
because: re-encodes paths that repeat a root and a relative part with no information loss
check: diff -rq lines are rewritten against two roots named once in a '§drq A<TAB>B' header: 'Files A/p and B/p differ' becomes '~ p', 'Only in A/d: n' becomes '< d/n' (B: '>'), 'File A/p is a X while file B/p is a Y' becomes '! p: X -> Y'; decode restores the exact text, and lines that do not follow the roots stay verbatim.

title: git merge and pull: fold create, delete, rename and mode lines into the stat rows
detail: git merge, git pull and git diff --stat --summary print a stat table and then 'create mode', 'delete mode', 'rename' and 'mode change' lines that restate paths already in the table. Mark the row instead, (new), (del 100755), (rename 98%) or (chmod 100644 => 100755), and drop the summary line; a summary line whose path the table abbreviated ('.../x.py') keeps its own line. Measured on a real merge capture (17 files, 15 summary lines, 14 folded): 444 vs 322 o200k tokens. git commit prints no table, so nothing folds there.
test: Capture git merge, git pull and git log --stat --summary for 10 real merges (renames with similarity, mode changes, binary files, long paths, submodules); encode; assert every summary fact survives (independent fact multiset) and that unmatched lines stay; compare tokens; ask which files were created, deleted or renamed.
because: re-encodes summary lines that restate stat-table paths with no information loss
check: In a stat table followed by its --summary block (git merge, git pull, git diff --stat --summary), each 'create mode', 'delete mode', 'rename' and 'mode change' line whose path is a table row is folded into that row as a trailing (new), (del), (rename 98%) or (chmod a => b) marker and removed; summary lines that match no row (paths the table abbreviated as '.../x') keep their own line.
check_loses: the position of a summary line that keeps its own line (it now sits right after the 'N files changed' line); otherwise nothing, the other lines are re-derived from the markers in table order (mode 100644 is the default)

title: git fetch ref-update rows: drop the destination that restates the source and the padding
detail: git fetch prints one row per updated ref as '* [new tag]      v1.2.3   -> v1.2.3' or '* [new branch]   x   -> origin/x', writing the name twice and padding two columns; a first fetch --tags in a CI checkout prints hundreds. A '§fetch W1 W2 REMOTE' header carries the widths and the remote, rows keep flag, summary and source, and a destination other than REMOTE/source or source follows '->'; decode restores the exact text. Measured on a real capture (26 rows): 527 vs 302 o200k tokens. #518 collapses ref series into ranges and drops most refs; this keeps every one.
test: Capture git fetch --tags, --prune and --all from 10 real remotes (forced updates, rejected tags, refs/pull/*, new refs, multiple remotes); encode; assert byte-exact decode, including the column widths git chose; compare tokens; ask which branches are new and which tag update was rejected.
because: re-encodes destination names and padding that restate the source with no information loss
check: git fetch ref-update rows lose the column padding and the destination that restates the source: '* [new tag]   v1.0   -> v1.0' keeps flag, summary and source (a destination other than REMOTE/source or source is kept after '->'), widths and the remote go in a '§fetch W1 W2 REMOTE' header, and decode restores the exact text.

title: GitHub Actions annotations: hoist the absolute checkout root and the restated path:line:col
detail: ruff --output-format=github (and ESLint's GitHub formatters) print '::error title=..,file=/home/runner/work/r/r/src/a.py,line=1,col=8,..::src/a.py:1:8: F401 ...', repeating the absolute checkout root on every line and stating path, line and column twice. A '§gha ROOT' header names the root once; file=@rel hoists it and file=@@rel also drops the restated 'rel:line:col: ' prefix; decode restores the exact bytes and other lines stay verbatim. Measured on real ruff 0.16.9 output (35 findings in 5 files, runner root substituted for the scratch path): 2,302 vs 1,816 o200k tokens.
test: Capture the annotation lines of 10 real CI logs (ruff, eslint-formatter-github, golangci-lint github-actions, mypy and phpstan reporters) with their real roots; encode; assert byte-exact decode; count logs whose paths are relative and therefore untouched; compare tokens; ask which file and line each finding points at.
because: re-encodes a repeated checkout root and a restated path:line:col with no information loss
check: In GitHub Actions workflow-command annotation lines that carry an absolute file path (ruff --output-format=github, ESLint formatters), the checkout root is named once in a '§gha ROOT' header; file=ROOT/rel becomes file=@rel, and when the message starts with 'rel:line:col: ' that restated prefix is dropped too (file=@@rel); decode restores the exact bytes, and lines that do not fit stay verbatim.

title: Byte-array source literals to joined hex lines: protoc-gen-go rawDesc, xxd -i
detail: Generated *.pb.go files, `xxd -i` headers and bin2c output spell binary blobs as `0x0a, 0x1e, ...` 16 (or 12) per line, about five tokens per byte against 1.3 as joined hex. Each regular run of such lines becomes one `§bytes cols= lines= tail=` header plus one joined-hex line per source line; the header carries the width, the line count and whether the last line ends in a comma, so decode rebuilds the original byte for byte, and short or irregular runs stay verbatim. Measured on a real capture (protobuf-go v1.31.0 durationpb and structpb rawDesc blocks): 1509 vs 499 and 4047 vs 1003 o200k tokens.
test: Capture the *.pb.go and generated-header files of 5 real repos plus xxd -i and bin2c output; transform; assert byte-exact decode and that gofmt reports nothing on the decoded Go; compare o200k tokens per file; ask whether an agent ever needs these bytes (it should not edit them, so keep the skip for files about to be edited).
because: re-encodes byte literals as hex with no information loss
check: Runs of 3+ lines of '0xNN, 0xNN, ...' byte literals (equal width, same indent, comma at line end) become a '§bytes' header plus one joined-hex line per source line; decode rebuilds the exact original, including the width of the last line and a comma-less last line.

title: kubectl get secret -o yaml: decode printable base64 values into stringData
detail: kubectl prints every Secret `data:` value as base64, roughly twice the tokens of the text it encodes. When all values of a `data:` block under `kind: Secret` are canonical base64 of printable UTF-8, the block becomes `stringData:` (the write-only plain-text twin that kubectl apply accepts) with plain, double-quoted or `|` block scalars behind a one-line comment; decode re-encodes each value to the identical base64, and blocks with a binary value, ConfigMaps and non-Secret YAML stay. Measured on a synthetic fixture (URL, token, JSON config, a real certificate and a PEM-shaped key, kubectl layout reconstructed from memory): 1806 vs 1288 o200k tokens.
test: Capture 10 real kubectl get secret -o yaml outputs (Opaque, TLS, dockerconfigjson, helm release secrets); transform; assert yaml.safe_load of the output equals the base64-decoded values and that decode restores the bytes; compare tokens; ask whether agents paste decoded plaintext into follow-up commands (base64 was never protection, but pair with #370 or #1122 if a leak guard is wanted).
because: re-encodes base64 values as plain text with no information loss
check: In a Secret's `data:` block whose values are all canonical base64 of printable UTF-8, the block becomes `stringData:` with plain, quoted or `|` block scalars (header comment line); decode re-encodes every value to the identical base64 and restores `data:`. Blocks with a binary value, ConfigMaps and non-Secret YAML are left alone.

title: HTML tables from pandas to_html and notebooks to TSV
detail: DataFrame.to_html() and notebook _repr_html_ emit a thead, a tbody and a tr with a th or td tag pair per cell. A plain table (th/td grid, no colspan or rowspan, no tags inside cells, on its own lines and not inside a comment or script) becomes one `§table rows= cols= head= rowth=` line plus TSV rows with entities unescaped; the oracle parses the original with html.parser and the output with a TSV reader and compares every cell, its th/td role and all text outside tables. Measured on a real pandas capture (5-row frame with a named index): 332 vs 83 o200k tokens; with the notebook style block kept, 395 vs 147.
test: Capture 20 real df.to_html, _repr_html_ and scraped-table outputs; transform; assert the cell grid, th/td roles and outside text through html.parser; compare tokens; ask a reader LLM cell-lookup questions on the TSV form against the HTML form.
because: re-encodes a plain HTML table as TSV with the same cells, roles and surrounding text
check: Plain HTML tables (th/td grid, no spans, no tags in cells, own lines) become a '§table rows= cols= head= rowth=' line plus TSV rows with entities unescaped; every cell's text and th/td role, and all text outside tables, is unchanged.
check_loses: table, row and cell attributes (border, class, style), thead/tbody/tfoot wrapper tags, the spelling of entities and the layout whitespace between tags

title: SQL DDL: drop quotes around plain lowercase identifiers
detail: Django's sqlite schema editor, sqlmigrate, .schema and pg_dump quote every name with double quotes, and MySQL SHOW CREATE TABLE with backticks. Inside CREATE/ALTER ... TABLE, INDEX or VIEW statements, lowercase [a-z_][a-z0-9_]* names that are not reserved words in PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite or the standard, and are not glued to a neighbouring word, lose their quotes; strings, comments, dollar-quoted bodies and text with backslashes are untouched, and a real sqlite3 engine builds the same schema from both texts. Measured on a synthetic fixture (Django-style DDL for five tables and three indexes stored by sqlite3): 441 vs 360 o200k tokens; a MySQL SHOW CREATE TABLE 170 vs 145.
test: Capture sqlite3 .schema of 5 Django dev databases, sqlmigrate output and mysql SHOW CREATE TABLE for 10 tables; transform; assert a real engine builds an identical schema (PRAGMA table_info, foreign_key_list, index_list); compare tokens; ask whether agents hand-write migrations that break on a reserved word (those names stay quoted).
because: removes only redundant identifier quotes; names, case and the token stream are unchanged
check: Inside CREATE/ALTER ... TABLE/INDEX/VIEW statements, quoted identifiers that are lowercase [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*, not reserved in PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite/standard SQL and not glued to a neighbouring word lose their quotes; strings, comments, dollar-quoted bodies, reserved or mixed-case names and text with backslashes are unchanged, and the SQL token stream is otherwise identical.
check_loses: the quote characters around plain lowercase non-reserved identifiers (names, case and token order are unchanged); double quotes are read as identifier quotes only when the text has no backtick

title: Java .properties bundles: decode \uXXXX escapes to characters
detail: ResourceBundle .properties files (LibreOffice, Spring, JDK and Android-style i18n) store every non-ASCII character as an escape like `\u30C7` or `\u00E9` at three or more tokens each. Active escapes (an even number of backslashes before the u, surrogate pairs combined) that denote a non-ASCII printable character are decoded; ASCII, control, no-break-space and invisible escapes stay, so the file's line structure cannot change, and only the hex-digit case of decoded escapes is lost. Measured on real LibreOffice resources: Japanese 899 vs 209, French 285 vs 169, German 364 vs 273 o200k tokens.
test: Capture 20 real .properties bundles (LibreOffice, Spring, JDK resources) across locales; transform; assert a Java 9+ UTF-8 properties reader gives the same map from both texts; compare tokens per script; ask whether an agent that edits the decoded file writes raw UTF-8 into a file an ISO-8859-1 loader reads (do not apply to files about to be edited).
because: re-encodes escapes as the characters they denote; only escape spelling changes
check: In .properties text, active \uXXXX escapes (even number of backslashes before the u, surrogate pairs combined) that denote a non-ASCII printable character become that character; ASCII, control, space-like and invisible escapes, escaped backslashes and malformed escapes stay, and the file's lines are unchanged.
check_loses: the hex-digit case (\u00E9 versus \u00e9) of the decoded escapes

title: UUIDs without dashes behind one legend line
detail: psql uuid columns, az and kubectl uid fields and .NET GUIDs spell 8-4-4-4-12 UUIDs at about four more tokens each than their 32 hex digits. Every word-bounded UUID loses its dashes behind a one-line legend and decode re-dashes every bounded 32-hex token, so text round-trips byte for byte; text that already holds a bare 32-hex token (an MD5) or too few UUIDs to repay the legend is left alone. Measured on a synthetic fixture (24-row psql table with three uuid columns, layout reconstructed from memory): 1758 vs 1456 o200k tokens; az-shaped JSON with three UUIDs per 330 characters only 1054 vs 943.
test: Capture 20 real psql uuid tables, az role and vm lists and kubectl -o json lists; transform; assert byte-exact decode; compare tokens on UUID-dominated versus mixed outputs; ask whether an agent pastes a dashless ID into kubectl --field-selector or az commands that need dashes.
because: re-encodes UUID spelling with no information loss
check: Every word-bounded 8-4-4-4-12 UUID loses its dashes behind a one-line legend and decode re-dashes every bounded 32-hex token, so the text comes back byte for byte; text that already contains a bare 32-hex token, or too few UUIDs to repay the legend, is left alone.

title: Maven pom.xml dependency blocks to G:A:V coordinate lines
detail: pom.xml spells each dependency as five to eight lines of groupId, artifactId, version and scope tags. A run of two or more canonical blocks (fixed tag order, one tag per line, no spaces in values) becomes a `§deps u= n=` header plus one `G:A[:V] [type=] [classifier=] [scope=] [optional]` line per block; decode rebuilds the exact XML, and blocks with exclusions, comments or another tag order stay verbatim. Measured on a synthetic fixture (Spring Boot style pom, nine dependencies, build section kept, reconstructed from memory): 561 vs 361 o200k tokens.
test: Capture 20 real pom.xml files (Spring Boot, multi-module, libraries); transform; assert byte-exact decode and that mvn -q validate accepts the decoded pom; compare tokens; ask whether an agent adding a dependency edits the right line after seeing only coordinates (do not apply to a pom about to be edited).
because: re-encodes dependency blocks as coordinate lines with no information loss
check: A run of two or more canonical Maven <dependency> blocks (groupId, artifactId, then version/type/classifier/scope/optional in that order, one tag per line, values without spaces) becomes a '§deps' header and one 'G:A[:V] [type=] [classifier=] [scope=] [optional]' line per block; decode rebuilds the exact XML, and blocks with exclusions or other tag orders stay verbatim.

title: CSV cells holding JSON: switch doubled-quote CSV to TSV
detail: Postgres COPY ... CSV, BigQuery and Stripe exports put JSON in a cell, so every quote is doubled (`"{""plan"":""pro""}"`). With at least six doubled quotes and no cell holding a tab, newline or leading quote, the file is re-emitted as TSV with the raw JSON; the rows parse to the same cells and the line-ending style is kept, and any file that cannot be tab-safe comes back unchanged. Measured on a synthetic fixture (csv.writer output, 12 rows with a JSON metadata column): 777 vs 608 o200k tokens.
test: Capture 20 real COPY CSV, BigQuery and Stripe exports with JSON columns; transform; assert csv.reader rows equal the TSV rows; compare tokens; ask whether agents load the TSV with pandas read_csv(sep='\t') without quote surprises.
because: re-encodes CSV quoting as TSV; the cells are identical
check: A CSV with at least six doubled quotes, whose cells contain no tab, newline or leading quote, is re-emitted as TSV with the raw cell text; the parsed rows are identical, line endings and the final newline are kept, and any file that cannot be TSV-safe comes back unchanged.
check_loses: the CSV quoting (quote characters and doubled quotes); the delimiter changes from comma to tab

title: Android values resources: same-tag string, color and dimen lines to name=value rows
detail: Android strings.xml, colors.xml and dimens.xml repeat `<string name="k">v</string>` on every line, about eight tokens of markup per entry. A run of three or more one-line resources of the same tag with only a name (optionally translatable="false") becomes a `§res tag= n=` header plus `name=value` lines; values are kept byte for byte, decode rebuilds the exact XML, and CDATA, nested tags, other attributes and short runs stay verbatim. Measured on a synthetic fixture (33 strings, a string-array, colors and dimens, reconstructed from memory): 587 vs 418 o200k tokens.
test: Capture the values/ folders of 10 real Android apps (strings, colors, dimens); transform; assert byte-exact decode and that aapt2 compile accepts the decoded XML; compare tokens; ask whether a translation task still finds the right key (do not apply to a file about to be edited).
because: re-encodes resource lines as name=value rows with no information loss
check: A run of three or more one-line Android resources of the same tag with only name (and optionally translatable="false") becomes a '§res' header and 'name=value' lines; decode rebuilds the exact XML, and CDATA, nested tags, other attributes and short runs stay verbatim.

title: Spreadsheet Markdown from MarkItDown and pandas: blank NaN cells, Unnamed: N headers and .0 floats
detail: MarkItDown (xlsx via pandas read_excel) and pandas to_markdown print empty cells as NaN, blank header cells as `Unnamed: 5` and an integer column that holds a NaN as `120.0`. In pipe tables NaN body cells and `Unnamed: N` headers become empty and a column whose non-NaN cells all end in .0 loses the suffix; padding, separators and every other cell are untouched, and pandas itself folded blank cells and NaN strings into NaN on import. Measured on a real MarkItDown capture (two sheets): 275 vs 241 o200k tokens; a sparse synthetic 20-row table 558 vs 450.
test: Capture 20 real MarkItDown xlsx outputs and pandas to_markdown frames; transform; assert cells are equal modulo NaN, Unnamed and .0 with the whole-column rule; compare tokens; ask whether a reader treats blank cells as missing when summing columns.
because: re-encodes missing-value and placeholder spellings; same facts
check: In pipe tables, body cells that are exactly NaN become empty, header cells 'Unnamed: N' become empty, and a column whose non-NaN cells all look like 123.0 loses the '.0'; cell padding, every other cell, separators and all non-table text are unchanged.
check_loses: the literal 'NaN' versus an empty cell, the synthetic 'Unnamed: N' header text, and the '.0' suffix on whole-number float columns

title: Drop SSE event: lines and sequence_number that the payload already states
detail: curl -N of an Anthropic Messages or OpenAI Responses stream sends 'event: content_block_delta' above data: {"type":"content_block_delta",...}, and every Responses event also carries sequence_number equal to its frame index. When every typed frame agrees, drop both and restore them from the payload's type and the frame position; a frame whose event name differs keeps its line. Measured on a synthetic fixture (documented format, reconstructed): Anthropic stream 1,489 vs 1,233 o200k tokens (-17%), Responses stream 4,349 vs 3,894 (-10%). Unlike #891 (reassembly) every frame survives.
test: Capture 10 curl -N streams from each of two streaming APIs, or replay saved SSE logs; encode; assert decode is byte exact; compare o200k tokens on each; check that a reader LLM still answers which event closed the message and with what stop_reason from the encoded stream with its one-line header.
because: re-encodes framing derivable from the frame's own JSON and position with no information loss
check: Removes each 'event: X' line whose X equals the type member of its data JSON, and the sequence_number member when it equals the frame's index in every typed frame (Anthropic Messages and OpenAI Responses streams); both are restored from the payload and position, frames that disagree stay as they are, and a stream with a typed data-only frame keeps its event lines.

title: Responses API stream: reference the repeated response snapshots and full-text copies
detail: An OpenAI Responses stream resends the whole answer in output_text.done, content_part.done, output_item.done and completed, and the full response object (instructions, tools, config) in created, in_progress and completed. Replace a response equal to created by '§created', its unchanged members by '§=' and each full-text copy equal to the streamed deltas by '§Δ', under a one-line legend; every event stays and decode rebuilds each byte (JSON string escapes included). Measured on a synthetic fixture (documented event sequence, reconstructed): 35-word answer with one function tool 4,349 vs 3,773 o200k tokens (-13%), two-word answer 1,706 vs 1,256 (-26%); the saving is roughly constant, so it shrinks as the answer grows.
test: Capture 10 Responses API streams (curl -N) with and without tools and with answers of 20 to 2,000 tokens; encode; assert decode is byte exact; plot saving against answer length; check a reader still answers the final text, usage and status from the encoded stream.
because: re-encodes repeated snapshots as references to the earlier event with no information loss
check: In an OpenAI Responses stream, a repeated response.created snapshot (in_progress) and the unchanged members of the completed snapshot become '§created' / '§=' references, and the full-text copies in the done and completed events become '§Δ'; every event stays, and decode rebuilds each byte.

title: LSP Range objects to line:character spans in language-server tool results
detail: MCP bridges and agent tools that return raw LSP Location, DocumentSymbol and Diagnostic JSON spell every range as {"start":{"line":10,"character":4},"end":{"line":10,"character":16}}. Replace each canonical range (compact, ', '-separated or 2-space pretty-printed) by "@10:4-10:16" under a one-line legend; decode rebuilds the exact object text. Measured on captured pyright-langserver 1.1.414 results: references 342 vs 250 o200k tokens (-27%), documentSymbol 769 vs 484 (-37%), the same references pretty-printed 672 vs 341 (-49%); a diagnostics frame with long messages only -12%.
test: Capture 10 results each of references, definition, documentSymbol and publishDiagnostics from pyright, tsserver, gopls and rust-analyzer through an LSP MCP bridge; encode; assert decode is byte exact; compare tokens; ask a reader for the file:line:column of each reference from the encoded result.
because: re-encodes Range objects as a span token with no information loss
check: Every LSP Range object ({start:{line,character},end:{line,character}}, compact, ', '-separated or 2-space pretty-printed) becomes a "@a:b-c:d" span under a one-line legend and decode rebuilds the exact object text; text that already contains a span-shaped string is left alone.

title: MCP filesystem directory_tree JSON to an indented outline
detail: The reference filesystem MCP server's directory_tree returns JSON.stringify(tree, null, 2) of {name,type,children} nodes, about 20 tokens per entry. Print one line per entry, directories with a trailing slash, children indented two spaces; decode rebuilds the identical JSON text, and any other shape or an unusual file name leaves the text alone. Measured on a fixture built the way server-filesystem 1.0.0's source builds it (86 entries of this repository; the server itself was not run): 1,809 vs 398 o200k tokens (-78%).
test: Run the filesystem server on 10 real repositories of 50 to 5,000 entries and call directory_tree with and without excludePatterns; encode; assert decode is byte exact; compare tokens; ask a reader to list the files under one directory from the outline.
because: re-encodes a nested name/type/children tree as an indented outline with no information loss
check: A directory_tree JSON text (exactly JSON.stringify(tree, null, 2) of name/type/children nodes) becomes one outline line per entry, directories marked with a trailing slash and children indented two spaces, and decode rebuilds the identical JSON text; anything else is left alone.

title: JSONL LLM request logs: back-reference the messages prefix shared with the previous request
detail: A tool-calling loop logged one request body per line resends every earlier message in each later request, so the log grows quadratically; tools and metadata repeat too. Replace the leading messages equal to the previous line's by one "§prev:n" element and any other member (tools, system, parameters) identical to the previous line's by "§same"; decode rebuilds every byte, including lines it could not parse. Measured on a synthetic fixture (OpenAI-format loop, reconstructed): six requests 5,406 vs 1,901 o200k tokens (-65%).
test: Collect request logs from 5 LLM-app debugging sessions (LiteLLM spend logs, Langfuse or Helicone exports, custom loggers); measure how often consecutive requests share a message prefix; encode; assert decode is byte exact; compare tokens; ask a reader what changed between request 4 and 5.
because: re-encodes a repeated message prefix as a reference to the previous line with no information loss
check: In a JSONL log of LLM request bodies, the leading messages that equal the previous request's become one "§prev:n" element and any other member (tools, system, parameters) identical to the previous request's becomes "§same"; decode rebuilds every byte, including lines it could not parse.

title: Pydantic and FastMCP tool schemas: nullable anyOf to type arrays, single-use $defs inlined
detail: model_json_schema emits anyOf [T, null] for every Optional parameter, hoists each nested model into $defs even when referenced once, and adds a title equal to the title-cased name. Rewrite to type [T, null], inline a definition referenced exactly once, and drop a property title equal to the default title-case of its name; anyOf branches with enum, const or $ref are left alone. Measured on captured mcp 2.3.0 + pydantic 2.13 output: tools/list of five tools with outputSchema 1,368 vs 953 o200k tokens (-30%). #248 strips such boilerplate and #1356 hoists repeats; this keeps every constraint and the oracle checks the same instances validate.
test: Capture tools/list from 10 real FastMCP, official TypeScript-SDK and pydantic-AI servers; transform in a proxy; validate generated sample calls against both schemas; run a tool-choice eval before and after; compare tokens per request.
because: rewrites schema syntax to an equivalent form that accepts the same instances
check: In pydantic/FastMCP tool schemas, anyOf [T, null] with a plain T becomes type [T, null], a $defs entry referenced exactly once is inlined, and a property title equal to the default title-case of its name is dropped; a mini JSON Schema validator accepts and rejects the same probe instances before and after, and descriptions, defaults, enums, property names and required lists are unchanged.
check_loses: the name of a single-use $defs entry as a separate definition (its own title stays), and which properties carried an explicit title equal to the default title-case of their name (annotation only, no validation effect); JSON formatting is kept

title: OpenAI SDK parse() reprs: drop the parsed= model that restates the content JSON
detail: print(completion) after client.chat.completions.parse() shows each ParsedChatCompletionMessage with content='{...}' (the structured-output JSON) and parsed=Order(...) holding the same object. When ast shows the parsed value equals json.loads(content), types and key order included, replace the parsed value by '<same object as content>'; a differing, None or truncated value stays. Measured on captured openai 3.45 output: a 2-item order 389 vs 307 o200k tokens (-21%), a 14-item order with non-ASCII names 944 vs 583 (-38%).
test: Run 10 real parse() calls (Order-like, nested, optional fields, n=2) against a recorded or live endpoint; print and repr the completions; encode; assert the oracle holds; compare tokens; ask a reader for a nested field value from the encoded text.
because: removes a second copy of the same object with no information loss
check: In a printed ParsedChatCompletionMessage, the parsed=Model(...) repr is replaced by '<same object as content>' when it holds exactly the object the content JSON string encodes (ast-checked, types and key order included); a differing, None or non-repr parsed value stays.
check_loses: the repr formatting of the parsed value (class names such as Order, Address, Item) and its exact whitespace; the data is the content string that stays

title: Ethereum JSON-RPC receipts: log fields inherited from the receipt and zero logsBloom
detail: eth_getTransactionReceipt and cast receipt --json repeat blockHash, blockNumber, transactionHash and transactionIndex in every logs[] entry although the receipt already carries them, and print logsBloom as 512 hex digits that are all zero when there are no logs. Replace each repeated member by "=" and a zero bloom by "0x[zeros:512]" under a one-line legend; decode restores the same JSON text. Measured on a synthetic fixture (geth field order, reconstructed): a swap receipt with 6 logs 2,216 vs 1,754 o200k tokens (-21%), a plain transfer 395 vs 265 (-33%).
test: Capture 20 receipts from a local anvil or hardhat node (swaps, mints, failed and plain transfers) and from a public RPC; encode; assert decode is byte exact; compare tokens; ask a reader which block and transaction each log belongs to.
because: removes members equal to the parent receipt's with no information loss
check: In Ethereum JSON-RPC receipts, a log's blockHash, blockNumber, transactionHash and transactionIndex equal to the receipt's become "=", and an all-zero logsBloom becomes "0x[zeros:n]"; decode restores the same JSON text (compact, ', '-separated or indent 2).

title: OpenAI logprobs: replace bytes arrays that equal the UTF-8 of the token
detail: chat.completion logprobs.content[] entries carry token, logprob and bytes, and every top_logprobs entry repeats the pair with another bytes array (ints, one per line when indent=2). Replace a bytes array equal to the UTF-8 encoding of its token by "utf8"; arrays for partial characters stay; decode restores the same JSON text. Measured on a synthetic fixture (documented shape, reconstructed): 15 tokens with top_logprobs=5 compact 2,431 vs 2,043 o200k tokens (-16%), pretty-printed with indent=2 4,414 vs 3,276 (-26%).
test: Request logprobs with top_logprobs=5 on 10 prompts including CJK, emoji and code; check how often bytes differs from the token's UTF-8; encode; assert decode is byte exact; compare tokens.
because: removes an array derivable from the sibling token string with no information loss
check: In a chat.completions logprobs payload, every "bytes" array that equals the UTF-8 encoding of its sibling token string becomes "utf8" (other arrays, such as partial-character tokens, stay), and decode restores the same JSON text (compact, ', '-separated or indented).

title: Postman collections: drop url pieces derivable from url.raw
detail: Postman v2.1 exports give every request url as raw plus protocol, host, port, path, query and hash members that split the same string. When splitting raw at ://, '.', ':', '/', '?', '&', '=' and '#' reproduces the members exactly, replace them with one "split":"raw" member and re-split on decode; urls with disabled query items, descriptions or odd characters keep theirs. Measured on a synthetic fixture (v2.1 format, tab-indented, reconstructed): 8 requests 1,518 vs 1,044 o200k tokens (-31%), minified 763 vs 587 (-23%).
test: Collect 10 real Postman or Newman collections from public repos; encode; assert decode is byte exact and count urls that keep their pieces; compare tokens; ask a reader for the host and query of one request from the encoded file.
because: removes members derivable from the sibling raw string with no information loss
check: In a Postman v2.1 collection, a request url object whose protocol, host, port, path, query and hash members are exactly what splitting url.raw gives loses them to one "split":"raw" member, and decode re-splits raw; urls whose pieces differ (disabled query items, strings with spaces) keep theirs.

title: Replay cursor-up and erase-line redraws to the final screen
detail: docker compose up, docker pull, pip (rich), ora and npm spinners redraw a block in place with ESC[nA cursor-up, ESC[2K erase-line and CR, so a pty capture or CI log holds every frame back to back; #9 only strips the escapes and #10 only collapses single-line CR frames. Replay the text on a character grid and keep the lines a terminal still shows; tabs, absolute addressing, the alternate screen, wide characters and unknown escapes leave the text untouched. Measured on a real capture (pip's vendored rich, 3 tasks, 6 refreshes, forced terminal): 761 vs 70 o200k tokens; a synthetic compose-style 7-refresh block 721 vs 68.
test: Run docker compose up, docker pull, npm install and pip install under script(1) or in a tmux pane and save the raw bytes; replay them; assert the result equals tmux capture-pane of the same run (pyte as a second opinion); compare tokens; ask which service is unhealthy from the replayed text and the raw text.
because: keeps exactly the screen a terminal shows and drops only frames the terminal itself overwrote
check: When the text uses relative cursor motion or erase codes (CSI A B C D E F G J K), it is replayed on a character grid (CR, LF, BS handled, SGR and OSC ignored) and only the final screen text is kept; tabs, absolute cursor addressing, the alternate screen, double-width characters and any unknown or truncated escape leave the text untouched.
check_loses: frames and cell contents a terminal overwrites or erases, trailing spaces, the \r\n versus \n versus bare \r distinction (every line feed also returns the carriage), SGR colours and other invisible escapes

title: Ditto the dev, inode and path tail in /proc/PID/maps
detail: cat /proc/PID/maps gives every mapping of one library its own line with the dev, inode and a padded path (libc.so.6 fills 5 consecutive lines). Replace a tail identical to the line above with a quote mark; addresses, permissions and offset stay, and a line that already ends in quote marks is escaped, so decode restores the text byte for byte. Measured on real captures: a python3.13 process with 34 threads 5,763 vs 4,245 o200k tokens, node 3,530 vs 2,508, cat 865 vs 609.
test: Capture /proc/PID/maps for python, node and java processes and for a process that imports many .so files (numpy, torch); encode; assert decode is byte-identical; compare tokens; ask which file is mapped executable at a given address from the encoded and the original text.
because: re-encodes a repeated line tail as a ditto mark with no information loss
check: In /proc/PID/maps, a mapping whose dev, inode and path tail equals the line above is written as a quote mark after the offset; start, end, permissions and offset stay on every line; decode restores the text byte for byte, including lines that already end in quote marks.

title: Alias hex Mems_allowed and Cpus_allowed masks to their list twins
detail: /proc/PID/status prints Mems_allowed as 32 comma-separated 8-digit hex groups on distro kernels (one line, 132 o200k tokens) and Mems_allowed_list on the next line says the same in a few characters; Cpus_allowed on 64+ CPU hosts is the same twin. The mask is a pure function of the list and the bit width, so write '@1024' and regenerate it on decode; the encoder aliases only when the re-rendered mask equals the original text. Measured on real captures: status of cat 649 vs 525, python 655 vs 531, node 652 vs 528 o200k tokens (-19%).
test: Capture /proc/PID/status for 20 processes on a distro kernel and on a 64-CPU host; encode; assert decode is byte-identical; check every Mems_allowed seen uses 8-digit groups; compare tokens.
because: re-encodes a mask that its *_list twin regenerates exactly, with no information loss
check: In /proc/PID/status, a Cpus_allowed or Mems_allowed hex mask that the following *_list line regenerates exactly is replaced by '@<bit width>'; decode rebuilds the mask byte for byte, and values that already start with '@' are escaped.

title: Group ps -eLf thread rows under one process row
detail: ps -eLf prints one row per thread and every row repeats UID, PID, PPID, NLWP, STIME, TTY and the whole command line, so a JVM or Node process with 100 threads and a 400-character argv prints that line 100 times. Keep the first row in full and write the others as '+LWP=n C=n TIME=t'; every field of every row is recoverable and only column padding is lost. Measured on real captures: this container's full 150-row ps -eLf 43,355 vs 23,970 o200k tokens (-45%); a 50-row excerpt with a 35-thread process 6,683 vs 1,151 (-83%).
test: Capture ps -eLf and ps -Lf -p PID on hosts running a JVM, Node, Go and a Python thread pool; encode; assert every parsed field of every row is recoverable; compare tokens; ask which LWPs of a PID have used CPU time and how many threads it has.
because: re-encodes rows that repeat all but three fields as short continuation lines, with no information loss
check: In ps -eLf output, consecutive thread rows that share UID, PID, PPID, NLWP, STIME, TTY and command line keep only the first row in full; the others become '+LWP=n C=n TIME=t' lines; every field of every row is recoverable, and a text that already contains such a line is left alone.
check_loses: column alignment padding of the collapsed thread rows

title: Drop forever lifetimes and mark derivable brd in ip addr
detail: ip addr prints 'valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever' under almost every address, an IPv4 'brd' equal to the subnet broadcast, and 'brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff' on every Ethernet link. When every address has its lifetime line, drop the forever lines (absent means forever) and write the derivable broadcasts as 'brd *'; the oracle recomputes both from the other fields. Measured on a synthetic fixture (Docker host with 7 interfaces, reconstructed from memory): 741 vs 597 o200k tokens (-19%).
test: Run ip addr on 5 hosts (Docker host, VM with DHCP, VPN client, container); encode; assert the facts (addresses, scopes, lifetimes, broadcasts) parse identically; compare tokens; ask which address is dynamic and when its lease ends.
because: drops lines and fields that other text on the same page determines, with no information loss
check: In ip addr output where every address has a lifetime line, 'valid_lft forever preferred_lft forever' lines are dropped (absent means forever), a brd equal to the IPv4 subnet broadcast (prefix <= 30) or to ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff on a link/ether line is written 'brd *', and every other line is kept verbatim.
check_loses: the spelling of the default lifetime line and of a computable broadcast address

title: Merge pstree -ap thread leaves into one PID-range line
detail: pstree -ap prints one rail line per thread, '|-{python3},17414', so a JVM, Go or Node process costs a line per thread and they differ only in the PID. Merge a run of leaves with the same indentation and name into '{python3} x34: 17414-17447', keeping every PID in order and the last rail; decode regenerates the lines byte for byte. Measured on a real capture (python3.13 with 34 threads and one child): 323 vs 33 o200k tokens (-90%); the saving grows with the thread count.
test: Capture pstree -ap for java, node and go processes with 50-500 threads; encode; assert decode is byte-identical; compare tokens; ask how many threads a process has and which PIDs belong to a child.
because: re-encodes a run of near-identical lines as a PID range with no information loss
check: In pstree -ap output, a run of thread leaves '|-{name},PID' with the same indentation and name is merged into one '{name} xN: PID-ranges' line keeping every PID in order and the final rail; decode regenerates the lines byte for byte, escaping lines that already look merged.

title: Fold IPv4 and IPv6 twin listener rows in ss
detail: A dual-stack daemon appears twice in ss -ltnp and ss -tuln, as 0.0.0.0:22 and [::]:22, with the same queues and process (only the fd differs). Merge adjacent twin rows into the first with '*46:22', peer '*46:*' and 'fd=3|4' (127.0.0.1/[::1] pairs use 'lo46'); an independent parser expands both forms to the same row set. Measured on a synthetic fixture (14 rows, reconstructed from memory): 645 vs 400 o200k tokens (-38%). The same pairing exists in netstat -tlnp (tcp/tcp6) and Windows netstat -ano, not measured.
test: Run ss -ltnp and ss -tuln on 10 hosts (web, database, desktop); encode; assert the expanded rows equal the originals; count how often twin rows are adjacent; compare tokens; ask which process listens on 5432 and on which address families.
because: re-encodes two rows that differ only in address family as one row with no information loss
check: In ss output, adjacent rows that differ only by 0.0.0.0:P/[::]:P (or 127.0.0.1/[::1]) and the fd numbers of the process column are merged into one row with a '*46:P' (or 'lo46:P') local address, '*46:*' peer and 'fd=a|b'; every other row is kept.
check_loses: column alignment padding

title: Drop dot leaders from ipconfig /all key-value lines
detail: ipconfig, ipconfig /all and netsh pad every key with '. . . .' up to a fixed column ('Host Name . . . . . . . . . . . . : DESKTOP'), 8-16 tokens of filler per line over 15-25 keys per adapter. Re-emit '   Host Name: DESKTOP'; the dots belong to the localized label and carry no data, and keys, values, indentation and continuation lines stay. Measured on a synthetic fixture (3 adapters, reconstructed from memory): 849 vs 529 o200k tokens (-38%).
test: Run ipconfig /all on 5 Windows 10 and 11 hosts (English plus German and Japanese); encode; assert the parsed key/value pairs are identical; compare tokens; ask for the default gateway and DNS servers of each adapter.
because: removes alignment dots that carry no data, with no information loss
check: In ipconfig-style listings, the run of ' .' alignment dots between a 3-space-indented key and its ': ' is removed; the key text, the value, the indentation and every other line are unchanged.
check_loses: the alignment dots between key and colon

title: Ditto repeated fd and AT_FDCWD path annotations in strace -y
detail: strace -y prints the path after every fd argument and the whole cwd after each AT_FDCWD, so openat, newfstatat and readlinkat lines each repeat a 30-150 character directory. An annotation equal to the last one shown for that fd in the same pid becomes 'N<>' behind a one-line header; decode restores the text byte for byte. Measured on a real 702-line trace of python3 startup (cwd rewritten to a 30-character path): 30,652 vs 24,512 o200k tokens (-20%); a 374-line fork-heavy trace saves 10%.
test: Capture strace -f -y on pytest, npm start and a compiler run from deep working directories; encode; assert decode is byte-identical; compare tokens; ask which file fd 7 was reading at a given line.
because: re-encodes a repeated annotation as a ditto marker with no information loss
check: In strace -y output, an fd or AT_FDCWD path annotation equal to the last one shown for the same fd in the same pid becomes 'N<>' behind a one-line header; decode restores the text byte for byte, and texts without the header, with empty annotations, or starting with the header are handled by leaving or escaping them.

title: Replace the mirrored reply tuple in conntrack rows with <mirror>
detail: conntrack -L and /proc/net/nf_conntrack print each flow's tuple twice, and without NAT the reply tuple is the original with source and destination swapped (src=10.0.0.9 dst=10.0.0.5 sport=443 dport=51234). Replace it with '<mirror>' (flags such as [UNREPLIED] stay between); NAT and ICMP rows keep their reply tuple, and decode restores the text byte for byte. Measured on a synthetic fixture (12 rows, 3 not mirrored, reconstructed from memory): 852 vs 643 o200k tokens (-24%), more on NAT-free hosts.
test: Run conntrack -L and cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack on a router, a Docker host and a Kubernetes node; encode; assert decode is byte-identical; count the share of rows whose reply is mirrored; compare tokens.
because: drops a tuple that the other tuple on the same row determines, with no information loss
check: In conntrack -L and /proc/net/nf_conntrack rows of tcp, udp, sctp and dccp flows, a reply tuple that is the original tuple with source and destination swapped is replaced by '<mirror>' (flags such as [UNREPLIED] between the tuples stay); NAT rows, ICMP rows and other lines are unchanged; decode restores the text byte for byte, and rows that already contain '<mirror>' are escaped.
